# thinkorswim UI Regression System (Sentinel): end-to-end specification

## Read this first: how Sentinel works in one page

**What it is for.** A change to one part of thinkorswim breaks another part, and nobody looks there. The standard example: a Flexible Grid change makes the Active Trader ladder overlap its order buttons at one cell size. User testing of Flexible Grid passes, and the ladder bug ships. Sentinel drives the whole desktop product the way a user does, compares every screen against the build before the change, and reports two things for every change. First, the intended change, with before and after pictures, so the developer no longer hand-screenshots their work. Second, anything else that moved or broke, ranked, with the reason it was tested.

**How it decides what changed and why.** Attribution comes from a build pair, not from AI. A PR run compares the branch build with its merge-base main build, a merge run compares new main with previous main, and an RC run compares the release candidate with the last released build. Both builds run on identically fingerprinted rigs against the same data. If a screen differs, the difference was caused by the code between those two builds.

**How it tests.** Five kinds of test feed one result model:

1. **Surface census.** Every tab, gadget, dialog, ticket variant and settings page in the Surface Registry is visited in each corpus workspace, captured, and diffed. This finds side effects nobody predicted.
2. **Size sweeps.** Every resizable gadget is placed in a Flexible Grid cell and stepped through a ladder of sizes and splitter positions. This is where the ladder overlap is found.
3. **Scripted flows.** Interactive states such as building an order, opening the Order Confirmation dialog or adding a study, with assertions on the values shown.
4. **Layout invariants.** Checks that need no baseline: no overlapping controls, nothing outside its parent, no clipped text, required labels present. They fire on the first run of any new layout.
5. **Oracle checks.** Numbers are read by OCR, export and API, then checked against expectations and arithmetic rules such as quantity times price equals cost.

A bounded Explorer agent runs last in RC runs to find edge cases. Every finding is replayed once before anyone sees it.

**How it decides scope.** The developer's change manifest names what was meant to change. The Dependency Map, plus a static impact step over the diff, lists every surface that consumes what changed. A PR run tests those surfaces plus a smoke set within 45 minutes. Merge runs test everything within 3 hours, and RC runs test everything deeper within 8 hours.

**How it classifies a difference.** A difference on a declared surface that the reviewer confirms matches the manifest is `intended`. A difference on an undeclared surface is `collateral`, the top-priority finding. A difference below the measured noise floor is `noise`. Invariant violations and failed assertions stand on their own and no AI can overrule them. The AI reviewer explains diffs and checks them against the manifest. It never approves baselines, never creates masks, and never changes a rule-based outcome.

**What "no gaps" means here.** No corner of the app is silent. Every checkpoint ends in exactly one outcome from a closed set of 25, with a reason and a named place a human sees it (section 1.10, reason table in 12.2). Every surface is validated against the running app on every run. Nightly synthetic faults prove the detector can still see a missing button or a changed digit. Every unknown about the app has both branches written down before the Phase 0 spike runs.

**Safety.** No order is ever sent by default. One input gateway is the only path to the keyboard and mouse. While a ticket or confirm dialog is open, it drops Enter, Space and order hotkeys. The settings that could bypass confirmation are attested at the start of every run. Paper mode is asserted from the account selector against an exact allowlist. A nightly fire drill proves each block works.

## 1. Purpose, guarantees and how it works end to end

### 1.1 The problem, in the author's terms

A change to one feature breaks another. A developer changes Flexible Grid so chart cells carry less chrome. The Active Trader ladder, which can also live in a Flexible Grid cell, now draws over its own order controls whenever the cell is short. User testing of Flexible Grid does not catch it, because nobody testing Flexible Grid puts an Active Trader panel in a small cell. The developer hand-screenshots the chart grid to prove the change works, which proves nothing about the surfaces the change did not mean to touch.

Sentinel drives the whole product like a user, compares every screen of the build after the change against the build before it, reports the intended change as evidence and anything else that moved as a suspected regression, and does so for every change, every time, without a human remembering to look.

Three facts shape everything else in this spec:

1. Attribution comes from the build pair, not from a model. Candidate and base are installed from pipeline artifacts on identically fingerprinted rigs and driven through identical checkpoints in the same data window (3.1 Build pair rules). What differs, differs because of the change set, or because of an environment fault that has its own outcome name.
2. The system does not need to know what a screen should look like. It needs to know that the candidate should look like the base, and that every layout obeys invariants that hold everywhere (2.7 Layout invariants, INV-01 to INV-15): no two siblings overlap, nothing extends outside its parent, no text is clipped, required labels are present, no placeholder text at capture.
3. The intended change is declared up front in a change manifest (4.3 Change manifest). The manifest, not the reviewer's judgement, decides which diffs may be called `intended`. A diff on a surface the manifest does not declare is `collateral`, the highest-priority finding the system produces.

### 1.2 Assumptions

Every row is verified or carries a Phase 0 branch; the rows are numbered AS-01 to AS-12 (attestation items keep A1 to A11, 12.6); the decision records DR-01 to DR-07 that close the open rows are in 11.8 Phase 0 spike plan: seven decision records, and the chosen branch of each is written to `phase0/branches.yaml`, which the CI lint reads. Sections 2 to 11 must not contradict these rows.

| # | Assumption | Status | Branch if false |

| AS-01 | Internal team: source, pipeline artifacts for branch, main, RC and released builds, Jira, paperMoney and internal test logins, security and compliance contacts. | Given (brief 0). The prerequisites table in 11.7 Prerequisites checklist names the providing team and date for each. | None. A missing prerequisite blocks the phase it gates; it is a project state, not a run outcome. |
| AS-02 | A pipeline artifact installs with auto-update disabled, and the build id is readable from the main window title with GetWindowText (7.3 Pinned build install and version read). The public launcher updates on every start (verified in Schwab's install guide). | To verify (DR-04). | Branch B: one VM snapshot per build taken after the updater ran, plus a release-night upgrade run. Title fallback: OCR of Help > About. Either branch: a build id at launch that differs from the requested build is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_mismatch)`; a change during the run is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` for every later checkpoint of that shard and the run ends `complete_with_env_errors`; on-call sees both ids. |
| AS-03 | thinkorswim is Swing with a custom look and feel; UIA and MSAA see one opaque window; Java Access Bridge exposure is unverified and the bundled runtime may omit the jdk.accessibility module. | To verify (DR-01). | Branch B: OCR word boxes plus template-located controls for invariants, image anchors first for locators (5.5 Locator ladder). The Oracle's API tolerance models the delay (3.2 Data modes); the delayed badge is attested at `fixture_verified` and a change is `env_error (gate: fixture_verified, reason: delay_state)`. |

MFA Branch A: test-backend credential without MFA; Branch B: trusted-device exemption, scripted recovery flow, accounts owner on call for codes during rebuilds (7.7 Login and re-login flows with MFA branches). Drift either way is `env_error`, never a diff. |

### 1.3 Goals and non-goals

Goals:

1. Every PR that touches UI code gets, within 45 minutes of its branch build, a comment separating the intended change (evidence) from everything else that moved (suspected regressions), ranked by tier, with one-click actions (9.2 PR comment template).
2. Every merge to main is compared with the previous main build across the full Surface Registry in the tier A workspaces plus every tier-1 flow within 3 hours.
3. Every release candidate is compared with the last released build across everything, including tier B and migration workspaces, size sweeps, soak and the Explorer, and is signed off N business days before GA (10.9 Release-day timeline).
4. Layout defects are found on the first run of any new layout, with no baseline.
5. Numbers on money surfaces are checked against an oracle, not only against pixels.
6. The system proves nightly that it still sees the defect classes it exists for, and the morning report says so when it does not.
7. Nothing the system does can send an order, except through the identity-gated `paper_send_ok` flow class, OPEN pending the risk owner (6.7 Send policy: both branches).

Non-goals:

- macOS and Linux in phases 1 to 3. Registry, flows, invariants and taxonomy are platform-neutral; only Rig Manager, Capture, Executor and the JAB rung are Windows-specific. Every report header names the platform (2.13, item B07).
- Live accounts, real routing, any customer account.
- Backend correctness beyond what the client displays.
- Load or latency testing beyond RC soak budgets.
- Accessibility conformance; keyboard-only flow variants are flow content.
- Replacing exploratory QA; the Explorer is bounded and runs last in RC runs only.
- Deciding what a screen should look like; baseline approval is human-only.

The full list of what the model cannot detect, each with an id and the label every merge and RC report prints for it, is 2.13 What this model cannot detect and how it is labeled.

### 1.4 The five "no gaps" guarantees as testable statements

"No gaps" does not mean the system knows every corner of the app. It means no corner is silent. Each guarantee has a scheduled test and a loud failure.

| # | Guarantee | Test | Loud failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Every surface is in the Surface Registry, validated against the running app on every run. | At the `workspace_loaded` gate of every run, on both builds, the Orchestrator runs probes P1 to P8 (main menu, tab bar, sub-tabs, gadget picker, Setup entries, settings tree, selectors, context menus, cell content selector) by OCR and template and diffs the result against the registry (2.2.3 Validation against the running app). A nightly self-test runs the same validation against a registry copy with one known surface removed and must yield exactly one `unregistered_surface`. | Any unlisted entry is an `unregistered_surface` checkpoint in Unexpected, tier 1 until classified. A probe whose anchor cannot be located is `landmark_missing` and run health prints "validation incomplete for P<n>". A self-test yielding anything but one is `harness_error`; the morning report says registry validation is blind. |
| G2 | Every checkpoint ends in exactly one outcome from the closed taxonomy (1.10). No silent skip, retry or fallback. | SQLite CHECK constraints generated from `taxonomy.yaml` restrict outcome columns to the closed sets and a trigger makes every outcome immutable except a pending `needs_human` (8.3 Schema). A post-run query asserts zero in-scope checkpoints without an outcome and matrix cells equal to surfaces x personas x entitlement profiles. Retries and fallbacks are named step outcomes rendered in the report. | A failing post-run query is `harness_error` and the run is `aborted_harness`; the Reporter refuses to publish a matrix whose cells do not sum and posts the abort block instead. |
| G3 | Every claim the system makes about itself is proven nightly by canaries. | The Canary Service injects 20 to 30 deterministic mutants per critical checkpoint (M01 to M33 in 12.5 Starter mutant catalog, one catalog at `sentinel-config/canaries/mutants.yaml`, seed 20260101, M25 the identical control) as candidate images through the normal diff, invariant and reviewer path, flagged `synthetic: true` so they never promote a baseline, create a decision or count in metrics (10.3 Canary Service and the mutant catalog). The nightly fire drill and safety canaries (6.5 Nightly fire drill and safety canaries) prove the Input Gateway, attestation reader, identity check, post-run proof and redaction. | The canary result states are `detected`, `missed`, `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded` and `generation_failed`; the Nightly run's own outcome stays `complete`. A money-cell miss sets `detector_blind` (the missed mutant's record is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)`, 10.3); a missed non-money mutant is canary state `missed` and counts toward its class's rolling floor, and a class below that floor sets `detector_degraded`; no canary generated at all sets `generation_failed`. `detector_blind` or `generation_failed` sets `system_state.detector_state`, pages P1, puts the banner "detector is blind" on every report until the next green canary and blocks RC sign-off. Only when no canary could run at all is the Nightly run `aborted_harness (reason: canary_generation_failed)`. Fire drill, two cases (6.5): a drill item the gateway did not block but no new order row appeared is `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)`, every flow that uses that path is quarantined (`not_run (reason: quarantine)`) and on-call is paged P1; a drill item that produced a new order row ends the run `aborted_safety (reason: drill_order_placed)`, the login is blocked and an S1 incident opens. |
| G4 | Every unknown has a decision branch written before the spike runs. | The seven Phase 0 unknowns each have a decision record DR-01 to DR-07 (11.8) with both branches specified in the owning sections; the chosen branch goes into `phase0/branches.yaml`; the CI lint fails on any unresolved branch marker after Phase 0. | Phase 0 cannot exit, and no threshold or run type is enabled, until all seven records carry a chosen branch; DR-07 alone may stay open, in which case Phase 1 starts on its Branch B. |
| G5 | Every failure mode of harness, rig, network, account or model API has a defined handling and a defined place a human sees it. | 5.2 Orchestrator (gate table), 10.1 Failure classes and the diff-engine rule, 10.7 Degraded modes and 7.11 Network preflight and chaos suite map each failure to an outcome name; 9.10 Alerting model maps each outcome to a destination (PR comment, report UI, Slack triage channel, on-call channel, morning report). The chaos suite runs in every RC run and asserts outcome and alert per scenario; the self-tests of 10.8 run at every run start; the dead-man alert fires if no run-completed event arrives by budget plus 15, 30 or 60 minutes (PR, merge, RC) or by 06:00 America/New_York (Nightly). | A chaos scenario without its outcome and alert is `harness_error`; the dead-man path is exercised in the acceptance test (10.10, part C) and by a monthly deliberate stall on rig 6, recorded in run health. |

### 1.5 Success criteria and kill criteria

Metrics are computed from run one, exclude synthetic items, and are printed in every report header with the harness commit, config commit, model id and prompt hash range (9.11 Metrics dashboard and kill criteria repeats this table and owns the dashboard). Targets are provisional until two release cycles have produced data; kill criteria are not.

| Metric | Formula | Target (Phase 1 exit / Phase 2 exit) | Kill or fix criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| False-positive rate | Findings dispositioned noise or expected over all findings shown to a human, per run and rolling 30 days; mutants and suppressed findings excluded. | Under 35 / under 20 percent | Above 50 percent after three releases: PR comments stop, fix, re-enter pilot. |
| Flake rate | Checkpoints whose verdict flips between runs of one build or between a run and its targeted re-run, over checkpoints run; the per-checkpoint flake score drives quarantine at 0.10 over the last 5 observations of the same build (10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine). | Under 5 / under 2 percent | Above 10 percent for two consecutive releases after a fix list: no new flows until under target. |
| Quarantine share | Tier-1 checkpoints currently `not_run (reason: quarantine)` over registered tier-1 checkpoints. | Under 2 percent at every RC cut | Above 2 percent: run health red and the RC gate blocks until flow owners clear rows. |
| Time to triage | Human minutes from report publish to every Unexpected finding dispositioned (capped at 10 minutes per finding); p90 latency to first decision shown beside it. | PR under 15 / 10 minutes; merge under 30 / 20 per morning; RC under 2 hours | Above 2x target for two releases: cut tier-3 scope. |
| Escape rate | Production bugs on a registered surface that a checkpoint existed for and did not flag, per release; each is a root-caused incident classed covered-missed, not run, not registered or not detectable. | Measured / zero on tier 1 | Two consecutive releases with a covered tier-1 escape: system owner review of whether to continue. |
| Coverage per tier | Covered cells over registered cells per tier (2.12 Coverage accounting and the matrix); `not_run` never counts as covered. | Tier 1 100 and tier 2 70 percent / tier 1 100, tier 2 90, tier 3 60 percent | Tier 1 below 100 percent in a merge run blocks that release's RC gate. |
| Canary pass rate | Detected over injected mutants, per class, nightly. | Money-cell 100 percent, others measured / money-cell 100, others at least 95 percent rolling | Any money-cell miss: canary state `detector_blind`, P1 page and the banner on every report; no verdict is trusted until the next green canary. This is whole-pipeline detection (diff, invariants, Oracle, Reviewer), distinct from the Reviewer's own eval gate in the Reviewer quality row. |
| A/A noise floor | Pixels over tolerance and diff components between two captures of one build (3.9 A/A calibration and threshold derivation). | Zero on frozen checkpoints; masked_live per-region floors recorded | A non-zero frozen floor is a flow or environment bug with a fix list, never a raised threshold; unfixed after 5 business days it quarantines the checkpoint. |
| Reviewer quality | Precision and recall per category on the labeled eval set (300 to 500 items, 3.14 Eval set, metrics and gates) per model and prompt version; calibration error; human-overturn rate. | Not required (zero model calls) / `intended` precision at least 0.95, `does_not_match_manifest` recall at least 0.98 on tier-1 eval-set mutants and at least 0.95 overall, per model and prompt version (3.14); this eval gate measures the Reviewer alone and is distinct from the Canary pass rate row, where the whole pipeline must detect 100 percent of money-cell mutants or the detector is blind | `intended` precision below 0.85: `intended` disabled, declared-surface diffs go to `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` until a new eval passes. |
| Harness health | `aborted_harness` and `aborted_budget` share of runs; `env_error` share of checkpoints; `passed_via_agent_fallback` steps over steps; cost per run (rig minutes plus model dollars). | Under 10 percent of runs and 3 percent of checkpoints / under 5 and 1 percent | Every `aborted_harness` and every `aborted_safety` pages harness on-call immediately (P1); two `aborted_harness` in a week freeze harness changes until root-caused. |

Pilot exit (end of Phase 2): two release cycles; false-positive rate under 20 percent; at least one real pre-release catch on an undeclared registered surface; triage within budget; canaries at target every night of the last cycle. The Phase 1 exit test is the worked example in 1.11 run as 10.10 End-to-end acceptance test: the Flexible Grid change, injected as a mutant and as a real branch, caught in a PR run and reported as `collateral` with the primitive FlexibleGrid named.

### 1.6 Run types

| Run type | Trigger | Candidate / base | Scope (algorithm in 2.11) | Budget and rigs (11.2) | Output and audience | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR run | Branch build artifact published for an open PR; one run in flight per PR, a newer push queues and only the latest queued push runs, the superseded push listed in the comment's run history | Branch build / main build at the merge-base (nearest ancestor main commit with an artifact; `base_commit_distance` in run health, intervening merge manifests loaded as declared) | Declared surfaces, Dependency Map expansion of the touched primitives, static impact step surfaces, the smoke census; Ladder S sweeps for tier-1 resizable surfaces in scope; tier-1 flows touching the scope | 45 minutes; pool rigs 1 to 4, up to 4 | PR comment (Intended, Unexpected, coverage matrix, run health) for the developer and PR reviewer; commit status `sentinel/pr-run` | Informational in Phase 1; once the Phase 2 false-positive target holds, the status blocks merge on tier-1 Unexpected findings without a decision and on aborted or unreported runs (status `error`); tier 2 and 3 never block (9.2) |
| Merge run | Merge to main, new main artifact published; merges that outrun capacity coalesce (candidate = newest main, base = last main with a completed merge run, manifest = union, report names the range) | New main / previous main | Full census over the tier A workspaces (900 checkpoints, 2.4), Ladder S sweeps for tier 1 and 2 resizable surfaces, all tier-1 flows | 3 hours; pool rigs 1 to 4 (worst case about 156 minutes, 1.8) | Report UI run page; Slack digest of new unsuppressed Unexpected findings to the triage rotation (9.4) | Triage within one business day (9.12) |
| RC run | RC cut; a new RC build of the same train supersedes a running RC run (RC respin, below the table) | RC build / last released build (lineage baseline, 9.8) | Full census over tier A and B workspaces including migration, all flows of every tier, Ladder F sweeps (tier 1 and 2) and Ladder S (tier 3), chaos suite, soak, Explorer last | 8 hours; all 6 rigs: pool for census, flows and sweeps, rig 5 soak, rig 6 Explorer | RC report for the release manager and triage rotation; Jira for confirmed bugs | Triaged and signed off N business days before GA under the conditions of 10.9, recorded with approver and build |
| Nightly run | 22:00 America/New_York; pre-empted by an RC run (below the table) | Current main / same build (A/A); approved captures as base for mutants | Canaries, A/A drift check, flake statistics refresh, fingerprint check, fire drill and safety canaries | 4 hours (about 2.7 h used); rig 5, with the A/A pass sharded over rigs 4 and 5 after the operating day (11.2) | Morning report to system owner and triage rotation; on-call on `harness_error` or `aborted_safety` | A money-cell miss blocks trust in every verdict and RC sign-off until a Nightly run passes |
| Calibration run | Before any threshold is used; after any fingerprint change (7.13) | One build; per checkpoint, 5 captures back to back on the same rig plus 1 on a second night (3.9) | Every registered checkpoint | One weekend `all_quiet` window (7.10), sharded across the pool (rigs 1 to 4) with every checkpoint's captures on one rig; the brief's "5 times on one rig" is per checkpoint on the same rig, not the whole library serially. That weekend the Nightly A/A check pauses; canaries and fire drill stay on rig 5 (11.2) | Per-checkpoint, per-region noise floors in SQLite; fix list of non-zero frozen floors to flow owners | No threshold is enabled until the fix list is empty or every item carries a human `floor_exception` |

RC respin and pre-emption. A new RC build supersedes the running RC run: the running run schedules no new flow, stops at the next flow boundary with run outcome `aborted_budget (reason: superseded)`, its unreached checkpoints are `not_run (reason: budget)`, teardown and the post-run proof run as usual, and the new RC run starts at once with the rig reservation transferred. RC runs pre-empt the Nightly run; a skipped Nightly run is alerted, and its canaries run at the next free window before any further PR comment is trusted (until then every report carries a stale-canary banner). The RC start deadline is 8 hours before the release gate (sign-off N business days before GA, section 11); an RC run that cannot start by it goes to the release manager to decide (9.12).

All run types share the Orchestrator state machine (provisioned -> launched -> authenticated -> paper_mode_asserted -> settings_attested -> workspace_loaded -> fixture_verified -> canary_flow_passed -> running -> teardown -> reported; gate table in 5.2 Orchestrator), the Input Gateway, the data-mode policy and the outcome taxonomy. Runs happen in the operating day, 06:00 to 22:00 America/New_York; safety depends on the gateway and the account identity, never on the clock.

Base and candidate are scheduled by data mode (11.3 Sharding and parallelism). Frozen checkpoints run both builds on the same rig, back to back, and a base capture is reused when it was taken under the identical fingerprint and fixture epoch (a PR run's base is the merge-base main build, already captured by its merge run). `masked_live` checkpoints run on two identically fingerprinted rigs in lockstep, the same checkpoint within 60 seconds on both, with fingerprint equality asserted before capture; a slip over 60 seconds re-queues the pair once at the end of the shard, and a second slip is `not_run (reason: budget)`, counted as `lockstep_slip` in run health, a counter and never a finding (3.1). If only one rig is free, `masked_live` checkpoints are `not_run (reason: budget)` rather than captured minutes apart.

### 1.7 How a PR run works, minute by minute

T+0:00 is the branch build artifact publish. The example uses the 4-rig pool: frozen shards run candidate then base on one rig each, a `masked_live` shard takes a lockstep pair. The capture deadline is the budget minus 10 minutes (T+0:35); the comment posts by T+0:45.

| Time | Component | What happens | Outcome | Who sees what |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T+0:00 | Pipeline, Orchestrator | Webhook delivers build id, commit, merge-base, PR number, diff and dependency index; run row opened; base resolved to the main artifact at the merge-base or the nearest ancestor main commit with one. Config lint of the pinned `sentinel-config` commit. | No main artifact on any ancestor: `aborted_harness (reason: base_build_missing)`. Lint failure: `aborted_harness (reason: config_invalid)`. | PR comment placeholder "Sentinel run started, base = main@abc123"; on abort the comment carries the abort block and the check fails; harness on-call paged (P1); the pipeline is asked to build the merge-base. |
| T+0:01 | Orchestrator | Reads the manifest for the candidate build (4.3). Two no-manifest cases. (a) The static impact step finds UI dependents and no manifest exists: finding `manifest_missing`, nothing is declared, and every diff above threshold will be `collateral`. (b) The static impact step finds no UI dependents and no manifest exists: no finding, `intended` is disabled, and every diff above threshold will be `needs_human (reason: no_manifest)`. A manifest with zero entries and an `empty_reason` is valid (pure refactor). | None at this step. | Comment, case (a): "No manifest entry; all diffs will be reported as collateral until you add one." Case (b): "No manifest; no UI code changed; any diff needs a human." |
| T+0:02 | Orchestrator (static impact step) | Changed classes -> reverse dependents on the candidate's dependency index (depth 6) -> hosting surfaces, unioned with declared surfaces and the Dependency Map expansion of the touched primitives (2.10.2). A static edge missing from the map is a `dependency_map_gap` finding with a proposed map PR; a changed class owned by no primitive and no surface is reported in the same finding as an unowned root. Scope = union plus smoke census, Ladder S sweeps for tier-1 resizable surfaces in scope, tier-1 flows touching the scope; every other registry surface is `not_run (reason: scope)`. Shards sized from historical durations; budget cuts hit the lowest tier first and never a declared or smoke surface. | Dependency index absent from the artifact: static step skipped, one `dependency_map_gap` with reason "no dependency index" in run health. Items cut: `not_run (reason: budget)`. | Run page shows scope and shard plan; `dependency_map_gap` in the comment's scope line with the PR link. |
| T+0:03 to 0:09 | Rig Manager, Watchdog | Reverts the pool rigs to the pinned snapshots, installs candidate and base (Branch A) or restores per-build snapshots (Branch B), drops corpus workspaces into usergui, applies vmoptions, starts the Watchdog, runs the preflight checklist (12.7 Preflight checklist, groups R, B, H, N, G). | Preflight R, B, G or N item failed: the effect 12.7 gives that item. For most items every checkpoint of the shard is `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)` and the run `complete_with_env_errors`; N3 affects only checkpoints with `api_within` assertions and N4 only frozen checkpoints. N2 or N5 (model endpoint, egress payload) is a degraded mode, never `env_error`: `review_mode: deferred`, agent fallback and the Explorer off, run continues. N7 (integrations): the run proceeds and publication retries. H item failed: `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.<item>)` before any product action. One rig only for a `masked_live` shard: its checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`. | On-call channel with rig name, item and screenshot; the comment's run health lists the 32 items. |
| T+0:09 to 0:15 | Orchestrator, Executor, Capture, Watchdog | Gate sequence per rig: launch (process tree by PID, build id by GetWindowText), scripted login with the vault secret step and MFA branch, popup catalog on first-launch dialogs (7.8), paper-mode assertion (account selector text equal to one allowlist entry), settings attestation A1 to A11 (6.3, 12.6; re-run on any new Active Trader panel), workspace load with hash check, `verify_account_fixture` with one reset attempt, canary flow; each gate anchor-checked and screenshotted. | Gate failure: `env_error` with gate name and screenshot for the shard's checkpoints. Build id differs from the request: `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_mismatch)`. Fixture still drifted after one reset: `env_error (gate: fixture_verified, reason: fixture_drift)` on checkpoints flagged `account_state: true`. Paper-mode or attestation mismatch: `aborted_safety (reason: paper_mode_mismatch)` or `aborted_safety (reason: attestation_mismatch)`, process tree killed. Undeclared working order: `aborted_safety (reason: unexpected_working_order)`. Attestation row unreadable after one re-read: `env_error (gate: settings_attested, reason: attestation_unreadable)`; account selector unreadable twice: `env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: identity_unreadable)` (6.3, 6.4). | `env_error`: on-call channel. `aborted_safety`: paged and notified per the single routing of 9.10 (harness on-call at P1, the accountable owner, `#sentinel-safety`); the comment's abort block names the gate. |
| T+0:15 | Orchestrator | Registry validation on both builds, probes P1 to P8 (2.2.3); environment fingerprint from live reads on every rig, compared field by field with the base rig or the reused base captures on every field but build id (3.3). | New entry: `unregistered_surface` checkpoint per entry. Probe anchor not located: `landmark_missing (reason: probe:<Pn>)`, run health "validation incomplete for P<n>". Fingerprint mismatch: every checkpoint of the shard `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field)`, nothing captured, run `complete_with_env_errors`. | Unexpected tier 1 and the system owner for new entries; on-call with the differing field. |
| T+0:15 to 0:35 | Executor, Capture, Invariant Checker, Oracle, Stores | Running, in tier order: tier-1 flows, sweeps, census (2.11 `order_and_cut`). The Executor navigates by the locator ladder (5.5), the Input Gateway resolves every target before emitting (5.4), the popup catalog runs before every step and capture, the settle rule gates capture (3.5), Capture grabs each top-level window of the process tree by DWM bounds, composites, redacts and stores content-addressed. The Invariant Checker runs on each capture at once; Oracle assertions run on flow checkpoints; on a frozen shard the base pass follows the candidate pass on the same rig unless its captures are reused; a `masked_live` shard captures both rigs in lockstep. Build id re-read before each flow. | Per checkpoint as they occur: `not_settled` (reason: `frames_unstable`, `anchor_missing`, `anti_anchor_present`, `timeout`, `unexpected_window:<title>`), `landmark_missing`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed`, `env_error (gate: running, reason: occluded)`, `harness_error`. Per step: one of the five step outcomes; after a `failed` or `blocked_by_gateway` step the flow ends and its later checkpoints are `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`. App crash or hang: `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` on the checkpoint in progress, with the cause in `detail`, `not_run (reason: app_crash)` for the rest of the flow or ladder, finding `app_crash` with artifacts, relaunch through every gate, after which the next flow starts from its preconditions (a ladder never resumes mid-way; a crash or hang during the relaunch gates, or during the gate sequence of the shard's first launch, is another `app_alive` failure, charged to the shard's first unreached checkpoint, that consumes the budget, never `env_error`); the first three app failures in a shard are each relaunched, and a fourth marks the shard's remaining checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)` and the run `aborted_budget (reason: app_restart_budget)`. A `process_exit` during a launcher update or with a changed build manifest is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` instead, with no `app_crash` finding and no relaunch consumed (10.2). Unmatched popup while `order_stage` is set: run `aborted_safety (reason: unknown_dialog_in_order_stage)`; otherwise the flow is quarantined and the window is an `unknown_popup` finding, dismissed by the agent's dismiss-only toolset or WM_CLOSE. Network drop past 15 minutes: `env_error (gate: connectivity)` for the shard's rest. Build id changed: `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` for the shard's rest. | Run page live with per-shard progress and counts; `blocked_by_gateway` also to the safety log and on-call; an attempted send on a scripted flow ends the run `aborted_safety` at once. |
| T+0:17 onward | Diff Engine, Reviewer | As each pair completes: whole-window translation pre-pass, per-region diffs against calibrated A/A floors, connected components (3.7). Signatures matching stored decisions inherit them (9.7) and skip the Reviewer. Classification by the decision table in 3.11: undeclared surfaces are `collateral` with no model call; declared surfaces above threshold queue for the Reviewer (asynchronous, idempotent, PR cap 60 calls); a stored `needs_human` with `review_state: pending` holds the slot until the verdict lands. | `identical`, `noise`, `intended`, `collateral`, `needs_human` (reasons: `reviewer_uncertain`, `reviewer_no_match`, `reviewer_unavailable`, `reviewer_cap`, `no_manifest`, `uncalibrated` for a region or fingerprint with no calibrated floor, `rescued_capture` after an agent fallback, `global_shift` under a `global_rendering_shift` run finding), `needs_baseline` when no pair can be formed. | Findings accumulate on the run page; suppressed items collapse under "suppressed by decision #id". |
| T+0:35 to 0:38 | Executor, Diff Engine | Targeted re-runs of above-threshold and `invariant_violation` checkpoints in the same session after the normalize routine, up to two re-captures per checkpoint (one for an `invariant_violation`, to confirm persistence) and max(30, 10 percent of checkpoints) re-captured checkpoints per run (3.10, 10.5): all captures agree = product change, classification stands; any disagree = instability. | Instability: `not_settled (reason: unstable)`, both images attached, `flake_event` written. Re-run budget exhausted: the classification stands with `stability: unknown (cause: budget)` and run health prints `rerun_budget_exhausted` (3.10). | Run health shows re-run counts; unstable items go to the flow owner, never to the Unexpected list or the Reviewer. |
| T+0:38 to 0:41 | Executor, Orchestrator, Watchdog | Teardown: `reset_input_state`, verified Cancel All per login, Working and Filled diffed against the start snapshot, positions-flat check, logout, crash artifacts and hs_err_pid collected, egress log closed, plaintext secret scan, snapshot revert scheduled; post-run proof produced (6.6). | Undeclared Working or Filled row: `aborted_safety (reason: undeclared_order_row)` after the fact, S1 incident. Proof UNPROVEN: `complete_with_env_errors (reason: unproven_proof)`, next run on that login blocked. Secret found: `aborted_harness (reason: secret_leaked)`, report withheld. Any other teardown fault: `complete_with_env_errors (reason: teardown_fault)`. | Post-run proof section in the comment and report; paging for `aborted_safety`, `aborted_harness` and UNPROVEN proof per 9.10. |
| T+0:41 | Reporter and Integrations | Comment posted per 9.2: Intended, Unexpected ranked by tier with primitive, manifest entry, layout and size and one-click actions, suppressed table, coverage matrix, run health, safety proof. If the Reviewer queue has not drained it is posted `unreviewed` with "Reviewer pending: N items" and edited in place later. Commit status set. | `complete` or `complete_with_env_errors`. | Developer and PR reviewer; tier-1 `collateral` and `invariant_violation` also to the Slack triage channel and the PR author; Jira only after a human clicks confirm bug. |
| T+0:45 | Orchestrator | Budget deadline: unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`; the comment still posts with what ran. | `aborted_budget (reason: wall_clock)` if scope did not finish. | Comment header shows `not_run` counts per tier; sharding review if the rate exceeds target. |
| T+1:00 | Reporter host (dead-man) | No run-completed event by budget plus 15 minutes, for a run that reached `running`; a PR run still queued at its start deadline is `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)` instead, never dead-man (9.10). | Run row `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)`. | On-call page naming run, rig and last heartbeat; the check fails with "Sentinel did not report". |

A push to the PR queues a new run; one run per PR is in flight, so a push during a run waits and a push superseded by a newer one never starts, which the comment's run history records. Same-signature findings inherit earlier decisions, and a signature under a confirm_bug decision that no longer appears is marked fixed in build on the decision (9.7).

### 1.8 How a merge run works

T+0:00 is the new main artifact publish. Base is the previous main build with a completed merge run (coalescing rule in 1.6). Scope is the full census over the tier A workspaces (900 checkpoints: five workspaces times about 180 hosted surfaces, 2.4), Ladder S sweeps for tier 1 and 2 resizable surfaces, and all tier-1 flows; 4 shards on the 4 pool rigs, frozen shards back to back on one rig with base reuse, `masked_live` shards as lockstep pairs. Pair rig time is about 550 minutes without base reuse and about 358 with it (11.2), so the worst case on the 4-rig pool is about 156 minutes of wall clock and the expected case about 104, inside the 3 hour budget; the capture deadline is T+2:50.

| Time | Component | What happens | Outcome | Who sees what |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T+0:00 | Orchestrator | Run row; manifest assembled as the union of every PR manifest merged since the base build, each entry with its PR number; config lint. | Lint failure: `aborted_harness (reason: config_invalid)`. | Run page. |
| T+0:03 to 0:12 | Rig Manager, Orchestrator | Preflight, provisioning and the gate sequence as in 1.7 on the 4 pool rigs; workspaces spread across shards by surface tab. | `env_error`, `not_comparable`, `aborted_safety`, `aborted_harness` by the same rules as 1.7. | On-call as in 1.7. |
| T+0:12 to 0:15 | Orchestrator | Registry validation P1 to P8 on both builds; fingerprint check per shard. | `unregistered_surface` per new entry; `landmark_missing (reason: probe:<Pn>)` per unlocated probe; `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field)` per mismatched shard. | Unexpected tier 1; system owner; on-call for fingerprints. |
| T+0:15 to 2:36 (worst case; about 1:55 expected) | Executor, Capture, Invariant Checker, Oracle, Diff Engine, Reviewer | Tier-1 flows with assertions, then sweeps, then census over every registered surface in every tier A workspace, per shard. Diffs stream; decisions from the merged PRs' runs are inherited by signature; the Reviewer queue drains asynchronously under the merge cap of 200 calls. | Full per-checkpoint taxonomy as in 1.7. A finding a PR run had in scope but did not report is recorded as finding `missed_in_pr_run` (report label "missed in PR run") and opens a harness task; a finding outside PR scope on a surface consuming a primitive a merged PR touched emits `dependency_map_gap`. A merge-run finding on a surface that the candidate's dependency index reaches from a class changed by a merged PR, whose PR run had the surface `not_run (reason: scope)`, is recorded as finding `missed_in_pr_run` with `detail: static_impact` (report label "missed by static impact") and opens a harness task for the system owner. | Run page live. |
| T+2:36 to 2:50 | Executor, Diff Engine, Orchestrator | Targeted re-runs and flake refresh; teardown with Cancel All, Working and Filled diff, positions-flat check, artifacts, secret scan, egress log, post-run proof. | `not_settled (reason: unstable)` per unstable checkpoint; run outcome by the 1.7 teardown rules. | Run health; post-run proof. |
| T+2:50 to 2:55 | Reporter and Integrations | Merge report in the report UI (9.4): Intended per PR with manifest reconciliation (entries verified visible, entries with a covering checkpoint but no visible change, entries with no covering checkpoint), Unexpected ranked by tier with suppressed items collapsed under decision ids, Known bugs, coverage matrix (covered / not_run (reason) / not_registered), run health, metrics header, safety proof. Slack digest to the triage rotation lists only new, unsuppressed Unexpected findings. | `complete`, `complete_with_env_errors`, or `aborted_budget` at the T+3:00 deadline with `not_run (reason: budget)` on unreached checkpoints. | Triage rotation disposes every Unexpected finding within one business day (9.12); confirm bug files Jira with crops, primitive and the PRs whose manifests touched it (9.9). |
| T+3:30 | Reporter host (dead-man) | No run-completed event by budget plus 30 minutes, for a run that reached `running`; a merge run still queued at its start deadline is coalesced into the next merge run instead (9.10). | Run row `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)`. | On-call page. |

Baseline promotion happens here and never in PR runs (9.8 Baseline lifecycle): an `intended` capture whose PR merged becomes a baseline candidate; a human approves it per checkpoint or per signature cluster with approver, build, reason and ticket.

### 1.9 How an RC run works

T+0:00 is the RC cut. Base is the last released build: its approved lineage baseline set when that set's stored fingerprint equals the current one, otherwise the Rig Manager installs the released build and re-captures it on the current fingerprint (3.1). Scope is everything. All 6 rigs: rigs 1 to 4 carry census, flows and sweeps (about 1,236 rig-minutes of pair work worst case, about 803 when the lineage captures match the fingerprint, 11.2: about 5 h 10 min worst and 3 h 20 min expected on four rigs), rig 5 carries the soak against the lineage soak of the last released build (10.11; there is no base soak rig), rig 6 carries the chaos suite first and the Explorer last with its full 90 minutes (6.8, 2.9). The Explorer starts when the last scripted shard has reported, T+6:20 at the latest, so the run ends about T+8:00 whatever the pair work took; the capture deadline is T+7:50. A new RC build arriving while this run is in flight supersedes it under the respin rule of 1.6.

| Time | Component | What happens | Outcome | Who sees what |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T+0:00 to 0:20 | Rig Manager, Orchestrator | Preflight, provisioning, gates, registry validation, fingerprint check on all 6 rigs. Rig 5 loads the tier B workspace with the most gadgets. Rig 6 is provisioned from the Explorer snapshot with the Explorer login (attestation item A10) and held idle. | As in 1.8. | On-call on `env_error`. |
| T+0:20 to 5:30 (worst case; about 3:40 expected) | Executor, Capture, Invariant Checker, Oracle, Diff Engine, Reviewer (rigs 1 to 4) | Flows of every tier with Oracle checks against declared expectations and the API within the delay tolerance; Ladder F sweeps (tier 1 and 2) and Ladder S (tier 3) for every `resizable: true` surface in a tier C harness cell and in-host splitters at the full fraction set, invariants at every step, diff against the base at the same step; census over tier A, tier B and migration workspaces (each tier B workspace saved under the previous release loaded on the candidate, every first-launch and conversion dialog captured). Reviewer cap 500. | Full taxonomy. Sweeps: `invariant_violation`, `collateral`, `intended`, `identical` per step; the Reporter names the first failing size and the failing range per surface. | Run page; tier-1 `collateral` and `invariant_violation` to Slack as they appear. |
| T+0:20 to 6:20 | Executor, Capture, Watchdog (rig 5, soak) | Six-hour scripted activity loop on the same login, 24 cycles; each cycle ends with a soak checkpoint `flow/<workspace-surface-id>/soak/c<nn>` diffed against the lineage soak capture of the last released build at the same cycle index (10.11; `needs_baseline` when that lineage's fingerprint differs); RSS, GDI and USER handles, thread count and screenshot staleness of a ticking clock region recorded against the budgets of `soak.yaml`; proactive relaunch disabled for the soak. | Standard taxonomy per soak checkpoint; a budget breach is `assertion_failed (assertion: soak.<metric>)`, tier 1. Process gone or EDT frozen past max wait: `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with the cause (`jvm_crash`, `hang`, `oom`, `process_exit`) in `detail` (an error dialog with the app alive is INV-14 instead), the rest of the loop `not_run (reason: app_crash)`, tier-1 finding `app_crash` with hs_err_pid, dumps and log slice; relaunch; a fourth app failure in the soak shard after its 3 relaunches marks the rest of the loop `not_run (reason: budget)` and the run `aborted_budget (reason: app_restart_budget)`. A new exception signature in the log slice with the app alive is a tier-2 `new_log_signature` finding, never an outcome. Session expiry or an inactivity logout (unverified) is a re-login checkpoint, counted in the soak summary. | RC report soak section with both curves and the budget lines, restarts and new log signatures. |
| T+5:30 to 6:00 (worst case) | Executor, Diff Engine (rigs 1 to 4) | Targeted re-runs; flake statistics. | `not_settled (reason: unstable)` per unstable checkpoint; flake stats. | Run health. |
| T+0:20 to 1:00 | Executor, Oracle (rig 6) | Chaos suite scenarios (7.11): latency, loss, throttle, 30 second and 5 minute disconnects, each with its connectivity assertions, in a session without census checkpoints, before rig 6 is re-snapshotted for the Explorer. | `assertion_failed` per failed scenario assertion; a scenario without its expected outcome and alert is `harness_error`. | RC report connectivity section; connectivity flow owner. |
| T+6:20 to 7:50 | Explorer, Input Gateway (rig 6) | Explorer last, after the last scripted shard (the soak) reported, on its own rig, login and snapshot, with the restricted toolset, deny list, 400 actions, 90 minutes, 20 consecutive no-change actions and the 25 dollar session cap (6.8, 2.9); `drag_named` only on splitters and detach handles, never an order bubble; a start later than T+6:20 is cut at the T+7:50 deadline, never the other way round. Each finding is emitted as a candidate flow and replayed once in scripted mode on the same build. | The Explorer produces no checkpoint outcomes itself. A replayed candidate flow produces outcomes through the normal path: `invariant_violation` or `assertion_failed` when the finding is one of those, else `needs_baseline` with the Explorer trace attached, since a new flow has no base capture. A finding that does not reproduce is held as flaky or agent, counted in Explorer precision, never reported as a product finding. A denied target (the 6.8 deny list, including chart and grid context-menu Buy and Sell items, BUY MKT and SELL MKT, every ladder or Level II bid or ask cell and every order-entry button) is `blocked_by_gateway`; three in a session end it; an attempted send ends the session and counts toward the per-run kill-switch trip (6.8, 5.4.8). If the ticket or dialog flag is ever set in the session, the gateway drops all input, closes the window through its recovery path (Escape token) and ends the session with finding `explorer_order_stage` (S1, paged and notified per 9.10, plus the Explorer owner), counted toward the per-run trip of 10; the run continues. With the model endpoint unavailable the session does not start and is `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` (2.9). Budget exhaustion ends the session, never the run. | RC report Explorer section (reproduced findings; "Explorer: not reproduced" list); the surface's flow owner gets the candidate flow; disposition by the triage rotation (confirm bug, agent mistake, expected behavior). |
| T+6:20 to 6:40 (rigs 1 to 5), T+7:50 to 7:55 (rig 6) | Executor, Orchestrator | Teardown everywhere: Cancel All, Working and Filled diffed against the start snapshot, positions-flat check, Explorer server-side mutation ledger replayed and verified, Explorer snapshot discarded, secret scan, egress log, post-run proof per login. | Run outcome by the 1.7 teardown rules. | Post-run proof. |
| T+7:55 to 8:00 | Reporter and Integrations | RC report (9.4): the merge report plus lineage comparison, Intended grouped by Jira epic and reconciled against the fixVersion export, sweep ranges per gadget and ladder step, soak summary, chaos results, Explorer candidates, tier B migration results, baseline approval status, escape-tracking seed, release gate checklist, sign-off block. | `complete`, `complete_with_env_errors`, or `aborted_budget` at the T+8:00 deadline. | Release manager and triage rotation; release Slack channel. |
| T+9:00 | Reporter host (dead-man) | No run-completed event by budget plus 60 minutes, for a run that reached `running`; an RC run that cannot start by its deadline goes to the release manager instead (1.6, 9.12). | Run row `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)`. | On-call page. |
| Following days | Triage rotation, release manager, system owner | Every Unexpected finding dispositioned; confirmed bugs in Jira with fixVersion; sign-off in the report UI N business days before GA under the conditions of 10.9 (no detector-blind banner, last Nightly money-cell rate 100 percent, every tier-1 cell covered or its `not_run` explained, quarantine under 2 percent of tier 1, no tier-1 `collateral` or `invariant_violation` without a disposition, fire drill passed, post-run proof present), recording approver, RC build, accepted open findings with tickets, and the approved baseline set that becomes the next lineage baseline. | Sign-off record; a respin after sign-off gets a full RC run and a new sign-off. | Release gate status on the RC report and the release channel; an undispositioned tier-1 finding blocks sign-off. |

### 1.10 Outcome taxonomy (authoritative)

This is the authoritative copy; 12.2 Outcome taxonomy carries it verbatim together with the reason table that lists every reason code used in this spec, and every section uses these names and no others. The sets are closed: 15 per checkpoint, 5 per step, 5 per run, enforced by SQLite CHECK constraints and the `outcome_reasons` lookup table generated from `taxonomy.yaml` (8.3 Schema). A reason is written as `outcome (reason: code)`, a gate as `env_error (gate: name)`; reasons refine an outcome and never add to the set.

Precedence. A checkpoint can produce several results (an invariant fires and the pixel diff is also above threshold). It ends in exactly one outcome, the first that applies in this order: `env_error`, app failure (`assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)`), `harness_error`, `not_run`, `not_comparable`, `not_settled`, `landmark_missing`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` (every other assertion), `needs_baseline`, `collateral`, `needs_human`, `intended`, `noise`, `identical`. Environment outranks the app and the harness because a hang during a network drop is an environment fact, and an app failure outranks the harness because an exception raised while handling an app failure is evidence of that failure, not a harness fault (10.1). Lower results that also applied stay on the finding record as evidence (a `collateral` classification on an `invariant_violation` finding) but are not outcomes. `unregistered_surface` is a checkpoint of its own created by registry validation and never competes. The rule list in 3.11 Classification decision table implements this order. One refinement inside that list: a region with no calibrated floor cannot be said to be above a threshold, so `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` is decided before `collateral` (3.11 row 15) and is ranked with `collateral` in the report.

Per checkpoint:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identical` | Candidate and base equal pixel for pixel outside mask and redaction regions after settle (`freeze` regions are pixel-diffed, 3.8); invariants and assertions pass; no step on the path ended `passed_via_agent_fallback`. | Diff Engine at pair comparison. | Counted as covered in the matrix as "identical (n)"; not listed. | Nothing. |
| `noise` | Diff below the checkpoint's and region's calibrated A/A floor (reason: `below_floor`), or matching a human-approved noise signature (decision #id). Never assigned by the Reviewer. | Diff Engine with the decision store. | Run health counts; report UI drill-down; suppressed table for signature matches. | Nothing; a weekly 5 percent re-label of signature-based `noise` feeds the overturn metric; a rising count on one checkpoint triggers a calibration review by the flow owner. |
| `intended` | Diff above threshold on a surface a loaded manifest entry declares, and the Reviewer, given the entry, crops and any mock, returns `matches_manifest` at confidence 0.80 or above; or the signature inherits a mark_intended decision. | Diff Engine classification plus asynchronous Reviewer confirmation (3.11 rows 14 and 20). | PR comment Intended with crops at 1:1 and the confirmation; merge and RC reports per PR. | At merge-run triage the capture becomes a baseline candidate; a human approves it with approver, build, reason, ticket (9.8). The Reviewer never promotes. |
| `collateral` | Diff above threshold on a surface no loaded manifest entry declares, including a UI-touching PR with no manifest; or a removed surface (label on base, absent on candidate) that no loaded manifest entry declares (3.11 row 26). | Diff Engine classification by surface declaration alone, no model call (3.11 rows 16 and 17); the Reviewer adds a description and a pointer when available and cannot move it. | Top of PR comment Unexpected by tier, with the consumed primitive, the manifest entry that touched it, layout and size, crops; tier 1 also to the Slack triage channel. | One-click: confirm bug (Jira), mark intended with ticket (manifest amendment; tier 1 and 2 need a second person), request mask with reason (human-created, owner and expiry; refused on money cells and identity fields, and refused with the reason shown when it would exceed the panel's mask budget, 3.8). The decision persists by signature (9.7). A later diff whose signature matches a confirm_bug decision keeps its computed outcome, files under that ticket and is listed under Known bugs without a new alert (3.11 input M, 9.6). |
| `needs_human` | Diff above threshold that is none of the above. Reasons, closed: `reviewer_uncertain` (below 0.80, partial match, no visible difference, cannot judge), `reviewer_no_match` (the Reviewer is confident the change on a declared surface is unrelated to its entry, or does not confirm the removal of a declared surface, 3.11 row 25a; ranked directly after `collateral`), `reviewer_unavailable` (API down, refusal, schema failure, `intended` disabled, or awaiting review with `review_state: pending`), `reviewer_cap` (beyond the per-run reviewer call cap, or still awaiting a verdict when the per-run spend ceiling or the weekly dollar cap stopped model calls, with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail`, 3.15), `no_manifest` (non-UI PR with no manifest), `uncalibrated` (region or fingerprint without a calibrated floor, threshold 0; never `not_comparable`), `rescued_capture` (reached through `passed_via_agent_fallback`, even with a clean or below-floor diff, 3.11 row 11a; never inherits a noise or intended decision), `global_shift` (text-edge-only diff under a `global_rendering_shift` run finding, one cluster), `oracle_unreadable`, `bounds_unreadable`. When two reasons apply, the first in 3.11's fixed order wins and the rest go in `detail`. An exhausted re-run budget is not a reason: the classification stands with `stability: unknown (cause: budget)` (3.10). | Diff Engine plus Reviewer output; Orchestrator for cap, budget and manifest reasons. | PR comment Unexpected below `collateral`; daily digest to the triage rotation at 08:00 America/New_York. | Human disposition within one business day (confirm bug, mark intended with ticket, mark noise); it persists by signature and becomes an eval-set item. When a pending verdict lands, the item is re-evaluated through 3.11's table with the verdict as input R and the outcome becomes what the table gives: `intended`, `noise` only via the A/A floor, or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` (including a removed declared surface the Reviewer does not confirm, 3.11 row 25a) or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_uncertain)`; `review_state` goes `pending` to `done`. If a human decision already exists on the item, the verdict is attached as an annotation only and never changes the outcome or the decision. The one other later change: when the per-run spend ceiling ends the run, an item still pending becomes `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail` and `review_state: done`, and when the job gives up the reason stays `reviewer_unavailable` with `review_state: done` (4.13, 3.15). Nothing else is ever rewritten. |
| `invariant_violation` | A layout invariant INV-01 to INV-15 (2.7 Layout invariants) failed on a capture on all 3 settled frames: sibling bounds intersect, component outside parent, text clipped, ellipsis, required label missing, unexpected scrollbar, font below minimum, placeholder or error text, window off screen, control count wrong, text runs overlap, columns misaligned, focus order wrong, error dialog present, sign and color disagree. Baseline-free. | Invariant Checker, right after capture, on both builds. | PR comment Unexpected with the bounds overlay and the base crop at the same layout and size, by tier and severity; Slack for tier 1. A violation present on both builds is reported once as pre-existing, one severity lower, never dropped. | Confirm bug, or waive with ticket and expiry at most 30 days (the outcome never changes; the finding is suppressed). A wrong invariant for a surface gets a registry exception with owner, reason and expiry. The Reviewer never reclassifies it. |
| `assertion_failed` | An Oracle assertion on the flow step failed: value outside its expectation, arithmetic invariant broken, API comparison outside the delay tolerance, chain header inconsistent with strikes or expirations; or a built-in assertion failed: `app_alive` (stored as `assertion:app_alive` with the cause, `jvm_crash`, `hang`, `oom` or `process_exit`, in `detail`, 4.13; an error dialog with the app alive is INV-14, not this), `size_reached` (a sweep step whose size was not reached after one retry, 2.5.1), `soak.<metric>` (a soak budget breach, 10.11). An OCR calibration miss is `harness_error (reason: ocr_calibration)`, never this. | Oracle at the step (OCR on upscaled crops, CSV export or Copy All, JAB where available, market-data API); Watchdog for `app_alive`. | PR comment Unexpected with extracted and expected values and source, or the crash artifacts; flow owner; tier 1 for `app_alive`. | Confirm bug, or fix the expectation by flow PR. For `app_alive` the rest of the flow or ladder is `not_run (reason: app_crash)` and the app is relaunched through every gate; the next flow starts from its preconditions and a ladder never resumes mid-way; a crash or hang during the relaunch gates, or during the gate sequence of the shard's first launch, is another `app_alive` failure that consumes the relaunch budget, never `env_error`; a `process_exit` during a launcher update or with a changed build manifest is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` with no `app_crash` finding and no relaunch consumed (10.2). The Reviewer never reclassifies it. |
| `not_settled` | Settle rule (3.5) not met within max wait, reason: `frames_unstable`, `anchor_missing`, `anti_anchor_present`, `timeout`, `unexpected_window:<title>`; or a targeted re-run disagreed (reason: `unstable`); or the Nightly A/A pass drifted on a frozen checkpoint (reason: `aa_drift`). Last frame kept. | Capture at the checkpoint; Diff Engine after re-run; Calibration Service nightly. | Run health; flow owner. Not an app finding; never in the Unexpected list and never sent to the Reviewer. | No diff, no retry within the run. `flake_event` written; quarantine when the flake score passes 0.10 over 5 observations, 3 unstable in 7 days, 2 verdict flips on one build, 3 consecutive `aa_drift` nights, a gateway threshold (one safety drop, or three integrity drops in one flow, 5.4.8), or, for a whole flow, a 30-day agent-fallback rate above 5 percent (11.5) (3.10, 10.5, 10.6). Time to settle above 2x the calibration p50 is a `settle_regression` finding. |
| `not_comparable` | No pair can be scored: `fingerprint_mismatch` (the differing field named: any must-match fingerprint field, including the data epoch and the bounds source), `window_mismatch` (window title or geometry class differs from the expected target window), `surface_mismatch` (active tab or panel headers do not match the expected screen id on one side). These three are the only `not_comparable` reasons. | Orchestrator at the fingerprint check (whole shard, nothing captured); Capture at the checkpoint. | Run health with the field or screen id; on-call for fingerprint mismatch; the run is `complete_with_env_errors`. | Nothing diffed. Fingerprint: rig fix and re-run. A fingerprint that merely lacks a calibration is not this outcome: its diffs are `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 and a Calibration run is queued (3.9). Screen id: flow owner checks the flow; candidate alone elsewhere is a suspected navigation regression and a finding. |
| `landmark_missing` | A Region Registry landmark, a registry validation probe anchor, or a step's locator anchor on every scripted rung and (when enabled) the agent rung, not found above its confidence floor on candidate or base. | Diff Engine when anchoring; Orchestrator at validation; Executor when a step fails on its locator. | PR comment Unexpected with the side it was missing on and both crops; flow owner. | Human decides bug or landmark update by region or flow PR. Never a blind diff. Missing on both sides is a flow bug. |
| `env_error` | An Orchestrator gate failed before the checkpoint (`provisioned`, `preflight.<item>`, `launched`, `authenticated`, `paper_mode_asserted`, `settings_attested`, `workspace_loaded`, `fixture_verified`, `canary_flow_passed`, `connectivity`, `rig_lost`; gate names equal the Orchestrator state names), or an environment fault occurred before capture (reasons include `version_mismatch`, `version_changed_mid_run` (gate `launched`, including a launcher restart seen as `process_exit`, 10.2), `rig_spec_mismatch`, `session_kicked` and `agreement_pending` (gate `authenticated`), `fixture_drift` and `delay_state` (gate `fixture_verified`), `occluded` (the gate in force when it was detected, `running` mid-run), `attestation_unreadable` (gate `settings_attested`), `identity_unreadable` (gate `paper_mode_asserted`), `vault_unreachable`, a catalog popup with action abort, a maintenance banner (`maintenance`, the gate in force)). Every `env_error` names its gate. Unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_safety` run take this outcome with the aborting gate as the gate name and the abort reason as the reason (for example `env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: paper_mode_mismatch)`, `env_error (gate: running, reason: kill_switch)`). | Orchestrator, with gate name, reason and screenshot. | On-call channel at once, one alert per run per gate; run health; the same gate in two consecutive runs escalates. Never enters the Diff Engine. | Rig or environment fix; shard re-run if budget allows; fixture drift triggers the fixture reset flow (7.6). |
| `harness_error` | Exception, crash or hang in the harness (Executor, Capture, Diff Engine, Oracle, Stores, Reporter), a failed self-test, a post-run taxonomy query failure, a registry entry found on neither build with the entitlement present, a bounds source or OCR calibration failure, canary generation failure, or canary detection below floor (reasons include `store_write_failed`, `artifact_persist_failed`, `redaction_version_missing`, `bounds_source_unavailable`, `ocr_calibration`, `mask_budget_exceeded`, `invariant_on_aa` (an enabled invariant firing on an A/A pair, 2.7), `registry_entry_not_found`, `export_header_mismatch`, `hook_lost`, `orchestrator_died`, `drill_failed:<item>`, `canary_generation_failed`, `canary_path_divergence`, `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded`, `safety_canary_blind:<canary>`, `validation_self_test`, `chaos_unobserved`, `aa_drift_global`). Unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_harness` run take this outcome with the run's abort reason (for example `harness_error (reason: dead_man)`, `harness_error (reason: watchdog_dead)`, `harness_error (reason: preflight.H8)`). On a Nightly run a missed money-cell mutant's record is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)` while the run itself stays `complete` (10.3); a missed non-money mutant is canary state `missed` and counts toward `detector_degraded`, which marks the class's missed mutants `harness_error (reason: detector_degraded)` once the class falls below its floor. | Watchdog or the failing component's handler. | On-call channel; run health; morning report headline "detector is blind" for the canary case, with the mask, decision or threshold that absorbed the mutant. | Harness bug ticket to the system owner (Jira SENT). Never enters the Diff Engine. |
| `not_run` | In the matrix but not executed. Reasons, closed: `entitlement` (the login lacks it, including every post-Send surface until `paper_send_ok` is approved); `budget` (wall clock, relaunch budget, no lockstep rig free or a lockstep pair that slipped twice, an RC run superseded); `scope` (outside this run type's scope, or no workspace of this persona hosts the surface); `quarantine` (flake statistics, fire drill failure, kill switch or incident; nothing un-quarantines automatically, 10.5; drill and safety-canary flows are never quarantined, their failures page per 9.10); `step_failed:<step>` (an earlier step of its flow ended `failed` or `blocked_by_gateway`); `base_step_failed` (the base build could not reach it and the surface is not new); `app_crash` (the app died earlier in its flow or ladder); `model_unavailable` (an Explorer session or an agent-only step skipped because the model endpoint is down). | Orchestrator at scope computation, budget deadline or flow end; quarantine records. | Coverage matrix cell with the reason verbatim. Never displayed as passed. | Entitlement: the system owner's weekly coverage review (9.12). Budget and model unavailable: run health and the harness on-call. Quarantine: flow owner fix, 5 clean Calibration captures, human removal of the record. Step failures: the step finding carries the fix. |
| `unregistered_surface` | Registry validation found a main menu, tab bar, sub-tab, gadget picker, Setup, settings tree, selector or context menu entry not in the Surface Registry; recorded against synthetic id `unregistered.<probe>.<slug>`. | Orchestrator at the `workspace_loaded` gate by probes P1 to P8. | Unexpected, tier 1 until classified; coverage matrix row `not_registered`; system owner. | Registry stub PR proposed automatically; a human merges it or adds an explicit ignored entry with reason. Repeats every run until then. |
| `needs_baseline` | Candidate captured and invariants passed, but no comparable base exists. Reasons, closed (3.11 input B): `new_surface` (manifest `new_surface: true`, or present on candidate and absent on base), `base_not_settled` (after one base re-capture), `base_env_error`, `base_harness_error`, `lineage_missing` (the RC lineage baseline lacks it), `reuse_missing` (a frozen base capture expected from reuse was not found), `explorer_replay` (a replayed Explorer candidate flow). | Diff Engine when no pair can be formed. | Report section Needs baseline, with the nearest existing baseline by perceptual hash; in a PR comment under Intended if declared as new, else Unexpected. | A human approves the capture as baseline (approver, build, reason, ticket) or files a bug. Never automatic; blocks a clean RC report for tier 1. |

Per step:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `passed` | First attempt completed on a scripted rung of the locator ladder; the step's post-condition passed. | Executor. | Step log; the resolved rung is recorded so drift from rung 1 to 2 or 3 is a maintenance metric. | Nothing. |
| `passed_after_retry` | First attempt failed on every scripted rung; after `reset_input_state` the single permitted retry of the scripted rungs succeeded. One retry per step, never across a capture; the first attempt's screenshot is kept. | Executor. | Run health; flow owner weekly. | Flake statistics; three in 30 days on one step opens a flow maintenance task. |
| `passed_via_agent_fallback` | Every scripted rung failed twice; the agent rung with the restricted toolset reached the target; the declared normalize routine ran before capture. A rescue is capped at 25 actions and 90 seconds; past either cap the step is `failed`. The locator failure is recorded as a `locator_failure` finding with every rung's result, the pre-attempt screenshot and the agent's action trace. | Executor. Disabled by preflight when the model API is unreachable, during login, secret and teardown steps, while the ticket flag is set, or under DR-07 Branch B; the step is then `failed`. | PR comment Unexpected, "scripted locator broke at step X", beside the checkpoint's diff; flow owner. | The checkpoint it leads to is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)` unless a higher-precedence outcome applies. Proposed anchor patch PR with the agent's final target and crop; two fallbacks on one step and build open an update-scripted-flow task. |
| `failed` | The step could not complete within the retry cap: locator not found on any rung, precondition missing, popup catalog action abort, app not responding. The flow ends; teardown and `reset_input_state` run. | Executor. | Unexpected, with the side it failed on and the pre-attempt screenshot beside the base build's screenshot at the same step; flow owner. | The checkpoint the step led to is `landmark_missing` (locator) or `assertion_failed` (assertion or `app_alive`); later checkpoints of the flow are `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`. On the base build only: `needs_baseline` when the manifest marks the surface `new_surface: true`, else `not_run (reason: base_step_failed)`. Candidate-only failure is a suspected regression; both-sides failure is a flow bug. |
| `blocked_by_gateway` | The Input Gateway dropped the step's event: a click without a matching one-shot token, a blocked key while a ticket or confirm dialog was foreground, an Explorer action on a denied target, or the kill switch armed. The flow ends. | Input Gateway hook, from in-memory arm/deny state; the slow half's refusal is logged the same way. | Safety log, on-call channel, flow owner; Explorer owner for deny-list hits. | Later checkpoints `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`. Safety-reason drops (a blocked key, or a click on a deny rect while `order_stage` is set) quarantine the flow and page P1. Integrity-reason drops (token mismatch, expired token, stale arm/deny state) get one retry of the step; three in one flow quarantine the flow and ten in one run trip the kill switch (5.4.8). An attempted send on a scripted flow, including inside its agent rescue, or a kill-switch trip, ends the run `aborted_safety`; in an Explorer session an attempted send ends the session and counts toward the per-run trip (6.8), and a ticket or dialog flag set in the session drops all input, closes the window through the gateway's recovery path, ends the session with finding `explorer_order_stage` and counts toward the per-run trip while the run continues; the 30-second open-dialog kill-switch timer applies to scripted flows and agent rescue only. |

Per run:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `complete` | Every in-scope checkpoint has an outcome, none is `env_error` or `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)`, teardown finished and the post-run proof reads PROVEN. | Orchestrator at `reported`. | Report header. | Normal triage. |
| `complete_with_env_errors` | As `complete`, but at least one checkpoint is `env_error` or `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)`, more than 3 re-logins were needed, teardown reported a fault, or the post-run proof reads UNPROVEN (the next run on that login is blocked until a human verifies the account); the cause is recorded as the run reason `relogin_budget`, `teardown_fault` or `unproven_proof` when it is not an `env_error` checkpoint. | Orchestrator. | Report header; on-call channel already notified. | Triage on what ran; env fix and shard re-run per budget. |
| `aborted_safety` | Paper-mode mismatch, attestation mismatch, undeclared working order at run start, kill switch, an attempted send blocked by the gateway, a new Working or Filled row at teardown, a live-format account id read at the paper-mode assertion (6.4), a fire drill that produced a new order row, or an unknown dialog while `order_stage` is set (reasons: `paper_mode_mismatch`, `attestation_mismatch`, `unexpected_working_order`, `kill_switch`, `attempted_send`, `undeclared_order_row`, `live_identity`, `drill_order_placed`, `unknown_dialog_in_order_stage`). Hook enters deny-all; process tree killed; a fresh scripted login performs verified Cancel All; Working and Filled diffed against the start snapshot; proof produced (6.6). | Orchestrator, Input Gateway, Watchdog. | Paged and notified per the single routing of 9.10 (harness on-call at P1, the accountable owner and `#sentinel-safety` among them); post-run proof section; the PR comment's abort block if a PR run. | Incident procedure (6.12), S1 or S2. The rig is disabled and its flows `not_run (reason: quarantine)`; no run starts on that rig or login until a human closes the incident. |
| `aborted_budget` | Wall-clock budget reached before scope finished, a fourth app failure in a shard after its 3 relaunches, a PR run still queued at its start deadline (`pool_saturated`; a queued merge run is coalesced into the next merge run and an RC run goes to the release manager instead, 9.10), the run's model spend reaching the per-run ceiling of 11.4 (ends the run at the next flow boundary; reviewer call caps never end a run, they give `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)`), a 6.4 rate cap reached, or an RC run superseded by a new RC build (1.6) (reasons: `wall_clock`, `app_restart_budget`, `pool_saturated`, `dollar_cap`, `rate_cap`, `superseded`). Explorer budget exhaustion is not this; it ends the Explorer session only. | Orchestrator at the deadline; Watchdog budget. | Report header with `not_run (reason: budget)` counts per tier; on-call for the relaunch case. | Findings triaged as usual; sharding or scope review if the rate exceeds target. |
| `aborted_harness` | Harness crash or hang past the Orchestrator restart budget, a failed preflight H item or self-test, store failure, config lint failure, missing base artifact, a secret found by the post-run scan (report withheld), a failed post-run taxonomy query, the dead-man deadline of a run that reached `running`, or the start deadline of a Nightly or Calibration run that never reached `running` (11.2) (reasons: `preflight.<item>` for a failed H item of 12.7, written as 12.7 writes it, for example `preflight.H8` when the Watchdog is absent at run start; `start_failed` for that start deadline, with every scoped checkpoint `harness_error (reason: start_failed)` and the "canaries pending" banner on the next PR comment; and, mid-run, `store_write_failed`, `artifact_persist_failed`, `import_conflict`, `watchdog_dead`, `heartbeat_unwritable`, `disk_full`, `rig_lost`, `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `config_invalid`, `base_build_missing`, `secret_leaked`, `taxonomy_check_failed`, `dead_man`, `dpi_awareness`, `hook_lost` (a second Gateway hook host restart in one shard; the hook host has its own budget of one restart per shard and never consumes an app relaunch, 5.4.2), `canary_generation_failed` (a Nightly run on which no canary could run at all), `egress_unlogged`, `secret_scan_unavailable`). | Watchdog, Orchestrator, Reporter host. | Harness on-call paged immediately (P1); dead-man alert names run, rig and last heartbeat; the PR check fails with the reason. | Harness bug to the system owner; the run is re-queued once; two in a week freeze harness changes. |

Findings that are not outcomes.
