- Budgets, enforced by the Orchestrator and never by the prompt: 400 actions, 90 minutes wall clock, 25 dollars per session (plus the weekly cap of 11.4), and early stop after 20 consecutive actions with no new screenshot hash. The RC run's capture deadline caps the session as well: a session that starts late ends at the deadline (1.9). Exhaustion ends the session with a run-health line naming the budget hit; it never ends the run. If the model endpoint is unavailable at T+6:20 (`agent_available: false` after preflight N2 or N5, 12.7, with no recovery logged), the session does not start: it is `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)`, the RC report's Explorer section and run health print "Explorer: not run, model endpoint unavailable", the Explorer owner is notified, and the run is unaffected; a recovery logged before T+6:20 lets it start as planned.
- Steering: toward surfaces with the fewest flow checkpoints in the current RC run and surfaces whose `primitives` intersect the manifest's touched primitives, from a target list the Orchestrator computes before the session starts. Odd inputs come from the seeded corpus with the pass rule of 2.6.3.
- Logging per action (`step_events`, 8.3 Schema): index, time, stated target and expected outcome, resolved rect, keys, gate decision, pre and post screenshot hashes, 96x96 click crop, model id, prompt hash, usage. Before each action the agent states target and expected outcome; after it, the post-action state is verified by the cheapest means available (JAB focused element under branch A, else a template or OCR check of the expected anchor). A mismatch is logged `agent_error` and is never a product finding.
- Findings: record with signature (surface, invariant or observation, crop hash), severity, confidence, raw values, trace reference, build, first and last seen; the same signature on a later night updates last seen instead of opening a new finding. Each is emitted as a candidate flow in `flows/quarantine/<finding-id>.yaml` (class `explorer_candidate`, 4.7 Flow file) from the trace since the last named stable state, anchored by click crops, and replayed exactly once in scripted mode on the same build within the RC run. No automatic trace minimization: a replay with steps removed costs minutes per probe against a live session, so trimming is a human step (an owner may enable a bounded mode of at most 8 replays for one finding). Only a reproducing finding is reported, through the replayed flow's own checkpoint outcomes: `invariant_violation` or `assertion_failed` when the finding is one of those, else `needs_baseline (reason: explorer_replay)` with the Explorer trace and the candidate flow attached, since a new flow has no base capture; never `needs_human`. A non-reproducing one is held with triage state `agent_mistake` or `expected_behavior` (8.3), listed under "Explorer: not reproduced" in the RC report (9.4 Merge and RC report structure) and counted in Explorer precision. A human trims and promotes the flow into the library; until the next good build captures a baseline, the promoted flow's checkpoints are `needs_baseline`.
- Teardown: every session ends by replaying the server-side mutation ledger (items the Explorer created on its login), deleting each and verifying by reading, then the snapshot revert (6.8).
- Metrics per RC run: Explorer precision (reproduced over emitted findings), agent-error ratio (agent errors over actions), deny-list hits, budget hit, dollars. Precision under 30 percent on two consecutive RC runs pauses the Explorer until the steering list or toolset is fixed; the pause is a run-health line, not silence.

The Explorer never produces checkpoint outcomes itself; the replayed flow does, through the normal path.

### 2.10 Coverage model: Dependency Map and static impact

#### 2.10.1 Dependency Map

`registry/dependency-map.yaml` maps each hosting primitive to its consuming surfaces. Its schema is 4.4 Dependency map: a `primitives` list (id, `source_packages`, owner, `global`) and an `edges` list, each edge `(primitive, surface, source: declared or static_analysis, confidence, evidence or reason, confirmed_from_source)`; a surface's own `roots` live on its registry entry. Illustrative content (timestamps omitted):

```yaml
primitives:
  - {id: FlexibleGrid,    source_packages: ["TBD.flexgrid.**"], owner: ui-platform}   # TBD. placeholders, filled from source in Phase 0 (12.9)
  - {id: Docking,         source_packages: ["TBD.docking.**"],  owner: ui-platform}
  - {id: ColumnModel,     source_packages: ["TBD.table.**"],    owner: data-ui}
  - {id: Theme,           source_packages: ["TBD.laf.**"],      owner: ui-platform, global: true}
  - {id: FontMetrics,     source_packages: ["TBD.text.**"],     owner: ui-platform, global: true}
  - {id: ChartEngine,     source_packages: ["TBD.charts.**"],   owner: charts}
  - {id: OrderTicketCore, source_packages: ["TBD.trade.**"],    owner: trade-ui}
  - {id: LadderModel,     source_packages: ["TBD.ladder.**"],   owner: trade-ui}
edges:
  - {primitive: FlexibleGrid, surface: charts.flexible-grid, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: FlexibleGrid, surface: trade.active-trader.ladder, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: FlexibleGrid, surface: sidebar.level2, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: Docking, surface: "*.detached", source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}     # every detachable surface
  - {primitive: ColumnModel, surface: monitor.activity.position-statement, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: ColumnModel, surface: trade.all-products.option-chain, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: Theme, surface: "*", source: declared, confidence: 1.0}
  - {primitive: FontMetrics, surface: "*", source: declared, confidence: 1.0}
  - {primitive: ChartEngine, surface: "charts.*", source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: ChartEngine, surface: analyze.risk-profile, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: ChartEngine, surface: sidebar.quick-chart, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: ChartEngine, surface: trade.active-trader.chart, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: OrderTicketCore, surface: "trade.order-entry.*", source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}   # every ticket variant
  - {primitive: OrderTicketCore, surface: dialog.order-confirmation, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: OrderTicketCore, surface: analyze.add-simulated-trades, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: LadderModel, surface: trade.active-trader.ladder, source: static_analysis, confidence: 0.9, evidence: "..."}
  - {primitive: Theme, surface: dialog.order-confirmation, source: declared, confidence: 1.0, reason: "colors via properties, invisible to bytecode scan"}
```

The map is derived, not hand-written. A pipeline job runs a bytecode dependency scan (jdeps at class verbosity, or an ASM scanner) over the build's jars, resolves each surface's `roots` to classes, computes for each primitive's `source_packages` the surfaces whose classes transitively depend on them, and proposes the `static_analysis` edges (confidence raised to 1.0 and `confirmed_from_source: true` once a named build's scan has seen the dependency, 4.4). `declared` edges are human-owned and add what the scan cannot see (reflection, resource bundles, properties-driven theming), each with a `reason`. The committed map is regenerated on every merge to main and reviewed like code. A scan that fails (jar unreadable, scanner crash) leaves the previous committed map in force and opens a `dependency_map_gap` with reason `scan_failed` on the next merge run, so a stale map is visible. The starter list is in 12.9 Dependency map starter list.

#### 2.10.2 Static impact step

PR runs do not trust the committed map alone. The Orchestrator takes the diff's changed classes, computes their reverse transitive dependents on the candidate build's own dependency index (depth bounded at 6, configurable), intersects with every surface's `roots`, and obtains the surfaces the change can reach. Any such surface not reached through the committed map's expansion of the touched primitives and not declared in the manifest produces `dependency_map_gap` naming the missing edge (primitive or unowned class root, surface) and opens a proposed PR against the map. A changed class in no primitive's and no surface's `roots` is reported in the same finding as an unowned root, so the primitive vocabulary grows instead of silently missing an edge.

### 2.11 Scope computation per run type

Inputs: registry R, committed Dependency Map D, manifest M (declared surfaces, touched primitives, tickets; may be absent), diff delta, candidate dependency index S (may be absent), entitlement profile E, quarantine list Q, flow library F, corpus W with its `hosted_by` relation, budget B with per-item durations from the run database, and the rig pool for the run.

```
function common_filters(items, E, Q):
  for item in items:
    if not item.entitlements subset_of E.entitlements: outcome(item) = not_run(entitlement); drop   # flows: requires
    if item.id in Q:                                outcome(item) = not_run(quarantine);  drop
  return items

function order_and_cut(items, B, rigs):
  sort by (tier asc, kind order flows, sweeps, census, estimated_duration desc)
  shard by stable hash of item.id across rigs; flows sharing a fixture stay on one rig
  frozen items: base then candidate on the same rig, back to back; a stored base capture is reused when
                fingerprint and fixture epoch match (3.1)
  masked_live items: two identically fingerprinted rigs in lockstep; with one rig free they are
                not_run(budget), never captured minutes apart
  while estimated duration on any rig > B:
     item = last item of the highest tier number on that rig, never a declared or smoke surface
     outcome(item) = not_run(budget); remove
  return items per rig

function smoke_subset(R):
  return { s in R : s.smoke }   # all tier-1 surfaces, one surface per top-level tab,
                                 # every attested Application Settings page; lint caps it at 40 (2.2.4)

function scope_pr(R, D, M, delta, S, E, Q, F, B):
  declared        = M.surfaces if M present else {}
  changed         = classes_in(delta)
  touched_prims   = (M.primitives if M present else {}) union { p in D : roots(p) intersects changed }
  map_expanded    = union over p in touched_prims of D[p].surfaces
  dependents      = reverse_closure(S, changed, max_depth = 6) if S present else {}
  static_surfaces = { s in R : roots(s) intersects dependents }
  if M absent:
     if static_surfaces union map_expanded non-empty or S absent:
          emit manifest_missing                      # case (a): UI-touching PR; diffs will be collateral
     else: mark run no_manifest                      # case (b): non-UI PR; diffs will be needs_human(no_manifest)
  for s in static_surfaces - map_expanded - declared:
      emit dependency_map_gap(edge = (owning_primitive_or_unowned_root(s, changed), s)); propose map PR
  for c in changed with no owning primitive and no owning surface:
      emit dependency_map_gap(unowned_root = c)
  census_surfaces = declared union map_expanded union static_surfaces union smoke_subset(R)
  census_items    = { (s, s.census.workspaces[0]) : s in census_surfaces }   # the canonical workspace only in PR runs
  sweep_items     = { (s, host, step) : s in census_surfaces, s.resizable, s.tier == 1,
                      host in s.hosts, step in ladder_S union splitters_short(s) }
  flow_items      = { f in F : f.tier == 1 and (f.surfaces intersects census_surfaces
                                                or f.primitives intersects touched_prims) }
  for s in R - census_surfaces: outcome(s) = not_run(scope)
  return order_and_cut(common_filters(census_items union sweep_items union flow_items, E, Q), B = 45 min, rigs)

function scope_merge(R, E, Q, F, W, B):
  census_items = { (s, w) : s in R, w in W.tierA, s hosted_by w or s.global }
  sweep_items  = { (s, host, step) : s in R, s.resizable, s.tier <= 2, host in s.hosts,
                   step in ladder_S union splitters_short(s) }
  flow_items   = { f in F : f.tier == 1 }
  for (s, w) with s not hosted_by w and not s.global: outcome = not_run(scope)
  return order_and_cut(common_filters(census_items union sweep_items union flow_items, E, Q), B = 3 h, rigs)

function scope_rc(R, E, Q, F, W, B):
  census_items = { (s, w) : s in R, w in W.tierA union W.tierB, s hosted_by w or s.global }
  sweep_items  = { (s, host, step) : s in R, s.resizable, host in s.hosts,
                   step in (ladder_F union splitters_full(s) if s.tier <= 2 else ladder_S) }
  flow_items   = F                          # all tiers and classes, migration flows on tier B
  soak_items   = the 24 soak cycle checkpoints flow/<workspace-surface-id>/soak/c<nn> on rig 5 (10.11 Soak; 1.9)
  plan = order_and_cut(common_filters(census_items union sweep_items union flow_items union soak_items, E, Q),
                       B = 8 h - 10 min - explorer_budget, rigs)   # explorer_budget = 90 min (2.9); scripted work ends by T+6:20
  append Explorer session on rig 6 with its own login, last (2.9); a later start is cut at the deadline (1.9)
  return plan
```

Rules the pseudocode relies on:

- A manifest with zero declared surfaces is allowed (pure refactor) and still yields the static impact set. A missing manifest file has two cases, decided by the static impact step. Case (a), the PR touches UI code (`static_surfaces` or `map_expanded` is non-empty): finding `manifest_missing`, the run proceeds with nothing declared, and every above-threshold diff is `collateral`, because an undeclared UI change is by definition unexpected and the developer must declare it or fix it. Case (b), the PR touches no UI code: no finding, `intended` is disabled, and every above-threshold diff is `needs_human (reason: no_manifest)`, since a side effect from non-UI code is possible but intent cannot be checked. The PR comment header states which case applied and links the manifest template.
- Budget cuts hit the highest tier number first and never a declared or smoke surface. If those alone exceed the PR budget the run proceeds, run health prints the projected overrun at scope time, and at the 45-minute deadline the Orchestrator marks every unreached checkpoint `not_run (reason: budget)` and the run `aborted_budget` (1.7 How a PR run works, minute by minute); the comment still posts.
- Every registry surface outside the computed scope is `not_run (reason: scope)`, so the PR matrix shows exactly what was not looked at.
- Checkpoints a run never reached because it aborted take the abort's class: `env_error` for `aborted_safety`, `harness_error` for `aborted_harness`, `not_run (reason: budget)` for `aborted_budget` (1.10).
- Nightly and calibration runs compute no scope; they take the canary and calibration checkpoint lists (10.3 Canary Service and the mutant catalog; 3.9 A/A calibration and threshold derivation).
- If the candidate's dependency index is missing from the pipeline artifact, the static step is skipped, all other outcomes are produced, and one `dependency_map_gap` with reason `no_dependency_index` appears in run health. Without the index case (b) cannot be told from case (a), so a missing manifest with a missing index is treated as case (a). The absence is never silent.
- `splitters_short(s)` and `splitters_full(s)` are the short and full fraction sets of 2.5.2 intersected with each declared splitter's `fractions` list (2.2.1); a surface with no `splitters` contributes no split checkpoints.

### 2.12 Coverage accounting and the matrix

The Reporter prints the coverage matrix for every run, defined exactly so runs compare cell by cell.

- Rows: every surface id at the build's registry commit, plus one synthetic row per `unregistered_surface` found this run.
- Columns: persona (active trader, options trader, futures trader, swing trader, beginner; a tier B workspace maps to its persona tag) times entitlement profile (phase 1: paperMoney margin, paperMoney IRA; more as logins are granted).
- Cell key: (surface id, persona, entitlement profile). State is exactly one of `covered`, `not_run`, `not_registered`.

```
cell(surface, persona, profile):
  if surface is synthetic: return not_registered
  C = checkpoints this run with this surface, a workspace carrying persona, a login with profile
  if C is empty:
     if not surface.entitlements subset_of profile.entitlements: return not_run(entitlement)
     if surface in Q:                                        return not_run(quarantine)
     if surface cut by budget:                               return not_run(budget)
     return not_run(scope)          # includes: no workspace of this persona hosts the surface
  usable = { c in C : outcome(c) in {identical, noise, intended, collateral, needs_human,
                                      invariant_violation, assertion_failed, needs_baseline} }
  if usable is empty:
     blocking = most frequent outcome in C among {not_run, not_settled, not_comparable,
                                                  landmark_missing, env_error, harness_error}
     if blocking == not_run: return not_run(the most frequent not_run reason in C)
                                    # entitlement, budget, scope, quarantine, step_failed:<step>, app_crash, base_step_failed, model_unavailable
     return not_run(blocked:<blocking outcome>)
  return covered(worst = max over usable in the order
                 invariant_violation > assertion_failed > needs_baseline > collateral > needs_human > intended > noise > identical   # the 1.10 precedence,
                 n = |usable|, kinds = test kinds that produced usable checkpoints)
```

Display rules:

- A `covered` cell shows the worst outcome and the count, never the word "passed"; all identical reads "identical (n)".
- A `not_run` cell shows its reason verbatim: `entitlement`, `budget`, `scope`, `quarantine`, `step_failed:<step>`, `app_crash`, `base_step_failed`, `model_unavailable`, or `blocked:<outcome>` naming the checkpoint outcome that stopped comparison (`not_settled`, `not_comparable`, `landmark_missing`, `env_error`, `harness_error`). A blocked cell is a fact about the run, counted in run health, not in coverage percent. The `coverage_cells.not_run_reason` column (8.3 Schema) accepts exactly this list.
- `needs_baseline` counts as covered for invariants and uncovered for comparison; the footnote gives the count.
- Coverage percent per tier is covered cells over cells that are not `not_run (entitlement)` or `not_run (scope)` by persona (a surface absent from a persona's workspace by design). A PR run's percent is relative to its computed scope, a merge run's to the whole registry; both print their denominators.
- Above 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints `not_run (quarantine)`, run health is red and the RC gate blocks (10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine). The share is counted in checkpoints, as 10.5 and 1.5 count it; the matrix also prints the share of tier-1 cells for display.
- Aggregated by surface, the matrix feeds the PR comment; the full matrix is a report UI page (9.5 Report UI pages). Merge, RC and Nightly runs store one `coverage_cells` row per cell; PR runs keep the matrix in the run summary (8.3).
- A manifest coverage table lists every manifest entry with the checkpoints whose surfaces it names. An entry with none prints "no covering checkpoint" and opens a flow-authoring task; an entry with a covering checkpoint and no diff above the noise floor, or whose visibility check in 3.12 (task C) returns `not_visible` or `unsure`, raises the run-level finding `intended_change_not_observed` in the Intended section and opens a triage-queue question to the PR author and feature owner with the entry and the covering checkpoints attached (9.4 Merge and RC report structure); it is a finding, and no checkpoint outcome changes. An intended change that failed to ship is a visible row, never a clean report.

### 2.13 What this model cannot detect and how it is labeled

What the model does not look at is printed, not implied. Each class below has a stable id, the mechanism that labels it in every merge and RC report under "Not detectable by design", and the phase that changes its status, if any.

| Id | Not detectable | How it is labeled | Changes in |
|---|---|---|---|
| B01 | Anything after Send: fills, rejections, server-side validation (buying power, price limits, exchange quantity rules), Working to Filled, cancel and replace, Blast All, status rows | Flows carry `requires: [paper_send]`; every cell `not_run (entitlement)`; the count and the line "send policy: no sends" print in every report | Phase 2 if `paper_send_ok` is approved (6.7 Send policy: both branches), else never; fills stay labeled untested even then until a human verifies that paperMoney simulates them on the delayed feed |
| B02 | A value wrong in both builds with no Oracle rule or assertion over it | Ends as `identical` or `noise`; an Oracle coverage table lists per tier-1 surface the value regions with and without a rule | Grows with rules; never complete |
| B03 | Temporal behavior: cell flashes, ladder re-centering, Level II and Time and Sales churn, flicker, frozen quotes | Captures are stills; streaming regions are `rule` or `mask`; the report lists surfaces with masked streaming regions and their masked share | Phase 3 soak adds frame-energy checks on a few checkpoints |
| B04 | Entitlement states paperMoney cannot produce: option approval tiers, cash-account unsettled funds, pattern day trade counter, portfolio margin, multi-account | `not_run (entitlement)` on every cell of the missing profile; the profile list prints what exists, and a paperMoney-versus-live known-gaps line (delayed data, simulated fills, no real rejections) prints under it | When fixed-entitlement test logins are granted; whether paperMoney mirrors the live login's option approval level is unverified and is read in-platform in Phase 0 |
| B05 | Live-feed data-format defects when `frozen` mode replays data (OnDemand or fixture) | Every checkpoint records its data mode; the report prints `frozen` versus `masked_live` counts per tier; `masked_live` chain and quote checkpoints stay in merge runs for this reason | DR-02 branch A reduces, never removes |
| B06 | Rendering at non-canonical configurations: 125 and 150 percent scaling, light theme, large app font, 1366x768, mixed-DPI multi-monitor | Configuration is in the fingerprint; the matrix is per configuration and prints "configurations covered: 1 of N planned" | Phase 3 tier B configurations; mixed-DPI needs physical hardware |
| B07 | macOS and Linux builds | Non-goal; no registry entries; the report header prints "platform: Windows 11 desktop only" | Not in phases 1 to 3; the registry, flow and checkpoint formats carry no Windows-only field, so nothing precludes it |
| B08 | Study mathematics beyond the verification set and thinkScript corpus | Only corpus studies have expected values; the report prints corpus size and the count of corpus-workspace studies without expectations | Grows with the corpus |
| B09 | Accessibility conformance | Branch A diffs the accessible tree build to build and reports lost names as `collateral`; nothing absolute is asserted; branch B prints "accessible tree: not available" | Not a goal |
| B10 | Side effects outside the window: email, SMS, push, sound, print, browser launches | Explorer login has no verified channels; the browser is a logging stub whose log is printed | Never |
| B11 | Cross-client state (thinkorswim Web, mobile) written by the desktop build, and the web client as a numeric oracle | Not observed; the report prints "cross-client sync: not observed". Not adopted as an Oracle source because web automation is outside the authorization of 6.12 and the session rule is unverified (DR-06) | A weekly read-only sync flow (create a watchlist, alert and drawing on desktop, read them back through a logged-in web session) only after a written automation ruling for the web client; until then never |
| B12 | Interactions outside the step vocabulary (touch, pen, IME, screen readers, drag between displays) | Flows cannot express them; the vocabulary is the closed list in 2.6.1 | Multi-monitor in Phase 3 on virtual displays |
| B13 | Surfaces unreachable because a gate failed (session rule, blocking popup) | `env_error` with gate name and screenshot; counted in run health, never in coverage | DR-06 in 11.8 sets parallelism |
| B14 | Defects whose only symptom is in the app log or a crash file | The Watchdog attaches logs and crash files per checkpoint; a crash is `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with the `app_crash` finding (2.6.1); a new exception signature in the log slice with the app alive is a tier-2 `new_log_signature` finding on the nearest checkpoint with the log lines attached (10.11), a finding that never changes the outcome; log content beyond signatures is not asserted | Phase 2 signature diff |
| B15 | A regression on a dialog the registry has but no flow reaches | Dialogs are not enumerable; the popup catalog catches those that appear on their own as `unknown_popup`; the report prints the count of registered dialogs with zero flow checkpoints | Grows with flows and Explorer candidate flows |
| B16 | Behavior with no visible symptom at any checkpoint: a key that does nothing, a setting saved but not displayed, timing, background network calls, memory growth within a run | Checkpoints and assertions are the only observation points; the report prints per flow the count of steps not followed by a checkpoint or assertion within 3 steps ("unobserved steps") and the share of tier-1 steps that are observed | Soak in Phase 3 covers memory, freeze and restart counts (10.11 Soak, 1.9 How an RC run works, 11.2); the log signature diff in Phase 2 covers B14; the rest never |

Everything else in this section ends in a closed outcome with a named mechanism. A newly discovered blind spot is added to this table with an id before work on it starts, so the report prints it the same day.

## 3. Comparison, classification and the reviewer

This section defines how two captures of one checkpoint become exactly one outcome. The build pair (3.1) and data mode (3.2) fix what is compared; the fingerprint (3.3) decides whether a comparison is allowed; capture (3.4), settle (3.5) and redaction (3.6) produce the images; the Diff Engine (3.7) measures them against the Region Registry (3.8) with thresholds from calibration (3.9); targeted re-runs (3.10) separate instability from change; the decision table (3.11) assigns the outcome; the Reviewer (3.12 to 3.16) supplies one input to that table and nothing more. Outcome names are those of 1.10 Outcome taxonomy (authoritative); reason codes are the spec-wide vocabulary listed in 12.2 Outcome taxonomy.

### 3.1 Build pair rules

The unit of comparison is a build pair: candidate and base, both installed from pipeline artifacts by the Rig Manager, both run under identical fingerprints, both driven through the same flows in the same data window. Attribution of a diff to the change under test comes from the pair; the Reviewer never attributes.

| Run type | Candidate | Base | Base selection rule | Manifest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR run | Branch build | Merge-base main build | The main build at `git merge-base branch main`. If that commit has no artifact the run is `aborted_harness (reason: base_build_missing)`, the pipeline is asked to build the merge-base, and the run is re-queued once (1.7 How a PR run works, minute by minute). There is no nearest-ancestor fallback: a diff against a different base attributes other people's changes to the PR. | PR manifest (4.3 Change manifest) |
| Merge run | New main build | Previous main build | The main build immediately before the merge. Its captures from its own merge run are the base captures where 3.1's reuse rule allows. | Union of the manifests of every PR merged since the previous main build |
| RC run | RC build | Last released build (lineage baseline) | The approved capture set of the last release when its stored fingerprint equals the current one; otherwise the Rig Manager installs the last released build and re-captures it on the current fingerprint, and approved decisions carry over by signature (3.11). | Union of merge manifests since the last release, reconciled against the Jira fixVersion export |
| Nightly run | Current main build | Same build (A/A) | Second capture of the same build in the same session; mutants injected as extra candidate images against the approved capture (10.3 Canary Service and the mutant catalog). | None loaded; every checkpoint is treated as `undeclared` (3.11), so `intended` cannot occur |
| Calibration run | One build | Same build | Per checkpoint, five back-to-back captures on one rig plus one on a second night (3.9), sharded across the pool in a weekend `all_quiet` window. Produces statistics, no classification. | None |

Rules for every pair:

- Build ids are read live at `launched` from the main window title and the install's version file (7.3 Pinned build install and version read); a mismatch between requested and read build is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_mismatch)` for that rig. The title is re-read at every flow boundary and after every relaunch; a change is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` for every remaining checkpoint of that session, on-call notified.
- Scheduling is by data mode. `frozen` checkpoints run base and candidate on the same rig back to back (base session first, then candidate session), which guarantees the fingerprint match. A frozen base capture is reused from an earlier run when the stored fingerprint id and `data_epoch` equal the live ones and the checkpoint id, Region Registry version and redaction version are unchanged; the outcome record names the source run. `masked_live` checkpoints run on two rigs provisioned from one snapshot in lockstep: fingerprint equality is asserted before the first capture, and both rigs execute the same checkpoint within 60 s of each other. A slip over 60 s re-queues that checkpoint pair once at the end of the shard; a second slip is `not_run (reason: budget)` with `lockstep_slip` counted in run health. If no second rig of the same fingerprint is free when the shard is scheduled, its `masked_live` checkpoints are `not_run (reason: budget)` rather than captured minutes apart; they appear in the coverage matrix and the sharding review (11.3 Sharding and parallelism). `masked_live` base captures are never reused.
- A stored capture (reused frozen base, RC lineage set) is compared against a fresh one only when its stored fingerprint, including `data_epoch`, equals the live fingerprint; otherwise it is re-captured, never scored.
- Checkpoint identity is the checkpoint id of 4.1 Conventions, repository layout and the lint: `<kind>/<surface-id>/<qualifier>`, where the qualifier is a workspace id, a host and size, a splitter and fraction, or a flow id and step id. Step ids are stable slugs, never indexes, and a rename needs a `flows/RENAMES.yaml` entry, so flow edits do not orphan decisions, baselines or calibration data. Target window, workspace, persona and size step are metadata on the outcome record (4.13 Outcome record).
- Step failures. A step that fails on the candidate (every scripted rung and, when enabled, the agent rung) is `failed`; its own checkpoint is `landmark_missing` (locator) or `assertion_failed` (assertion), and each downstream checkpoint of that flow is `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)` pointing at the step finding, which the Reporter ranks in Unexpected with the pre-attempt screenshot and the base build's screenshot at the same step, so a control that moved stays visible. A step that fails on the base build only makes the flow's downstream checkpoints `needs_baseline (reason: new_surface)` when the manifest entry marks the surface `new_surface: true`, else `not_run (reason: base_step_failed)` for the flow owner; the candidate captures of those checkpoints still run the Invariant Checker and the Oracle, and their findings are listed in Unexpected even though the outcome is `not_run`. A step that fails on both builds is a flow bug: candidate rule above, finding labeled both sides, flow owner.
- App failure (process gone, EDT frozen past max wait) is `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)`, with the cause in `detail`, on the checkpoint being captured and `not_run (reason: app_crash)` for the rest of that flow, with the tier-1 finding `app_crash` and crash artifacts (10.1 Failure classes and the diff-engine rule). After the relaunch the next flow starts from its preconditions and a ladder never resumes mid-way; a crash or hang during the relaunch gates, or during the gate sequence of the shard's first launch, is another `app_alive` failure that consumes the relaunch budget, never `env_error`, and a fourth app failure in a shard ends it as 1.10 states. A `process_exit` during a launcher update or with a changed build manifest is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` instead, with no `app_crash` finding and no relaunch consumed (10.2).
- A checkpoint reached through `passed_via_agent_fallback` is captured after the declared normalize routine and tagged `rescued`. It is never `identical`, `noise` or `intended` automatically, even when the diff is clean or a decision matches: at or below threshold it is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)` (3.11 row 11a); above threshold it is `collateral` on an undeclared surface, the higher-precedence outcome, or `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)` on a declared one (row 19).

### 3.2 Data modes

Each checkpoint declares `data_mode: frozen | masked_live`. The mode decides which Region Registry kinds are legal and which noise floor is expected. Operational detail (fixture, OnDemand, epoch, churn calendar) is in 7.9 Data modes operationally.

| Mode | Data source | Legal region kinds | Expected A/A floor | A non-zero floor means |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `frozen` | Deterministic market-data fixture from the backend team (Phase 0 unknown 2, Branch A), else OnDemand paused at the pinned timestamp (Branch B) where the login allows it | `freeze`, `diff`, `rule`; `mask` only for the clock, the connection indicator, the caret of a `keep_focus` checkpoint and the parking rectangle (3.5) | Zero on every region | Flow, settle or environment defect; fix before thresholds exist (3.9) |
| `masked_live` | paperMoney live-delayed data | `diff`, `rule`, `mask`, `freeze` | Zero on `diff` and `freeze` regions | A region that legitimately changes is declared `diff`; Region Registry defect |

Facts the modes depend on:

- paperMoney data is delayed about 20 minutes by default (confirmed by Schwab material); real time on a paperMoney login is community-reported to need a linked funded account and is not assumed. So the "Delayed" badge is the normal state, pinned as `fixture.delayed: true` and attested at `fixture_verified` by OCR of the status indicator; a mismatch is `env_error (gate: fixture_verified, reason: delay_state)`. Oracle comparisons against the market-data API use the delay tolerance of 2.8.2 Tolerances; Oracle values handed to the Reviewer carry timestamps and that tolerance, so a delayed quote is never reported as wrong.
- OnDemand advances in real time once started, so Branch B is deterministic only if the flow presses Pause before capture; its availability to the test login, gadget coverage and stability are unverified and are measured in Phase 0 (DR-02 in 11.8 Phase 0 spike plan: seven decision records). If it fails, chart checkpoints run `masked_live` with fixed aggregation and lookback and all data regions as `rule`.
- Every capture carries a data epoch (window date, dataset id or OnDemand timestamp, front-month futures contract, nearest option expiration, delayed or real-time state, hash of the 24-hour trading list). `data_epoch` is a match field of the fingerprint (7.4 Environment fingerprint), so base and candidate with different epochs are `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field: data_epoch)`. The RC lineage baseline is re-captured, never scored, when the epoch changes.

### 3.3 Environment fingerprint and comparability

The fingerprint fields and how each is read are defined in 7.4 Environment fingerprint; this section states the comparability rule and adds one field. Every field of class `match` in 7.4 must be equal between base and candidate; `build_id` is the variable under test and is excluded; `record` fields serve diagnosis only.

`render_probe_hash`, added by this section and included in 7.4's table, is the perceptual hash (3.7) of the Help > About text region captured after `authenticated`, compared at Hamming distance zero. It turns a rasterization change the other fields miss (a font or driver update inside the same Windows build, an anti-aliasing flag) into one fingerprint mismatch instead of hundreds of text-edge diffs.

Rules:

- The fingerprint is read on both sides at `launched`, before any capture. Any must-match mismatch makes every checkpoint of the shard `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field: <name>)`, nothing is captured on that shard, the run ends `complete_with_env_errors`, and on-call sees the field name. For same-rig back-to-back pairs the comparison is between the base session's fingerprint and the candidate session's.
- Cheap fields (window title, display, input desktop, ClearType state) are re-read at every flow boundary and after every relaunch; a change makes every remaining checkpoint of the session `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field: <name>)`.
- A fingerprint with no completed Calibration run has no thresholds: it is not a comparability failure, so nothing is `not_comparable`. Every diff with any changed pixel on that fingerprint is `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 per 3.9 step 6, invariants and assertions run as usual, the Reporter shows the count, and the Calibration Service schedules the run (7.13 What invalidates calibration). The only `not_comparable` reasons are `fingerprint_mismatch`, `window_mismatch` and `surface_mismatch`.
- Per-capture geometry (window class, title, DWM rect, z-order, monitor, DPI awareness) is stored with every image. When base and candidate rects differ in size, the images are padded to the common size with a sentinel color, padded pixels count as changed, and a `window_geometry_changed` finding records both sizes; a window opening at a different size is a product change, not an environment fault.

### 3.4 Capture rules

Capture is per top-level window of the thinkorswim process tree, not per screen and not one HWND. Component detail is in 5.7 Capture.

1. Enumerate with `EnumWindows`; keep windows whose `GetWindowThreadProcessId` belongs to the launched PID or its children and whose class name starts with `SunAwt`. The process image is expected to be the install4j launcher hosting the JVM in-process rather than `javaw.exe`; Phase 0 confirms it and the filter is by PID either way. Every kept window's rect must intersect the virtual screen, else INV-09 fires (2.7 Layout invariants).
2. Read `DWMWA_EXTENDED_FRAME_BOUNDS` via `DwmGetWindowAttribute`, grab the virtual screen with `mss`, crop to the bounds. One composite virtual-screen image per checkpoint is saved for the report; it is never diffed and never sent to the Reviewer. The cursor is not part of a screen grab.
3. The checkpoint names its `target_window` by title regex plus template; other windows present are listed in metadata. A target window not found, or found with a rect outside the virtual screen, is `not_comparable (reason: window_mismatch)`; a window whose active tab or panel headers do not match the expected screen id is `not_comparable (reason: surface_mismatch)`, with the side named. An unexpected thinkorswim window follows 7.8 Popup catalog policy and starter entries (catalog action, or the dismiss-only toolset with an `unknown_popup` finding); a foreign-process window intersecting the target rect (`WindowFromPoint` sampled on an 8 by 8 grid) is `env_error (gate: running, reason: occluded)` with pid and title.
4. `IsWindowEnabled(main_hwnd)` false means a modal is up; if it is not the expected target window and the popup policy has not cleared it by max wait, the checkpoint is `not_settled (reason: unexpected_window:<title>)`.
5. The capturing process declares Per-Monitor-V2 DPI awareness before importing any screen or input library and logs `GetProcessDpiAwareness` at run start as a self-test (10.8 Self-tests at run start); any other value ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: dpi_awareness)` before any capture. Captures are lossless PNG, content-addressed, stored with the metadata above.

### 3.5 Settle rule

Capture happens only when all of the following hold, checked in order, within the checkpoint's `max_wait` (default 15 s; chart and scan checkpoints 30 s):

1. Mouse parked at the declared coordinate in a dead area outside every gadget, and 1 s has passed (tooltip delay). The coordinate is recorded in capture metadata and a 16 by 16 px system mask around it is applied on both sides.
2. Focus dropped by clicking the declared neutral control, never by Esc (which can close the order-entry panel). Checkpoints that need a focused field declare `keep_focus: true` plus a caret mask.
3. Must-see anchors present: each anchor template matches at 0.92 normalized correlation or better.
4. Anti-anchors absent anywhere in the target window: `Loading`, `Reconnecting`, `Disconnected`, the spinner templates, the empty-grid placeholder.
5. Three consecutive frames 250 ms apart are pixel-identical outside masks and redactions.

The first frame of the triple is the capture (so 5.7 Capture and this rule agree; the three frames are identical outside masks, so which one is stored is a naming convention). At `masked_live` checkpoints the per-pixel median 7.9 describes equals this frame outside masks, because the frames are identical there, and masked pixels are never diffed; the median changes nothing the Diff Engine sees. Otherwise the outcome is `not_settled` with the failing condition as reason (`anchor_missing` for conditions 2 and 3, naming the control or anchor; `anti_anchor_present`; `frames_unstable`; `timeout` when max wait elapses, with the last failing condition), the last frame and the time elapsed; no retry, no diff. Time-to-settle is recorded per checkpoint; a p50 above twice the calibration p50 raises a `settle_regression` finding in run health for the flow owner, because a panel that takes 10 s instead of 2 s is a product signal.

### 3.6 Redaction before storage

The redaction stage runs inside Capture before any image is stored, hashed, diffed or sent (pipeline and egress log in 6.10 Redaction pipeline and egress log).

- Anchored boxes: a redaction list, owned by the security contact and separate from the Region Registry's four comparison kinds, names boxes per checkpoint as offsets from a landmark: account selector, Account Info identifiers, the user name in title and status bars, the ticket's and the Order Confirmation dialog's account field. A redaction landmark not found at its floor on either side is `landmark_missing (landmark, side)`; nothing is stored and nothing leaves the rig for that checkpoint.
- OCR sweep at 3x nearest-neighbor upscale: every word box matching the `D-` paperMoney account pattern, the 8 to 9 digit account number pattern or the test login's display name is added. A hit outside the anchored boxes is blacked out and recorded as a `redaction_miss` finding with the crop location and the side; it opens a ticket for the flow owner and the security contact because the anchor list is incomplete. A hit present on the candidate side only is ranked tier 1 in Unexpected as a suspected identifier leak, since the union rule below would otherwise hide a new place the account number appears.
- Fill with the theme background color, so the same box yields identical pixels on both sides; the union of boxes from both captures is applied to both, and per-side box counts are stored. Redacted pixels are excluded from the diff like a mask with `owner: system`. Identity redaction (the account number and the account holder or login name) is excluded from the mask budget, never diffed and proven nightly by the redaction canary (6.5, 6.10); any other redaction box counts toward the panel's mask budget (3.8).
- Only redacted images are stored. Box counts per checkpoint, a post-run plaintext scan of artifacts and OCR of a 5 percent sample for the patterns above go to the egress log; a post-run scan hit ends the run `aborted_harness` and withholds the report (6.10).

### 3.7 Three-granularity diff: algorithms and parameters

Inputs: two redacted same-size captures, the located landmarks, the Region Registry entry. Outputs: per-region metrics, components, a heatmap, findings. Pass or fail is never decided on a whole-window score. All parameters live in `diff_engine.yaml` in git; any change re-runs the canary catalog before the next product run.

**Landmarks and alignment.** A checkpoint declares one or more landmarks (one per panel it compares); each region names its landmark. Each landmark template (1:1 from the approved base) is located in both images with `cv2.matchTemplate` (`TM_CCOEFF_NORMED`) inside its search box (expected position plus or minus 200 px); accepted when the best score is at least 0.92 (overridable per landmark by `confidence_min`) and the second peak outside a 5 px radius is below 0.85. A landmark missing in either image makes the checkpoint `landmark_missing (landmark, side)` with both crops; no region of that checkpoint is diffed, so there is never a blind diff and never a partial one. Regions are cut relative to their own landmark in each image, so a panel that moved is compared against itself and the move is a `landmark_moved (dx, dy)` finding, not a pixel storm.

**Granularity 0: run-level global shift pre-pass.** Before any Reviewer call, once per run, after at least 20 pairs have been diffed: the fraction of compared checkpoints above floor, and the share of changed pixels that lie within 1 px of a text edge (Canny edges of the base crop dilated by 1 px) are computed. If more than 2 percent of compared checkpoints are above floor and more than 70 percent of their changed pixels are text-edge pixels, the run finding `global_rendering_shift` is raised: the Reviewer queue for the run is stopped, every above-threshold diff whose components are all text-edge components is `needs_human (reason: global_shift)` collapsed into one cluster under that finding, and diffs with any non-text-edge component are classified normally. On-call and the system owner see one finding instead of hundreds; a human disposes the cluster once (intended with ticket, for example a bundled JRE bump, or bug). On the Nightly run the same signal is `harness_error (reason: aa_drift_global)` per 10.6 A/A drift on the Nightly run, since there the two builds are the same.

**Granularity 1: whole window, translation only.** Float32 grayscale, `cv2.createHanningWindow`, `cv2.phaseCorrelate`. A shift is accepted when the response is at least 0.25 and 1 <= max(|dx|, |dy|) <= 64 px. The candidate is shifted back by the integer vector, borders cropped, and the per-pixel diff re-run; if the residual changed-pixel count is under 10 percent of the unshifted count, the finding is `layout_shift (dx, dy, residual_components)`. The same estimate runs per region, so one gadget moving inside a still window is caught at its region. A shift is a change, never noise; it reaches classification as an above-threshold diff (3.9).

**Granularity 2: per-pixel diff inside regions (pixelmatch-style).** For each `diff` or `freeze` region, per pixel: RGB to YIQ (Y = 0.29889531 R + 0.58662247 G + 0.11448223 B; I = 0.59597799 R - 0.27417610 G - 0.32180189 B; Q = 0.21147017 R - 0.52261711 G + 0.31114694 B), delta = 0.5053 Y^2 + 0.299 I^2 + 0.1957 Q^2, changed when delta > 35215 x t^2 with t = 0.1 (352.15). Anti-aliasing detection follows pixelmatch: a changed pixel is marked anti-aliased and not counted when, in its 3x3 neighborhood in either image, at most two neighbors are identical to it, it has both a darker and a brighter neighbor by luminance, and that darkest or brightest neighbor has at least three identical neighbors of its own in both images. Masked and redacted pixels are skipped. `edge_tolerance_px: 1` (ignore a pixel whose color appears within 1 px in the other image, symmetrically) is off by default and allowed only on a region with a human-approved `floor_exception` (3.9).

SSIM per region: `skimage.metrics.structural_similarity` on grayscale, Gaussian weights, sigma 1.5 (an 11x11 window), K1 = 0.01, K2 = 0.03, data_range 255, `use_sample_covariance=False`, plus the minimum over 16x16 blocks of the full map. SSIM feeds ranking, the heatmap and the Reviewer and decides nothing, with one exception: a region whose CIELAB mean color moves by CIEDE2000 > 2.0 while the per-pixel map is nearly empty is a `color_shift` finding (a tint below the YIQ threshold).

**Granularity 3: connected components.** Dilate the changed-pixel map with a 5x3 rectangular kernel, one iteration (merges the glyphs of a word without bridging rows), then `cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats` with 8-connectivity. Per component: area in undilated changed pixels, bounding box, centroid, owning region (by bounding-box center), mean CIEDE2000 over its changed pixels, and `color_semantic_flip` when base pixels sit in the theme's green band and candidate pixels in the red band or the reverse. Components under 4 changed pixels are dropped; everything else is reportable. There is no "small enough to ignore" above 4 px: a one-digit change is about 6 to 10 pixels at the default 9 to 11 px fonts and must survive, and the canary catalog proves nightly that it does.

**Heatmap and hash.** Heatmap: base at 40 percent brightness, changed pixels red, anti-aliased pixels yellow, region boundaries and numbered component boxes; a report artifact and Reviewer input, never a basis for a decision. Perceptual hash of every anchored component crop (box plus 8 px): 32x32 grayscale, DCT, top-left 8x8, median threshold, 64 bits. Hamming tolerance 8 of 64 for decision-signature matching on tier-2 and tier-3 checkpoints, 6 for tier-1 checkpoints and for cross-checkpoint clustering; calibration may lower a region's tolerance, never raise it (9.7 Decision persistence and inheritance), and the tolerance used is stored on every decision row.

### 3.8 Region Registry semantics

Per checkpoint, the Region Registry (schema in 4.8 Region Registry and mask record) declares named regions as offsets from landmarks. Every pixel of the target window belongs to exactly one comparison kind; pixels not covered by a declared region belong to the implicit `diff` region `_rest`.

| Kind | Pixel-diffed | Oracle rule | Who may create | Required fields | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `diff` (default) | Yes (3.7) | Optional | Anyone via PR | name, landmark, offset, size | None |
| `freeze` | Yes (3.7) | Optional | Anyone via PR | as `diff` plus `fixture_dependency` | None; a non-zero floor is a fixture defect |
| `rule` | No | Required: typed assertion by the Oracle (format, decimals, range, must-advance, must-change-within, must-not-change-when-closed, min rows) | Anyone via PR | as `diff` plus `rule` | None; listed in the sensitivity report |
| `mask` | No | None | Human only (`created_by` is a named person; the Reviewer, agent mode and the Explorer cannot create one) | owner, reason, ticket, `created_run`, `expires_at` (default plus 30 days) | Per critical panel, below |

Rules:

- Kinds do not overlap, except that a `mask` may lie inside any region and then excludes those pixels.
- Pixels under a `mask` are never diffed and never produce a finding. That is a declared blind spot, and its only guards are the budget, the expiry, the A/A re-evaluation at renewal and the canary mutants bound to the panel (10.3), which is why a mask over a value cell is refused: a non-money value cell that legitimately changes is declared `rule`, and a money cell stays pixel-diffed with a rule on top (below).
- Mask budget per critical panel (share of the panel's located bounds covered by masks plus non-identity redaction boxes): Order Confirmation dialog 10 percent, order entry ticket 10 percent, Position Statement 10 percent, Account Info 5 percent, and 0 percent over any `money_cell` region. Money cells are Qty, Price, Buying Power Effect, Max Loss and the Send, Cancel and Delete buttons, and the list is closed: the ladder price column, P/L, balances and the BUY and SELL labels are tier-1 regions, not money cells, and their mutants are non-money mutants (10.3). The account number and the account holder name are identity fields, not money cells: always redacted (3.6), excluded from the mask budget, never diffed, and proven nightly by the redaction canary (6.10). The CI lint (L-MSK-03 in 4.8) rejects a registry change that breaks a budget. The report UI refuses to submit a mask request that would exceed a budget and says why (9.6); the finding stays open in Unexpected until a `confirm_bug` or `mark_intended` decision, and raising a budget is a system-owner PR to `sentinel-config`. At run time the budget is re-evaluated per capture against the located panel bounds; a landmark move or geometry change that pushes a panel's masked plus non-identity redacted share over its budget, or any mask or redaction box onto a `money_cell`, makes the checkpoint `harness_error (reason: mask_budget_exceeded)` with the panel named in `detail`, posted to on-call and the mask owner, because a broken mask configuration must never be diffed around.
- A `money_cell` region is always pixel-diffed and rule-asserted: it is a `diff` (or `freeze`) region with a zero floor that also carries an Oracle rule (an exact expected value or an API comparison, 2.8.2), and it is never `rule`-only and never `mask`; the lint rejects either (4.8). Money-cell values come from the flow (typed quantity and limit price) and the account fixture, not from market ticks, so the zero floor holds in both data modes. A change to Buying Power Effect inside the R02 bracket on an undeclared surface is therefore `collateral` even though R02 passes, and the nightly swapped-digit money-cell mutants (10.3) reach the pixel diff.
- A mask stops applying at `expires_at`; the Reporter warns the owner seven days before. Renewal is a human action that must quote the latest nightly A/A result for the region; a region now stable in A/A is dropped, not renewed. An expired mask that nobody renews is simply gone: its pixels diff as their enclosing region from the next run, and the first above-threshold diff there is classified by 3.11 like any other.
- A failed `rule` is `assertion_failed`; a `rule` region is never pixel-diffed, so it never produces `noise`.
- The Reporter prints effective sensitivity per checkpoint: percent `diff` plus `freeze`, percent `rule`, percent `mask` plus redaction, budget use per panel, and the week-over-week change; mask growth over 30 days above 2 percent of a tier-1 checkpoint is a lint warning (L-MSK-04).

### 3.9 A/A calibration and threshold derivation

Calibration measures how much two captures of one build differ when nothing has changed. It runs before any threshold is used and again whenever the fingerprint, a flow, a region, a mask, a crop or the redaction version changes (invalidation table in 7.13 What invalidates calibration).

Procedure (Calibration Service, target rig, current main build):

1. Gates `fixture_verified` and `canary_flow_passed` passed; fingerprint recorded.
2. Capture every checkpoint five times back to back in one session on one rig (r1 to r5) and once more the following night in a fresh session on the same rig (r6), through the same settle, redaction and landmark steps as a product run. The rule "five times on one rig" holds per checkpoint, not for the library as a whole: the checkpoint set is sharded across the pool rigs and the whole run is scheduled into one weekend `all_quiet` window (7.10), from Friday 22:15 to about 11:10 Saturday for r1 to r5 and Saturday night for r6 (11.2). A checkpoint that ends `not_settled`, `landmark_missing`, `env_error` or `harness_error` in any of the six captures is a fix-list item of cause class `settle` or `landmark_jitter` with that outcome attached; it is never dropped from the set silently.
3. For every checkpoint form the 15 pairs (10 among r1 to r5, 5 between r6 and each of them) and run the Diff Engine on each. Store per region and pair in `calibration_stats`, keyed by fingerprint: changed pixel count and fraction, component count, largest component area and box, mean and minimum-block SSIM, region CIEDE2000, translation estimate, time-to-settle.
4. Floor per region and metric = maximum over the 15 pairs, published sorted by floor descending.
5. Acceptance: every `diff` and `freeze` region must have a zero changed-pixel floor. A non-zero floor goes on the fix list with a cause class read off the pair (`caret`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `flash`, `scroll`, `sort`, `live_data`, `settle`, `landmark_jitter`, `unknown`), each with a standard fix (caret mask or focus drop, parking coordinate, tooltip wait, settle anchor, explicit scroll or sort step, human re-declaration as `rule` or `mask`, longer max wait, sharper template). For `live_data` and `flash` items the Calibration Service attaches a proposed region (the dilated union of changing pixels, snapped to the landmark) as a candidate `rule` or `mask` for a human to accept by PR; nothing is applied automatically. The checkpoint is re-calibrated after the fix. Calibration completes when the fix list is empty or every remaining item has a human-approved `floor_exception` (owner, reason, 30-day expiry, measured floor). This is Phase 0 unknown 5: Branch A is an empty fix list on frozen checkpoints; Branch B is the list worked down before Phase 1 thresholds exist (DR-05 in 11.8).
6. Until calibration completes for a fingerprint, no threshold exists for it: every region of every checkpoint on that fingerprint has threshold source `uncalibrated`, and every diff with any changed pixel is `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` by 3.11, with the fix list (item, cause, owner, age in business days) printed in run health and the daily digest. Invariants and assertions are baseline-free and unaffected. A fix-list item on a `frozen` checkpoint that is older than 5 business days quarantines that checkpoint, `not_run (reason: quarantine)`, per 10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine; nobody can leave the floor non-zero indefinitely without the coverage matrix showing it. A region added to the Region Registry after the last calibration has no floor and is `uncalibrated` on its own until the checkpoint is re-calibrated; the rest of the checkpoint keeps its thresholds.
7. The A/A false-positive rate (region pairs over floor divided by region pairs compared) is a first-class metric. The Nightly run repeats step 3 for one pair of the current build on tier-1 checkpoints plus a rotating 20 percent of the rest; a zero-floor region that shows any change makes that checkpoint `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` for the night, updates flake statistics and notifies the flow owner; three nights running quarantines it; more than 2 percent of checkpoints above floor is `harness_error (reason: aa_drift_global)` and thresholds are invalid until a Calibration run passes (10.6).

Threshold derivation is mechanical, per region and metric; no human picks a number.

| Metric | Threshold rule | With a zero floor (expected) |
|---|---|---|
| Component area | report when area >= max(4, ceil(2 x floor_component_area)) | 4 px |
| Changed pixels per region (diffuse test) | report when count >= max(4, ceil(2 x floor_count)) | 4 px |
| Region mean color shift | report when CIEDE2000 >= max(2.0, 2 x floor_deltaE) | 2.0 |
| Translation | report when the accepted shift >= max(1 px, ceil(2 x floor_shift)) | 1 px |
| Settle time | `settle_regression` when p50 > 2 x calibration p50 | n/a |

Factor 2 is the margin. A region with a `floor_exception` gets the derived non-zero threshold and appears in the sensitivity report; the canary catalog must still detect every mutant bound to it, else the exception is revoked and the region becomes `rule` or `mask`. Thresholds are never raised after a noisy week; the legal responses to noise are a fix, a `rule`, a human-created `mask`, or a human decision record (3.11). The threshold record a region carries (4.8) is the set of four values above for the current fingerprint; SSIM is stored for ranking and has no threshold.

### 3.10 Targeted re-run and flake logic

A diff above threshold is re-captured before it is classified; looking again is the cheapest way to separate instability from change.

1. Trigger: a reportable component, color shift or translation in any region, or an `invariant_violation`, which is re-captured once to confirm persistence, like a diff; an `assertion_failed` is final without a re-run.
2. Re-capture: the Executor runs the declared normalize routine (Esc only where the flow declares it safe, park the mouse, drop focus on the neutral control, reset scroll, reselect the sub-tab), waits for the settle rule and captures again on the candidate side in the same session (no relaunch or re-login), never across a flow step. On the base side the same happens when the base session is still at or past that checkpoint (`masked_live` lockstep, or a frozen base session still open); a reused or closed base is not re-captured. Checkpoints declared `recapturable: false` (a ticket after Cancel) skip to step 4 with `stability: unknown (cause: not_recapturable)`.
3. Compare: every settled candidate capture against every other (and base captures likewise when more than one exists). All pairs under threshold: `stable`. Any pair above threshold: `unstable`. A re-capture that itself ends `not_settled` is retried once more; a second `not_settled` is `unstable`. For an `invariant_violation`, the invariant firing again on the re-capture is `stable` and the outcome stays `invariant_violation`; not firing is `unstable`, so the checkpoint is `not_settled (reason: unstable)` with the violation kept as evidence (2.7). The first capture is always kept and never discarded.
4. Budget: at most two re-captures per checkpoint (one for an `invariant_violation`) and max(30, 10 percent of the run's checkpoints) re-captured checkpoints per run. Beyond the run budget the checkpoint is classified with `stability: unknown (cause: budget)`; run health prints `rerun_budget_exhausted` with the count for the sharding review, and the finding shows "stability not verified". Stability and its cause are stored on the outcome record as `stability` and `stability_cause` (4.13, 8.3); there is no `needs_human` reason for an exhausted re-run budget.
5. Every `unstable` result is `not_settled (reason: unstable)` with both captures and the metrics attached, routed to the flow owner, never to the Reviewer and never to the Unexpected list (10.5). It writes a row in the `flake_events` table of 8.3 (checkpoint, region, both captures, metrics, run). The Nightly run refreshes `flake_stats` per checkpoint over a rolling 30 days: captures, re-captures, unstable outcomes, verdict flips between two runs of one build, step retries, agent fallbacks.
6. Quarantine: flake score (unstable outcomes plus verdict flips over observations) above 0.10 computed over the last 5 or more observations of the same build; or 3 unstable outcomes in 7 days; or 2 verdict flips on one build; or `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` on 3 consecutive Nightly runs (3.9 step 7, 10.6); or a gateway threshold (one safety-reason drop, or three integrity-reason drops in one flow, 5.4.8); or a non-zero A/A floor on a frozen checkpoint not fixed within 5 business days (3.9); or, for a whole flow, a 30-day agent-fallback rate above 5 percent (11.5). Drill and safety-canary flows (6.5) are exempt from quarantine: their failure pages per 9.10 instead. The Orchestrator opens the `quarantine.yaml` record as a PR; from then on the checkpoint is `not_run (reason: quarantine)`, shown in the coverage matrix in its own color, never as covered. Exit requires a fix plus 5 consecutive clean captures in a Calibration run, cited in the PR that removes the record. Nothing un-quarantines automatically. Above 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints quarantined, run health is red and the RC gate blocks.

Flake rate for the dashboard: checkpoints with a verdict flip between captures of one build (unstable re-runs plus Nightly A/A drift hits) over checkpoints compared, per run and per 30 days (9.11 Metrics dashboard and kill criteria).

### 3.11 Classification decision table

Classification assigns one outcome per checkpoint by a first-match-wins rule list over ten inputs. Each rule tests input values and the list is exhaustive, so every combination of values reaches exactly one row; the row order implements the precedence of 1.10. Findings are many per checkpoint (every component, invariant, assertion, step event and reviewer description is recorded); the outcome is one. `unregistered_surface` is a checkpoint of its own created by registry validation (2.2.3) and never enters this table; Explorer findings become checkpoints only through the replayed flow (2.9), which enters this table like any other.

| Input | Values and how each is set |
|---|---|
| G, gate | `env`: an Orchestrator gate failed before the checkpoint, `version_mismatch`, `version_changed_mid_run` (including a launcher restart seen as `process_exit`, 10.2), `session_kicked`, `fixture_drift`, `occluded`, `connectivity`, `rig_lost`, or the checkpoint was unreached in an `aborted_safety` run; every `env` value carries its gate (`gate: <state>` or `gate: preflight.<item>`). `app`: the Watchdog found the process gone or the EDT frozen past max wait while this checkpoint was being captured (`app_alive`, with the cause `jvm_crash`, `hang`, `oom` or `process_exit` in `detail`), including a crash or hang during a relaunch's gate sequence or during the gate sequence of the shard's first launch, charged to the first unreached checkpoint of the shard (10.1). `harness`: a harness exception or crash at capture or diff (Watchdog event id), `ocr_calibration` (checkpoints with OCR assertions after a calibration-panel miss, 2.8), `bounds_source_unavailable`, `mask_budget_exceeded` (3.8), `artifact_persist_failed`, `invariant_on_aa` (an enabled invariant firing on an A/A pair, 2.7), or unreached in an `aborted_harness` run. `not_run`: `entitlement`, `budget`, `scope`, `quarantine`, `step_failed:<step>`, `base_step_failed`, `app_crash`, `model_unavailable`. `not_comparable`: `fingerprint_mismatch (field)`, `window_mismatch`, `surface_mismatch`. `not_settled`: `frames_unstable`, `anchor_missing`, `anti_anchor_present`, `unexpected_window`, `timeout` on the candidate capture, or `unstable` when the targeted re-capture did not reproduce an invariant violation (3.10). `landmark`: a Region Registry or redaction landmark not found at its floor on either side. `ok`: none of these. |
| H, hard checks on the candidate capture | The first that applies: `invariant` (any INV rule of 2.7 fired), `assertion` (any Oracle assertion of 2.8 failed, or a built-in assertion other than `app_alive`, which is G `app`: `size_reached`, `soak.<metric>`), `unreadable` (an Oracle operand below its confidence floor on every source, `oracle_unreadable`, 2.8.1, or an element whose bounds could not be read, `bounds_unreadable`, 2.7), `none`. Masks do not apply to any of them. |
| B, base capture | `present`; `absent` with reason `new_surface` (manifest `new_surface: true`), `base_not_settled` (after one base re-capture), `base_env_error`, `base_harness_error`, `lineage_missing` (RC run), `reuse_missing` (frozen reuse expected, capture not found), `explorer_replay` (a replayed Explorer candidate flow, which has no base capture, 2.9); `removed` (the surface's label is on the base and absent, unpaired, on the candidate, so the candidate has no capture and the two probe screenshots are the crops, 2.2.3). |
| D, diff level | `zero` (hash-equal, or no changed pixel outside masks and redactions), `below` (changed pixels, no region over threshold), `above`. |
| S, stability | `stable`, `unstable`, `unknown (cause: not_recapturable | budget)` (3.10). |
| M, decision memory | `noise`, `intended`, `none`. A match is a persisted human decision with the same checkpoint id, region and category and a pHash within the stored tolerance (8 of 64, 6 on tier-1 checkpoints). A matching `confirmed_bug` verdict is not a row selector: the outcome is computed as if M were `none`, and the finding carries the decision id and ticket and is shown under Known bugs without a new alert (8.3 Schema, 9.7). An `intended` verdict matches only on the build pair it was made on or on a run whose loaded manifest carries the decision's manifest entry or ticket (the ticket scope of 9.7); otherwise M is `none` for it. |
| T, threshold source | `calibrated`, `uncalibrated` (3.9 step 6). |
| P, path | `scripted` (every step `passed` or `passed_after_retry`), `rescued` (the checkpoint was reached through `passed_via_agent_fallback`). |
| X, manifest | `declared` (the checkpoint's surface is in a loaded manifest entry), `undeclared` (a manifest is loaded and the surface is not in it; also every checkpoint of a Nightly run), `no_manifest_ui` (PR run, no manifest, and the static impact step of 2.10.2 found UI dependents of the change), `no_manifest_nonui` (PR run, no manifest, no UI dependents found). |
| R, reviewer | `match_hi` (`matches_manifest`, confidence at or above the routing threshold, 0.80 until 3.14 derives it), `match_lo` (`matches_manifest` below it, or `partially_matches_manifest`), `no_match` (`does_not_match_manifest` at or above the threshold), `nothing` (`no_visible_difference`), `unsure` (`cannot_judge`, or `does_not_match_manifest` below the threshold), `unavailable` (API down, preflight failed, reviewer disabled, refusal, schema violation after one retry, batch item expired or errored past the deadline, pinned model not served), `capped` (the item is beyond the run's reviewer call cap, or still awaiting a verdict when the per-run spend ceiling or the weekly dollar cap stopped model calls, 3.15), `pending` (queued, not yet answered). |

Rule list (first match wins; `*` is any value; who sees each outcome and what happens next is in 1.10):

| # | G | H | B | D | S | M | T | P | X | R | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `env` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `env_error` (gate, reason, screenshot) |
| 1a | `app` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `assertion_failed` (assertion: app_alive, cause in `detail`, crash artifacts; finding `app_crash`) |
| 2 | `harness` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `harness_error` (reason, Watchdog event) |
| 3 | `not_run` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `not_run` (reason) |
| 4 | `not_comparable` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `not_comparable` (reason, field or side) |
| 5 | `not_settled` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `not_settled` (condition, last frame, elapsed) |
| 6 | `landmark` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `landmark_missing` (landmark, side, both crops) |
| 7 | `ok` | `invariant` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `invariant_violation` (rule ids, bounds overlay) |
| 8 | `ok` | `assertion` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `assertion_failed` (assertion ids, expected, extracted) |
| 9 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `absent` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `needs_baseline` (reason) |
| 9a | `ok` | `unreadable` | `present` | `zero`, `below` | * | * | * | * | * | * | `needs_human` (reason: oracle_unreadable or bounds_unreadable, crop, field or element) |
| 10 | `ok` | `none` | `present` | `zero` | * | * | * | `scripted` | * | * | `identical` |
| 11 | `ok` | `none` | `present` | `below` | * | * | * | `scripted` | * | * | `noise` (reason: below_floor) |
| 11a | `ok` | `none` | `present` | `zero`, `below` | * | * | * | `rescued` | * | * | `needs_human` (reason: rescued_capture, locator finding) |
| 12 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `unstable` | * | * | * | * | * | `not_settled` (reason: unstable, both captures) |
| 13 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | `noise` | * | `scripted` | * | * | `noise` (suppressed by decision #id) |
| 14 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | `intended` | * | `scripted` | * | * | `intended` (suppressed by decision #id) |
| 15 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `uncalibrated` | * | * | * | `needs_human` (reason: uncalibrated, fix-list item) |
| 16 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | * | `undeclared` | * | `collateral` (primitive consumed, manifest entry that touched it) |
| 17 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | * | `no_manifest_ui` | * | `collateral` (run finding `manifest_missing`) |
| 18 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | * | `no_manifest_nonui` | * | `needs_human` (reason: no_manifest) |
| 19 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | `rescued` | `declared` | * | `needs_human` (reason: rescued_capture, locator finding) |
| 20 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | `scripted` | `declared` | `match_hi` | `intended` (reviewer confirmation, confidence) |
| 21 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | `scripted` | `declared` | `no_match` | `needs_human` (reason: reviewer_no_match, defect class) |
| 22 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | `scripted` | `declared` | `match_lo`, `nothing`, `unsure` | `needs_human` (reason: reviewer_uncertain, verdict) |
| 23 | `ok` | `none`, `unreadable` | `present` | `above` | `stable`, `unknown` | * | `calibrated` | `scripted` | `declared` | `unavailable`, `capped`, `pending` | `needs_human` (reason: reviewer_unavailable for `unavailable` and `pending`, reviewer_cap for `capped`; `review_state: pending` while queued, `done` once the job gives up) |
| 24 | `ok` | * | `removed` | * | * | * | * | * | `declared` | `match_hi` | `intended` (removal confirmed against the entry, 2.2.3) |
| 25 | `ok` | * | `removed` | * | * | * | * | * | `declared` | `pending` | `needs_human` (reason: reviewer_unavailable, `review_state: pending`) |
| 25a | `ok` | * | `removed` | * | * | * | * | * | `declared` | `match_lo`, `no_match`, `nothing`, `unsure`, `unavailable`, `capped` | `needs_human` (reason: reviewer_no_match when the verdict does not confirm the removal; reviewer_unavailable for `unavailable`, reviewer_cap for `capped`; both probe screenshots) |
| 26 | `ok` | * | `removed` | * | * | * | * | * | * | * | `collateral` (removed surface that no loaded manifest entry declares, both probe screenshots) |

Notes:

- Rows 1, 1a and 2 to 9 implement the precedence `env_error`, app failure (`assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)`), `harness_error`, `not_run`, `not_comparable`, `not_settled`, `landmark_missing`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed`, `needs_baseline` of 1.10; an exception raised while handling an app failure is evidence on that checkpoint, not a harness failure of it (10.1). A checkpoint with both an invariant violation and a reviewer verdict ends in row 7; the verdict and description are attached as a finding and the Reviewer never moves it. The same holds for an assertion failure (row 8). A `waived` decision on either (9.6 One-click actions and who may perform them) suppresses the finding in the report and never changes the outcome.
- Row 9: a base that ends `not_settled` is re-captured once under the settle rule while its session is still at that checkpoint; only a second failure sets B to `absent`. The candidate's invariants and assertions have already run (rows 7 and 8 come first), so a `needs_baseline` checkpoint is still a product finding when they fired.
- Rows 9a and 11a: an unreadable Oracle value or element bounds, or an agent-rescued path, means the checkpoint was not fully looked at, so a clean or below-floor diff is `needs_human`, never `identical` or `noise`. Fixed order of `needs_human` reasons: the row order of this table, 9a (`oracle_unreadable`, `bounds_unreadable`), 11a (`rescued_capture`), 15 (`uncalibrated`), 18 (`no_manifest`), 19 (`rescued_capture`), 21 (`reviewer_no_match`), 22 (`reviewer_uncertain`), 23 and 25 (`reviewer_unavailable`, `reviewer_cap`), 25a (`reviewer_no_match`, `reviewer_unavailable`, `reviewer_cap` for a removed declared surface), with `global_shift` in place of rows 16 to 23. When two reasons apply, the first matching row's reason is the outcome reason and every other applicable reason goes in `detail`; rows 9 and 12 to 23 accept H `unreadable`, so an unreadable value never outranks the row the checkpoint reaches and is recorded in `detail` there.
- Row 12 goes to the flow owner, not the triage rotation, and is never a product finding; rows 11 and 12 never reach the Reviewer, so it is never asked what changed between two near-identical images. A row 11 result on a `money_cell` region cannot occur: such regions have a zero floor and no mask, so any changed pixel is `above`.
- Rows 13 and 14 require `P = scripted`; a `rescued` checkpoint ignores decision memory and falls through to rows 15 to 19, so an agent-rescued capture is never auto-suppressed (3.1). Decision inheritance is by verdict (`noise`, `intended`), per 8.3.
- Row 15 precedes the manifest rows because "above threshold", which `collateral` requires, cannot be asserted without a threshold; the item is ranked with collateral in Unexpected by tier and names the fix-list item that withholds the threshold. Rows 16 to 18 are decided by surface declaration alone; the Reviewer's description is attached when available but cannot move the checkpoint. Row 17 puts the `manifest_missing` finding and "no manifest; every change is reported as collateral until one is added" in the report header; row 18 puts "no manifest, no UI code touched; changes need a human" there (the two cases of 4.3 and 1.7). The Flexible Grid change that overlaps the Active Trader ladder lands in row 16 when no invariant fires: the ladder surface is undeclared, the diff is stable, and the finding names `FlexibleGrid` and the manifest entry that touched it.
- Row 21 is the collateral-on-a-declared-surface case: the Reviewer is confident the change is unrelated to the entry that declared the surface.
