```sql
  captures_json  TEXT NOT NULL,             -- sha256 of every capture compared
  metrics_json   TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at     TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE flake_stats (                  -- rolling 30 days, refreshed by the Nightly run (10.5)
  checkpoint_id    TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES checkpoints(checkpoint_id),
  observations     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- captures compared
  recaptures       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  unstable_total   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  unstable_7d      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  flip_total       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- verdict flips between runs of one build
  flips_same_build INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  step_retries     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  agent_fallbacks  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  flake_score      REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,      -- unstable plus flips over observations
  last_flip_run_id TEXT,
  quarantined      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (quarantined IN (0,1)),
  quarantine_commit TEXT,                   -- sentinel-config commit whose quarantine.yaml holds the record
  quarantined_at TEXT, quarantined_by TEXT, quarantine_owner TEXT, quarantine_ticket_ref TEXT, quarantine_reason TEXT,
  updated_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
  CHECK (quarantined = 0 OR (quarantine_commit IS NOT NULL AND quarantine_owner IS NOT NULL
                             AND quarantine_ticket_ref IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE TABLE canary_results (
  canary_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  kind              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'mutant' CHECK (kind IN ('mutant','safety_canary','fire_drill','path_equivalence')),   -- 10.3 mutants; 6.3 to 6.10 safety canaries; 6.5 drill items; the nightly re-evaluated real pair of 10.3
  mutant_id         TEXT NOT NULL,          -- M01 to M33 of sentinel-config/canaries/mutants.yaml (12.5); drill items are drill-1 to drill-5; safety canaries name their control (6.3 to 6.10)
  catalog_version   TEXT NOT NULL,
  checkpoint_id     TEXT NOT NULL,
  defect_class      TEXT NOT NULL,          -- the snake_case class names of 10.3 (erased_control, swapped_digit, swapped_label, color_swap,
                                            -- shifted_panel, clipped_label, overlapped_panels, missing_row, header_change, placeholder,
                                            -- font_height, scrollbar, redaction, sub_floor, global_shift, landmark_loss, study_removed,
                                            -- aa_control, wrong_quantity, blank_field, gateway) plus the classes M29 to M33 of 12.5 add
                                            -- (outside_parent, window_offscreen, misaligned_column, focus_order, error_dialog); 26 names, equal to the
                                            -- class enum of 4.11; one list, kept in canaries/mutants.yaml
  money_cell        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (money_cell IN (0,1)),
  seed              INTEGER NOT NULL,
  base_sha256 TEXT, mutant_sha256 TEXT,
  expected_json     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- the mutant's expected outcome list
  produced_outcome  TEXT,
  produced_reason   TEXT,
  state             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('detected','missed','detector_blind',
                      'detector_degraded','generation_failed')),
  absorbed_by       TEXT,                   -- mask id, decision id, threshold or landmark that swallowed a miss
  class_rate REAL, class_floor REAL,        -- that night's class detection rate and rolling floor
  reviewer_verdict TEXT, reviewer_confidence REAL,
  mask_version TEXT, threshold_version TEXT, model_id TEXT, prompt_hash TEXT,
  created_at        TEXT NOT NULL,
  CHECK (NOT (money_cell = 1 AND state = 'missed')),            -- a money-cell miss is always detector_blind
  CHECK (NOT (money_cell = 0 AND state = 'detector_blind')),
  CHECK (state <> 'detector_degraded' OR (class_rate IS NOT NULL AND class_floor IS NOT NULL)),
  CHECK (state NOT IN ('missed','detector_blind','detector_degraded') OR produced_outcome IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE calibration_floors (
  floor_id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  checkpoint_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoints(checkpoint_id),
  region_id          TEXT NOT NULL,         -- '*' for whole window
  fingerprint_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,         -- a floor is valid for one fingerprint only
  calibration_run_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  samples            INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- A/A pairs measured
  diff_pixels_p50 INTEGER, diff_pixels_p95 INTEGER, diff_pixels_max INTEGER,
  ssim_min           REAL,
  components_max INTEGER, largest_bbox_max TEXT,
  phash_noise_spread INTEGER, fault_separation INTEGER,   -- inputs to the tolerance rule of 9.7
  pairs_json         TEXT,                  -- the per-pair metrics of 3.9 step 3 (15 pairs per checkpoint and region)
  threshold_pixels   INTEGER NOT NULL,      -- derived per 3.9
  threshold_ssim     REAL NOT NULL,
  nonzero_on_frozen  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- 1 marks a flow or environment bug to fix
  exported_commit    TEXT,                  -- sentinel-config commit of calibration/<fingerprint_id>.yaml
  valid_from         TEXT NOT NULL, superseded_at TEXT
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_floor_current ON calibration_floors(checkpoint_id, region_id, fingerprint_sha256)
  WHERE superseded_at IS NULL;

CREATE TABLE calibration_fixes (            -- the fix list of 3.9: one row per non-zero floor on a frozen checkpoint
  fix_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  floor_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES calibration_floors(floor_id),
  checkpoint_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES checkpoints(checkpoint_id),
  region_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
  cause_class    TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (cause_class IN ('timing','state','animation','landmark','redaction','rendering','unknown')),
  owner          TEXT NOT NULL,
  ticket_ref     TEXT,
  opened_at      TEXT NOT NULL,             -- age = now minus opened_at; open 5 business days quarantines the checkpoint (10.5)
  closed_at TEXT, closed_by TEXT, floor_exception_ref TEXT,   -- closed by a fix, or by a human-approved floor_exception (3.9)
  CHECK ((closed_at IS NULL) = (closed_by IS NULL))
);

CREATE TABLE reviewer_evals (               -- one row per evaluation of a model and prompt version (3.14, 10.4)
  eval_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  eval_set_version TEXT NOT NULL, model_id TEXT NOT NULL, prompt_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  items INTEGER NOT NULL, metrics_json TEXT NOT NULL,   -- precision and recall per category, tier 1 recall, ECE
  passed_gate INTEGER NOT NULL, run_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE soak_samples (                 -- 10.11: one row per process per 60 s sample on the soak rig
  run_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  sampled_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  pid        INTEGER NOT NULL,
  metric     TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- working_set, private_bytes, gdi_objects, user_objects, handles, threads, cpu, heap_after_gc, clock_tick
  value      REAL NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, sampled_at, pid, metric)
) WITHOUT ROWID;
```

Soak (10.11) stores nothing else of its own: its 24 cycle checkpoints are `outcomes` rows with ids `flow/<workspace-surface-id>/soak/c<nn>`, a budget breach is `assertion_failed (assertion: soak.<metric>)` on the cycle checkpoint, a freeze or crash during soak is the app-failure trio of 10.1 (never `env_error`), and the curves the RC report draws come from this table.

Canary states: `detected` when the produced outcome is in the mutant's expected list; `missed` when a non-money mutant was absorbed but its class stayed at or above the rolling floor that night; `detector_degraded` when a non-money miss took its class below the floor; `detector_blind` for any missed money-cell mutant; `generation_failed` when the landmark for the mutant was missing (its checkpoint outcome is `harness_error (reason: canary_generation_failed)`). The Nightly run's `summary_json` and the `detector_state` key of `system_state` carry the resulting banner state (ok, degraded, blind) with its start time, which is what the Reporter stamps on every report until a Nightly run passes. The Nightly run's outcome stays `complete` whatever these rows say: `detector_blind` or `generation_failed` sets `system_state.detector_state`, pages P1 and puts the banner on every report until the next green canary, and the run is `aborted_harness (reason: canary_generation_failed)` only when no canary could run at all (10.3). The fire drill and the safety canaries of 6.3 to 6.10 are rows with `money_cell = 1`, so a miss is `detector_blind` with the blind detector in `defect_class`; a drill item not blocked is in addition the checkpoint outcome `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)`, and a drill that placed an order is not a canary state but the run outcome `aborted_safety (reason: drill_order_placed)` (6.5). A `path_equivalence` row that misses is `harness_error (reason: canary_path_divergence)` on the re-evaluated pair (10.3).

**Egress, coverage, artifacts, proofs, incidents and system state.**

```sql
CREATE TABLE egress_log (                   -- 6.10: every outbound request
  egress_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id            TEXT REFERENCES runs(run_id),   -- NULL for the daily digest and the model check
  shard_id          TEXT, checkpoint_id TEXT,
  sent_at           TEXT NOT NULL,
  destination       TEXT NOT NULL,          -- host name
  purpose           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('review','batch_review','agent_step',
                      'explorer_step','pr_comment','jira','slack','digest','preflight','model_check')),
  status            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('sent','refused','failed')),
  response_status   INTEGER,
  artifact_sha256   TEXT,                   -- redacted artifact that left, when one did
  bytes             INTEGER NOT NULL,
  redaction_version TEXT,
  model_id TEXT, request_id TEXT,
  refusal_reason    TEXT,                   -- destination not allowlisted, redaction version missing
  CHECK (status <> 'refused' OR refusal_reason IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE outbox (                       -- 9.1: every outbound post is a job before it is a send
  job_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id          TEXT REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  kind            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('pr_comment','commit_status','jira_create','jira_comment','jira_transition',
                    'slack','page','digest','manifest_pr','mask_pr')),
  destination     TEXT NOT NULL,
  payload_sha256  TEXT NOT NULL,            -- the payload is an artifact; the row carries its hash
  attempts        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  next_attempt_at TEXT,
  last_error      TEXT,
  state           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (state IN ('queued','sent','failed','abandoned')),
  created_at      TEXT NOT NULL, sent_at TEXT,
  CHECK ((state = 'sent') = (sent_at IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE TABLE coverage_cells (               -- merge, RC and nightly runs only; PR runs keep the matrix in runs.summary_json
  run_id           TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  surface_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  persona          TEXT NOT NULL,
  entitlement      TEXT NOT NULL,
  tier             INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('covered','not_run','not_registered')),
  not_run_reason   TEXT CHECK (not_run_reason IN ('entitlement','budget','scope','quarantine','base_step_failed','app_crash','model_unavailable')
                     OR not_run_reason LIKE 'step_failed:%' OR not_run_reason LIKE 'blocked:%'),   -- 2.12; blocked:<outcome> names the outcome that blocked every checkpoint of the cell
  worst_outcome    TEXT,                    -- covered cells: the worst usable outcome
  checkpoint_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, surface_id, persona, entitlement),
  CHECK ((state = 'not_run') = (not_run_reason IS NOT NULL)),
  CHECK ((state = 'covered') = (worst_outcome IS NOT NULL))
);

CREATE TRIGGER trg_coverage_run_type BEFORE INSERT ON coverage_cells
WHEN (SELECT run_type FROM runs r WHERE r.run_id = NEW.run_id) NOT IN ('merge','rc','nightly')
BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'coverage_cells rows exist only for merge, RC and nightly runs'); END;

CREATE TABLE artifacts (                    -- index of the artifact store; a row exists only for verified bytes on disk
  sha256            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  kind              TEXT NOT NULL,          -- capture, crop, heatmap, diff_mask, ocr_json, bounds_json, csv_export,
                                            -- agent_frame, video, crash, log_slice, attestation, gate, request,
                                            -- manifest, ledger, journal, mutant
  media_type        TEXT NOT NULL,
  bytes             INTEGER NOT NULL,
  width INTEGER, height INTEGER,
  redaction_passed  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (redaction_passed = 1),   -- images: redaction stage; text: plaintext scan
  redaction_version TEXT,
  set_path          TEXT NOT NULL,          -- runs/<run_id>, baselines/<lineage>/<build_id>, eval/<version>
  first_run_id      TEXT,
  created_at        TEXT NOT NULL,
  pinned            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,   -- referenced by a baseline or an unclosed finding
  audit_state       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ok' CHECK (audit_state IN ('ok','missing','corrupt')),
  last_audit_at     TEXT,
  deleted_at        TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE post_run_proofs (              -- 6.6: ORDER SAFETY PROOF, one per shard
  shard_id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES shards(shard_id),
  run_id            TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  login_alias       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES logins(login_alias),
  verdict           TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (verdict IN ('proven_no_sends','proven_declared_sends','proven_no_session','unproven')),   -- proven_no_session: no token issued, read from the gateway log (6.6)
  reason            TEXT,
  send_policy_ref   TEXT NOT NULL,          -- risk owner decision id from policy/send_policy.yaml
  counts_json       TEXT NOT NULL,          -- working, filled, canceled, position rows: start, end, new, expected; net liq start, end, drift
  cancel_all        TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (cancel_all IN ('not_needed','performed_verified','performed_unverified')),
  paper_mode_assertions INTEGER NOT NULL, paper_mode_mismatches INTEGER NOT NULL,
  gateway_events INTEGER NOT NULL, gateway_drops INTEGER NOT NULL,
  start_snapshot_sha256 TEXT, end_snapshot_sha256 TEXT,
  produced_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
  verified_by TEXT, verified_at TEXT,       -- human clearance of an unproven verdict
  CHECK (verdict <> 'unproven' OR reason IS NOT NULL)
);

CREATE TABLE incidents (                    -- 6.12: S1 to S3 rows, linked from the report
  incident_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  run_id        TEXT REFERENCES runs(run_id),
  rig_id        TEXT, login_alias TEXT,
  severity      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (severity IN ('S1','S2','S3')),
  trigger       TEXT NOT NULL,
  opened_at     TEXT NOT NULL,
  closed_at TEXT, closed_by TEXT, close_reason TEXT, ticket_ref TEXT, postmortem_ref TEXT,
  CHECK ((closed_at IS NULL) = (closed_by IS NULL)),
  CHECK (closed_by IS NULL OR closed_by NOT IN ('reviewer','system','orchestrator','reporter'))
);

CREATE TABLE system_state (                 -- keys: last_backup_at, last_backup_error, last_integrity_check_at,
  key TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                     --   last_restore_drill_at, last_artifact_audit_at, kill_switch_state,
  value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL   --   detector_state, schema_version, free_bytes_at_last_preflight
);
```

**Indexes.** Run health counts (env errors, harness errors, not settled, quarantined, agent fallbacks, gateway drops, store failures) are computed by the Reporter over these indexes and stored in the run's summary JSON.

```sql
CREATE INDEX ix_runs_type_time   ON runs(run_type, started_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_runs_pair        ON runs(pair_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_shards_run       ON shards(run_id, state);
CREATE INDEX ix_outcomes_cp_run  ON outcomes(checkpoint_id, run_id);      -- history per checkpoint
CREATE INDEX ix_outcomes_run_out ON outcomes(run_id, outcome, reason);
CREATE INDEX ix_outcomes_pending ON outcomes(run_id) WHERE review_state = 'pending';
CREATE INDEX ix_steps_run_seq    ON step_events(run_id, shard_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX ix_steps_notable    ON step_events(run_id, step_outcome)
  WHERE step_outcome IN ('passed_after_retry','passed_via_agent_fallback','failed','blocked_by_gateway');
CREATE INDEX ix_steps_dropped    ON step_events(run_id) WHERE gate_decision IN ('dropped','refused');
CREATE INDEX ix_findings_open    ON findings(triage_state, tier, created_at) WHERE triage_state = 'open';
CREATE INDEX ix_findings_run     ON findings(run_id, kind);
CREATE INDEX ix_decisions_sig    ON decisions(checkpoint_id, region_id, category) WHERE revoked_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_reviews_run      ON reviews(run_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_reviews_model    ON reviews(model_id, prompt_hash);
CREATE INDEX ix_baselines_cp     ON baselines(checkpoint_id, lineage, state);
CREATE INDEX ix_regions_commit   ON regions(config_commit, checkpoint_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_masks_commit     ON masks(config_commit, checkpoint_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_flake_events_cp  ON flake_events(checkpoint_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_canary_run       ON canary_results(run_id, money_cell, state);
CREATE INDEX ix_egress_run       ON egress_log(run_id, sent_at);
CREATE INDEX ix_artifacts_sweep  ON artifacts(set_path, pinned, created_at) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_incidents_open   ON incidents(rig_id) WHERE closed_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_outbox_due       ON outbox(state, next_attempt_at) WHERE state IN ('queued','failed');
CREATE INDEX ix_soak_run         ON soak_samples(run_id, metric, sampled_at);
```

### 8.4 Artifact layout on disk

Every file is stored under its SHA-256 within a set, and every set has a manifest mapping human names to hashes. Hashing is for integrity and linking, not for space: screenshots of a trading UI are almost never byte-identical across runs (quotes, clocks and anti-aliased text change bytes even inside masked regions), so 8.8 assumes no cross-run deduplication.

```
RIG   C:\sentinel\run\<shard_id>\
        run.db, run.db-wal, run.db-shm   Run Store
        writer.lock                      PID of the single writer
        heartbeat.json                   10.2
        results.jsonl                    append-only ledger of every database row of this shard
        gateway_drops.jsonl              drop-log drainer's journal of the hook host's ring (5.4.2)
        watchdog_events.jsonl            Watchdog journal
        manifest.json                    names -> hashes for this shard
        objects\<aa>\<sha256>.<ext>      aa = first two hex digits of the hash

CONTROL HOST   D:\sentinel\artifacts\
  incoming\<shard_id>\            upload staging; moved into runs\ after hash and ledger verification
  runs\<run_id>\
    manifest.json                 union of the shards' manifests
    shards\<n>\results.jsonl      the ledgers and journals, kept verbatim
    objects\<aa>\<sha256>.<ext>
  baselines\<lineage>\<build_id>\
    manifest.json                 the approved set for this build in this lineage
    objects\<aa>\<sha256>.<ext>
  eval\<eval_set_version>\        manifest.json and objects, same shape
  quarantine\<run_id>\            objects moved here by the plaintext scan; security clears them
```

Manifest entries carry `name` (for example `flow/dialog.order-confirmation/flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit/s07/candidate/capture.png`), `sha256`, `kind`, `bytes`, `media_type`, `checkpoint_id`, `side`, `redaction_version` and `captured_at`; the header carries the run or build id, the shard, the config commit, the harness commit and `created_at`. A name may map to a hash present in another set; the object is written again under this set because sets are the unit of retention and backup.

Write path on the rig. Capture runs the redaction stage, hashes the redacted bytes, writes them to a temporary name under `objects`, flushes, verifies the hash by reading back, and renames into place; only then does the Orchestrator queue the batch that names the hash. A write that fails (disk full, I/O error) is retried once; a second failure ends the checkpoint `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)` and the run can no longer be `complete` (8.9). A failure with `ENOSPC` is the same checkpoint outcome and also makes the Orchestrator request the Watchdog's immediate free-space check; only that check, the Watchdog's free-space check, ends the run, as `aborted_harness (reason: disk_full)` with every remaining checkpoint `harness_error (reason: disk_full)` (10.2, 8.9). An artifact without a redaction version is refused by the writer, so no path exists by which an unredacted image reaches a stored object on either host. Text artifacts (crash files, log slices, exports, reviewer requests, ledgers, journals) pass the post-run plaintext scan instead (6.9 Credentials and secret steps); a hit moves the shard's objects to `quarantine` and the run ends `aborted_harness (reason: secret_leaked)` with the report withheld.

Write path on the control host. The import streams each object to `incoming`, recomputes the hash, rejects a mismatch, flushes, renames into `objects` and inserts the `artifacts` row inside the shard's import transaction. A mismatch is re-requested from the rig up to three times; a persisting mismatch marks the shard `import_failed` with reason `upload_hash_mismatch`, the run `aborted_harness (reason: artifact_persist_failed)`, and the rig keeps its copy until a human has looked (8.9).

Kinds and sources: capture (Capture, one per checkpoint per side); crop, heatmap and diff mask (Diff Engine, above threshold only); OCR and bounds sidecars (Oracle, Invariant Checker); CSV export (Oracle); agent frame (Executor in agent mode and the Explorer, JPEG quality 80 at half resolution); video (Capture at 3 frames per second: full length for RC runs and the nightly fire drill, a 30 second ring buffer around failures otherwise); crash (Watchdog: `hs_err_pid*.log`, WER dumps, thread dumps); log slice (Watchdog); attestation and gate screenshots (Orchestrator, every gate pass or fail); request (Reviewer input JSON); ledger and journal (Orchestrator, hook host, Watchdog); mutant (Canary Service).

### 8.5 What lives in git and how a run pins it

The `sentinel-config` repository holds everything that tells a run what to do; its layout and lint are owned by 4.1 Conventions, repository layout and the lint, and the paths below are that layout plus the files this section adds. Baseline images do not live in git; a manifest naming them does. The harness, its schemas and `sentinel lint` live in the `sentinel` repository.

```
taxonomy.yaml                                  outcome enums, reasons, finding kinds, triage states; the source of every CHECK and lookup row
schemas/*.schema.json                          generated record schemas (4.1)
builds/*.yaml                                  build identity and build pairs
manifests/<build_id>.yaml, manifests/mocks/    change manifests
registry/surfaces/<area>/*.yaml                Surface Registry
registry/dependency-map.yaml                   primitive -> surfaces
registry/ladders.yaml                          size-sweep ladders S and F
corpus/workspaces/<id>/                        Workspace Corpus entries and workspace files
flows/<tier>/*.yaml, flows/RENAMES.yaml        flows; checkpoint rename map
flows/quarantine/<finding-id>.yaml             Explorer candidate flows awaiting promotion (2.9)
regions/<checkpoint_id>.yaml                   Region Registry: freeze, rule, mask, diff, redaction regions and landmarks
regions/landmarks/<landmark_id>.png            landmark templates
masks/<checkpoint_id>/*.yaml                   mask records
fixtures/*.yaml, profiles/*.yaml               account and data fixtures; pinned settings profiles
popups/catalog.yaml                            popup catalog
canaries/mutants.yaml                          the one mutant catalog: ids M01 to M33, classes of 10.3, money_cell flag, seed 20260101 (12.5, 10.3)
gateway/allowlist.yaml                         exact paper account ids per rig, hashed into the fingerprint (6.4)
gateway/default_order_hotkeys.yaml             default order-action chords of the pinned build, read once in Phase 0 (6.2)
configs/allowed.yaml                           display configurations, each its own fingerprint (7.1)
diff_engine.yaml                               Diff Engine parameters (3.7)
budgets.yaml                                   dollar caps per run and per week (11.4)
soak.yaml                                      soak budgets (10.11)
ops/rotation.yaml                              credential rotation calendar (7.7)
model_deprecations.yaml                        vendor deprecation notices the system owner records (10.7)
policy/release_gate.yaml                       sign-off lead N per release train (11.1)
calibration/<fingerprint_id>.yaml              per-region A/A floors, exported by the Calibration Service from calibration_floors
quarantine.yaml                                quarantined checkpoints: checkpoint, owner, ticket, entered, reason (10.5)
policy/send_policy.yaml                        the OPEN paper_send_ok switch, signed by the risk owner
phase0/branches.yaml                           the chosen branch for each unknown
eval/<eval_set_version>/labels.jsonl           reviewer eval labels; images live in the artifact store
baselines/<lineage>/<build_id>/manifest.json   committed by the sign-off bot at RC sign-off
authorization/<version>.md                     the signed authorization of 6.12, referenced by every run
CODEOWNERS                                     flow owner per surface tier approves flows/ and registry/
```

Pinning. At run creation the Orchestrator on the control host side of the Scheduler resolves one commit of `sentinel-config` (HEAD of main, or the commit a config smoke lane names), records it as the run's config commit, builds a tarball of that tree, records its hash, and the Rig Manager ships the same tarball to every shard. Alongside it goes a read-only snapshot of the Central Store's decisions, baselines, regions, masks, calibration floors and quarantine records as of run creation, hashed into `snapshot_set_sha256`, so every shard applies the same inheritance and the run can name the decision set it used. Both sides of a build pair run the same registry, flows, masks, corpus and catalogs, and no run reads a moving branch. The workspace hash in the environment fingerprint is computed from the corpus files in that tarball, so a corpus change produces a new fingerprint and invalidates calibration (7.13 What invalidates calibration). The `regions` and `masks` tables are loaded from the same commit, which is how the Reporter shows mask growth by commit. Harness code is pinned separately as the run's harness commit, installed by the Rig Manager at snapshot build. Run health prints both commits, the tarball hash and the snapshot hash.

Change control. Every pull request to `sentinel-config` runs `sentinel lint` (4.15 Cross-file rules and the lint pipeline): schema validation, checkpoint ids unique across the tree and matching the grammar of 8.3, a rename map whenever an id disappears, a landmark template for every region, masks inside the checkpoint window and under the per-panel coverage budget, every mask with owner, reason, expiry and a human author, `taxonomy.yaml` equal to the taxonomy table of 1.10 and the appendix copy. Masks are created only through this path: the report UI's request mask action opens a pull request with the record prefilled and the requester as author; the Reviewer may only propose, and a proposal is a finding, not a mask. Quarantine records and Explorer candidate flows are opened as pull requests by the Orchestrator and merged by humans. The Nightly run reports orphaned baselines (an approved baseline whose id no longer exists at the current commit and has no rename) as findings and never aborts over them.

Baseline manifests. The Central Store is the live system of record for baseline state. At RC sign-off the sign-off bot exports the approved set for the lineage to `baselines/<lineage>/<build_id>/manifest.json` and commits it, so the released configuration and its approved images are named by one git commit, which the next release's RC run records (gap G32).

### 8.6 Retention and backup

Retention is per artifact class and never deletes a pinned object. The sweep runs nightly after the backup on the control host, sets `deleted_at` before unlinking, and refuses to remove anything referenced by a baseline row or by a finding whose triage state is not closed.

| Class | Keep |
|---|---|
| Central Store rows other than step_events | indefinitely |
| step_events rows | 90 days; indefinitely for runs with an open finding, any `blocked_by_gateway` row, an incident or an `aborted_safety` outcome |
| Run Store, ledgers and objects on the rig | until the shard is `imported` plus 7 days, and in any case until the next snapshot revert; a shard that is `import_failed` or `lost` is kept on the rig until a human releases it |
| Ledgers and journals in `runs\<run_id>\shards\` | life of the run's artifact set |
| Baseline images, every state | never deleted |
| Artifacts referenced by an open, confirmed or fixed-pending-verify finding | until the finding closes plus 180 days |
| Full checkpoint sets of the last 3 `complete` merge runs on main and the last 2 RC runs per release | until superseded |
| PR run artifacts | 14 days after the run, or 7 days after the PR merges or closes, whichever is earlier |
| Merge run artifacts not pinned above | 14 days |
| Nightly run artifacts (A/A pairs, fire drill video, mutants) | 7 days; mutants regenerate deterministically from the seed |
| Calibration run captures | until the next calibration completes plus 30 days |
| Agent and Explorer frames, run video | 14 days unless referenced by a finding |
| Crash artifacts and log slices | 180 days, pinned while a finding references them |
| Reviewer request payloads | 30 days, or the life of the eval item when promoted into the eval set |
| Quarantined objects | until security clears them in writing |

Backup. At 02:00 America/New_York a job on the control host runs `VACUUM INTO` for a consistent snapshot while the service runs, exports decisions, baselines, masks, flake statistics, incidents and quarantine records as JSONL, and mirrors the snapshot, the exports, all of `baselines\` and every pinned object under `runs\` to the backup location with robocopy. Snapshots are kept 7 daily and 8 weekly. On success it writes `last_backup_at` to system state; on any failure it writes `last_backup_error` and raises the 9.10 Store health alert (P2, posted at 06:00 under the after-hours rule of 11.6), and a `last_backup_at` older than 36 hours raises the same alert from the Nightly run's state check as a second line of defence. The retention sweep is skipped on any night whose backup failed, and run health prints "retention skipped: backup failed". Weekly, `PRAGMA integrity_check` runs on the snapshot and records `last_integrity_check_at`; a failure on the snapshot is a service stop and restore (8.9), not a warning.

Artifact audit. Weekly, the control host re-hashes every pinned object and a 5 percent sample of the rest, writes `audit_state` and `last_audit_at`, and opens an `artifact_missing` finding for any object that is missing or whose hash no longer matches; a pinned object that fails is restored from the backup mirror and the restore is logged.

Restore drill, quarterly, owned by the system owner: restore the latest snapshot and `baselines\` to a scratch host, start the report UI against it, re-diff ten checkpoints of one RC run against the restored baselines, and confirm the outcomes match the original rows. The date goes into `last_restore_drill_at`; older than 100 days is a red row in Run health.

Storage preflight. The `provisioned` gate requires free space on the rig above the larger of 20 GB (R7 in 12.7) and twice the projected shard size, and on the control host above the larger of 100 GB and twice the projected run size (scope count times two sides times the mean capture size from the last calibration run); the failure outcome is in 8.9. Schema migrations run only after a successful `VACUUM INTO` of the pre-migration file.

### 8.7 Report UI data access

The report UI is the FastAPI application of 5.13 Reporter and Integrations (technology in 5.18 Technology choices), on the control host behind SSO; page contents are defined in 9.5 Report UI pages.

Reads open the Central Store with `mode=ro` and `PRAGMA query_only = 1` from a small pool, one short transaction per request. Pages follow the indexes in 8.3: run page (outcomes by run joined to checkpoints and findings, ordered by tier then outcome, with the shard list and import state), checkpoint history, finding page (finding, review and the live decision lookup from 8.3, so the page shows what a new diff would inherit), coverage matrix (coverage cells by run; for a PR run, the matrix from the run's summary JSON), trends (flake stats, canary results by night and defect class, calibration floors by fingerprint, egress by day, mask area by commit), safety (post-run proofs, incidents, blocked logins). Lists paginate at 200 rows. The run page reads the run's summary JSON first and expands to rows on demand; the Reporter renders the PR comment from that summary, written when the last shard imports, which keeps it inside the 45 minute PR run budget.

Artifacts are served at `/a/<sha256>` with the media type from the `artifacts` table and immutable cache headers. A hash with `deleted_at` set returns a page saying what the object was and when retention removed it, never a broken image; a hash with `audit_state` other than `ok`, or a hash an outcome names that has no `artifacts` row, returns a page saying the evidence is missing and names the finding that records it. PR comments and Slack messages link to these URLs; images are never uploaded to the PR host, Jira or Slack, so only text leaves for those destinations, logged as such in the egress log.

Writes (confirm bug, mark intended with ticket, mark noise, request mask, approve or reject a baseline, revoke a decision, quarantine or un-quarantine, Explorer disposition, clear an unproven proof, close an incident, override a check) post to the Reporter service's local API with the SSO identity of the person acting. The service validates against the constraints in 8.3, writes through the single writer, appends to the day's decisions ledger and returns the row id. `decided_by`, `approved_by`, `quarantined_by`, `retired_by`, `verified_by`, `closed_by` and `check_override_by` always hold a person; service accounts are rejected by the API and by the CHECK constraints. Request mask, quarantine and un-quarantine write no table row of their own; they open the pull requests of 8.5, and the mirror tables follow the merged commit. Metrics jobs (9.11 Metrics dashboard and kill criteria) read the same path and write results into the Nightly run's summary JSON through the writer.

### 8.8 Growth estimates

Planning figures. Checkpoint counts and run frequency come from 11.1 Planning assumptions; the byte sizes below are this section's and are measured in Phase 0: the calibration run records the real mean capture size, and the storage preflight uses that figure, not this table.

| Id | Assumption | Value |
|---|---|---|
| SA-01 | Mean 1920x1080 PNG capture of thinkorswim at 100 percent DPI | 1.5 MB (expected 0.8 to 2.5) |
| SA-02 | Sidecars per capture (OCR boxes, bounds, redaction map) | 0.1 MB |
| SA-03 | Diff products when a checkpoint exceeds its floor (heatmap, two crops, diff mask) | 0.8 MB on 5 percent of checkpoints in a typical merge run, 20 percent on a large UI change |
| SA-04 | Checkpoints per run, a ceiling over 11.1 and 11.2 (PA-13 gives a PR census of about 80 checkpoints, the smoke subset being capped at 40 surfaces by 2.11; the 250 here adds flows and Ladder S sweeps with margin) | PR 250; merge 1,380 (census 900 per 2.4 and PA-02, flows, Ladder S sweeps and splitters 225); RC 2,900 (census 900, tier B census 600, all flows, Ladder F sweeps, soak) |
| SA-05 | Frequency, from 11.1 PA-10, taken as a ceiling | 10 PR runs and 4 merge runs per business day; 1 Nightly run per day; 3 RC runs and 1 Calibration run per month |
| SA-06 | Explorer 1,500 frames at 0.15 MB; run video 0.5 GB per side per 8 hours | as listed |
| SA-07 | Step events 12 rows per checkpoint per side at 350 bytes with indexes; Nightly A/A scope of 10.6 about 550 checkpoints captured twice (11.2) | as listed |

| Run type | Checkpoints | Captures and sidecars | Diff products | Other | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR run | 250 | 250 x 2 x 1.6 MB = 0.8 GB | 0.1 GB | ring buffer video 0.05 GB | 0.95 GB |
| Merge run | 1,380 | 1,380 x 2 x 1.6 MB = 4.4 GB | 0.1 GB | 0.05 GB | about 4.5 GB |
| RC run | 2,900 | 2,900 x 2 x 1.6 MB = 9.3 GB | 0.5 GB | Explorer 0.2 GB, video 1 GB | about 11 GB |
| Nightly run | 550 A/A pairs plus 750 mutants | 1,100 x 1.6 MB = 1.8 GB | 750 x 1.5 MB = 1.1 GB of mutant images | fire drill video 0.1 GB | about 3 GB |
| Calibration run | 1,380 x 6 passes | 8,280 x 1.6 MB = 13 GB | 0 | 0 | about 13 GB |

Raw growth per business day: 10 x 0.95 + 4 x 4.5 + 3 = about 31 GB, about 0.7 TB per month before retention. Steady state under 8.6 (14 calendar days taken as 10 business days): PR runs 95 GB, merge runs 180 GB, pinned merge sets 14 GB, RC runs 35 GB, nightly 21 GB, calibration 26 GB, artifacts pinned by findings 1 GB, about 370 GB hot. Baselines only grow: an approved set is 2,900 x 1.6 MB = 4.6 GB, and with candidate and retired images kept a lineage adds about 14 GB per release, 170 GB per year at twelve releases. The control host gets a 1 TB local NVMe volume, which holds the hot set and the first two years of baselines with headroom, an alarm at 70 percent and the preflight threshold above; if PA-10 doubles, the volume is 2 TB. The backup location gets 2 TB because it keeps baselines and pinned objects forever, 15 database snapshots and the exports. Each rig needs 40 GB free for the largest shard with its video: an RC shard of about 620 checkpoints is about 2.5 GB of captures plus 1 GB of video, so the R7 floor of 20 GB holds a margin for retries and the 7 day post-import retention. These figures are the ceiling 11.4 cites; the storage preflight uses the measured mean capture size, never this table.

Database. About 9,100 outcome rows per business day (10 x 250 + 4 x 1,380 + 1,100), under 4 MB per day with indexes, under 1 GB per year; step_events about 220,000 rows and 75 MB per day, held to about 7 GB by the 90 day retention; reviews about 700 per day at 3 KB; coverage cells about 15,000 rows per day on merge, RC and Nightly runs, 0.5 GB per year; canary results, egress and shard rows are small. The Central Store reaches about 7 GB in year one and grows about 2 GB per year after, which SQLite handles on local NVMe because every query path in 8.7 is an index lookup. A Run Store holds one shard and stays under 100 MB. SHA-256 of a 1.5 MB capture costs a few milliseconds, on the rig and again on the control host.

### 8.9 Store failure modes

Every store failure has an outcome in the closed taxonomy and a place where a human sees it. A store failure never produces a diff, never leaves a checkpoint without a row, and never lets a run report `complete` (the trigger in 8.3).

| Failure | Detection | Outcome | Who sees it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Database or artifact root on a share, UNC or mapped path | startup preflight (H7) | process refuses to start; run `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H7)` if during preflight; dead-man alert at the next deadline otherwise | on-call channel |
| Free space below threshold on the rig or the control host | storage preflight at `provisioned` | `env_error (gate: preflight.R7)` on every checkpoint in scope; run `complete_with_env_errors`; the disk alarm of 9.10 | on-call channel, Run health |
| Rig disk full during a run | the Watchdog's free-space check (in its sampling loop, read by the Orchestrator at every flow boundary) below 2 GB, including the immediate check an `ENOSPC` on any write requests (10.2) | run `aborted_harness (reason: disk_full)`; the checkpoint in progress `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)` when its own write failed with `ENOSPC` (8.4), otherwise `disk_full`, and every remaining checkpoint `harness_error (reason: disk_full)`, the run's abort reason; a heartbeat write that fails with `ENOSPC` is this case, not `heartbeat_unwritable`; run re-queued once | on-call channel, Run health |
| Single artifact write or read-back verification fails on the rig (`ENOSPC` or any other error) | Capture write path | retried once; then checkpoint `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)`; the run cannot be `complete` and ends `aborted_harness (reason: artifact_persist_failed)` at teardown, unless the free-space check ends it first as `disk_full` | Run health, on-call channel |
| Run Store writer cannot commit (locked, busy timeout and 3 retries, I/O error, `SQLITE_FULL`) | writer thread | shard `aborted_harness (reason: store_write_failed)`; remaining checkpoints `harness_error (reason: store_write_failed)`, the run's abort reason; the ledger already holds the rows for replay | on-call channel, Run health |
| Central Store writer cannot commit | Reporter service writer | the shard stays `shipping` and the import retries with backoff; past the dead-man deadline the run row is `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)`; rows are intact on the rig | on-call channel |
| Integrity check fails at service start or on the weekly snapshot | startup, weekly job | service stops; operator restores the last good snapshot and replays later ledgers and the decisions ledger; every run since the snapshot is re-imported from the rigs' retained shard directories | on-call channel, system owner |
| Shipped shard rows disagree with the ledger, or a replayed row differs from a stored row with the same natural key | import | shard `import_failed`, run `aborted_harness (reason: import_conflict)`; nothing imported; the rig keeps its copy | on-call channel, system owner |
| Upload hash mismatch | import | re-requested up to 3 times; then shard `import_failed` with `upload_hash_mismatch`, run `aborted_harness (reason: artifact_persist_failed)` | on-call channel, Run health |
| Artifact without a redaction version | rig writer or import | refused; the checkpoint `harness_error (reason: redaction_version_missing)`; egress log row with status refused if a send was attempted | Run health, security digest |
| Secret found by the post-run plaintext scan | teardown scan | objects quarantined, run `aborted_harness (reason: secret_leaked)`, report withheld, credential rotated | security contact, on-call channel |
| Shard lost (rig unreachable past the deadline) | Rig Manager heartbeat, dead-man timer | shard `lost`; run `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)` with "rig unreachable, run data intact on rig"; imported when the rig returns, after which the run is re-evaluated | on-call channel |
| Artifact named by an outcome missing or corrupt after import | weekly artifact audit, or a report page request | `artifact_missing` finding, tier of the checkpoint; the report shows the hash with a missing marker; pinned objects restored from backup | triage rotation, Run health |
| Backup job fails, or `last_backup_at` older than 36 hours | backup job, Nightly state check | the 9.10 Store health alert (P2, posted at 06:00 per 11.6); red row in Run health; the retention sweep skipped that night | on-call channel, system owner |
| Restore drill older than 100 days | Nightly state check | red row in Run health | system owner |
| Retention sweep would remove a pinned or referenced object | sweep | object kept; count reported | Run health |
| Schema migration fails | migration step | service stops with the pre-migration snapshot intact | on-call channel |
| Decision, baseline or incident write rejected by a constraint | Reporter service API | request refused with the constraint name; nothing written; the UI shows the reason | the acting person; weekly summary |

## 9. Reporting, triage and integrations

The Reporter turns the rows written by the Orchestrator, Diff Engine, Invariant Checker, Oracle and Reviewer (`runs`, `checkpoints`, `outcomes`, `findings`, `decisions`, `baselines`, `masks`, `step_events`, `flake_stats`, `canary_results`, `egress_log`; see 8.3 Schema) into the PR comment and commit status, the merge and RC reports, the report UI, Jira tickets, Slack posts, pages and the metrics dashboard. It never computes an outcome, never changes one, and never decides anything a human is supposed to decide; every human action it offers is written as a decision record that the next run inherits.

### 9.1 Rules for every report

- Every checkpoint shows its outcome name from the closed taxonomy (1.10 Outcome taxonomy (authoritative)) and nothing else. `not_run` always carries its reason and is never rendered as passed or green. When several results apply, the outcome follows the precedence order in 1.10 (`invariant_violation` and `assertion_failed` above `collateral`); the lower results stay on the finding as evidence and are shown under it.
- Synthetic items (canary mutants, `synthetic = 1`) appear only on the canary panel, never in finding lists, counts or metrics. Crops are shown at 1:1 (image width equals crop pixel width, `image-rendering: pixelated`); the checkpoint page adds flicker at 2 Hz and a heatmap overlay.
- Screen text and model text are data. Reviewer descriptions, OCR strings, popup titles, manifest summaries and ticket titles are HTML-escaped and rendered as plain text or code spans, never as markdown, links or images. The only links in a comment or post are report UI URLs the Reporter composes itself. A manifest summary containing markdown image syntax therefore prints literally; nothing on screen or in a model response can inject a link, an image or a heading into a PR comment (5.13 Reporter and Integrations).
- One PR comment per PR, identified by a hidden marker (`<!-- sentinel:pr:{pr} -->`), created by the first run and edited in place by later runs, older runs in a collapsed history table. If the marker comment is missing (deleted, or lost by the PR host) the Reporter creates a new one and says so in Run health. Images are links to the report UI's `/a/<sha256>` artifact URLs behind SSO (8.7 Report UI data access); no image is uploaded to the PR host, Slack or Jira, so only text leaves, logged in `egress_log` with purpose `pr_comment`, `jira` or `slack`. Section labels in the comment are bold lines, not markdown headings, so they render at comment scale and do not pollute the assembled table of contents.
- Size. GitHub caps a comment at 65,536 characters. The Reporter renders, measures and shrinks in this order until it fits: inline Unexpected and Intended items 10, then 5, then 3; the Suppressed table collapses to a count and a link; the run history collapses to a link. The header, result line, check line, abort block, coverage table and Safety row are never dropped. Assumption to verify in Phase 0: the PR host is GitHub Enterprise; if Bitbucket, confirm that tables and `<details>` render, else the Reporter emits a flat-list variant with the same fields, and the commit status states map to Bitbucket build statuses (`error` and `failure` both to FAILED, the description carrying the distinction).
- A one-click action in the comment is a link into the report UI with finding and action pre-selected; after SSO one click completes it, plus a ticket key or reason where required. In the UI the same actions are buttons. Both post to the Reporter service API (8.7 Report UI data access; the Reporter service is the Central Store's only writer, 5.13, 8.2) with the SSO identity and write the same decision record (9.6, 9.7); if the Reporter service is down the UI shows a read-only banner and refuses the action rather than queueing it, so nobody believes a decision was made that was not. The Orchestrator writes only the Run Store of its shard on the rig and the Watchdog writes only its JSONL journal; neither serves this API.
- Suppressed findings are always listed, collapsed, under "suppressed by decision #id", so humans can audit what is not shown. A suppressed finding keeps its full evidence on the checkpoint page.
- Delivery never fails silently. Every outbound post (PR comment, commit status, Jira create or comment, Slack post, page) is an outbox job written through the single writer before the send is attempted (the `outbox` table of 8.3 Schema: job id, run id, kind, destination, payload hash, attempts, next attempt, last error, state `queued`, `sent`, `failed` or `abandoned`). The Reporter retries a failing job at 1, 2, 5, 15 and 60 minutes, then hourly until 24 hours; each attempt is an `egress_log` row with status `sent` or `failed`. A job still failing after 15 minutes raises the integration outage alert (9.10) on every other channel; after 24 hours it is `abandoned`, listed in the daily digest and on the run page until a human closes it. The report UI page is rendered first and locally, so a report exists even when every integration is down. A PR comment not posted by the PR run's budget deadline is posted late with a `report_late` note in Run health (5.13).

### 9.2 PR comment template

The comment is rendered from the run's summary JSON at teardown (8.7) and posted when the run reaches `reported`; the Reporter host posts it on a dead-man timeout when the run never reports. Braces are fields. Unexpected and Intended list at most 10 items inline, the rest counted and linked.

What the comment shows for each run state ("all" means the Unexpected, Intended, Suppressed, Coverage and Run health blocks):

| Run state | Result line | Blocks | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `complete`, `review_state = reviewed` | `complete` | all | Normal. |
| `complete`, `review_state = unreviewed` or `partial` | `complete (unreviewed: {n} items pending review)` | all; each pending item is listed in Unexpected as `needs_human (review_state: pending)` with "Reviewer: pending since {time}, batch {id}" in place of a description, and all three actions available | Edited in place as verdicts land (10.7 Degraded modes). A pending tier-1 item counts as undecided for the check. |
| `complete_with_env_errors` | `complete_with_env_errors` | all, plus an Environment errors line in Run health (gate names, shards, screenshot links) and the not-compared count per tier in Coverage; "shard re-run queued" when the budget allows | When the cause is an UNPROVEN post-run proof (6.6 Kill switch, recovery and post-run proof), the Safety row prints the proof verdict and reason and "next run on login {alias} blocked until a human verifies the account". A run whose login never authenticated (vault down, authentication failed) and was never issued a gateway token prints `PROVEN: no session established`, read from the gateway log, and blocks nothing. After `session_kicked` the proof waits `session_release_wait` and logs in fresh; if the login is still unavailable after one retry the verdict is `UNPROVEN: session_unavailable`, the login is blocked and the human verification line is printed (6.6). |
| `aborted_budget` | `aborted_budget (reason: {reason})` | all, with what ran; line "Scope not finished: {n} checkpoints not_run (budget), {n} of them tier 1". For `aborted_budget (reason: dollar_cap)` the line adds "per-run model spend ceiling reached ({cost} of {cap}, 11.4 Cost model)". For `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)` (11.2 Cadence and time budgets per run type) nothing ran: the abort block alone, with the text "Sentinel did not run: pool saturated, {n} runs ahead; push again or re-run the build job" | Findings are triaged as usual (1.10). Explorer budget exhaustion never aborts a run; it ends the Explorer session only (2.9 Explorer). Check `error` with "Sentinel did not run" for `pool_saturated`. |
| `aborted_safety` | `aborted_safety (reason: {reason})` | Intended and Unexpected replaced by the abort block: trigger (attestation, paper mode, kill switch, gateway block, undeclared Working or Filled row, `unexpected_working_order`), gate, last screenshot link, post-run proof verdict, incident id, "no run starts on rig {rig} until the incident closes" | Findings recorded before the abort stay on the run page, collapsed. Check `error`. |
| `aborted_harness` | `aborted_harness (reason: {reason})` | abort block: reason (`base_build_missing`, `config_invalid` with rule ids, `preflight.<item>` for a failed group H item of 12.7, `store_write_failed`, `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `hook_lost`, `watchdog_dead`, `dead_man`, the rest of 1.10's list), last gate reached, screenshot if any, "re-queued once: {run id, or 'already re-queued'}" | For `dead_man` the Reporter host writes the comment: "Sentinel did not report: no run-completed event by {deadline}; last heartbeat {time}". For a secret leak (6.9 Credentials and secret steps, 8.9 Store failure modes) the comment says only "report withheld; security contact notified". Check `error`. |

Banners. When `detector_state` in `system_state` is `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded` or `generation_failed` (set from the last Nightly run's canary result states, 10.3 Canary Service and the mutant catalog; the Nightly run itself stays `complete`), or a `harness_error (reason: canary_path_divergence)` was recorded, the banner from 10.3 is the first line of the comment and stays until a Nightly run passes green. When the Reviewer is disabled by a failed eval gate (10.4 Eval set and Reviewer change control), the line "Reviewer disabled since {date}: eval gate {name} failed; {n} items await a human" follows it. When the run-level `global_rendering_shift` finding fired (3.7 Three-granularity diff: algorithms and parameters), the header line "Global rendering shift: {n} checkpoints collapsed into one `needs_human (reason: global_shift)` cluster; no reviewer calls made" follows. When no manifest is loaded, the Intended block opens with one of the two lines of 4.3 Change manifest: "No manifest entry and the PR touches UI code (`manifest_missing`): every diff is reported as collateral until you add one", or "No manifest and no UI code touched: diffs are `needs_human (reason: no_manifest)`".

Unexpected ranking: tier ascending; then kind order: `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with its `app_crash` finding, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` (invariant and assertion findings of checkpoints whose comparison ended `not_run (reason: base_step_failed)` are listed here too, because the candidate capture was still checked, 3.1 Build pair rules), `collateral` together with `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` (an above-zero diff on an undeclared surface with no calibrated floor, ranked with collateral within the tier, 3.11 Classification decision table), `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` (a declared surface whose change the Reviewer confidently said does not match the entry, directly after collateral within the tier, 3.11), `landmark_missing` (candidate side only), `unregistered_surface`, other `needs_human` (pending review included; `rescued_capture` items never inherit a decision), `needs_baseline` on an undeclared surface, step `failed` (candidate side only), `passed_via_agent_fallback` (scripted locator broke, `locator_failure` finding), `dependency_map_gap`, `manifest_missing`, `unknown_popup`; then reviewer confidence descending; then novelty (signature unseen in 30 days first). Clusters (9.7) are one item with a member count.

The commit status. The context `sentinel/pr-run` is posted on the candidate commit with the run page as target URL. It has two modes, set in configuration and recorded with the date of every change:

- Informational (Phase 1, and the default): the state is computed by the rules below, but the context is not in the branch protection's required list, so it never blocks a merge; the description ends "(informational)". This is the mode 1.6 Run types gives for Phase 1.
- Blocking: the system owner adds the context to branch protection on main once the Phase 2 false-positive target holds, which means a rolling 30-day false-positive rate under 20 percent for two consecutive release cycles (1.5 Success criteria and kill criteria, pilot exit). The switch is announced in the release channel. The system owner reverts to informational, with the same announcement, when the rolling 30-day false-positive rate is above 35 percent for 10 business days or the kill criterion fires.

States, identical in both modes:

| State | When | Description text |
|---|---|---|
| `pending` | Run queued or running; set from the run row at T+0:00 | "Sentinel run started, base = {base_build}" |
| `failure` | Any tier-1 Unexpected item without a decision: `collateral`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` (including `app_alive`), `needs_human` (review pending included), `landmark_missing` on the candidate side only, step `failed` on the candidate side only | "{n} tier-1 findings have no decision" |
| `error` | `aborted_safety`; `aborted_harness` (including `dead_man`); `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)`; report withheld; no comment posted by budget plus 15 minutes | "aborted_safety: incident {id}", "Sentinel did not run" (pool saturated), or "Sentinel did not report" |
| `success` | Otherwise | "{n} unexpected ({n} tier 2 and 3 open); {n} tier-1 surfaces not compared ({outcomes}): see the merge run" |

Tier 2 and 3 items never fail the check. `unregistered_surface`, `dependency_map_gap`, `unknown_popup`, `manifest_missing` and harness-side findings never fail it, since they belong to the registry owner or the system owner, not to the PR. Tier-1 surfaces that were not compared (`env_error`, `not_settled`, `not_comparable`, `landmark_missing` on both sides, `not_run` for budget) do not fail it either: they are named in the description and the merge run compares them within hours; that merge run blocks the RC gate when tier-1 coverage is below 100 percent (1.5). The status is re-posted within one minute of any decision. Only the system owner may override it: forced `success` for one run, reason required, recorded in the run row and printed in Run health and the comment.

### 9.3 Filled sample: Flexible Grid change breaks the Active Trader ladder

This is the worked example of 1.11, as the developer sees it at T+0:41 (11:12 ET). PR 4812 shrinks the Flexible Grid cell header from 28 to 22 px and gives hosted content the full cell height; its manifest entry `tos-48120-1` (ticket TOS-48120) declares only the chart cell. It is a PR run, so the one tier-1 surface among the four Flexible Grid surfaces, the Active Trader cell, is swept with Ladder S (2.5.2 The ladders: widths {320, 480, 640, 960} by heights {360, 480, 720}, 12 steps, descending order), and all four Flexible Grid surfaces are compared by the scoped census in their registry workspaces, five census checkpoints in all: the chart cell in the tier A workspaces of the active trader and swing trader personas, and the Active Trader, Level II and Time and Sales cells in the active trader one (2.5.3 Which gadgets get the sweep). The base is the merge-base main build of 07:55, whose merge run completed at 09:39, so every base capture is reused under the same fingerprint and fixture epoch. The overlap reproduces at heights 300 to 420, so under Ladder S it fires at height 360 at every width. Checkpoint ids follow the grammar `<kind>/<surface-id>/<qualifier>`. The commit status is in informational mode (Phase 1). Artifact hashes are shortened.

Expected triage. The developer, who is the PR author, clicks Confirm bug on item 1; any role may confirm a bug, so the decision row is written at once with verdict `confirmed_bug`, the outbox files TOS-48391 with both crops, the overlay, primitive, entry, PR and failing range, and the ticket key lands on the decision and the finding. On items 2 and 3 the developer clicks Mark intended with ticket TOS-48120, because the 6 px shift is the declared header change on a surface the entry did not declare. Both are tier 1, so each click is a proposal: it is recorded on the finding, the triage rotation sees it in the queue with a 4-business-hour clock, confirms it, and the decision rows are written with the rotation member as `decided_by` and "proposed by {developer}" in the reason; the manifest amendment PR declares `charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell` on tos-48120-1. Item 4 is tier 2 and goes the same way with the same ticket; the amendment also adds the Level II and Time and Sales cells, and the evidence comment lands on TOS-48120. The check stays `failure` in informational mode until items 1 to 3 have decisions, which they now do; it turns `success` within a minute. After the ladder fix is pushed, the next run shows no invariant at the 4 height-360 steps; those 4 and the other 8 steps are `intended` under the amended manifest (the 8 steps and the census checkpoint inherit the item-2 and item-3 decisions, 3.11 row 14; the 4 height-360 steps are confirmed by the Reviewer against the amended entry, row 20), and the item-1 `invariant_violation` signature is absent. When TOS-48391 reaches Done with a fixVersion the Jira poller records `fixed_in_build` on dec-000517, the next run asserts the signature is gone, and the finding closes.

### 9.4 Merge and RC report structure

The merge report is a report UI page plus a Slack digest to the triage rotation listing only new, unsuppressed Unexpected findings (9.9). Its manifest is the union of the manifests of the PRs merged between the two main builds; when merges coalesced (11.2 Cadence and time budgets per run type) the header names the range of main builds and PRs covered. Sections in order:

1. Header: build pair, fingerprint match, run outcome, duration against the 3 hour budget, shards, reviewer model id and prompt hash, cost, metrics header (9.11), detector banner if any.
2. Unexpected: PR comment item format, full list, ranked as in 9.2. A finding a PR run had in scope but did not report is labelled "missed in PR run", recorded as finding `missed_in_pr_run`, and opens a harness task; one outside PR scope on a surface consuming a primitive the PR touched emits `dependency_map_gap`. A finding on a surface that the candidate's dependency index reaches from a class changed by a merged PR, whose PR run had the surface `not_run (reason: scope)`, is labelled "missed by static impact", recorded as finding `missed_in_pr_run` with `detail: static_impact`, and opens a harness task for the system owner.
3. Intended: per merged PR, declared surfaces with confirmed diffs; then manifest reconciliation: entries verified visible, entries with a covering checkpoint but no visible change (`intended_change_not_observed`, a question to the PR author and feature owner, not a bug), entries with no covering checkpoint (flow-authoring task). Manifest coverage prints as entries verified over entries.
4. Known bugs: findings inheriting an open `confirm_bug` decision, with ticket status and age; contested and conflicting decisions (9.7) listed here with both deciders.
5. Suppressed by decision (full table), then census, invariants and flows: counts per outcome per tier, with links.
6. Coverage matrix: full surface x persona x entitlement matrix (9.5) from `coverage_cells`, and the "Not detectable by design" table of 2.13 What this model cannot detect and how it is labeled.
7. Run health: as in the PR comment plus popup catalog hits, `unknown_popup` findings, retries, fallbacks clustered by anchor template, p50 and p95 step time, egress log count, disk free, orphaned baselines, mask budget status, outbox state.
8. Safety proof: the A1 to A11 attestation results with evidence hashes (12.6 Run-start attestation checklist), paper-mode assertions with their count, end-of-run Cancel All result, Working and Filled diff against the start snapshot, positions flat, the proof verdict and reason block of 6.6 Kill switch, recovery and post-run proof, and the previous night's fire drill and safety canary results: pass, `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)` with the quarantined flows, or `aborted_safety (reason: drill_order_placed)` with the blocked login (6.5 Nightly fire drill and safety canaries).
9. Baseline candidates: every `intended` capture of a merged PR and every `needs_baseline` checkpoint, queued for approval. This is the only place baseline candidates are created from product runs (9.8).

The RC report adds: comparison against the lineage baseline (9.8); Intended grouped by Jira epic and reconciled against the release's ticket export (4.3 Change manifest, `source: ticket_export`); size sweep results per gadget and Ladder F step; soak summary per 10.11 Soak: long sessions, resource budgets and the freeze detector (both builds' curves per metric with the budget line, restarts, `new_log_signature` findings, the memory ceiling reached and the 24 cycle outcomes); Explorer findings, shown only when the single replay reproduced them, each carrying the replayed flow's own outcome (`invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed`, else `needs_baseline` with the trace attached, never `needs_human`; 2.9 Explorer), the rest under "Explorer: not reproduced", or the single line "Explorer: not run, model endpoint unavailable" when the session was `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` (10.7); tier B workspace migration results; baseline approval status; an escape-tracking seed listing every tier-1 surface not compared in this RC; the release gate checklist (the G-N conditions of 10.9 Release-day timeline); and a sign-off block recording system owner and release manager, time, RC build, accepted open findings with tickets and the approved baseline set that becomes the next lineage baseline, N business days before GA (N is PA-14 in 11.1 Planning assumptions: 3 business days by default, per train in `policy/release_gate.yaml`). The report is frozen at sign-off; later decisions create a new version and the block names the version signed. An RC run superseded by a newer RC build (`aborted_budget (reason: superseded)`, 10.9, 11.2) still publishes its partial report, labelled "superseded by {build}" in the header, to the release manager and the release channel; it cannot be signed, and its decisions are inherited by the new RC run (9.7).

### 9.5 Report UI pages

The report UI is the FastAPI application of 5.13 Reporter and Integrations, on the controller host behind SSO. It reads SQLite through read-only WAL connections and writes only through the Reporter service API (8.7 Report UI data access), the Central Store's single writer. Every page shows the run's provenance: harness commit, config commit, VM image id, build pair, model ids, prompt hash.

| Page | Shows | Actions |
|---|---|---|
| Run list and run detail | List: runs by type with outcome, build pair, counts per outcome, duration, cost, open items by tier, outbox state. Detail: the sections of 9.4, or the PR comment content for PR runs; an Alerts panel with every alert raised for the run and its acknowledgement | Compare two runs, re-run reviewer on pending items, all finding actions, refresh the PR comment, close an abandoned outbox job |
| Checkpoint detail | Base and candidate at 1:1, flicker, heatmap, connected-component boxes, region overlay (freeze, rule, mask, diff), landmark match score, outcome with the lower results as evidence, reviewer inputs and output, Oracle values with tolerances, invariant results with bounds source (JAB or OCR), step events, log slice, settle timing, re-run results, flake score, history over 30 runs, the live decision lookup (what a new diff here would inherit) | Finding actions; request targeted re-run; quarantine or un-quarantine; open region in the Region Registry |
| Triage queue | Every finding without a decision, ranked as in 9.2, with SLA clock, assignee and pending proposals awaiting a second person | Finding actions, assign, confirm or decline a proposal, apply to a whole cluster |
| Decisions | Search by signature, checkpoint, ticket or decider; active, expired, superseded, reopened, revoked and contested decisions; conflicts; decisions without tickets; expiring in 7 days; suspect decisions (two reopenings) | Supersede, revoke, re-confirm an expiring noise signature |
| Baseline approval queue | Candidates per checkpoint or cluster from merge runs (9.8), base and candidate at 1:1, nearest existing baseline by perceptual hash for `needs_baseline` items, "epoch changed" flags | approve_baseline, reject_baseline, retire checkpoint |
| Coverage matrix | Surface x persona x entitlement, each cell covered / `not_run` (reason) / not registered, per run and per release, tier filter, red rows for "in manifest, no covering checkpoint" | Open a flow-authoring task for a cell |
| Canary panel | Nightly results per mutant and class, detector state, what absorbed each miss | Open the mask, decision or threshold named |
| Metrics | The dashboard of 9.11 | Change window, export CSV |

### 9.6 One-click actions and who may perform them

Actions are the `decision` enum of 4.14 Decision record (confirm_bug, mark_intended, request_mask, noise_signature, agent_mistake, expected_behavior, approve_baseline, reject_baseline, fixed_in_build). What the store keeps is the verdict enum of 8.3 (confirmed_bug, intended, noise); the decision row carries both the action and the verdict. Each action is idempotent per finding and action and is logged with actor, role, time, finding and run; the actor is always a human login (L-DEC-01 in 4.14). Roles are defined in 9.12. The Reviewer performs none of these; it may only pre-fill the baseline queue and rank the triage queue.

Action to verdict to effect on later runs:

| Action | Verdict stored | Finding `triage_state` (8.3) | A later matching diff (9.7) | Ends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| confirm_bug | confirmed_bug | confirmed_bug | Keeps its computed outcome; filed under the ticket, listed under Known bugs, no new alert | fixed_in_build |
| mark_intended on `collateral`, `needs_human` or `intended` | intended (ticket required) | intended | Outcome `intended` with the decision id; listed under Suppressed | Baseline approved for the release, or the ticket leaves every manifest in scope |
| mark_intended on `invariant_violation` or `assertion_failed` (waiver) | intended (ticket required, expiry at most 30 days) | intended | Outcome unchanged; finding suppressed as waived | Expiry, no silent renewal |
| request_mask | noise, inert until `mask_ref` is set | open until the mask PR merges, then noise | Nothing until the mask merges; afterwards the region is type mask at the new config commit, so no diff exists; the decision row is the audit link L-MSK-01 requires | Mask expiry (default 30 days) |
| noise_signature | noise | noise | Outcome `noise` with the decision id; listed under Suppressed | 30 days unless re-confirmed |
| agent_mistake | noise | agent_mistake | An Explorer finding with the same signature is held, not reported; its candidate flow is discarded | Revoked, or signature absent 30 days |
| expected_behavior | noise | expected_behavior | Held as above; the candidate flow is kept and may be promoted with an assertion that encodes the expected behavior | Same |
| approve_baseline | intended (ticket) plus the `baselines` row `approved` | closed for the `needs_baseline` finding | RC runs on the lineage compare against the image; the Canary Service mutates it; `needs_baseline` clears for the checkpoint | Superseded or retired |
| reject_baseline | confirmed_bug when a ticket is given (the candidate shows a defect), else noise (not representative; a new candidate comes from the next merge run); the `baselines` row `retired` | confirmed_bug, or open | `needs_baseline` persists until a new candidate is approved; with a ticket the finding is a Known bug | New candidate approved |
| fixed_in_build | confirmed_bug (a new row that supersedes the confirm_bug row, `fixed_in_build` set) | fixed_pending_verify, then closed | On or after that build the signature must be absent. Absent for one run: finding closed. Present: decision status reopened, finding returns to Unexpected, ticket reopened (9.9) | Finding closed |

Who may perform each action, what it writes and what the next run does:

| Action | Who may perform | Writes | Next run |
|---|---|---|---|
| Confirm bug | Any role in 9.12, including the PR author | Decision row (action confirm_bug, verdict confirmed_bug, signature, run, build, reason); finding `confirmed_bug`; outbox job: Jira Bug or link to an open ticket (9.9); ticket key on decision and finding when it lands | Matching diffs keep their outcome, appear under Known bugs with ticket and age, no alert; the PR check stays `failure` only while a tier-1 item has no decision, so confirming clears it |
| Mark intended with ticket | Tier 3: any role, the PR author alone. Tier 1 and 2: the PR author proposes; the row is written when the triage rotation or the tier's flow owner confirms (two-person rule below). Other roles alone | Decision row (action mark_intended, verdict intended, ticket, reason naming the proposer); finding `intended`; outbox jobs: manifest amendment PR if the surface was undeclared, evidence comment on the ticket | Matching diffs become `intended` (decision id) and are suppressed; the merge run that lands the PR queues the capture as a baseline candidate (9.8) |
| Waive invariant or assertion | Flow owner of the tier; tier 1 also needs the system owner | Decision row (mark_intended on category `invariant_violation` or `assertion_failed`, ticket, `expires_at` at most 30 days) | Outcome unchanged; finding suppressed as waived until expiry. A wrong invariant is instead a registry exception with owner, reason and expiry (2.7 Layout invariants) |
| Request mask with reason | Anyone with report UI access; refused on `money_cell` regions (L-DEC-04). The UI also refuses to submit a request whose prefilled mask would take the panel's masked share (masks plus non-identity redaction, 3.8) over its budget, computed on the finding's capture, and says why: it shows the current share, the budget and the advice to declare a `rule` region instead. The finding then stays open in Unexpected until it is decided by `confirm_bug` or `mark_intended`; raising a budget is a system-owner pull request to `sentinel-config`, never a triage action | Decision row (action request_mask, verdict noise, `mask_ref` null); outbox job: Region Registry pull request with the mask record prefilled (anchor, owner, reason, expiry default 30 days, human author, `decision_ref`) | Nothing until the PR merges; the finding stays in Unexpected marked "mask requested, PR {n}" |
| Approve mask | Triage rotation; tier-1 panels also need the tier-1 flow owner as reviewer; never the requester | Merges the mask PR after the lint and per-panel budget check (4.8); sets `mask_ref` on the decision; `masks` row at the new config commit. A mask PR that fails the budget check at merge (another mask merged first) is closed by the Reporter, the request_mask decision is revoked with reason `mask_budget_exceeded`, the requester and the triage rotation are notified, and the finding returns to the triage queue with its SLA clock restarted | The region is masked; the finding closes as noise when the run on the new config commit shows no diff there |
| Mark noise | Triage rotation, flow owner of the tier; refused on `money_cell` regions | Decision row (action noise_signature, verdict noise, `expires_at` 30 days); finding `noise` | Matching diffs become `noise` (decision id); the signature joins the approved noise library used by classification (3.11 Classification decision table, input M) |
| Approve or reject baseline | Tier 1: tier-1 flow owner, never the author of the change. Tier 2 and 3: flow owner of the tier or triage rotation. Lineage set: system owner and release manager at RC sign-off. Refused from PR runs, from runs with synthetic outcomes and from runs not `complete` (L-DEC-05) | `baselines` row state change with approver, time, reason, ticket, cluster id; decision row (approve_baseline or reject_baseline, `baseline_ref`) | As in the mapping table |
| Explorer disposition | Triage rotation | Decision row (confirm_bug, agent_mistake or expected_behavior) on the Explorer finding's signature; for confirm_bug the Jira job as above. The finding carries the replayed flow's own outcome (`invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` or `needs_baseline` with the trace, never `needs_human`; 2.9 Explorer), and these actions apply to it | As in the mapping table; the Explorer precision and agent-error ratio metrics update |
| Promote candidate flow | Flow owner of the surface's tier | Pull request moving `flows/quarantine/<finding-id>.yaml` into `flows/` after trimming (2.9 Explorer); not a signature decision | The flow runs in its class from the next run; its checkpoints are `needs_baseline` until the next good build captures one |
| Accept anchor patch | Flow owner of the tier, triage rotation | For step findings (`passed_via_agent_fallback`, `failed` locator, broken anchor): anchor-patch PR and SENT maintenance task; not a signature decision | The step resolves on a scripted rung again |
| Record fixed in build | The Jira poller on Done with a fixVersion or build id, writing the resolver's login; or any role in 9.12 by hand | Decision row (fixed_in_build, supersedes the confirm_bug row); finding `fixed_pending_verify` | Signature asserted absent on or after the build; reopened if present |
| Revoke decision | Triage rotation, flow owner, system owner | `revoked_at`, `revoked_by`, `revoke_reason` on the row and status `revoked` (8.3, 4.14; distinct from `superseded`, which only a replacement sets); finding reopened | The finding returns to Unexpected on the next matching diff |
| Supersede decision | Same roles; see the conflict rule in 9.7 | New decision row with `supersedes`; the old row status superseded | The new verdict applies |
| Quarantine or un-quarantine | Flow owner of the tier, system owner | Quarantine record PR (10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine); `flake_stats.quarantined` | `not_run (reason: quarantine)` on every run, or re-entry after 5 clean Calibration captures |
| Override check | System owner only | Run row override fields with reason | Commit status forced `success` for that run only; printed in Run health and the comment |

Two-person rule. (a) The PR author (any committer on the PR branch, as the PR host reports it) may not mark a tier 1 or tier 2 diff on their own PR intended alone. Their click is a proposal: it is stored on the finding (`evidence_json.proposal`: action, proposer, time, ticket, reason), shown in the triage queue with a 4-business-hour clock (9.12), and becomes a decision row only when the triage rotation or the tier's flow owner confirms it; `decided_by` is the confirmer and the reason names the proposer. Declining returns the finding to Unexpected with the reason. (b) Nobody approves a mask they requested. (c) Nobody approves a baseline for a change they authored. (d) A tier-1 waiver needs the flow owner and the system owner. The Reporter service API enforces every clause from the PR host's committer list and the mask PR's author, and a refused write names the clause. 6.12 Authorization, accountable owner and incident procedure references this rule.

### 9.7 Decision persistence and inheritance
