Only when no canary could run at all (the stage produced no mutants and no behavioral canary flow started) is the Nightly run `aborted_harness (reason: canary_generation_failed)`. A detector that was not tested is not trusted; nothing is skipped silently.

Injection. Each image mutant is the candidate capture of its checkpoint against the approved capture as base, through the Diff Engine, Invariant Checker, Oracle, classification and the Reviewer queue, as in a merge run; behavioral mutants run their `canary` flow on the Nightly rig. The record carries `synthetic: true`, which the Stores enforce: synthetic records never promote a baseline, never create or match a decision, never post to Jira or Slack, never appear in finding lists, and count in no metric but canary pass rate (9.1 Rules for every report).

Path equivalence (5.15 Canary Service and Calibration Service). Mutants enter through the same `evaluate_checkpoint` entry point and the same harness commit as the day's merge run captures. Every night one real merge-run pair is re-evaluated through the canary entry point and must reproduce its outcome, metrics and components exactly; a difference is `harness_error (reason: canary_path_divergence)` on the self-test row, with the detector-blind banner until it clears.

Safety canaries. The attestation canary (6.3), the identity canary (6.4), the proof canary (6.6), the denied-action test (6.8), the secret-scan canary (6.9) and the redaction canary (6.10) run beside the mutants as flow-class `canary` items of the Nightly run (6.5 Nightly fire drill and safety canaries). A miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:<canary>)` with the blind detector named (`attestation`, `identity`, `proof`, `deny_list`, `secret_scan`, `redaction`), the same P1 and banner as `detector_blind`, and the flows that depend on that detector `not_run (reason: quarantine)` until it passes. The fire drill runs after them: an item the gateway did not block with no new order row is `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)` with the flows that use that path `not_run (reason: quarantine)` and a P1 page; a new Working or Filled row is run `aborted_safety (reason: drill_order_placed)` with the login blocked. In both cases the Nightly run's outcome follows the ordinary rules (`complete` for the first, `aborted_safety` for the second).

Registry validation self-test. The Nightly run also runs the probes P1 to P8 of 2.2.3 against a registry copy with one surface removed; exactly one `unregistered_surface` must result, else `harness_error (reason: validation_self_test)` and the morning report says the registry probes are blind (guarantee G1 of 1.4).

Scoring. A mutant is detected when its final outcome is in its `expected` list; otherwise the result row names the mask, decision, threshold or landmark that absorbed it (`identical`, `noise`, `intended` or, for the controls, any finding). The result rows are `canary_results` in 8.3.

- Money-cell mutants (`money_cell: true`: mutants on the money cells of 3.8, a closed list: Qty, Price, Buying Power Effect, Max Loss, Send, Cancel and Delete; the ladder price column, P/L, balance and BUY and SELL label cells are tier-1 regions, not money cells, so their mutants, M12 among them, are non-money and count toward `detector_degraded` under the next bullet; the account number and account holder name are identity fields, always redacted and never diffed, so no money-cell mutant targets them and the redaction canary M19 proves them instead): 100 percent. One miss sets the mutant's result state and the canary state to `detector_blind`: `detector_state` in `system_state` is written, run health is red, the banner is posted, on-call is paged P1 and RC sign-off is blocked. The mutant's synthetic outcome row is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)` (1.10, 4.13), and its `canary_results` row keeps the outcome the path produced (`identical`, `noise` or `intended`, the evidence of the miss) in `produced_outcome` and names what absorbed it; the Nightly run's own outcome stays `complete`. This is what the brief's "the run is `harness_error`" means: a red detector state, not a run outcome, since the run set is closed. Detection here does not depend on the Reviewer: an unmasked diff above threshold cannot be `noise` under 3.11 Classification decision table, so a miss means a mask, a decision, a threshold or a landmark swallowed the cell.
- All other mutants: detection rate per class at or above the rolling floor, the lower of the 14-night median for that class minus 5 points and 90 percent, and never below the 95 percent rolling target of 9.11 Metrics dashboard and kill criteria once Phase 2 exits. A borderline Reviewer verdict is re-sampled per the borderline rule of 3.15 before it counts as a miss. A missed non-money mutant has result state `missed` and counts toward its class rate; a miss that takes the class below the floor has result state `detector_degraded` (8.3) and sets the canary state `detector_degraded`, the synthetic outcome row of each missed mutant of that class is `harness_error (reason: detector_degraded)` while the class stays below the floor (4.13), and the banner names the class.

Result states per mutant are `detected`, `missed`, `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded` and `generation_failed` (`state` in `canary_results` in 8.3 Schema); the run's canary state (`ok`, or the worst mutant state) is written into the Nightly run's `summary_json` and into `detector_state` in `system_state`, which 9.10 and the report banner read, and a green Nightly run clears it.

Morning message. On `detector_blind` or `generation_failed` the Reporter posts to on-call and stamps a banner on every report and PR comment until a Nightly run passes; on `detector_degraded` it posts and lists the classes:

```
DETECTOR BLIND since 2026-11-09 03:12 ET.
Missed 1 of 24 money-cell mutants: M05 swapped_digit, Price 150.25 -> 150.52
  (checkpoint flow/dialog.order-confirmation/flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit/s07).
Absorbed by: threshold: calibration for fingerprint 9e1f03 carries a non-zero floor on rgn.confirm.price
  (fix-list item FL-31, owner jdoe).
Reports for the affected checkpoints cannot be trusted until this clears.
RC sign-off is blocked.
```

PR and merge runs continue under the banner; the RC gate cannot be signed while it is up. The Reporter also files a SENT Bug: Highest for `detector_blind` and `generation_failed`, High for `detector_degraded` (9.9 Jira and Slack rules).

Gate and governance. The full catalog also runs in CI on any change to masks, thresholds, the Region Registry, the Reviewer prompt or few-shot set, the pinned model id, the redaction stage or the downscale path, and on every Calibration run; the change merges only with a passing result attached. Catalog changes are PRs reviewed by the tier's flow owner and the system owner: adding a class requires the generator, a unit test (the mutant differs from base only inside the target region) and the expected-outcome mapping; removing or weakening a mutant requires a reason and a ticket. Each result row stores the catalog version, and the morning report lists critical checkpoints with fewer than 20 live mutants as a coverage gap.

### 10.4 Eval set and Reviewer change control

Eval set (construction and shares in 3.14 Eval set, metrics and gates). 300 to 500 labeled items stored content-addressed, labels as JSON lines in `sentinel-config` with labeler ids: mutants from the same generators on a different seed stream than the nightly catalog; A/A pairs from Calibration runs labeled `no_visible_difference`; real PR and merge diffs labeled by two humans independently with a third adjudicating. Tier-1 checkpoints are at least 40 percent of the set; the held-out 30 percent is never used to choose a prompt or a threshold.

Metrics, per model id and prompt version, stored in `reviewer_evals` (8.3): precision and recall per verdict; tier-1 recall of `does_not_match_manifest` on mutants on its own; hallucination and rubber-stamp rates; a reliability diagram and expected calibration error for the confidence field; the `needs_human` routing threshold read off the curves, not set by hand.

Change control. A change to any element of the reviewer version tuple of 3.15 Model and prompt change control; degraded modes (model id, prompt hash, schema version, few-shot ids, effort, crop policy version, redaction version), or to any Region Registry semantic the Reviewer depends on, runs the eval set on the held-out split and the full mutant catalog in CI. Merge is blocked if any gate in 3.14 falls, if tier-1 recall drops more than 1 point even while the gate holds, or if any critical mutant is missed; the result is attached to the PR. The model id from the API response, prompt hash, few-shot version, mask version and redaction version are stamped on every verdict so a shift in the verdict mix can be attributed.

Gate failure mid-release. The nightly 30-item eval subset of 3.14 runs on the deployed tuple every night. If it fails a gate, or a weekly full evaluation does, the Reviewer is disabled by config (`reviewer_enabled: false`) from the next run: no model calls are made, every above-threshold diff on a declared surface is `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending`, `collateral` and all invariant and assertion outcomes are unaffected because they need no model, and every report and PR comment carries the line "Reviewer disabled since <date>: eval gate <name> failed; N items await a human". An RC in flight is not blocked by the disabled Reviewer, because sign-off already requires human triage of every `needs_human` and `collateral` item (3.16 What the reviewer may never do, item 10); it is blocked by the untriaged items themselves until triage clears them. The Reviewer returns only when a tuple passes the full gate set in CI and the system owner merges the pin.

Runtime controls. Borderline confidence (within 0.10 of the routing threshold) is re-sent twice and the majority verdict with the median confidence is kept (3.15). Each week a human re-labels a random 5 percent of `noise` outcomes that came from an approved signature and the 5 percent of `intended` verdicts 3.15 samples; the overturn rates are report metrics.

### 10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine

Targeted re-run (mechanics in 3.10 Targeted re-run and flake logic). When a checkpoint's diff exceeds its region threshold, or an invariant fired, and no assertion failed, the Executor runs the declared normalize routine (Esc, park the mouse, drop focus on the neutral control, reset scroll, reselect the sub-tab), waits for the settle rule and re-captures, up to twice in the same session for a diff, and once for an `invariant_violation`, which is re-captured only to confirm that it persists (an `assertion_failed` is final without a re-run). All captures must agree within the A/A floor, and a re-captured invariant must fire again; a violation that does not reproduce is instability like a disagreeing diff. All agree: a product change, and classification proceeds (3.11). Any disagree: instability, outcome `not_settled (reason: unstable)`, both images attached, routed to the flow owner, never to the Reviewer or the Unexpected list. A re-capture never crosses a flow step and the first capture is always kept. Checkpoints declared `recapturable: false` (4.7 Flow file: the state cannot be re-entered in the session) skip the re-run and classify from the single capture, with the finding marked "not re-captured: recapturable false". The run carries a re-run budget; when it is spent before stability is decided the outcome row records `stability: unknown (cause: budget)`, run health prints `rerun_budget_exhausted` for the sharding review, and the finding is listed with "not re-captured: budget" (3.10).

Flake statistics. `flake_stats` in SQLite (8.3), per checkpoint over a rolling 30 days: captures, re-captures, unstable outcomes, verdict flips between two runs of the same build (the merge run versus the Nightly A/A pass), step retries, agent fallbacks. An observation is one compared capture of the checkpoint on one build. The flake score is unstable outcomes plus verdict flips over observations; the dashboard flake rate of 9.11 is the same ratio over all checkpoints compared.

Quarantine. A checkpoint enters quarantine on any of: flake score above 0.10 over the last 5 or more observations of the same build; `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` on 3 consecutive Nightly runs (10.6); the gateway drop thresholds of 6.2 and 5.4.8 (any safety-reason drop quarantines the flow; 3 integrity-reason drops in one flow quarantine it); 3 unstable outcomes in 7 days; 2 verdict flips on one build; a non-zero A/A floor on a frozen checkpoint not fixed within 5 business days (7.13 What invalidates calibration); or a flow whose 30-day agent-fallback rate exceeds 5 percent, which quarantines the whole flow (11.5). Drill and safety-canary flows (6.5) are exempt: a trigger on one pages per the safety routing of 9.10 instead of quarantining it (3.10). Quarantine is a record in `quarantine.yaml` in `sentinel-config` (checkpoint or flow, owner, ticket, entered, reason: `flake`, `aa_drift`, `aa_floor`, `maintenance_budget` from 11.5, `fire_drill` and `safety_canary` from 6.5 and 10.3, `kill_switch` and `gateway_drops` from 6.6 and 5.4.8, `fallback_rate` from 11.5) opened by the Orchestrator as a PR, or by the Quarantine action of 9.6 One-click actions and who may perform them, and merged by the system owner; at run start the Orchestrator mirrors the file at the pinned commit into `flake_stats.quarantined`, so git is the record and SQLite the mirror. While quarantined, the checkpoint is `not_run (reason: quarantine)` on every run, shown in the coverage matrix in its own color, never as covered. Exit requires a fix plus 5 consecutive clean captures in a Calibration run with a zero floor, cited in the PR that removes the record; nothing un-quarantines automatically. Above 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints quarantined, run health is red and the RC gate blocks.

Step retries and agent fallbacks are recorded as `passed_after_retry` and `passed_via_agent_fallback` with the locator failure as a finding beside the checkpoint; two fallbacks on the same step and build open an "update scripted flow" ticket, and flows in fallback is a run health metric.

### 10.6 A/A drift on the Nightly run

Every Nightly run captures, on the current main build, all tier-1 checkpoints plus a rotating 20 percent of the rest, twice in one session on one rig (the pass is sharded over rigs 4 and 5 with each checkpoint's two passes in the same session, 11.2 Cadence and time budgets per run type), and compares pass 1 with pass 2 and both with the day's merge run captures of the same build, per region, against the Calibration floor (3.9 A/A calibration and threshold derivation). The environment fingerprint is checked first. When it differs from the Calibration fingerprint no floor exists for it: every A/A diff is evaluated at threshold 0 and reported `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)`, the morning report names the changed field and a Calibration run is queued (7.13 What invalidates calibration). `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` is reserved for a candidate and base that differ from each other, which two passes on one rig cannot.

- A frozen checkpoint with any diff above its floor: `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` for the night, flake statistics updated, flow owner notified; three nights running triggers quarantine.
- More than 2 percent of checkpoints above floor, or the global-shift pre-pass of 3.7 Three-granularity diff (fraction of checkpoints above epsilon, and whether diff pixels sit on text edges by an edge-density measure) indicating a rendering change: `harness_error (reason: aa_drift_global)`, and the morning report says thresholds are invalid until a Calibration run passes. On a product run the same pre-pass yields one `needs_human (reason: global_shift)` cluster under the run-level `global_rendering_shift` finding with zero Reviewer calls (3.7).

### 10.7 Degraded modes

Model API.

- Review is asynchronous and idempotent. A run reaches captured-and-diffed with zero model calls; every checkpoint above threshold that needs a verdict is recorded `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending`, and the Reporter publishes the report in state `unreviewed` with the line "Reviewer pending: N items". `collateral`, invariant violations and assertion failures are already final.
- The Reviewer job drains a queue keyed by (run_id, checkpoint_id, region, cluster, diff_hash); a key already answered by the same model id and prompt hash is not re-sent. When a pending verdict lands, the item is re-evaluated through the 3.11 table with the verdict as input R and the outcome becomes what the table gives (`intended`, `noise` only via the A/A floor, or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)`, which is also the outcome for a declared removed surface the Reviewer does not confirm (3.11 row 25a), or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_uncertain)`), `review_state` goes from `pending` to `done`, and the Reporter re-renders. If a human decision already exists on that item, the verdict is attached as an annotation only and never changes the outcome or the decision.
- Late results. A verdict that lands after the report was published creates a new report version, edits the PR comment in place (9.1), re-runs decision matching for the item because the category is part of the signature (9.7 Decision persistence and inheritance), re-ranks the Unexpected list, and fires the new-high-confidence-collateral alert of 9.10 at that moment if the item now qualifies. An item a human decided before its verdict landed is the exception: the outcome stays as the decision left it, `review_state` becomes `done`, the verdict is stored as an annotation, the item is not re-ranked, re-matched or re-alerted, and a verdict that disagrees with the decision is listed in the weekly summary and joins the eval development split (3.15). If a newer run of the same PR has published since, the late verdict is recorded against its own run and the comment's history table shows it; the live comment keeps showing the latest run.
- Synchronous calls serve every PR run item inside the 45 minute budget under a concurrency semaphore of 4 with the SDK's default retries on 429 and 5xx; tier-1 items not back from a batch by the report deadline minus 10 minutes are sent synchronously the same way (3.15). After 3 consecutive failures, a 429 burst, or a queue over 20 items, the rest of the run's reviews go to the Message Batches API: one batch per run, `custom_id` equal to the queue key, results read by `custom_id` in any order, `expired` entries resubmitted once, `errored` entries retried once and then left `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)`. Most batches finish within an hour and the hard maximum is 24 hours, so a batched run is posted `unreviewed` at its deadline and completed later. Whether the security-approved endpoint offers the Batch API is confirmed in Phase 0 under DR-07; an endpoint without it uses the synchronous path with the semaphore and the queue drains over time. Reviewer caps per run (PR 60, merge 200, RC 500) leave items beyond the cap `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)`. No run ever waits on the model.
- Spend ceilings (11.4 Cost model, `policy/budgets.yaml`). The Orchestrator sums the usage block of every model response of the run (Reviewer, agent rescue, Explorer) against three ceilings. An Explorer session that reaches 25 dollars ends that session only, with the run-health line of 2.9 Explorer; the run continues. The weekly ceiling stops model calls until the week ends, with the items it excludes `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` and `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail` (3.15); it aborts no run. The per-run ceiling is the only one that ends a run: when the run's model spend reaches it, the Orchestrator makes no further model call, finishes the step in progress and ends the run `aborted_budget (reason: dollar_cap)` at the next flow boundary; checkpoints not yet captured are `not_run (reason: budget)`, items still waiting for a verdict are `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail` and `review_state: done` (the later change 4.13 allows for a pending item), teardown and the post-run proof run as usual, and on-call is told (9.10). Recorded outcomes stand.
- Deprecation. Full model ids are pinned per component in config and stamped on every verdict and agent step. Agent mode uses the harness's own tool definitions (`click_named`, `type_fixture`, `press`, `zoom`, `scroll` and the Explorer-only `drag_named`; 5.6 Agent-mode toolset) with image inputs, not the computer-use beta tool, so there is no computer-use tool type to pin; the second pinned item is the harness toolset schema version, also stamped on every agent step. A daily job calls `GET /v1/models/{id}` for each pinned id; a missing id is an alarm. The Models API does not publish retirement dates, so the system owner records each vendor deprecation notice in `model_deprecations.yaml` (the published policy is at least 60 days before a public model is retired; verify at Phase 0); alarms fire at announcement, T-45, T-30 and T-14 until the migration PR, which must pass 10.4, merges. Preflight N2 sends one agent request with the pinned toolset schema version and fails the item if the request shape is rejected.
- Preflight N2 or N5 failing (12.7) is a degraded mode, never `env_error`: the run continues, and the failure sets `review_mode: deferred` and `agent_available: false`, which disables both agent fallback and the Explorer. `review_mode: deferred` means every item that needs a verdict is `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending` until the endpoint returns (3.15). With the agent unavailable the locator ladder of 5.5 Locator ladder ends at the OCR text anchor; a locator failure is step `failed`, the checkpoint the step led to is `landmark_missing`, the flow's downstream checkpoints are `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`, and the failure is posted as a finding with the pre-attempt screenshot and the base build's screenshot at the same step, labeled "scripted locator failed; agent fallback disabled". Nothing hangs and nothing falls back silently. An agent-only step (one with no scripted rung) is skipped and its checkpoints are `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)`. The flag is re-checked once per flow and a recovery is logged. If `agent_available` is still false when the Explorer is due (T+6:20 of an RC run, 10.9), the Explorer does not start: its session is `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)`, the RC report's Explorer section and run health print "Explorer: not run, model endpoint unavailable", the Explorer owner and harness on-call are told, and the run is otherwise unaffected; a recovery logged before T+6:20 lets it start as planned. DR-07 branch B (computer use not covered) sets the same flags permanently; there the Explorer is out of scope (11.8), not `not_run`.

Network.

- Preflight failures (N1 to N5) are `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)` or a degraded mode, never a diff. A failure inside a listed `maintenance_windows` entry (7.10 Quiet windows from the exchange calendar) reschedules the run once with a notice instead, per 7.11 Network preflight and chaos suite.
- Mid-run, the anti-anchors Disconnected and Reconnecting stop capture. The Orchestrator pauses up to 5 minutes polling connectivity (the post-login probe of 7.11 Network preflight and chaos suite: indicator not Disconnected, pinned quote fresh). Network back within 5 minutes: re-assert paper mode (a reconnect may re-authenticate), run the light fixture check, then retry the current step once; the step is `passed_after_retry` and its checkpoint is captured normally, or `not_settled (reason: timeout)` if it will not settle. Between 5 and 15 minutes: the checkpoint in progress and the rest of its flow are `env_error (gate: connectivity)`, and the run resumes at the next flow boundary after the same re-verification. Past 15 minutes: the shard's remaining checkpoints are `env_error (gate: connectivity)` and the run ends `complete_with_env_errors`. A paused masked_live checkpoint pauses its lockstep partner too; a partner that cannot resume in the same minute makes the checkpoint `not_run (reason: budget)` per 11.3 Sharding and parallelism. Pause time counts against the wall budget.
- Loss of the central store: artifacts and SQLite are local, so the run continues and publication retries with backoff; if the rig cannot reach the host by the deadline, the dead-man alert fires with "rig unreachable, run data intact on rig" and the late-arrival rule of 10.2 applies when it reconnects.

Rig.

- Rig Manager heartbeat per rig every 30 s to the control host; 3 minutes of silence is a lost rig. The shard is re-queued once, in full (its Run Store is on the lost rig and rows ship only at `reported`), to a rig of the same fingerprint class if the wall budget allows; when no budget or rig allows it, the shard's checkpoints are `env_error (gate: rig_lost)` and the run ends `complete_with_env_errors`. A second loss of the same shard ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: rig_lost)` with `harness_error (reason: rig_lost)` on every unfinished checkpoint, because two lost rigs in one run is a fleet or harness fault, not weather. When a lost rig returns, its Run Store rows ship with their `attempt` number and are kept as a superseded attempt for diagnosis, never merged into the live attempt.
- Snapshot checksum mismatch, a non-interactive desktop or wrong display mode: `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)` at `provisioned` with the item id (R1, R6, R2); a black probe screenshot from the capture self-test is `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H3)` (12.7). A Windows update outside the snapshot process changes a rig's fingerprint: when its pair rig differs, every checkpoint of the pair is `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` naming the field; when both rigs changed alike and no Calibration exists for the new fingerprint, diffs are evaluated at threshold 0 as `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` and a Calibration run is queued (7.13); either way on-call is alerted.

### 10.8 Self-tests at run start

Preflight is the 32-item checklist of 12.7 Preflight checklist, run on the reverted rig before the state machine leaves `provisioned` (5.2); this section does not define a second list. Groups R (rig), B (build), N (network) and G (gateway and registries) are environment checks: a failure has the effect 12.7 and 7.11 give the item. For most items (R1 to R7, B1 to B3, N1, N6, G2 to G4) every scheduled checkpoint is `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)`, the run ends `complete_with_env_errors` and on-call is alerted. The N items each state their own outcome: N1 and N6 as above; N2 and N5 a degraded mode, never `env_error` (table below, 10.7); N3 `env_error (gate: preflight.N3)` on the checkpoints with `api_within` assertions only; N4 `env_error (gate: preflight.N4)` on frozen checkpoints only; N7 none, the run proceeds and publication retries with backoff. G1 and G5 are as 12.7 writes them. Group H is the harness self-test: a failure ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.<item>)` before any product action, as 12.7 writes it. Every failure names the item, attaches a screenshot, and the run health block lists all 32 with pass or fail. The fourteen self-tests an earlier draft of this section numbered 1 to 14 are, in 12.7's ids: 1 = H8 Watchdog, 2 = R6 console session, 3 = R2 and R3 display and ClearType, 4 = H1 and H2 injection and hook, 5 = H3 capture, 6 = H4 gateway deny self-test, 7 = R4 and R7 time zone, layout, disk and clock, 8 = H7 and G1 stores and config commit, 9 = B1 build artifacts plus the version read at the `launched` gate (`env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_mismatch)`), 10 = G5 fingerprint pre-match, 11 = H10 crash plumbing, 12 = N2 and N5 model endpoint and egress payload, 13 = N1 network hosts plus the `fixture_verified` gate's connectivity probe, 14 = the `canary_flow_passed` gate. The mechanisms this section adds to the checklist's one-line methods:

| Item | Mechanism added here | On failure |
|---|---|---|
| H1 Input injection, H2 Global hook | SendInput a click and a key chord into a harness-owned probe window and confirm receipt; install and remove a low-level hook and measure callback latency, which must stay under 1 ms at p99.9 over 1,000 events and under the 20 ms hook timeout at worst (5.4); no Recorder process present, checked by psutil (5.16 Recorder); a blocked action names the control when EDR logs show it | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H1)` or `(reason: preflight.H2)` |
| H3 Capture | mss capture of the probe window equals its known pattern byte for byte; a desktop probe is not uniform (a black or single-color frame means a locked or headless console) | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H3)` |
| H4 Gateway deny self-test | With the probe window flagged as a ticket, inject Enter and an untokened click; both must be dropped and logged | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H4)` |
| H7 Stores | `PRAGMA quick_check`; WAL writable; single-writer lock acquired; free space above the R7 rig floor (the larger of 20 GB and twice the projected shard size, 8.6); git checkout at the pinned `sentinel-config` commit with the CI lint hash (also G1) | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H7)` |
| H8 Watchdog | Watchdog PID alive and distinct from the Orchestrator's; `watchdog.json` age under 10 s; `heartbeat.json` written and read back | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H8)`; a Watchdog lost later in the run is `watchdog_dead` (10.2) |
| H10 Crash plumbing | The `-XX:ErrorFile` and `-XX:HeapDumpPath` folders writable, the WER LocalDumps key present, the vmoptions hash equal to the checked-in template that carries the flags (also B3) | `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H10)` |
| N2 Model endpoint | `GET /v1/models/{id}` for each pinned id; a 1-token message on the reviewer model; one-step agent request with the harness toolset at its pinned schema version (there is no computer-use tool type to pin, 10.7); a zero cache read on the second of two identical requests means a silent prompt change and fails the item | `review_mode: deferred`, `agent_available: false` (agent fallback and Explorer disabled); the run continues; a degraded mode (10.7), never `env_error` and not a checkpoint outcome |
| N5 Egress payload | POST of a 2 MB redacted test image through the corporate proxy to the approved host | As N2, naming the blocking control |
| N3 Market-data API | One quote for a fixture symbol under 5 s | `env_error (gate: preflight.N3)` on the checkpoints with `api_within` assertions only; the symbol pre-check falls back to the app quote (7.9) |
| N7 Integrations | PR host API, artifact store and controller reachable | None: the run proceeds and publication retries with backoff under the dead-man deadline (10.2) |
| G5 Fingerprint pre-match | Candidate and base rig fingerprints equal, and a Calibration exists for that fingerprint | Rigs differ: every checkpoint `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` naming the field, captures still collected. No Calibration for the fingerprint: diffs at threshold 0 as `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` and a Calibration run queued (7.13) |

The `canary_flow_passed` gate (a 60-second smoke flow on a tier-1 surface whose capture matches the base within floor) is an Orchestrator state machine gate, not a preflight item; its failure is `env_error (gate: canary_flow_passed)` per 5.2 (gate names equal state names).

### 10.9 Release-day timeline

Times are relative to GA (G). N is PA-14 of 11.1 Planning assumptions: 3 business days by default, per train in `policy/release_gate.yaml`; an RC cut at G-7 is assumed when the file is missing.

| When | What happens | Actor | System output |
|---|---|---|---|
| RC cut (G-7 or per train) | Pipeline publishes the RC artifact; RC run starts on all 6 rigs, base = last released build (lineage baseline); soak on rig 5 (10.11); Explorer last on rig 6, or `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` when the model endpoint is down at T+6:20 (10.7) | Pipeline, Orchestrator | Run starts within 10 minutes and never later than the RC start deadline, the G-N sign-off time minus 8 hours (11.2); past it the release manager decides (9.12); dead-man armed for 9 hours |
| RC cut + 8 h | RC run captured-and-diffed; `unreviewed` report published; Reviewer queue drains | Reporter, Reviewer | Reviewed report within the batch window |
| RC cut night | Nightly run: canaries, A/A drift, fire drill (6.5 Nightly fire drill and safety canaries), fingerprint check. An RC run still holding rigs 4 and 5 at 22:00 pre-empts the Nightly run: the skipped Nightly is alerted (9.10) and its canaries, fire drill and safety canaries run in the next free window | Canary Service, Calibration Service | Morning report; detector-blind banner if any; while a skipped Nightly's canaries have not run, every report and PR comment carries the banner "canaries pending: last Nightly skipped for RC run {run_id}" and no PR comment is trusted |
| G-6 to G-(N+1) | Triage works the Unexpected list by tier; decisions recorded; a respin gets a new RC run. A new RC build supersedes an RC run still in flight: that run schedules no new flow, stops at the next flow boundary with teardown and the post-run proof on every rig, and ends `aborted_budget (reason: superseded)` with its unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`; its partial report is published labelled "superseded by {build}"; the new RC run starts at once with the pool reservation transferred (11.2) | Triage rotation, flow owners, Orchestrator | Every finding has a disposition; decisions made on the superseded run are inherited by the new one (9.7) |
| G-N | System owner signs the RC report. Conditions: `detector_state` in `system_state` is `ok` after the last Nightly run (no `detector_blind`, `generation_failed` or `canary_path_divergence`); every tier-1 cell covered or its `not_run` explained; quarantine under 2 percent of tier-1; no tier-1 `collateral`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` or `needs_human` without a disposition; soak within budget or its findings dispositioned; fire drill passed (no `drill_failed`, no `drill_order_placed`); post-run proof PROVEN on every RC shard. A respin after G-N gets a full RC run and a new sign-off; the clock does not reset unless the release manager records an exception | System owner, release manager | Signed report with hash; Jira release ticket updated |
| G-1 | Release-night rehearsal: one rig upgrades in place from the previous released build over a tier B workspace (migration path; DR-04 branch B flow) | Rig Manager, Orchestrator | Migration checkpoints appended to the RC report |
| G | GA ships. A merge-run-scope run against the released build as pulled by the launcher on a non-pinned rig catches server-side changes that alter the UI without a client change; the lineage baseline becomes the release's approved set | Orchestrator, system owner | Approved set tagged with the release |
| G+1 | 24-hour confirmation run; escape tracking opens: every production bug is tagged with the checkpoint that should have shown it, or `not_registered` | Triage rotation | Escape rate updated |

### 10.10 End-to-end acceptance test: the Flexible Grid and Active Trader ladder scenario

Phase 1 exits when this test passes on the target rigs on two consecutive days (11.9 Phases 1 to 3); the test stays in the repository as a permanent check. The scenario is 1.11 Worked example; the PR comment it must produce is 9.3 Filled sample.

Fixtures kept in git:

- `acceptance/manifests/flexgrid-chrome.yaml`: a change manifest with one entry in the 4.3 schema, `entry_id: sent-acc-1`, `tickets: [SENT-ACC-1]`, `touched_primitives: [FlexibleGrid]`, declaring only `charts.flexible-grid.chart-cell`.
- Branch `acceptance/flexgrid-ladder` in the product repository, rebased each release by its owner, carrying the 1.11 change: the Flexible Grid cell header shrinks from 28 to 22 px and `layoutContainer` gives the hosted component the full remaining cell height, so the Active Trader ladder viewport draws 14 px under its order-control strip at cell height 360 and sits 6 px higher than base at 480 and above. Phase 1 assumption: the product team supplies it as the revert of the original fix commit; if that commit is not recoverable, the flow owner and an Active Trader developer write a change in the grid cell layout class with the same effect.
- Mutant M12 (10.3, 12.5), the acceptance mutant, on `sweep/charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell/flexgrid/480x360`.

Part A, injected mutant. Run the canary path for M12 against the approved capture of its checkpoint, and for M08 against its. Pass for M12: the Invariant Checker reports `invariant_violation` INV-01 with both component rects and INV-03 on the clipped MKT word box; the Diff Engine reports region `rgn.ladder.viewport` above threshold with the component's bounding box; no Reviewer call is made for it, since invariant violations never go to the Reviewer (9.7, 3.16); the result row is detected, `synthetic: true`; no baseline is promoted and no decision is created. M08 passes under its 12.5 expectation (INV-01 on the Trade-tab ladder, `sweep/trade.active-trader.ladder/flexgrid/480x360`).

Part B, real branch change. Open a PR from `acceptance/flexgrid-ladder` with the manifest above. The PR run must, inside the 45 minute budget on the pool of 11.2:

1. Static impact step (2.11 Scope computation per run type): the changed grid cell layout classes lead through dependents to every surface consuming `FlexibleGrid`, so the scope includes the sweep of `charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell` although the manifest did not declare it (the Active Trader cell hosted in a Charts-tab Flexible Grid, `charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell`, is a tier-1 surface of its own; the Trade-tab ladder `trade.active-trader.ladder`, bound to M08, is a different registry surface; both are swept with host `flexgrid`, the Flexible Grid cell mode of 2.5.1 Hosting modes, and both ids are valid under the grammar of 4.1); `dependency_map_gap` is not emitted because the map carries the edge.
2. Size sweep on Ladder S (2.5.2 The ladders): widths {320, 480, 640, 960} by heights {360, 480, 720}, 12 steps, descending, candidate and base in the tier C harness workspace. At height 360 the candidate shows the overlap at all four widths and the base does not.
3. Invariant Checker: `invariant_violation` (INV-01 sibling bounds intersect; INV-03 text clipped) on the candidate only at the four height-360 steps, under both DR-01 branches, with the size that triggered it; the first failing step in ladder order (descending) is 960x360 and the failing range is height 360 at every width, as 1.11 and 9.3 state.
4. Diff Engine: region `rgn.ladder.viewport` above threshold at all 12 steps; the targeted re-run (3.10) agrees across captures (product change, not instability): one confirming re-capture at each of the 4 `invariant_violation` steps shows the same intersection, and two re-captures at each of the other 8 steps agree within floor, as in 1.11.
5. Classification: `invariant_violation` by precedence at the 4 overlapping steps, with `collateral` kept on the finding as evidence; `collateral` at the 8 steps at heights 480 and 720, naming primitive `FlexibleGrid` and manifest entry `sent-acc-1` (ticket SENT-ACC-1), with no model call deciding either; and `collateral`, tier 1, by 3.11 row 16 on the Active Trader cell's census checkpoint `census/charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell/ws.tier-a.active-trader` (header 6 px shorter, viewport 6 px higher, no overlap at that cell size), whose description comes from its own Reviewer call, since a census checkpoint is not in the sweep cluster (9.7 Clustering); the run makes 4 Reviewer calls (the 8-step `collateral` cluster, this census checkpoint, the tier-2 cluster and the intended chart cell) and none for the 4 `invariant_violation` steps, as 1.11 and 9.3 state, at 3 x 0.009 + 0.012 = 0.039 dollars mid tier or 3 x 0.018 + 0.024 = 0.078 top tier (the synchronous prices of 11.4, the sweep-cluster call carrying two crop sets).
6. PR comment (9.2 PR comment template): the Intended section shows the declared chart cell's diff with the Reviewer's confirmation, or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending` and the report state `unreviewed` if the API is down, which also passes; the Unexpected section lists the ladder overlap first, tier 1, as a cluster of 4 with base and candidate crops at 1:1, the first failing size and range, the primitive, the manifest entry and the three one-click actions, then the `collateral` cluster of 8, then the tier-1 `collateral` of the Active Trader census checkpoint, ahead of any tier-2 item; the coverage matrix shows the ladder covered for the active trader persona and everything outside scope as `not_run (reason: scope)`.
7. Controls: the same PR with the change reverted yields the 12 ladder checkpoints and the Active Trader census checkpoint `identical` and no `collateral`; a "confirm bug" decision on the finding is inherited by a re-run: the finding keeps its outcome and appears under Known bugs with the ticket and no new alert (9.6).

Part C, reliability controls in the same acceptance session, each with its pass criterion:

- Kill the JVM mid-flow: `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with cause `process_exit` in `detail` on the checkpoint being captured, `not_run (reason: app_crash)` for the rest of that flow, tier-1 finding `app_crash` with artifacts, relaunch through every gate, run `complete` with the finding under Unexpected.
- Freeze the app during a chart load (`SuspendThread` on the AWT threads): hang detected by screenshot staleness within `max(2 x max_wait_s, 60 s)`, thread dump attempted, outcome `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with cause `hang` in `detail`, same downstream handling.
- Kill the Orchestrator: the Watchdog restarts it with `--resume`; completed checkpoints are not repeated; the one in progress is `harness_error (reason: orchestrator_died)`; the run completes.
- Kill the Watchdog: the Orchestrator ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: watchdog_dead)` at the next flow boundary with teardown and proof complete; the control host receives the run.
- Kill the Gateway hook host mid-flow: the step is `blocked_by_gateway (hook_host_dead)`, its checkpoint `harness_error (reason: hook_lost)`, the rest of the flow `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`, the app tree is killed and the hook host restarted without consuming an app relaunch; kill it a second time in the same shard: run `aborted_harness (reason: hook_lost)`.
- Make the heartbeat path read-only: run `aborted_harness (reason: heartbeat_unwritable)` within one flow, no Watchdog restart loop, proof complete.
- Suppress the `run_completed` event: dead-man alert within 15 minutes of the deadline; run row `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)`; then release the rows and confirm the row is replaced by the real outcome and the alert closes as late arrival.
- Power off the rig mid-shard: the shard is re-queued once and completes on another rig; power off the second rig too: run `aborted_harness (reason: rig_lost)`.
- Block the model host at the proxy: N2 and N5 defer review and disable the agent; the PR comment posts `unreviewed` within budget; a flow with a deliberately broken locator ends `failed` with `landmark_missing` on its checkpoint, downstream `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`, never in agent mode. Then hold one batch past the deadline and release it: the report gains a version, the PR comment is edited in place, the item's reason changes from `reviewer_unavailable`.
- Delete the approved capture of one critical checkpoint before the Nightly run: that mutant `harness_error (reason: canary_generation_failed)`, canary state `generation_failed`, banner present, P1 paged, RC sign-off blocked, the Nightly run `complete`.
- Add a mask over `rgn.ladder.viewport` in a test branch of `sentinel-config`: the CI canary gate fails on M12, names the mask, blocks the merge, and the message matches 10.3.

The acceptance report records the run ids for A, B and C and is the first entry in the metrics history.

### 10.11 Soak: long sessions, resource budgets and the freeze detector

Why. Leaks, handle exhaustion and six-hour freezes never appear in a 45-minute run, and a user keeps thinkorswim open all day. Soak is the RC-only activity that 2.11 schedules as `soak_items` and 11.2 places on rig 5 for 6 hours in parallel with the census shards.

Schedule and base. One rig, the candidate build, the tier B workspace with the most gadgets, data mode masked_live with the Region Registry (a six-hour frozen window is not available on either DR-02 branch). The base curve is the lineage soak of the last released build, recorded when that build was the RC and stored with its fingerprint in the Central Store; it is comparable only when the fingerprint matches, otherwise every soak comparison checkpoint is `needs_baseline` and the candidate curves are shown alone. There is no base soak rig: the fleet of 11.2 has none to spare and a 12-hour back-to-back pair does not fit the 8-hour budget.

Activity loop. A scripted loop of tier-1 and tier-2 flows with no order-stage steps beyond building and deleting a ticket (symbol changes on every gadget, chart period and study changes, tab switches, a scan, Monitor sub-tab cycling, a ticket built and deleted), one cycle every 15 minutes, 24 cycles. Each cycle ends with a soak checkpoint `flow/<workspace-surface-id>/soak/c<nn>`: settle, capture, invariants, and two diffs: against the lineage soak capture at the same cycle index, and against the run's own cycle-1 capture, which catches drift inside the session (a leaked window, a growing panel, a stuck tooltip, a stale quote badge). Both diffs classify through 3.11 with the same taxonomy as any checkpoint.

Resource sampler, every 60 s, for every process in the tree: working set and private bytes, GDI and USER object counts (`GetGuiResources`), handle and thread counts, CPU, and JVM heap after GC by `jcmd GC.heap_info` where attach is allowed (best effort, as in 10.2). The ticking clock region of the status bar is hashed every 2 s as the freeze detector: a hash unchanged for 10 s with no anti-anchor on screen is a freeze, handled as the app-failure trio of 10.1 with cause `hang` in `detail`, and the soak continues after relaunch under the same 3-relaunch budget; the relaunches are the finding. A crash in soak is the same trio: a product finding, never `env_error`.

Budgets, declared in `soak.yaml` in `sentinel-config` and calibrated from the lineage curve, each an assertion `soak.<metric>` evaluated at every cycle checkpoint:

| Metric | Default budget | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| Working set growth | Under 25 percent above the hour-1 value, and under 1.5 GB absolute growth | `soak.working_set` |
| Monotonic growth | Linear fit over the trailing 3 hours of working set or private bytes with slope under 60 MB per hour | `soak.growth_slope` |
| GDI objects | Under 9,000 at every sample (quota 10,000) | `soak.gdi_objects` |
| Handles and threads | Within 20 percent of the hour-1 value | `soak.handles`, `soak.threads` |
| Heap after GC | Under 80 percent of `-Xmx` at every sample where readable | `soak.heap` |
| Freezes and relaunches | Zero freezes; zero relaunches | `soak.freezes`, `soak.relaunches` |
| Render latency | Clock tick observed at least once per 2 s window in 99 percent of windows | `soak.render_latency` |

A breach is `assertion_failed (assertion: soak.<metric>)` on the cycle checkpoint, tier 1, with both curves attached, a product finding the Reviewer never sees. New exception signatures in the client log slice (stack headers whose normalized first three frames are absent from the lineage run's signature set) are a tier-2 finding `new_log_signature` on the cycle checkpoint, with the count and the first occurrence; findings, not outcomes, so they never change the checkpoint's outcome. When the client log cannot be located (10.2), the report's soak section says "log signatures: not available" rather than reporting zero.

Report. The RC report's soak section (9.4 Merge and RC report structure) shows both builds' curves per metric with the budget line, restarts, new exception signatures, the memory ceiling reached, and the 24 cycle outcomes. Sign-off at G-N (10.9) requires every soak finding dispositioned. A soak that did not run or did not finish is `not_run (reason: budget)` per unreached cycle and is printed as such in the release gate checklist, never as passed.

## 11. Operations and delivery plan

Every number here is a locked budget from the brief or a planning assumption with an id PA-01 to PA-14 (11.1; the attestation checklist keeps A1 to A11, 12.6, and 1.2 and 8.8 use AS- and SA- ids); the Reporter prints measured durations from run one and the system owner recomputes these tables at every phase exit. Metric targets and kill criteria are those of 1.5 Success criteria and kill criteria and are repeated here only where a phase exit depends on them.

### 11.1 Planning assumptions

| ID | Assumption | Value |
|---|---|---|
| PA-01 | Registered surfaces at the end of Phase 2 | 300 |
| PA-02 | Tier A workspaces (of 5) hosting an average surface (global surfaces such as dialogs, settings pages and ticket variants count in all five); census checkpoints per build = PA-01 x PA-02; the same 60 percent figure as 2.4 Surface census procedure and 8.8 Growth estimates | three, so 900 |
| PA-03 | Seconds per census checkpoint with navigation and settle (max wait 15 s, 30 s for charts and chains); 2.4 budgets 15 to 25 s per visit, and the sensitivity line in 11.2 shows what 20 s does to the merge budget | 12 p50, 25 p95 |
| PA-04 | Session startup per shard, launch through the canary flow; workspace switch within a session | 4 min; 45 s |
| PA-05 | Flows at the end of Phase 3, by tier | 40 / 60 / 50 |
| PA-06 | Seconds per flow including preconditions and teardown, by tier | 90 / 75 / 60 |
| PA-07 | Size sweeps: 25 resizable gadgets, 15 in tiers 1 and 2 and 10 in tier 3; 8 s per step. Merge runs: tiers 1 and 2 on Ladder S (12 steps) plus the short splitter set (3), 225 checkpoints. RC runs: tiers 1 and 2 on Ladder F (about 46 steps) plus the full splitter set (7) and about 3 corpus sizes, and tier 3 on Ladder S, about 960 checkpoints. PR runs: the resizable tier-1 surfaces in scope, about 5, on Ladder S plus the short set, 75 checkpoints (2.5.2 The ladders, 2.5.3 Which gadgets get the sweep) | as stated |
| PA-08 | Tier B census: 6 workspaces x 100 checkpoints | 600 |
| PA-09 | Share of checkpoints in `data_mode: frozen` (depends on DR-02) | 70 percent |
| PA-10 | Runs per day at steady state (confirm in Phase 0) | 10 PR, 4 merge (coalesced), 1 nightly |
| PA-11 | Checkpoints above threshold reaching the Reviewer per run, expected; the caps of 3.15 are PR 60, merge 200, RC 500 | PR 25, merge 30, canaries 300 per night |
| PA-12 | Rig pool operating day, America/New_York (decision) | 06:00 to 22:00 |
| PA-13 | PR census: smoke subset capped by CI at 40 surfaces (2.11 Scope computation per run type) plus about 40 surfaces from the manifest, map and static impact step, one workspace each | 80 checkpoints |
| PA-14 | Sign-off lead N (decision; the release train may override it per train in `policy/release_gate.yaml`) | 3 business days |

Scheduling rule by data mode (decision, stated identically in 3.1 Build pair rules and 7.9 Data modes operationally). Frozen checkpoints run base and candidate on the same rig, back to back, and the base capture is reused when it was taken under the identical fingerprint and fixture epoch: a PR run's base is the merge-base main build, already captured by its merge run; a merge run's base is the previous main build, captured as the candidate of the previous merge run; an RC run's base is the lineage capture set when its stored fingerprint equals the live one. masked_live checkpoints run base and candidate on two identically fingerprinted rigs in lockstep (the same minute; 3.1 records a slip over 60 s as `lockstep_slip`), with fingerprint equality asserted before the first capture, and their base is never reused. When only one rig is free at the moment a masked_live shard is due, its checkpoints are `not_run (reason: budget)`; they are never captured minutes apart on one rig. Tables below show no reuse (worst case) and reuse at PA-09 (expected).

### 11.2 Cadence and time budgets per run type

| Run type | Trigger and scope rule | Budget | Rigs |
|---|---|---|---|
| PR run | Branch build artifact published for an open PR (pipeline webhook). One run in flight per PR: a push while one is queued replaces it; a push while one is running lets it finish and queues the newest. Scope per 1.6 Run types and 2.11, with the smoke subset of PA-13 | 45 min | Pool, up to 4 |
| Merge run | Every merge to main; merges that outrun capacity coalesce (candidate = newest main, base = last main with a completed merge run, manifest = union, report names the range) | 3 h | Pool, 4 |
| RC run | RC cut; gate = triaged and signed off N business days before GA (PA-14, 10.9 Release-day timeline); Explorer last, or `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` when the model endpoint is down at T+6:20 (10.7); a newer RC build supersedes a run in flight (RC respin, below) | 8 h; start deadline G-N sign-off time minus 8 h | All 6 |
| Nightly run | 22:00: image mutants offline on the controller, behavioural mutants, A/A drift pass per 10.6, flake refresh, fingerprint check, fire drill and the safety canaries of 6.5 | 4 h window, dead-man 06:00 (10.2) | Rig 5 plus rig 4, which stays on after the operating day for the A/A pass |
| Calibration run | Before any threshold is used and after any fingerprint change; per checkpoint five passes on one rig from Friday night into Saturday morning and a sixth on the Saturday night of one weekend, all inside the `all_quiet` window of 7.10 | One weekend `all_quiet` window (two nights) | Sharded across the pool, rigs 1 to 4 (1.6; see below); rig 5 keeps the Nightly canaries, fire drill and safety canaries through the weekend |

Inside a run: a checkpoint past its max wait (PA-03) is `not_settled (reason: timeout)`; a flow's budget is 3 x its measured p50 (5 min until measured) and its declared `budget.max_duration_s` is checked against this table by lint rule L-FLW-10 (4.7 Flow file); the run deadline is the wall budget minus 10 min for diff, classification and report, after which the run ends `aborted_budget (reason: wall_clock)` and every unreached checkpoint is `not_run (reason: budget)`. Order: tier 1, then the manifest's declared surfaces, then longest-first within tier; budget cuts never remove a declared or smoke surface (2.11).

Rig time per side, excluding session startup (PA-01 to PA-08, PA-13): tier A census 185 min (900 x 12 s plus 4 workspace switches); tier-1 flows 60 min (40 x 90 s); tier-2 and tier-3 flows 125 min; merge sweeps 30 min (225 x 8 s); RC sweeps 128 min (960 x 8 s); tier B census 120 min (600 x 12 s); PR run 40 min (80 census checkpoints at 12 s with one workspace switch, 17 min; 75 sweep steps, 10 min; 8 tier-1 flows, 12 min). Per side: PR 40, merge 275, RC 618 min.

Rig-minutes per pair follow the scheduling rule. With S the per-side time, frozen work is 0.7 S and masked_live work 0.3 S (PA-09). Without reuse a pair costs 2 S (frozen twice on one rig, masked_live once on each of two rigs); with reuse it costs 1.3 S (frozen once, masked_live twice). Session startups: a frozen shard without reuse opens two sessions on its rig (base, then candidate), 8 min; every other shard opens one per rig, 4 min. Wall on n rigs = rig-minutes / n + startup + 10 min report.

| Run type | Pair, no reuse | Pair, reuse at PA-09 | Rigs | Wall on recommended rigs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PR run, 45 min | 80 rig-min | 52 rig-min | 2 with reuse (40 min wall); 3 without (45 min, no slack); recommended 4 | 80 / 4 + 8 + 10 = 38 min worst; 52 / 4 + 4 + 10 = 27 min expected |
| Merge run, 3 h | 550 rig-min | 358 rig-min | 4 minimum without reuse (24 min slack); 3 with reuse; recommended 4 | 550 / 4 + 8 + 10 = 156 min worst; 358 / 4 + 4 + 10 = 104 min expected; the time left (24 min worst, 76 expected) absorbs targeted re-runs and p95 settle |
| RC run, 8 h | 1,236 rig-min of pair work; soak 6 h on rig 5 from T+0:20, candidate only (the base curve is the lineage soak of the last released build, 10.11 Soak: long sessions, resource budgets and the freeze detector, so no rig is spent on a soak base); Explorer on rig 6 | 803 rig-min when the lineage captures match the fingerprint | 6 | Pair work on rigs 1 to 4 for the whole run (rig 4 stays in the pool, since the soak has no base rig): 1,236 / 4 + 4 + 10 = 323 min worst and 803 / 4 + 4 + 10 = 215 min expected by the wall formula; starting after provisioning at T+0:20, the pair work is done about T+5:30 worst case (1,236 / 4 = 309 min) with targeted re-runs to T+6:00, and about T+3:40 expected (803 / 4 = 201 min), the same times 1.9 How an RC run works shows. Rig 6 runs the chaos suite of 7.11 from T+0:20 to T+1:00, then the Explorer last, after the last scripted shard (the soak, done at T+6:20) has reported: 90 minutes, T+6:20 to T+7:50, the full 90 of its budget ending on the capture deadline T+7:50; a session that starts late is cut at T+7:50, never the other way round. Teardown T+6:20 to T+6:40 on rigs 1 to 5 and T+7:50 to T+7:55 on rig 6; report by T+8:00 |
| Nightly run | A/A scope of 10.6 (every tier-1 checkpoint, about 360, plus a rotating 20 percent of the rest, about 190) captured twice in one session, 1,100 captures at 12 s = 220 rig-min, sharded over rigs 4 and 5 so each checkpoint's two passes share one session; behavioural mutants 10, fire drill 15, safety canaries 20, fingerprint check 5 on rig 5 | same | 2 | About 2.7 h; the 4 h window is the budget |
| Calibration run | 5 x 618 min = 52 rig-hours; each checkpoint's five passes run on one rig (the brief's one-rig rule applies per checkpoint, since all VM rigs share one fingerprint), shards spread across the pool, rigs 1 to 4 (1.6); rig 5 keeps the Nightly canaries, fire drill and safety canaries | same | 4 | Friday: the Nightly A/A pass pauses for the weekend (1.6 Run types) and the Nightly canaries, fire drill and safety canaries run on rig 5 as usual (about 50 min); the five passes start about 22:15 on rigs 1 to 4 and finish about 11:10 Saturday (3,090 / 4 = 773 min); Saturday: the same short Nightly run on rig 5, and the sixth pass on rigs 1 to 4, about 2.6 h (618 / 4 = 155 min); all inside `all_quiet` (Friday 20:00 to Sunday 17:00) |

Emergency calibration (decision): a fingerprint change that was not planned as a new snapshot generation (7.2) leaves every checkpoint without a calibrated floor, so each above-zero diff is `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 until a Calibration run passes (7.13; `not_comparable` is reserved for a candidate and base that differ from each other). The pool rigs 1 to 3 then run a tier-1-only Calibration run the same night, sharded across them as 1.6 shards the weekend run (five passes of about 180 min, about 5 h on three rigs; rigs 4 and 5 carry the Nightly run), so tier-1 thresholds are valid the next morning, while tiers 2 and 3 stay `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)`, visible in every matrix and in run health, until the weekend run. Planned fingerprint changes land on Friday after the operating day for this reason.

Sensitivity (PA-03): if Phase 0 measures the census at the 20 s per visit that 2.4 budgets, the merge per-side time is 390 min; a pair without reuse is then 780 rig-min, 213 min on four rigs, over the 3 h budget, and the run proceeds by the cut rule of 2.11 with the lowest-tier census checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)` printed in the matrix; with reuse it is 507 rig-min, 141 min, inside the budget. The PR run stays inside its budget either way (49 min per side, 43 min wall worst). So a slow census makes base-capture reuse a requirement, not an optimization, or grows the pool to six pool rigs with eight logins.

Daily capacity (PA-10), counting startups: with reuse a PR run costs about 70 rig-minutes and a merge run about 375, so the day needs about 37 rig-hours, 57 percent of the 64 rig-hours a 4-rig pool offers in the operating day; without reuse about 56 rig-hours, 87 percent, above the growth trigger of R15. Base-capture reuse is therefore a Phase 1 week 4 deliverable, and the pool grows by one rig pair if two weeks of measured utilization exceed 70 percent.

Queue and saturation. Runs wait in one queue per pool with priority RC, then merge, then PR, then age. A queued run emits `run_queued` with its queue position every 60 s, which the dead-man timer (9.10 Alerting model, 10.2 Watchdog) accepts in place of `run_started` until the start deadline. Start deadlines, measured from the pipeline trigger: PR run 45 min (one budget), merge run 3 h; an RC run has the RC start deadline, the G-N sign-off time minus 8 hours (8 hours being its budget), and an RC run that cannot start by it is not aborted: the release manager decides (9.12) and the on-call and release channels are told (9.10). A PR run that has not started by its deadline is written `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)`; its comment is the abort block of 9.2 PR comment template with the text "Sentinel did not run: pool saturated, N runs ahead; push again or re-run the build job", the check `sentinel/pr-run` fails with "Sentinel did not run", and the on-call channel gets one P2 per hour naming the queue depth. A merge run that misses its start deadline is not aborted: merges coalesce, so it joins the next merge run and the report names the range. Nightly and Calibration runs have start deadlines too: a Nightly run 02:00 (its 4-hour budget before the 06:00 dead-man deadline), a weekend Calibration run Saturday 02:00 (the latest start whose five passes and Saturday-night sixth pass still end inside `all_quiet`), and an emergency calibration 01:00 (its five passes of about 5 hours end by the 06:00 start of the operating day). A Nightly or Calibration run that has not reached `running` by its start deadline, for example because rig 5 or the pool rigs cannot be provisioned or the run is stuck in its gate sequence, ends `aborted_harness (reason: start_failed)`, written by the Orchestrator when the run is on a rig and otherwise by the Reporter service; every scoped checkpoint without an outcome is `harness_error (reason: start_failed)`; the harness on-call is paged at P1 per the `aborted_harness` row of 9.10; and until a Nightly run's canaries, fire drill and safety canaries next pass, every report and the next PR comment carry the banner "canaries pending: {run type} run {run_id} did not start". A Calibration run that did not start is queued again for the next `all_quiet` window (the next night for an emergency calibration), and checkpoints without a floor stay `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` until one passes. An RC pre-emption of the Nightly run is the skip below, not this outcome. During an RC run the pool is reserved until the pair work and its targeted re-runs end (about T+4:00 expected, T+6:00 worst case): PR runs triggered in that window are held with their deadline suspended, the placeholder comment says "queued behind RC run, pool expected free at HH:MM", the check stays pending, and goal 1's 45-minute promise is suspended for that window and printed as such in the RC report. RC respin. A new RC build supersedes the RC run in flight for its train: the running run schedules no new flow, stops at the next flow boundary, runs teardown and the post-run proof on every rig, and ends `aborted_budget (reason: superseded)` with its unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`; its partial report is published labelled "superseded by {build}" (9.4); the new RC run starts at once on all six rigs with the pool reservation transferred, so queued PR runs stay held. RC runs pre-empt the Nightly run: when an RC run still holds rigs 4 and 5 at 22:00, the Nightly run is skipped and alerted (9.10), and its canaries, fire drill and safety canaries run in the next free window, on rig 5 after the RC run or at the next 22:00, before any further PR comment is trusted; until then every report and PR comment carries the banner "canaries pending: last Nightly skipped for RC run {run_id}". Outside the operating day the pool is off (11.4); a PR run triggered then is queued with the placeholder "queued until 06:00 America/New_York" and its deadline starts at 06:00. Queue depth above 3 PR runs, or any PR run waiting over 20 min outside an RC reservation, posts P2 "pool saturated".

Fleet (decision): 6 rigs, 6 logins, one login per rig. Rigs 1 to 4 are the pool; rig 5 runs the Nightly run and the soak (candidate only, compared against the lineage soak curve of 10.11); Calibration runs are sharded across the pool, rigs 1 to 4, in one weekend `all_quiet` window, while rig 5 keeps the Nightly canaries, fire drill and safety canaries (1.6); rig 4 stays on after the operating day for the Nightly A/A pass; rig 6 is the Explorer rig with the Explorer login (6.8 Explorer boundary and deny list), which cannot load the fixture workspaces, so rig 6 does no scripted work. Rig 6 is the hardware spare: it replaces a failed pool rig only after the Rig Manager re-snapshots it with that rig's login, recorded with the operator's name, because a login is never on two rigs at once.

### 11.3 Sharding and parallelism

Parallelism equals the number of logins. Each rig has one login and no login has two sessions at once whatever DR-06 finds, because positions, watchlists, alerts and settings are per login and appear in captures. The Explorer login never does scripted work.

Shards are keyed by surface tab (Monitor, Trade, Analyze, Scan, MarketWatch, Charts, Tools, Setup, each with its dialogs and context menus) and split by data mode, so a shard is all frozen or all masked_live; a shard is one session on one rig (frozen) or one session on each rig of a pair (masked_live), loads only the workspaces it needs, and is packed longest-first by measured p50. Flow shards are keyed by a stable hash of flow_id within tier and rebalanced by duration; flows touching the same server-side state declare a `state_scope` and are pinned to one shard so teardowns do not race. The shard planner assigns masked_live shards to rig pairs first, frozen shards to the rigs that remain; the Rig Manager asserts fingerprint equality on a pair before the first capture and a mismatch makes the shard's checkpoints `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)`. A frozen shard whose base capture is reused runs the candidate only; otherwise its rig runs base then candidate (one snapshot per build, 7.2 Snapshot lifecycle, so the switch is a revert to the other build's snapshot and a second session startup, counted in 11.2).

### 11.4 Cost model

Rig VMs. A rig is a 4 vCPU, 16 GB, 100 GB Windows 11 Enterprise VM (7.1 Rig specification). Rigs 1 to 3 run only in the operating day (PA-12) on business days, rig 4 also through the Nightly run, rig 5 always, rig 6 only during RC runs, plus about 60 VM-hours a month of weekend calibration: about 2,500 VM-hours a month, 4,320 if all six stay on; at an internal chargeback of 0.10 to 0.25 dollars per VM-hour including the Windows licence (placeholder) that is 250 to 625 dollars a month, or 430 to 1,080 always on. The controller host (8.1 Stores and systems of record) is one more VM or a small server with 1 TB of local NVMe (2 TB if PA-10 doubles, 8.8 Growth estimates).

Model calls. Only diffs above threshold reach the Reviewer, as 1:1 crops and heatmap plus the manifest entry, dependency edge, expected-screen text and Oracle values; identical and below-floor checkpoints cost nothing. An 800x500 crop is about 530 image tokens, so a review is about 3,000 input and 300 output tokens. The pinned model id is a DR-07 output: the brief requires zero-data-retention terms and the vendor documents its newest tier as excluded from ZDR unless expressly authorized, so the table brackets the two tiers most likely to be approved, at current list prices (confirm with the account team): mid tier 2 dollars per million input and 10 per million output tokens, top tier 4 and 20.

| Item | Volume (PA-10, PA-11) | Mid tier, dollars | Top tier, dollars |
|---|---|---|---|
| One review, synchronous | 3,000 in + 300 out | 0.009 | 0.018 |
| One review, Batch API (50 percent discount) | same | 0.0045 | 0.009 |
| One sweep-cluster review, synchronous | 4,600 in + 300 out | 0.012 | 0.024 |
| Product runs per day, synchronous for the first report | 4 x 30 + 10 x 25 = 370 | 3.33 | 6.66 |
| Nightly canaries through the full pipeline, Batch | 300 | 1.35 | 2.70 |
| Per month (22 business days, 30 nights) | | about 115 | about 230 |
| Agent-mode step (1280x720 screenshot, cached system prompt) | 5,000 in + 150 out | 0.012 | 0.023 |
| Explorer per RC run | 400 actions, 90 min, early stop after 20 actions with no new screenshot hash (6.8) | 4.80 | 9.20, cap 25 |

The global-shift pre-pass (5.8 Diff Engine, 10.6 A/A drift on the Nightly run) runs before any Reviewer call and reports a run-wide rendering shift with zero reviewer calls instead of hundreds. Hard caps, kept in `policy/budgets.yaml` of `sentinel-config` (the Explorer's action and time budgets are `policy/explorer_budget.yaml`, 4.1): reviewer items PR 60, merge 200, RC 500 (items beyond the cap are `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)`, 3.15), an agent rescue capped at 25 actions and 90 seconds (5.5) and at most 25 rescued steps per run (the per-run rescue cap of 5.5), 25 dollars per Explorer session, 50 per run, 500 per week; the Orchestrator stores every response's usage block per component and a 2x week-over-week change or a cap hit posts to the on-call channel (9.10). The three dollar caps act differently. An Explorer session that reaches 25 dollars ends the session, never the run (2.9). The per-run ceiling of 50 dollars counts every model call of the run (Reviewer, agent rescue, Explorer) and is the trigger of `aborted_budget (reason: dollar_cap)`: when the run's model spend reaches it, no further model call is made and the run ends at the next flow boundary, with checkpoints not yet captured `not_run (reason: budget)` and items still waiting for a verdict `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail` (3.15, 10.7 Degraded modes). The weekly cap of 500 stops model calls for the rest of the week in the same way and aborts no run. At the volumes in the table a run spends a few dollars, so reaching 50 means a runaway loop of rescues or reviews, not load. After the `unreviewed` report publishes with zero model calls, merge-run and nightly queues drain through the Batch API (most batches within an hour, 24-hour ceiling per vendor documentation; confirm under the agreement); every PR run item stays synchronous (3.15, 10.7 Degraded modes).

Storage follows 8.8 Growth estimates, which sizes the store at PA-10 taken as a ceiling with its own assumptions SA-01 to SA-07 (1.5 MB mean capture plus 0.1 MB of sidecars): raw growth about 31 GB per business day (about 0.7 TB a month before retention), about 370 GB hot under the retention of 8.6 Retention and backup, baselines growing about 14 GB per release. The control host therefore gets a 1 TB local NVMe volume (alarm at 70 percent; 2 TB if PA-10 doubles), the backup location 2 TB, and each rig keeps 40 GB free for its largest shard above the R7 floor of 20 GB. 8.8's figures are the ceiling this plan cites; the storage preflight uses the measured mean capture size, never this table.

### 11.5 Maintenance model

Repositories (8.1, 8.5 What lives in git and how a run pins it). `sentinel` holds the harness and is pinned per run as the harness commit. `sentinel-config` holds everything a run is asked to do: Surface Registry, Dependency Map, flows, Region Registry and masks, Workspace Corpus, popup and mutant catalogs, fixtures, eval labels, released baseline manifests, `taxonomy.yaml`, `phase0/branches.yaml`, `policy/send_policy.yaml`, `policy/release_gate.yaml`, `quarantine.yaml` (10.5) and the credential rotation calendar of 7.7 under `ops/`. CODEOWNERS routes `flows/` and `registry/` to the tier's flow owner. Every maintenance action in this section is a pull request to `sentinel-config` that passes `sentinel lint` (4.1 Conventions, repository layout and the lint; 4.15 Cross-file rules and the lint pipeline); nothing here edits SQLite by hand.

Recorder. A flow is authored by driving the app once with the Recorder on (global mouse and keyboard hook plus a screenshot per action); it emits YAML steps whose targets are image anchors (a template of about 40x20 px around a stable icon or label, versioned with the flow) plus an offset, with an OCR text anchor as the next rung and JAB first under DR-01 A. Secret steps record as `secret: vault_ref` with the hook paused and capture suspended; anchors are per display tier. Re-anchor mode shows each broken anchor beside the agent's final click target and lets the owner accept the proposed crop or re-record the step.

Pre-run anchor lint. Before every run the Orchestrator matches every anchor of every scheduled flow and every Region Registry landmark against the latest approved base-build capture of its checkpoint. A miss is a maintenance item posted to the flow owner in run health, not a checkpoint outcome; the flow still runs and ends `passed_via_agent_fallback` with the locator failure recorded as a finding, `failed` when the ladder is exhausted or fallback is disabled, or `landmark_missing` for a region. It exists so the owner hears about a broken anchor before the fallback quietly takes the flow over, and it runs in CI on every PR touching a flow, mask or registry file.

Flow fields. Every flow carries `owner`, `tier`, `last_repaired`, `agent_fallback_rate` and `flake_rate` (30-day). A successful agent fallback records the final click target and anchor crop, which Phase 3 turns into an anchor-patch PR to the owner. Two consecutive fallbacks on one step on one build open an "update scripted flow" ticket (9.9 Jira and Slack rules). Checkpoint quarantine follows 10.5 Flake tracking, targeted re-runs and quarantine exactly: flake score above 0.10 over at least 5 observations, `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` on 3 consecutive Nightly runs (10.6), the gateway drop thresholds (any safety-reason drop, or 3 integrity-reason drops in one flow, quarantine the flow; 6.2), 3 unstable outcomes in 7 days, 2 verdict flips on one build, or a non-zero frozen A/A floor unfixed for 5 business days; the Orchestrator opens the `quarantine.yaml` PR and the system owner merges it. In addition a flow whose 30-day fallback rate exceeds 5 percent is quarantined whole by the same mechanism (reason `fallback_rate`, a trigger 10.5 and 3.10 list), because a flow the agent keeps rescuing no longer tests what it was written to test. A quarantined item is `not_run (reason: quarantine)` on every run, in its own color in the coverage matrix, never covered; the owner has five business days, and exit needs the fix plus five clean captures in a Calibration run (10.5). Above 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints quarantined, run health is red and the RC gate blocks.

| Role | Hours per week | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| System owner | 16 | Run health, metrics, change control, environment changes |
| Triage rotation, one person per week | 5 | One hour per business day; one-business-day time box on every `needs_human` and `collateral`; answering two-person proposals within 4 business hours and resolving decision conflicts (9.6, 9.7) |
| Tier-1 flow owner | 4 | Repairs, re-anchoring, assertions, baseline approvals for tier 1 |
| Tier-2 flow owner | 3 | Same for tier 2 |
| Tier-3 flow owner | 2 | Same for tier 3 |
| Registry and dependency map owner | 2 | Surfaces, edges, popup catalog, one-day SLA on `unregistered_surface` and `unknown_popup` stubs |
| Accounts owner | 1 average | Fixture re-seeding on the expiration calendar, credential rotation, login ownership, SMS device under DR-03 B |
| Harness on-call | 2 average | env_error, harness_error and dead-man responses |

About 35 hours a week, under one FTE across six to eight people, reset after two releases from flows_repaired_per_release, fallback_rate_per_flow, triage minutes per run and maintenance items past SLA, all printed by the Reporter. Hours are logged per maintenance item (ticket, PR or triage decision) so the ledger is measured, not estimated.

Budget overrun (decision). When a role's logged hours exceed its budget for two consecutive weeks, the cut is made visibly, never by letting items age past SLA: the system owner quarantines the lowest-tier flows with the highest fallback or flake rate until the open backlog fits the budget, each through the `quarantine.yaml` PR with reason `maintenance_budget`; their checkpoints are `not_run (reason: quarantine)`, the coverage percent for that tier drops in the matrix and the report header prints "tier 3 coverage reduced: maintenance budget, N flows". Tier 3 is cut first, then tier 2; tier 1 is never cut this way. A tier-1 overrun pages the system owner, freezes new flows until the backlog clears (the flake kill rule of 1.5) and is reported to the release manager because tier-1 coverage below 100 percent blocks the RC gate. The same rule applies when time to triage runs above 2x target for two releases (1.5): tier-3 scope is cut and the cut is printed.

The morning after a toolbar redesign. The merge run that lands it declares the toolbar surfaces, so their census diffs classify `intended`, while diffs on undeclared surfaces that merely host the toolbar classify `collateral` and are triage's first item. Flows anchored on the toolbar miss their first rung and walk the ladder: the OCR text anchor usually holds if labels survived, otherwise the step is `passed_via_agent_fallback` with a finding or `failed` if preflight disabled fallback; regions anchored to toolbar landmarks are `landmark_missing`; run health clusters by anchor template ("38 flows in fallback, 31 on anchor toolbar_trade_tab"). Next morning triage confirms the redesign against the manifest; tier owners open re-anchor mode, accept the proposed crops for rescued steps, re-record the rest, re-anchor the landmarks, pass the lint in one PR per tier, and a targeted re-run returns `passed` in scripted mode: about 15 minutes per flow with proposals, so 40 flows is two people for half a day, against three person-days without the Recorder. The next merge run uses the redesigned build as base, so the census diffs disappear; a human approves the RC lineage baseline at the RC run.

### 11.6 On-call and ownership
