Ownership (roles defined in 6.12 Authorization, accountable owner and incident procedure and 9.12 Triage SLA and roles; every role is a named person with a deputy): the system owner is accountable for the system, owns kill criteria and change control, leads incidents and signs the RC report with the release manager; the accountable owner answers for any order sent or account restricted and receives every S1 page; the risk owner decides the OPEN `paper_send_ok` policy (6.7 Send policy: both branches) and receives every `aborted_safety`; the security contact owns the redaction list, egress allowlist, endpoint ruling and secret incidents; the Explorer owner keeps the deny list; the weekly triage rotation opens every report by 10:00 the next business day and disposes `needs_human` and `collateral` within one business day; flow owners per tier repair within five business days; the registry owner keeps surfaces, edges and popups; the accounts owner keeps logins, MFA, rotation and fixtures; the harness on-call roster answers pages; the contacts in 11.7 keep the prerequisites.

| Event | Channel | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `aborted_safety` (including `drill_order_placed`, a fire drill that placed an order row); working order found at run start; UNPROVEN post-run proof | P1 page and `#sentinel-safety` post per the safety routing of 9.10 | Immediate; rigs stay stopped until the incident procedure in 6.12 closes; after UNPROVEN or `drill_order_placed` the next run on that login is blocked until a human verifies the account (6.6, 6.5) |
| Fire drill item not blocked with no new order row: `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)`; safety canary miss: `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:<canary>)` (6.5, 10.3) | P1 per the safety routing of 9.10 | Immediate; the flows on that path are `not_run (reason: quarantine)` until the drill or the canary passes; the Nightly run itself stays `complete` |
| Gateway safety drop: `blocked_by_gateway` with a safety reason (a blocked key, or a click on a deny rect while `order_stage` is set, 6.2) | Page harness on-call and the flow owner (P1) | Immediate; the flow is quarantined `not_run (reason: quarantine)` until repaired (6.2, 10.5) |
| Gateway integrity drops: 3 in one flow; 10 in one run | S3 ticket to the flow owner; kill switch, `aborted_safety`, as above | Flow quarantined `not_run (reason: quarantine)` until repaired (6.2, 6.6) |
| `explorer_order_stage`: the ticket or dialog flag set in an Explorer session (6.8) | S1, P1 per the safety routing of 9.10 | Immediate; the session has ended and the run continues; the event counts toward the per-run trip of 10 |
| Dead-man alert (PR budget plus 15 min, merge plus 30, RC plus 60, Nightly and Calibration by 06:00) | Page harness on-call | 15 min acknowledge, root cause same day |
| Canary state `detector_blind` or `generation_failed` (P1), `detector_degraded` (P2), or `harness_error (reason: canary_path_divergence)` (P1); the Nightly run itself stays `complete` (10.3) | Page harness on-call, post to product and release channels | Report banner says the detector is blind; no RC sign-off until canaries pass |
| `aborted_harness` (any reason) | Page harness on-call (P1) | Immediate; root cause same day |
| `env_error`, `complete_with_env_errors`; the same gate in two consecutive runs escalates to P1 | On-call channel with gate name and screenshot | Next business morning; same day if an RC run is blocked |
| Login lockout or authentication challenge (`env_error` at the authenticated gate) | Page the login owner and accounts owner | Same day; the rig is out of the pool until the owner clears it, never retried by the harness (7.7) |
| Pool saturated (queue depth above 3 or a PR run waiting over 20 min); `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)` | On-call channel, P2, one per hour | Same day; two weeks above 70 percent utilization triggers R15 |
| Nightly run skipped because an RC run held its rigs (11.2) | On-call channel, P2, to harness on-call and system owner | Catch-up canaries in the next free window; the "canaries pending" banner until they pass |
| Nightly or Calibration run not at `running` by its start deadline: `aborted_harness (reason: start_failed)` (11.2) | Page harness on-call (P1), per the `aborted_harness` row of 9.10 | Immediate; the "canaries pending" banner on every report and the next PR comment until a Nightly run's canaries pass; a Calibration run moves to the next `all_quiet` window |
| RC run past its start deadline (G-N sign-off time minus 8 hours), or superseded by a newer RC build | Release channel and on-call channel, P2, to release manager and system owner | Same day; the release manager decides (9.12) |
| `not_run (reason: budget)` (masked_live checkpoints with no free rig pair included) and `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` | Run health, read by harness on-call; P2 when over 5 percent of a day's masked_live checkpoints starve (R22) | Next business day; totals go to the weekly coverage review |
| `not_run (reason: entitlement)` cells | No alert; the system owner's weekly coverage review (9.12), which asks the accounts owner for an entitled login or records the gap | Weekly |
| Reviewer backlog, model preflight failure, Reviewer disabled by a failed eval gate (10.4), deprecation notice, cost 2x week over week or a cap hit | On-call channel, P2 | 4 hours for backlog; before the next run for preflight; same day for cost |
| New high-confidence `collateral` on a tier-1 surface | PR author and triage, Slack, deduplicated by diff signature | One business day |
| `needs_human` digest | 08:00 America/New_York to triage | One business day |

Runs happen in the operating day, so after-hours on-call covers only the Nightly run and the weekend Calibration run, and only the pages 9.10 lists for that window: `aborted_safety`, `aborted_harness`, a gateway safety drop, `explorer_order_stage`, fire-drill failure (`drill_failed:<item>` or `drill_order_placed`), safety canary miss (`harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:<canary>)`), UNPROVEN post-run proof, canary state `detector_blind` or `generation_failed`, and dead-man; every other alert posts at 06:00. Message formats are in 9.10 Alerting model.

### 11.8 Phase 0 spike plan: seven decision records

Two weeks on the target rig: days 1 to 2 build the rig and attempt the pinned install (DR-04), which every other spike needs; days 2 to 4 run DR-01 and DR-06; DR-03, DR-02 and DR-07 are requested on day 1 with answers due days 5, 8 and 10; DR-05 runs days 6 to 9. Exit: all seven branches chosen and written to `phase0/branches.yaml` (a CI lint fails on any unresolved marker after day 10, per 1.4), fingerprint identical across ten launches, A/A floor recorded, security ruling in hand. Every record names a default branch so a late answer never stalls the project: at its deadline an undecided record takes its default, Phase 1 starts on it, and a later answer that changes the branch is a configuration change with its own Calibration run where 7.13 requires one.

DR-01 Java Access Bridge exposure

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | Swing app; UIA sees one SunAwtFrame. Whether the bundled runtime ships `jdk.accessibility` and what custom-painted panels expose is unverified |
| Options | A: JAB exposes names, roles and bounds. B: opaque |
| Decision rule | `java --list-modules` on the bundled runtime; module absent means B. Else `jabswitch -enable` from a full JDK of the same major (the setting survives a JRE replacement) and dump the tree for order ticket, confirm dialog, option chain, Monitor grid and Active Trader ladder. A if at least 80 percent of visible controls on all five expose name, role and bounds within 2 px of the template-located control and a dump takes under 2 s; else B, with JAB optional on panels that passed |
| Branch A | JAB is the first ladder rung and the bounds and value source (5.5 Locator ladder, 2.7 Layout invariants); a changed accessible tree at build intake (tree hash differs from the approved one) switches the affected surfaces to Branch B bounds for that run and files a `jab_tree_changed` finding for the registry owner, which stays a finding, never an outcome or a `not_comparable` reason (4.13 Outcome record); when the two builds of a pair still end up with different bounds sources, the pixel diffs that accompany the finding are `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch, field: bounds_source)` while invariants still run (1.2 Assumptions, AS-03) |
| Branch B | OCR word boxes plus templates for invariants (2.7), image anchors first, OCR and exports for the Oracle (2.8 Oracle checks) |
| Default if undecided | B; JAB can be added per panel later without a calibration change, since pixel floors do not depend on it |
| Owner, deadline | Harness lead, day 4 |

DR-02 Deterministic data fixture

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | paperMoney data is delayed 20 minutes by default (verified); OnDemand's availability on a paperMoney-only login and its stability are unverified |
| Options | A: replayable market-data mode on the test backend. B: OnDemand at a pinned, paused timestamp where the login allows, else masked_live with a larger rule set |
| Decision rule | A written yes with delivery inside Phase 1 week 4 is A, otherwise B. Inside B, 20 OnDemand launches (pinned timestamp, Go, 90 s buffer timeout, Pause, capture): OnDemand is used if at least 18 settle and two paused captures 10 minutes apart are pixel-identical outside the clock mask, else masked_live |
| Branch A | Frozen checkpoints run on the fixture, `fixture_verified` checks the epoch, PA-09 holds |
| Branch B | Frozen share drops, a rule per derived value joins the Region Registry, OnDemand account panels get their own baselines, masked_live bases are never reused and need rig pairs (rig time toward the no-reuse column of 11.2) |
| Default if undecided | B with masked_live for every quote-bearing checkpoint and fixed historical ranges for charts; PA-09 is re-measured from the registry and 11.2 recomputed at the Phase 1 exit |
| Owner, deadline | System owner with backend contact; request day 1, decision day 8 |

DR-03 Login and MFA

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | Schwab 2-step verification is reported to offer a Symantec VIP token or SMS codes, always or on untrusted devices only, with no generic TOTP option (verify); risk-based prompts can appear with 2-step off; Guest Pass logins are not used |
| Options | A: test-backend credential without MFA. B: trusted-device exemption with a scripted recovery flow and an owner on call for SMS codes during rebuilds |
| Decision rule | Platform answer by day 5; A if granted, else B, verified by establishing trust, snapshotting, reverting ten times and logging in each time (7.7); any prompt means trust is re-established before every snapshot. Both branches: one attempt per run, an authentication error is `env_error` at the `authenticated` gate, never a retry loop; risk-based prompts go to the gate state machine and on-call |
| Branch A | Scripted silent login; only the rotation calendar remains |
| Branch B | A `trusted_device_prompt` checkpoint in the login flow; rebuilds in business hours with the accounts owner on call and the team-owned SMS device at hand; a VIP software credential only with written security approval (7.7) |
| Default if undecided | B |
| Owner, deadline | Platform contact and harness lead; ask day 1, answer day 5, verified day 10 |

DR-04 Pinned build install

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | The retail launcher checks for and installs updates every start (verified) |
| Options | A: pipeline artifact installs with auto-update disabled (expected). B: a VM snapshot per build with a release-night upgrade run |
| Decision rule | Install the artifact, launch five times over two days, read build id from the window title, the JRE release file and the vmoptions hash each time; A if all three are unchanged and no update or agreement dialog appears, else B. The record also pins the main-window title regex (7.3, 10.2) and states whether the install4j launcher hosts the JVM in-process or spawns a `javaw` child (10.2 covers both) |
| Branch A | The pipeline artifact installed with auto-update disabled into its own `app.<build_id>.<gen>` snapshot (7.2); the fingerprint pins the build; a frozen shard without base reuse reverts to the base snapshot, captures, then reverts to the candidate snapshot (two session startups, 11.2, 11.3) |
| Branch B | One snapshot per build built from the launcher's own public build with the updater held (the same two-revert model, 7.2; disk joins the storage plan); the release-night upgrade run (N-1 snapshot, updater under a hard timeout, every first-start dialog captured, pre and post diff) becomes a Phase 3 flow run at every RC cut, not only at G-1 |
| Default if undecided (artifact not delivered by day 2) | B, on the public build the launcher produces, until row 1 of 11.7 lands |
| Owner, deadline | Build contact and Rig Manager owner, day 2 |

DR-05 A/A noise floor

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | Java2D text rendering is deterministic on a pinned machine; A/A noise comes from state and timing (caret, hover, tooltips, flashes, scroll and sort position, settle, live data) |
| Options | A: near-zero on frozen checkpoints. B: non-zero |
| Decision rule | Calibration run over the Phase 0 smoke census (at least 60 checkpoints across the five tier A workspaces) and five starter flows. A if at least 95 percent of frozen checkpoints have zero diff pixels outside masks across all six captures and none exceeds 0.1 percent; else B |
| Branch A | Per-checkpoint, per-region thresholds by the rule of 3.9 A/A calibration and threshold derivation: the maximum over the 15 A/A pairs times 2 with a floor of 4 px, a CIEDE2000 floor of 2.0 and a 1 px shift tolerance; masked_live `rule` regions have no pixel floor and get their own rule checks |
| Branch B | Root cause and fix per non-zero checkpoint; no threshold until the list is closed and a repeat run is clean; a floor is never raised to absorb a cause |
| Default if undecided (calibration did not complete) | B with no thresholds: every region is `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` above zero (4.8), which is loud by design, until the first clean Calibration run |
| Owner, deadline | Harness lead; days 6 to 9, fix list day 10 |

DR-06 Session rule

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | Whether a second login from another machine ends the first session is unverified; reports conflict |
| Options | The second session ends the first; sessions coexist |
| Decision rule | One login, a session on rig 1, a second on rig 2, watch rig 1 for five minutes and record any dialog; measure `session_release_wait`, the time until the first server session is gone after its process tree is killed (default 60 s, 10.2). Parallelism equals the number of logins either way |
| Branch ends | The dialog is POP-04 of the popup catalog with action abort (`env_error (gate: authenticated, reason: session_kicked)`, no re-login); a human using a rig login mid-run ends the run as `env_error` at the next gate with the screenshot; the Watchdog's relaunch kills the orphan tree first (10.2) |
| Branch coexists | No catalog entry; per-login serialization and the ownership rule stay for account-state reasons; the re-login flow checks for a surviving orphan session |
| Default if undecided | Ends, the conservative branch: the catalog entry costs nothing if the dialog never appears |
| Owner, deadline | Harness lead, day 3 |

DR-07 Computer use under the data agreement

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Context | ZDR eligibility differs by model tier, and computer use is a beta feature whose coverage under the agreement is unverified (6.10, 6.11) |
| Options | A: computer use allowed on the approved endpoint. B: agent mode and Explorer deferred; scripted flows and census carry Phase 1 |
| Decision rule | A written ruling naming endpoint, retention terms, approved tiers and computer use coverage; A needs all four. Reviewer approved without computer use is B with the Reviewer on. The record also states whether the Message Batches API exists on the approved endpoint (10.7 keeps a synchronous fallback) |
| Branch A | Agent mode is the last ladder rung with the restricted toolset; Explorer in Phase 3; model id and harness toolset schema version pinned with the deprecation alarm (10.7; agent mode uses the harness's own tool definitions, not the computer-use beta tool, so no tool type is pinned) |
| Branch B | The ladder ends at the OCR text anchor and a failed step is `failed`, never a fallback; Explorer leaves Phase 3 and the RC budget; the Reviewer runs only on the approved tier, or not at all with `unreviewed` reports |
| Default if undecided | B with zero model calls and `unreviewed` reports; the Reviewer is switched on by a later ruling without a calibration change |
| Owner, deadline | System owner with security contact; request day 1, ruling day 10 |

Phase 0 items outside the seven decision records. Each has an owner, a deadline and the default that holds until it is answered; an undecided item takes its default at its deadline, as the decision records do. 6.13 Phase 0 assumptions, both branches, and known residuals carries the safety items in full; they are spike items of the harness lead with the accounts owner for the by-hand sends on the EMPTY account.

| Item | Owner, deadline | Default until answered |
|---|---|---|
| Jira label character set: whether labels accept `/` and `.` (9.9 Jira and Slack rules) | Tooling team, day 5 | Every id-bearing label is hashed (`sentinel-cp-<12 hex>`); `sentinel-surface-<id>` is emitted only if `.` and `-` are accepted, else hashed too |
| Paging service name and webhook (9.10 Alerting model, 11.7 row 10) | Tooling team, day 5 | The firm's existing on-call paging tool; until it is wired a P1 goes by Slack mention plus email to the roster and the Alerts panel marks it "page degraded" |
| Order Confirmation dialog cancel-button label (6.2 dialog allowlist, 6.13 item 10) | Harness lead, day 4 | Allowlist `Delete` and `Edit`; any other label inside the dialog is refused and quarantines the flow |
| IRA sell-to-open rejection for the drill ticket (6.5, 6.13 item 6) | Accounts owner with the harness lead, day 6 | Branch B drill ticket: a 1-share buy limit far below market on the EMPTY account, whose worst case is a Working row the recovery Cancel All deletes |
| Package globs of the Dependency Map: list the packages of the pinned build's jars and fill `source_packages` in `registry/dependency-map.yaml`, replacing every `TBD.<area>.**` placeholder of 12.9 by pull request (4.4 L-DEP-01) | Harness lead with the primitive owners, day 10 | The `TBD.` placeholders: the scan proposes no `static_analysis` edge and the declared edges are the whole map; L-DEP-01 fails on any `TBD.` glob from Phase 1 |
| 6.13 items 1 to 5, 7, 8 and 9 (Enter as default button, Shift+click label and page, confirmation-off setting location, chart order-bubble drag, paper account id format, hotkeys honoring confirmation, login toggle memory and title-bar badge, Cancel All label and one-action behavior) | Harness lead, day 8 | The conservative branch 6.13 names for each |

The send policy is OPEN but not a Phase 0 spike item: the risk owner's `paper_send_ok` decision has a signed record in `policy/send_policy.yaml` (6.7), no deadline, and the default of no sends; until it changes every report prints the untested order lifecycle line and the matrix marks those surfaces `not_run (reason: entitlement)` (2.13 B01).

### 11.9 Phases 1 to 3

Phase 1 (6 weeks) deliverables, in build order: Rig Manager, Orchestrator gates, preflight self-tests (10.8), Input Gateway, attestation and paper-mode assertion, Watchdog (week 1); Capture with redaction, settle rule, Surface Registry for tiers 1 and 2 with validation probes P1 to P8, Workspace Corpus tier A, login flow (week 2); Diff Engine, Invariant Checker on the DR-01 branch, Stores, Calibration Service and the first weekend Calibration run (week 3); build pair with base-capture reuse and the data-mode scheduling rule, Dependency Map with the static impact step, scope computation, sharding and the queue, targeted re-runs and flake statistics, PR comment and commit status (week 4); Canary Service and mutant catalog, Nightly run, fire drill, popup catalog, kill switch with post-run proof (week 5); the acceptance test of 10.10 End-to-end acceptance test (the Flexible Grid change that overlaps the Active Trader ladder, as a mutant and as a real branch change, caught in a PR run and reported `collateral` naming FlexibleGrid) and hardening (week 6). The PR commit status is informational throughout Phase 1 (1.6). Exit, every item measured by the Reporter: the acceptance test passes in both forms on two consecutive days; the fingerprint is identical across ten launches per rig; the A/A floor is recorded for every census checkpoint and is zero on frozen ones; PR runs finish inside 45 minutes and merge runs inside 3 hours on the 11.2 fleet for two consecutive weeks; canary detection is 100 percent on money-cell mutants and the fire drill passes for seven consecutive nights with zero `aborted_safety` false alarms; every checkpoint has exactly one outcome and every `not_run` prints its reason; and the Phase 1 columns of 1.5 hold over the last two weeks: false-positive rate under 35 percent, flake rate under 5 percent, time to triage under 15 minutes per PR run and 30 per merge morning, coverage tier 1 at 100 and tier 2 at 70 percent, `aborted_harness` plus `aborted_budget` under 10 percent of runs and `env_error` under 3 percent of checkpoints.

Phase 2 (6 weeks) deliverables: tier-1 flows complete with assertions, preconditions and teardown; Oracle sources with declared tolerances; Region Registry with freeze, rule, mask and diff regions and the mask budget; size sweeps on the tier C workspace; Reviewer on the approved endpoint with the 300 to 500 item double-labeled eval set, per-category precision and recall, and change control (3.14, 3.15); decision persistence with inheritance; Jira and Slack with dedup; the metrics dashboard; the commit status starts blocking on tier-1 Unexpected findings once the false-positive target below has held for two weeks (1.6, 9.2). Exit: every tier-1 surface has a flow with assertions; the Phase 2 columns of 1.5 hold for two consecutive weeks of merge runs: false-positive rate under 20 percent, flake rate under 2 percent, time to triage under 10 minutes per PR run and 20 per merge morning, coverage tier 1 at 100, tier 2 at 90 and tier 3 at 60 percent, money-cell canaries at 100 percent and other classes at least 95 percent rolling, Reviewer `intended` precision at least 0.95 and `does_not_match_manifest` recall at least 0.98 on tier-1 eval-set mutants and at least 0.95 overall, per model and prompt version (3.14; distinct from the whole-pipeline money-cell canary rate), `aborted_harness` plus `aborted_budget` under 5 percent of runs and `env_error` under 1 percent of checkpoints; no human-disposed diff reappears undisposed; the size sweep reproduces the ladder overlap as `invariant_violation` at the recorded cell size; and the pilot exit of 1.5 is met: two release cycles, at least one real pre-release catch on an undeclared registered surface, canaries at target every night of the last cycle.

Phase 3 (6 weeks) deliverables: RC runs inside 8 hours with the lineage baseline workflow and sign-off N business days before GA under the G-N conditions of 10.9; the soak on rig 5 against the lineage soak curve, with the resource sampler and freeze detector (10.11); Explorer under DR-07 A with its own login, snapshot, deny list and budgets (400 actions, 90 minutes, 20 consecutive no-change actions, 25 dollars per session; 6.8), findings recorded as candidate flows and replayed once; tier B workspaces, including workspaces saved under the previous release; tier B configuration cells (light theme, 125 and 150 percent scaling, 1366x768 restored window, large app font) on 15 to 20 smoke flows with their own anchor sets and baselines; the D3D rig; the Recorder with re-anchor mode and anchor-patch proposals; the release-night upgrade flow under DR-04 B at every RC cut. Exit: one RC run completed inside budget, triaged and signed off before GA with the lineage baseline approved and the G-1 migration checkpoints appended; quarantine under 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints at sign-off (10.5); the Explorer stays inside its budgets with zero deny-list violations; at least 80 percent of flows authored or repaired through the Recorder in the last four weeks; fallback rate per flow under 5 percent; the kill criteria of 1.5 evaluated after two release cycles and the result recorded in the metrics history.

Beyond Phase 3, listed so the non-goals stay visible (1.3, 2.13): macOS and Linux builds, which need their own Rig Manager, Capture, Executor and locator rung and a second rig fleet; a thinkorswim Web sync flow after an automation ruling on the web client (2.13 B11); locale and time zone cells beyond en-US and America/New_York; fixed-entitlement test logins for the account states paperMoney cannot produce (B04); mixed-DPI multi-monitor rendering on physical hardware (B06). None is scheduled; the matrix prints "configurations covered: 1 of N planned" and the report header names the platform until they are.

### 11.10 Risk register

| ID | Risk | L | I | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R01 | JAB opaque or module absent (DR-01 B) | M | M | Branch B fully specified; the Recorder emits image anchors either way; false-positive controls in 2.7 Layout invariants | Harness lead |
| R02 | No data fixture and OnDemand unavailable or unstable (DR-02 B) | M | H | masked_live with a rule per derived value and fixed chart ranges; rig time re-planned from the no-reuse column, which needs rig pairs | System owner |
| R03 | MFA blocks unattended login or trust does not survive revert | M | H | DR-03 B recovery flow, rebuilds in business hours, one attempt per run; escalate for a test-backend credential | Accounts owner |
| R04 | A/A floor non-zero on frozen checkpoints | M | M | DR-05 B: root cause and fix per checkpoint, thresholds withheld until closed; A/A false-positive rate is a first-class metric | Harness lead |
| R05 | Team stops triaging | M | H | Decision persistence so nothing returns undisposed, ranked and capped Unexpected section, one-business-day SLA on a named rotation, kill criterion in 1.5 | System owner |
| R06 | Model endpoint not approved, or approved without computer use (DR-07 B) | M | M | `unreviewed` reports with zero model calls; scripted flows and census carry Phase 1; Explorer out of scope | System owner |
| R07 | Auto-update cannot be disabled (DR-04 B) | L | H | Snapshot per build, release-night upgrade flow, build id read at every launch and before every flow with a mid-run change as `env_error` | Rig Manager owner |
| R08 | Rigs render differently from user machines | H | L | Both sides of a pair render on the same pinned pipeline, so comparability holds; the D3D rig and a weekly opposite-pipeline cell cover representativeness | Rig Manager owner |
| R09 | Flows rot after every release | H | M | Anchored locators, anchor lint, re-anchor mode and anchor-patch proposals, fallback rate per flow, visible quarantine, budgeted hours and the overrun rule in 11.5 | Flow owners |
| R10 | Rendering drift (JRE bump, driver, font update) arrives as hundreds of findings | M | H | Live-read fingerprint with `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` on a pair mismatch and `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` until the new fingerprint is calibrated, global-shift pre-pass before any Reviewer call, new Calibration run after any fingerprint change | Harness lead |
| R11 | Account state drifts between runs | H | M | `verify_account_fixture` at run start, reset flow, end-of-run Cancel All and flat check, one login per rig, humans barred from rig logins | Accounts owner |
| R12 | Account lockout or automated-access restriction from repeated scripted logins | M | H | One login attempt per run, never retried (6.9, 7.7); orchestrator caps on logins, symbol changes and staged orders per hour (6.4); written authorization referenced in every run manifest (6.12); a lockout is `env_error` that pages the login owner and removes one rig, not the fleet; named incident contact at the platform team | Accounts owner |
| R13 | EDR, DLP, AppLocker or TLS inspection blocks injection, hooks, capture or egress | M | H | Prerequisite 4 before Phase 1, code-signed binaries, preflight that exercises injection, hook, capture and a 2 MB egress, each failure naming the control | Security contact |
| R14 | Pinned model retired, request shape changes (tool-definition schema), or the brief's "temperature 0" cannot be sent as one of the sampling parameters | M | M | Deprecation alarm and migration gate (3.15, 10.7); eval set re-run before any pin moves; the harness toolset schema version pinned and checked at preflight N2 (agent mode uses the harness's own tool definitions, not the computer-use beta tool, so no tool type is pinned); preflight failure disables agent fallback so flows end `failed`; the brief's "temperature 0" means what 3.12 and 3.15 define: no sampling parameters, pinned effort, byte-stable prompt, majority vote at borderline | System owner |
| R15 | Rig pool saturated | M | M | Coalesced merge runs, one PR run in flight per PR, the queue and start deadlines of 11.2 with `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)` and a comment that says so; pool and logins grow by one pair when utilization exceeds 70 percent for two weeks | System owner |
| R16 | Explorer damages shared state or pages a human | L | H | Own login with no verified contact, own snapshot, deny list, budgets, scheduled last, server-side teardown after every session | System owner |
| R17 | Registry rot: a new surface ships and nothing looks at it until the registry is updated | M | M | Registry validation probes on every run yield `unregistered_surface` with a stub PR (2.2.3); `unknown_popup` with a one-day catalog SLA; `not_registered` matrix cells never shown as passed; the registry owner's hours in 11.5 | Registry owner |
| R18 | A baseline is poisoned by a rubber-stamped or AI-suggested approval and later regressions on it read `identical` | L | H | The Reviewer never promotes or approves (3.16); approval is human-only with the two-person rule on tier 1 and 2 (9.6); approval is a pointer change, so revert is one action and any run can be re-diffed against the previous set (9.8); nightly mutants are generated from the approved capture, so a poisoned money-cell baseline is `detector_blind` the next night (10.3); 5 percent of approved-signature `noise` outcomes re-labeled weekly (10.4) | Tier flow owners |
| R19 | PR-comment fatigue when false positives exceed target, and developers stop reading | M | H | False-positive rate in every report header; Unexpected capped at 10 inline items and ranked by tier; suppression by decision; commit status informational until the Phase 2 target holds (1.6, 9.2); the 1.5 kill rule stops PR comments above 50 percent after three releases; time-to-triage printed per run | System owner |
| R20 | The release-night upgrade run finds a migration bug at G-1, too late to fix | M | M | Tier B workspaces saved under the previous release are in every merge run, so migration diffs surface at merge time (1.8); under DR-04 B the upgrade flow runs at every RC cut; a G-1 migration finding is tier 1 and blocks sign-off under 10.9 unless the release manager records an exception | Release manager |
| R21 | An unplanned fingerprint change leaves every checkpoint uncalibrated (`needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0) for days | M | H | Snapshot generations only on Friday nights with the weekend Calibration run; emergency tier-1 calibration overnight on the pool rigs 1 to 3 (11.2); the gap is visible in every matrix and in run health as `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` | Rig Manager owner |
| R22 | masked_live shards starve when no rig pair is free and silently lose coverage | M | M | The pair-first shard planner (11.3); starved checkpoints are `not_run (reason: budget)` in the matrix; a day with over 5 percent of masked_live checkpoints starved posts P2 and counts toward R15 | System owner |
| R23 | A Phase 0 decision record is undecided at its deadline and the plan stalls | M | M | Every record in 11.8 names a default branch; the lint fails on an unresolved marker after day 10; a late answer is a configuration change with its own Calibration run | System owner |
| R24 | Calibration cannot fit its window (brief: five passes back to back) once the registry is full | H | M | Per-checkpoint one-rig rule with shards across the fleet (11.2); the weekend `all_quiet` window; the budget table recomputed at every phase exit from measured p50s | Harness lead |

## 12. Appendices

Reference material for sections 1 to 11. Where a table copies a brief definition or another section's table, it copies it verbatim and names the source; where it collects vocabulary that other sections introduce, every entry names the section that produces it. Markers: `[verified]` = confirmed by official documentation or the reviewers' notes in final_gaps.json; `[unverified]` = community-reported or inferred, checked on the rig in Phase 0 with the handling branch named in the section cited; `[confirm from source]` = read from the thinkorswim source tree before Phase 1 exit. Nothing marked unverified is used as a gate value until confirmed.

### 12.1 Glossary

Terms from the brief first, then terms the sections introduced. Outcome names are defined in 12.2, invariants in 12.3, reason codes in 12.2.

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| A/A floor | Per-checkpoint, per-region diff level from comparing one build with itself in Calibration runs (3.9); thresholds derive from it (factor 2 margin, floor of 4 px). Non-zero on a frozen checkpoint = bug to fix, never a tolerance to raise. |
| Agent mode | Fourth locator rung and the Explorer's driver: the pinned model driving the harness's own tool definitions (`click_named`, `type_fixture`, `press`, `zoom`, `scroll`; Explorer-only `drag_named`), not the computer-use beta tool, only through the Input Gateway (5.6). The pinned items are the model id and the harness toolset schema version. Disabled by the N2 and N5 degraded mode when the model endpoint is unreachable (an agent-only step is then `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)`), or under DR-07 Branch B. |
| Agent rescue | One agent-mode session that completes a scripted step whose rungs 1 to 3 failed; capped at 25 actions and 90 seconds; records a `locator_failure` finding; the checkpoint it leads to is a rescued checkpoint, `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)`, which never inherits a noise or intended decision (5.5, 9.7). |
| Assumption id spaces | AS-01 to AS-12 are the assumptions of 1.2; PA-01 to PA-14 the planning assumptions of 11.1; SA-01 to SA-07 the storage assumptions of 8.8; A1 to A11 are the attestation rows of 12.6 and nothing else. |
| Anchor / anti-anchor | Template or OCR text that must be present (anchor) or absent (anti-anchor: Loading, Reconnecting, Disconnected, spinner, empty-grid placeholder) before capture (3.5). |
| Anchor lint | Pre-run and CI match of every flow anchor and Region Registry landmark against the latest approved base capture; a miss is a maintenance item, never a checkpoint outcome (11.5). |
| Anchor patch | Proposed flow change built from an agent rescue's final target and 40x20 crop; accepted by the flow owner in re-anchor mode (5.5, 9.6, 11.5). |
| Arm/deny state | In-memory shared-memory state the hook callback consults: `armed`, `deny_all`, `flag_ticket`, one-shot tokens, `move_allow`, `deny_rects`, `blocked_vk`, drop ring (5.4.2). |
| Attestation canary | Nightly check that feeds the attestation reader planted crops with every setting flipped and one unreadable crop; a miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:attestation)` and the morning report says the attestation reader is blind (6.3, 10.3). |
| Base build / candidate build | Older and newer build of a build pair (merge-base main vs branch; previous main vs new main; last release vs RC). |
| Base-capture reuse | A frozen checkpoint's base capture is reused when it was taken under the identical fingerprint and fixture epoch; masked_live checkpoints capture both sides in the same window every run (11.1). |
| Baseline | Approved capture set per checkpoint; lifecycle candidate -> approved -> retired; approval human-only (9.8). |
| Blocked key set | Keys and chords the hook drops while `flag_ticket` is set or unknown: Enter (both), Space, Ctrl+Enter, Shift+Enter, Alt+Enter, Alt+letter, Shift-held clicks, every attested order hotkey (5.4.7). |
| Build pair | Candidate vs base, both from pipeline artifacts, on identically fingerprinted rigs in the same data window (3.1). The unit of comparison. |
| Calibration cause class | Label the Calibration Service puts on a non-zero floor: `caret`, `hover`, `tooltip`, `flash`, `scroll`, `sort`, `live_data`, `settle`, `landmark_jitter`, `unknown`, each with a standard fix (3.9). |
| Calibration run | Per checkpoint, 5 captures back to back on one rig plus 1 on a second night, run in one weekend `all_quiet` window sharded across the pool, rigs 1 to 4; every checkpoint's captures stay on one rig, so the brief's "5 times on one rig" is per checkpoint, not the whole library serially. The Nightly A/A pass pauses that weekend, and the Nightly canaries, fire drill and safety canaries stay on rig 5 (1.6, 3.9, 11.2, 7.13). Yields the A/A floors; required before any threshold is used; re-run on a fingerprint change. A fingerprint without one diffs at threshold 0 as `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)`. |
| Emergency calibration | A tier-1-only Calibration run the same night on the pool rigs 1 to 3, sharded as the weekend run is, after a fingerprint change that was not planned as a new snapshot generation; until it passes, above-zero diffs are `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 (11.2, 7.13, 11.10 R21). |
| Canary | Nightly injection of mutants as candidate images through the normal diff and review path (10.3). Also `canary_flow_passed`, the gate that runs one known-good flow first (5.2). |
| Canary result states | Per mutant: `detected`, `missed`, `detector_blind` (a money-cell mutant missed), `detector_degraded` (a class below its rolling floor), `generation_failed` (the mutant could not be generated). The worst state becomes `detector_state` in `system_state`, which pages P1 for `detector_blind` and `generation_failed` and puts the banner on every report until the next green Nightly run. They are neither checkpoint outcomes nor reason codes, and the Nightly run's own outcome stays `complete`; it is `aborted_harness (reason: canary_generation_failed)` only when no canary could run at all (10.3, 12.2). |
| Canary detection versus Reviewer recall | Two different numbers. Canary detection of money-cell mutants through the whole deployed pipeline must be 100 percent, else `detector_blind` (10.3, 1.5). The Reviewer's eval-set recall gate on tier-1 items is at least 0.98 per model and prompt version (3.14). Neither substitutes for the other. |
| Census | Visit every Surface Registry surface in every Workspace Corpus workspace that hosts it, capture, diff against base, run invariants (2.4); a persona whose workspace does not host a surface is `not_run (reason: scope)` for that cell by design. Baseline-free and flow-free. |
| Central Store and Run Store | The Run Store is the SQLite WAL database plus `results.jsonl` of one shard on its rig, written only by the Orchestrator; the Central Store on the control host is written only by the Reporter service, which imports every shard at `reported` and owns the API the report UI and one-click actions call. The Watchdog never writes SQLite; it writes a JSONL journal the Orchestrator ingests (8.1, 8.2, 5.13, 10.2). |
| Change manifest | Per-PR list of entries: tickets, declared surfaces, touched primitives, changed paths, expected visual, optional mock image (4.3). The reviewer's only source of intent. |
| Checkpoint | Named capture point in a flow, census visit or sweep step; declares target window and data mode; ends in exactly one outcome. Id format `<kind>/<surface-id>/<qualifier>` with kind `census`, `sweep`, `split` or `flow` (4.1): a census qualifier is the workspace id, a sweep qualifier `<host>/<w>x<h>` with host `tab`, `sidebar`, `flexgrid`, `detached` or `dialog` (for example `sweep/charts.flexible-grid.active-trader-cell/flexgrid/480x360`), a flow qualifier `<flow-id>/<step-id>` with the full `flow_id` including its `flow.` prefix (for example `flow/dialog.order-confirmation/flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit/s07`) (2.5.2, 4.7, 8.3). |
| Classification decision table | The first-match-wins rule list of 3.11 over ten inputs (G gate, H hard checks, B base, D diff level, S stability, M decision memory, T threshold source, P path, X manifest, R reviewer) that gives each checkpoint one outcome in the 1.10 precedence. Row 1a (G `app`) is the app failure `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)`; row 9a (H `unreadable`, zero or below-floor diff) is `needs_human (reason: oracle_unreadable)` or `needs_human (reason: bounds_unreadable)`; row 11a (P `rescued`, zero or below-floor diff) is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)`; rows 24 to 26 (B `removed`) give `intended` when the Reviewer confirms the removal, `needs_human` with `review_state: pending` while the verdict is pending, `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` when a declared removal is not confirmed (row 25a), and `collateral` when no manifest entry declares the surface (row 26). When two `needs_human` reasons apply, the first in row order wins and the rest go in `detail` (12.2). |
| Churn calendar | Dated list of option expirations, futures rolls, exchange holidays, earnings and ex-dividend dates for fixture symbols, generated from the exchange calendar and the market-data API; an epoch change on a frozen region triggers baseline re-approval, never scored diffs (7.9, 4.9). |
| Coalesced merge run | When merges outrun capacity, one merge run compares the newest main with the last main that has a completed merge run; manifest is the union and the report names the range (11.2). |
| Collateral | Above-threshold diff on a surface the manifest did not declare, including a UI-touching PR with no manifest (3.11 rows 16 and 17), and a removed surface that no manifest entry declares (row 26); a declared removed surface the Reviewer does not confirm is `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` (row 25a). A later diff that matches a `confirm_bug` decision keeps its computed outcome and is listed under Known bugs. Highest-priority finding. |
| Coverage matrix | Surface x persona x entitlement profile; every cell `covered`, `not_run` (reason) or `not_registered` (2.12). |
| Data epoch | Window date, dataset id or OnDemand timestamp, front-month futures contract, nearest option expiration, delayed or real-time state, 24-hour list hash; a fingerprint field, so a pair mismatch is `not_comparable` (3.2, 7.4, 7.9). Also called fixture epoch. |
| Data mode | `frozen` (deterministic fixture, or OnDemand paused at a pinned timestamp) or `masked_live` (paperMoney delayed data with the Region Registry) (3.2, 7.9). |
| Dead-man alert | Alert for a run that reached `running` (scope manifest uploaded, `run_started` received) and then stopped reporting: no run-completed event by the run's deadline plus grace; the run row is written `aborted_harness (reason: dead_man)` and every checkpoint left without an outcome `harness_error (reason: dead_man)`, the run's abort reason (10.2, 9.10). A run that never reached `running` is never `dead_man`: at its start deadline a PR run is `aborted_budget (reason: pool_saturated)`, a merge run is coalesced into the next merge run, an RC run is decided by the release manager, and a Nightly or Calibration run is `aborted_harness (reason: start_failed)` with the "canaries pending" banner on the next PR comment (11.2, 9.12); a trigger with no `run_started` or `run_queued` within 15 minutes raises the alert as "run not started". |
| Decision | Human triage verdict persisted in SQLite by diff signature; matching diffs on later runs inherit it (9.7, 4.14). A row carries both the UI action (4.14 enum) and the stored verdict (`confirmed_bug`, `intended`, `noise`), and a `source` of `report_ui`, `pr_comment`, `jira_sync` or `explorer_triage`. Status is `active`, `expired`, `superseded` (a newer row replaced it), `reopened` (a fixed signature returned) or `revoked` (a human withdrew it; the revoked fields are set). The lookup returns every active decision within tolerance; conflicting verdicts inherit nothing and are listed as conflicting. Actions, verdicts and inherited outcomes are in 12.2. |
| Detector state | `detector_state` in `system_state`: `ok` or the worst canary result state of the last Nightly run; source of the detector banner (10.3, 9.2). |
| dialog_ok | The slow half's proof, written to shared memory, that its synchronous re-check of the window under the pointer ran for this click; the hook requires it on every button down while `flag_ticket` is set (5.4.2, 5.4.3). |
| Decision records DR-01 to DR-07 | The seven Phase 0 unknowns written as decision records with both branches (11.8): JAB exposure, data fixture, login and MFA, pinned install, A/A floor, session rule, computer use. |
| Deny rects | Inflated bounds of send-like controls currently visible, written by the Window Watcher; the hook drops any button down inside them (5.4.2, 5.4.6). |
| Dependency Map | Git YAML, primitive -> consuming surfaces, derived by bytecode scan with a human overlay (2.10.1, 4.4); drives PR-run scope. Starter in 12.9. |
| dependency_map_gap | Finding (not an outcome) when the static impact step finds an edge the map lacks; edge proposed as a PR (2.10.2). |
| Dialog allowlist | Inside the Order Confirmation dialog only a button whose label is exactly in the pinned set (expected Delete and Edit) may be clicked; elsewhere the slow half refuses labels matching `/send\|submit\|replace\|flatten\|blast\|auto/i` (6.2). |
| Diff signature | Checkpoint id, region id (or 8x8 grid cell), 64-bit pHash of the anchored crop with Hamming tolerance (8 default, 6 for tier 1 and for clustering), category (9.7). |
| Dismiss allowlist | OCR labels the dismiss-only toolset may click on an unmatched popup: OK, Close, Later, Not now, Dismiss, Cancel; never Accept, Agree, Confirm, Send, Yes (7.8). |
| Egress log | Per-run record of every artifact or message that left the rig, with destination, purpose, bytes, redaction version and status (6.10, 8.3). |
| Entitlement | Login capability a surface or flow needs, from the closed vocabulary of 2.2.1 and 4.5: `margin`, `options_L1`, `options_L2`, `options_L3`, `futures`, `forex`, `ira`, `portfolio_margin`, `multi_account`, `paper_send`. Paper send is modeled as an entitlement until the `paper_send_ok` decision; a missing entitlement is `not_run (reason: entitlement)`. |
| Environment fingerprint | Live-read tuple at `provisioned` and `launched`, 22 fields (7.4, 4.12): build id, JRE release, vmoptions hash, jar listing hash, Java2D pipeline, `render_probe_hash`, Windows build, display, ClearType, GPU, OS theme, app theme (color scheme and font size), workspace hash, settings profile hash, time zone, keyboard, data epoch, account, input desktop, rig, harness, run date. Pair mismatch on a match field = `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` naming the field; a fingerprint with no Calibration = `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 and a Calibration run queued (7.13). |
| Eval set | 300 to 500 labeled items (mutants 40 percent, A/A pairs 15, real intended 25, wrong-manifest 10, labeled real diffs 10), 70/30 development and held-out split; gates in 3.14. |
| Explorer | Bounded sixth activity: agent, own login and snapshot, deny list, budgets of 400 actions, 90 minutes, 25 dollars and early stop after 20 consecutive no-change actions; last in RC runs only, on rig 6 from T+6:20 to T+7:50 after the soak reports (1.9, 11.2); budget exhaustion ends the session, never the run; findings replayed once before reporting, and the replayed flow's outcome is `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` or `needs_baseline` with the trace, never `needs_human` (2.9, 6.8). `drag_named` is allowed only on splitters and detach handles; order-bubble drags are denied as order paths. The deny list also covers the chart and grid context-menu Buy and Sell items, BUY MKT and SELL MKT, every ladder or Level II bid and ask cell and every order-entry button; three denied attempts end the session, and a ticket or dialog flag set in the session ends it with the `explorer_order_stage` finding while the run continues. With the model endpoint down the session does not start and is `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` (10.7). |
| Explorer candidate flow | A reproducing Explorer finding written as `flows/quarantine/<finding-id>.yaml` with `class: explorer_candidate`; a human trims and promotes it (2.9, 4.7 L-FLW-14). |
| explorer_order_stage | Finding (not an outcome) raised when the ticket or dialog flag is set in an Explorer session: the gateway drops all input, closes the window through its recovery path (the Escape token), ends the session and counts it toward the per-run trip of ten drops; an S1 routed by the safety routing of 9.10 (P1 to the `aborted_safety` recipients and the Explorer owner, posted to `#sentinel-safety`); the run itself continues. The 30-second open-dialog kill-switch timer applies to scripted flows and agent rescue only (2.9, 5.4.6, 6.8, 4.13). |
| Failure classes | Harness, environment and app failures (10.1); none enters the Diff Engine, the Invariant Checker or the Reviewer. |
| Fire drill | Nightly attempt of every forbidden send path (Enter, Space, Ctrl+Enter on the Order Confirmation dialog; Auto Send ladder click; bound hotkey chords; Shift+click; kill switch end to end); passes only if the gateway blocked each and Monitor > Activity and Positions shows no new row (6.5). An item not blocked with no new row is `harness_error (reason: drill_failed:<item>)`, the flows on that path quarantined; a new order row is run `aborted_safety (reason: drill_order_placed)` and the login is blocked. Both page P1 per the safety routing of 9.10. |
| First-launch rule | A crash or hang signal during the gate sequence of a shard's first launch, before `launched` passes as well as after, is an app failure like any other: `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with the cause in `detail` on the shard's first checkpoint, finding `app_crash`, one relaunch consumed, never `env_error`; with the relaunch budget spent the run is `aborted_budget (reason: app_restart_budget)` and the unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`. A missing main frame with no crash or hang signal at first launch stays `env_error (gate: launched)` (10.1, 10.2, 5.2). |
| Fixture | Declared login, accounts, symbols, positions, watchlists, settings profiles, data mode, epoch and churn calendar (4.9); restored by the fixture reset flow (7.6), verified by `verify_account_fixture`; drift = `env_error (gate: fixture_verified, reason: fixture_drift)`. The fixture epoch (data epoch plus fixture file hash plus golden `seeded_at`, 7.9) is one of the two keys for base-capture reuse. |
| Fixture reset flow | Scripted-only two-stage flow: profile (Application Settings page by page, watchlists, alerts, saved orders, studies, drawings) closing `settings_attested`; account (`verify_account_fixture`, Reset All Balances and Positions, Set Account Cash) closing `fixture_verified` (7.6). |
| flag_ticket (order-stage flag) | Gateway knowledge that an order could be sent from the current screen: OR of window enumeration, the send-control template detector and the flow step's `order_stage: true` declaration; cleared only after two clear polls; `unknown` is treated as set (5.4.6, 6.2). |
| Flake | Verdict flip between runs of one build or between targeted re-runs; tracked per checkpoint in `flake_stats` (10.5). |
| Flow | YAML sequence of header, preconditions, steps, checkpoints, assertions and teardown (4.7); classes standard, login, fixture_reset, teardown, canary, paper_send_ok, explorer_candidate. |
| Gateway drop | Step event for every event the hook dropped or the slow half refused, stored in `step_events` with `gate_decision` `dropped` or `refused`, `gate_reason` (the 5.4.3 or 5.4.4 code, never a coarse class) and `gate_class` `safety` or `integrity`, plus mode, point and keys (5.4.8, 8.3, 4.13). Drop counts are rows with `gate_decision IN ('dropped','refused')`. A safety-reason drop (a blocked key, or a click on a deny rect while `order_stage` is set) quarantines the flow and pages P1; integrity-reason drops (token mismatch, expired token, stale state) get one retry, three in one flow quarantine the flow and ten in one run trip the kill switch. An attempted send on a scripted flow or its agent rescue ends the run `aborted_safety`; in an Explorer session it ends the session and counts toward the ten. |
| GOLDEN and EMPTY | Roles of the two paper accounts on one login: margin account seeded with the golden portfolio by a named human; IRA account kept empty for census, sweeps and most flows (7.6, 4.9). |
| Hook host | The gateway's fast half: a separate stdlib-only Python process holding `WH_MOUSE_LL` and `WH_KEYBOARD_LL`, consulting only the seqlock shared memory, failing closed to `deny_all` when the Orchestrator dies (5.4.2, 5.4.4). One of the three harness processes with the Orchestrator and the Watchdog. |
| Identity canary | Nightly dry run of the paper-mode assertion against a synthetic live-format selector and a `D-` id not on the allowlist; both must abort (6.4). A miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:identity)` with the dependent flows `not_run (reason: quarantine)`; the run stays `complete` (4.13, 10.3). |
| Identity fields | The account number and the account holder (login display) name wherever they appear: always redacted in Capture (3.6, 6.10), excluded from the mask budget, never a region, never diffed and not money cells; proven nightly by the redaction canary and the redaction mutant M19. A miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:redaction)` (3.8, 4.8, 12.5). |
| Input Gateway | Only path to the OS for flows, agent mode and Explorer. Slow half resolves and tokens before emission; the hook consults only arm/deny state (5.4, 6.2). |
| Intended | Declared surface and the reviewer confirms the diff matches the manifest entry at or above the 0.80 routing threshold (3.11 row 20). |
| Invariant | Baseline-free rule about bounds, text, labels and colors (12.3). Violations are outcomes and are never reclassified; a violation is re-captured once to confirm it persists (3.10). An enabled invariant that fires on a Nightly A/A pair is `harness_error (reason: invariant_on_aa)` (2.7). |
| Kill switch | File flag (controller command over the hypervisor guest channel) plus named pipe, both proven by preflight H5, and automatic trip-wires: hook drops all events, process tree killed, fresh scripted login does verified Cancel All and diffs Working and Filled against the start snapshot (6.6). |
| Known bugs | Report section listing findings that inherit an open `confirm_bug` decision, with ticket status and age (9.4). |
| Ladder S and Ladder F | Size-sweep ladders (2.5.2). S: widths {320, 480, 640, 960} by heights {360, 480, 720}, 12 steps, PR and merge runs. F: 6x6 grid {320, 400, 480, 640, 800, 960} by {300, 360, 420, 480, 600, 720}, four corners with MAXW and MAXH, corpus sizes and an ascending pass, about 46 steps plus corpus, RC runs. Both contain 480x360. Splitter sets: short {0.15, 0.50, 0.85}, full {0.00, 0.15, 0.30, 0.50, 0.70, 0.85, 1.00}. |
| Landmark | Template-located feature from which regions, masks and redactions are offsets (3.7). Missing = `landmark_missing`, never a blind diff. |
| Lineage baseline | Approved capture set of the last released build on the same release channel; the base for RC runs; re-captured when its stored fingerprint differs from the live one (3.1, 9.8). |
| Locator ladder | JAB -> image anchor -> OCR text anchor -> agent; one scripted retry after `reset_input_state`; rung logged per step (5.5). |
| locator_failure | Finding, never an outcome, recorded when every scripted rung of a step failed, whether the agent rescued the step (`passed_via_agent_fallback`) or it ended `failed`; carries every rung's result, the pre-attempt screenshot, the agent trace, the final target, the 40x20 crop and the proposed anchor patch (5.5, 1.10, 4.13). |
| Lockstep | masked_live checkpoints run on two identically fingerprinted rigs within 60 s of each other; a larger slip re-queues the pair once and a second slip is `not_run (reason: budget)`, counted as `lockstep_slip` in run health (a counter, never a finding); if only one rig is free they are `not_run (reason: budget)` (3.1, 1.6). |
| Mask | Region allowed to change, with owner, reason, ticket, expiry (default 30 days), human creator, per-critical-panel budget over masks plus non-identity redaction boxes: Order Confirmation 10 percent, order entry 10, Position Statement 10, Account Info 5, money cells 0 (3.8, 4.8). The report UI refuses a mask request that would exceed a budget and the finding stays open until `confirm_bug` or `mark_intended`; raising a budget is a system-owner PR to `sentinel-config` (9.6). |
| mask_budget_exceeded | Run-time breach of a mask budget: a landmark move or geometry change pushes a panel's masked plus non-identity redacted share over its budget, or a mask or redaction box lands on a money cell; the checkpoint is `harness_error (reason: mask_budget_exceeded)` with the panel and share in `detail`, and a `mask_budget_exceeded` finding goes to on-call and the mask owner (3.8, 4.8, 4.13). One spelling everywhere. |
| Merge run | Every merge to main; new main vs previous main; full census plus all tier-1 flows; 3 hours; 4 pool rigs (1.6, 11.2). |
| Missed in PR run and missed by static impact; `missed_in_pr_run` | Merge-run report labels (1.8, 9.4), both stored as the finding kind `missed_in_pr_run`. "Missed in PR run": a merge-run finding on a surface its PR run had in scope but did not report; it opens a harness task. "Missed by static impact": a finding on a surface the candidate's dependency index reaches from a class a merged PR changed, whose PR run had the surface `not_run (reason: scope)`; it is the same kind with `detail: static_impact` and opens a harness task for the system owner (1.10, 4.13). |
| model_unavailable | `not_run` reason for an Explorer session or an agent-only step skipped because the model endpoint is down (the N2 and N5 degraded mode); counted in run health for the harness on-call and in the weekly coverage review, and printed in the RC report as "Explorer: not run, model endpoint unavailable" (10.7, 9.12). |
| Money cell | Qty, Price, Buying Power Effect, Max Loss and the Send, Cancel and Delete buttons: always pixel-diffed and rule-asserted, a `diff` (or `freeze`) region at a zero floor that also carries an Oracle rule, never `rule` only and never `mask` (L-RGN-04); 0 percent mask budget; 100 percent canary detection (3.8, 4.8, 10.3). The list is closed: the ladder price column, P/L, balances and the BUY and SELL labels are tier-1 regions, not money cells, and their mutants are non-money, counting toward `detector_degraded` (12.5). A change to Buying Power Effect inside the R02 bracket on an undeclared surface is therefore `collateral`. The account number and holder name are identity fields, not money cells. |
| Mutant | Deterministic synthetic fault image from an approved capture with the catalog seed 20260101, or a behavioural canary flow on the live app; one catalog, `sentinel-config/canaries/mutants.yaml`, ids M01 to M33 in 12.5; `synthetic: true`, never promotes a baseline, never creates a decision, never counts in product metrics (10.3, 12.5). |
| Never-tokenize list | Resolved control names the slow half refuses in every profile: Send, Confirm and Send, Auto Send, Flatten, Blast All, plus the Explorer deny list under profile `explorer` (5.4.3). |
| Nightly run | Canaries, A/A drift on current main, flake refresh, fingerprint check, fire drill and the other safety canaries; 22:00 on rig 5, with the A/A pass sharded over rigs 4 and 5. Not a product test (1.6, 11.2). An RC run pre-empts it: a skipped Nightly run is alerted, its canaries run in the next free window, and until then every report and PR comment carries the banner "canaries pending: last Nightly skipped for RC run {run_id}" (11.2, 9.10). |
| Noise / noise signature | Diff below the A/A floor (`noise (reason: below_floor)`), or matching a human-approved pattern persisted as a `noise_signature` decision with a 30-day expiry (`noise (reason: decision:<id>)`); never assigned by the Reviewer (3.11, 4.13, 9.7). |
| Normalize routine | Flow-declared steps run before a rescued capture or a targeted re-run: Escape, park the mouse, drop focus, reset scroll, reselect the sub-tab (5.5, 10.5). |
| Not detectable by design (B01 to B15) | Stable ids for classes the model does not look at, printed in every merge and RC report with their label mechanism (2.13). |
| One-shot token | Per-event permission the slow half writes to shared memory: coordinates with 2 px tolerance, 500 ms expiry, `half_consumed` on button down, `consumed` on button up; the hook drops any event without one (5.4.5). |
| Operating day | 06:00 to 22:00 America/New_York for the rig pool (PA-12); after hours only the Nightly run and the weekend Calibration run, with pages only for `aborted_safety`, `aborted_harness`, a gateway safety drop, `explorer_order_stage`, fire-drill failure (`drill_failed:<item>` or `drill_order_placed`), UNPROVEN proof, canary state `detector_blind` or `generation_failed`, and dead-man (11.1, 11.6, 9.10). |
| Outbox | Table of every outbound post (PR comment, commit status, Jira, Slack, page) written through the single writer before the send; retried at 1, 2, 5, 15 and 60 minutes then hourly to 24 hours; 15 minutes of failure raises the integration outage alert, 24 hours marks the job `abandoned` (9.1). |
| Oracle | Numeric truth layer: OCR on 3x upscaled inverted crops, CSV export, grid copy, JAB values, market-data API, fixture (2.8.1); evaluates assertions and the arithmetic rules R01 to R10 within declared tolerances. |
| Oracle rules R01 to R10 | Arithmetic invariants of 2.8.3: cost arithmetic, buying-power consistency, bid-mark-ask order, strike and expiration counts, Greeks bounds, put-call parity (SPX only), DTE, P/L Open, export totals, number format. A failure is `assertion_failed`. |
| paper_send_ok | OPEN flow class for identity-gated 1-share or 1-contract far-from-market DAY limit paperMoney sends with a single-use send token; both branches in 6.7; switched by `policy/send_policy.yaml`. |
| Paper-mode assertion | Account selector text after login, before every flow, after re-login, on a two-minute timer and before any order-stage step must equal one entry of the rig's hard-coded allowlist of exact paper account ids (not a `D-` prefix check); else deny-all, kill process tree and `aborted_safety`: reason `live_identity` for a live-format id, which also blocks the login, and `paper_mode_mismatch` for any other text that is not an allowlist entry; unreadable twice is `env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: identity_unreadable)` (6.4). |
| Persona | Workspace archetype: active trader, options trader, futures trader, swing trader, beginner default; matrix columns (2.3, 2.12). |
| Popup catalog | Versioned list of title regex plus template plus action for windows the app throws on its own (7.8, 4.10, 12.8). Unmatched = `unknown_popup` finding. |
| Post-run proof | Report section ORDER SAFETY PROOF with one of four verdicts: PROVEN: no orders sent; PROVEN: only declared sends (gated branch); PROVEN: no session established (the login never authenticated and the gateway log shows no token issued); UNPROVEN with reason `recovery_login_failed`, `monitor_unreadable`, `cancel_all_failed`, `snapshot_missing` or `session_unavailable` (a kicked session's login still unavailable after one retry). UNPROVEN makes the run `complete_with_env_errors` (or leaves it `aborted_safety`), pages P1 and blocks the next run on that login until a human verifies the account (6.6, 8.3, 12.2). |
| PR run | Branch build vs merge-base main; Dependency Map expansion of the manifest plus static impact plus the smoke subset; 45 minutes, sharded on up to 4 pool rigs (1.6, 2.11, 11.2). |
| Pre-existing violation | An invariant violation present on both builds: reported once, one severity level lower, keyed by diff signature; never dropped (2.7). |
| Pre-input checkpoint | Ticket flow checkpoint taken right after the ticket appears, asserting default quantity, order type, price basis, TIF and routing before any typing (2.6.3). |
| Popup sentinel and Window Watcher | The Window Watcher is the slow half's poller that enumerates the process tree's top-level windows, writes `flag_ticket`, `deny_rects` and `blocked_vk` every poll and stamps `watcher_mono_ts`; the popup sentinel is its pass before every step and capture that matches unexpected windows against the popup catalog (5.4.3, 5.4.6, 7.8). |
| Proposal | A PR author's Mark intended click on a tier-1 or tier-2 diff of their own PR: stored on the finding, shown in the triage queue with a 4-business-hour clock, and written as a decision only when a second person confirms (9.6, 9.12). |
| Primitive | Shared UI building block the Dependency Map keys on: FlexibleGrid, Docking, ColumnModel, Theme, FontMetrics, ChartEngine, OrderTicketCore, SymbolLinking, QuoteStream (brief 1.3) and LadderModel (2.2.1); PascalCase ids (4.4). |
| Proof canary | Nightly dry run that plants one extra Working row in the end snapshot and must yield `aborted_safety` naming the row (6.6). |
| Quarantine | Visible `not_run (reason: quarantine)` for a checkpoint whose flake score exceeds 0.10 over 5 observations, or with `not_settled (reason: aa_drift)` on 3 consecutive Nightly runs, or past a gateway threshold (one safety-reason drop, or three integrity-reason drops in one flow), or with 3 unstable outcomes in 7 days, 2 verdict flips on one build, or an unfixed non-zero frozen floor, or in a flow whose 30-day agent-fallback rate exceeds 5 percent (the whole flow, reason `fallback_rate`) (3.10, 10.5, 11.5); drill and safety-canary flows (6.5) are exempt: a trigger on one pages per the safety routing of 9.10 instead of quarantining it (3.10); exit needs a fix plus 5 clean calibration captures. Above 2 percent of tier-1 checkpoints quarantined blocks the RC gate. |
| Quarantine share | Tier-1 checkpoints `not_run (reason: quarantine)` over registered tier-1 checkpoints; above 2 percent at an RC cut blocks the RC gate (1.5, 9.11, 10.5). |
| Quiet window | Span from the exchange-calendar library (America/New_York) in which a symbol's data does not move; named windows `all_quiet`, `equities_quiet`, `futures_break`, `none` (7.10). |
| RC run | RC build vs lineage baseline; full census, all flows, Ladder F sweeps, soak, Explorer last; 8 hours on all 6 rigs; signed off N business days before GA (1.6, 10.9). A newer RC build supersedes a running one (RC respin), and an RC run must start by the RC start deadline. |
| RC respin (superseded RC run) | A new RC build of the same train supersedes the RC run in flight: the running run schedules no new flow, stops at the next flow boundary, runs teardown and the post-run proof, and ends `aborted_budget (reason: superseded)` with its unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`; its partial report is labelled "superseded by {build}"; the new RC run starts at once with the pool reservation transferred (1.6, 11.2, 9.4, 9.10). |
| RC start deadline | The G-N sign-off time minus 8 hours, that is 8 hours before the release gate (1.6, 11.2); an RC run that cannot start by it is not aborted: the release manager decides (move GA, sign on the last complete RC run with an exception, or accept a shortened scope), alerted P2 to the release manager and system owner (9.10, 9.12). |
| Recorder | Flow-authoring tool: global hook in observe mode plus screenshot per action, emits anchored YAML with about 40x20 px templates; pause on the login dialog; re-anchor mode (5.16, 11.5). |
| Redaction stage | Capture step masking the identity fields (account number, account holder or login name) and other identifiers by anchored boxes plus an OCR-regex sweep, before storage, diff or egress; only redacted artifacts exist outside Capture memory. Identity boxes are excluded from the mask budget; every other redaction box counts toward it (3.6, 6.10). |
| Redaction canary | Nightly synthetic frames with planted identifiers; re-OCR must find zero hits and one request to a non-allowlisted host must be refused (6.10). A miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:redaction)` (10.3). |
| Region Registry | Per checkpoint, every region is `freeze`, `rule`, `mask` or `diff`, anchored to landmarks, with its own threshold from the A/A floor; pixels outside declared regions form the implicit `_rest` diff region (3.8, 4.8). |
| Registry validation probes P1 to P8 | Eight OCR and template enumerations run at `workspace_loaded` on both builds and diffed against the registry (2.2.3): P1 top tabs, P2 sub-tabs and sections, P3 sidebar gadgets, P4 Setup entries, P5 settings pages, P6 ticket and chain selectors, P7 context menus, P8 Flexible Grid cell contents and detach controls (sets `hosts` and `resizable`). |
| render_probe_hash | Perceptual hash of the Help > About text region captured after `authenticated`, compared at Hamming distance zero; turns a rasterization change into one fingerprint mismatch (3.3, 7.3). |
| Rescued checkpoint | A checkpoint reached through `passed_via_agent_fallback`, captured after the normalize routine, tagged `rescued`; its outcome is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)` unless a higher-precedence outcome applies; it is never `intended` or `noise` automatically (5.5, 3.1). |
| reset_input_state | Key-up Shift, Ctrl, Alt, Win; mouse-up all buttons; optional Escape; at flow start, teardown, every exception handler and Watchdog recovery (5.4.10). |
| Reverse reconciliation | Checking that every manifest entry was actually observed: the manifest coverage table prints "no covering checkpoint" or "declared change not visible" per entry (2.12); the reviewer's Task C `manifest_visibility` emits the `intended_change_not_observed` finding (3.12); the merge and RC reports carry the reconciliation (9.4). |
| Reviewer | Pinned Claude model on the approved zero-retention endpoint, structured output, byte-stable prompt, pinned effort, majority vote at borderline; the brief's "temperature 0" means no sampling parameters are sent (3.12, 3.15). Verdict vocabulary in 12.2. Never promotes baselines, creates masks or overrides invariants and assertions (3.12 to 3.16). |
| Reviewer version | The tuple (model id, prompt hash, schema version, few-shot ids, effort, crop policy version, redaction version); changes only by PR with an eval report (3.15). |
| rerun_budget_exhausted | Run-health counter of checkpoints whose targeted re-run budget ran out with `stability: unknown (cause: budget)`; never a `needs_human` reason and never an outcome (3.10, 9.11). |
| review_state | Per outcome row: `none`, `pending`, `done`; per run: `unreviewed`, `partial`, `reviewed` (8.3). A report published with pending items is in state `unreviewed`. |
| Rig | Windows 11 VM with pinned display, fonts, pipeline, time zone and layout; one login; one worker. Fleet of 6: rigs 1 to 4 pool, rig 5 Nightly run and soak (with rig 4 for the Nightly A/A pass), rig 6 Explorer and spare; Calibration runs shard across the pool, rigs 1 to 4, in one weekend window while rig 5 keeps the Nightly canaries and fire drill (7.1, 11.2). |
| Safety channel `#sentinel-safety` | The Slack channel that carries every safety event and nothing else (9.9): `aborted_safety`, every S1 incident including `explorer_order_stage`, UNPROVEN post-run proof, fire-drill failures and safety canary misses. The one authoritative routing of those events (who is paged at P1, who is notified) is the safety routing table of 9.10; 1.10, 6.4, 6.6, 6.12 and 11.6 refer to it. |
| Scope manifest | The list of scheduled checkpoints a shard uploads to the control host on entry to `running`, so a dead-man or `aborted_safety` finalization can fill every checkpoint that never got an outcome with the run's abort reason: `harness_error (reason: dead_man)` or the other `aborted_harness` reason, or `env_error` with the aborting gate and reason, for example `env_error (gate: running, reason: kill_switch)` (5.2, 8.2, 10.2). |
| Secret step | Types a vault reference with the Recorder paused and Capture suspended; logs show `<redacted:login.password>`; allowed only in `login` flows (4.7, 6.9). |
| Slow half and fast half | The Input Gateway's two halves: the slow half (in the Orchestrator) resolves targets, re-checks the window under the pointer and writes one-shot tokens; the fast half is the hook host's `WH_MOUSE_LL` and `WH_KEYBOARD_LL` callbacks, which consult only shared memory and drop every event without a token (5.4.2 to 5.4.5). |
| Soak and lineage soak | The RC-only six-hour session on rig 5 with 24 cycle checkpoints `flow/<workspace-surface-id>/soak/c<nn>`, a resource sampler and the clock-region freeze detector; compared against the lineage soak, the curve recorded when the last released build was the RC. A freeze or crash in soak is the app-failure trio, never `env_error` (10.11). |
| Send token | Single-use token the gateway issues only for a `paper_send_ok` flow when attestation passed, paper mode was asserted in a frame under 500 ms old, the account equals the fixture allowlist entry and the per-run and per-day caps hold (6.7). |
| Settle rule | Mouse parked 1 s, focus dropped on the neutral control, must-see anchors at 0.92, anti-anchors absent, 3 identical frames at 250 ms outside masks, within max wait (default 15 s, charts and scans 30 s); else `not_settled` (3.5). |
| Severity S1 to S3 (invariants) | S1 heads the Unexpected section, S2 is listed, S3 is under a fold; a tier-1 surface bumps each one level (2.7). |
| Severity S1 to S3 (incidents) | S1 undeclared order row, live identity, secret or identifier leak, Explorer external effect; S2 drill or canary failure, attestation mismatch; S3 drop thresholds, redaction miss caught by the sweep (6.12). |
| Shard | One session on one rig with the work items assigned to it; census shards keyed by tab, flow shards by hash of flow id within tier; same-state flows pinned to one shard (11.3). |
| Size sweep | Every `resizable: true` surface placed in each of its hosts (host enum `tab`, `sidebar`, `flexgrid` for a Flexible Grid cell, `detached` for a detached window, `dialog`; plus the in-host splitter) and stepped through Ladder S or F and the splitter set, descending order mandatory, invariants at each step (2.5, 4.1). |
| Smoke subset | Registry surfaces with `smoke: true`: all tier-1 surfaces, one surface per top-level tab, every attested Application Settings page; CI caps it at 40 (2.11); always in PR scope. |
| Spend ceilings | Dollar caps of 11.4 kept in `policy/budgets.yaml`: 25 dollars per Explorer session (ends the session only), 50 per run and 500 per week. The per-run ceiling counts every model call of the run (Reviewer, agent rescue, Explorer) and is the only one that ends a run, at the next flow boundary: reaching it is `aborted_budget (reason: dollar_cap)`, with checkpoints not yet captured `not_run (reason: budget)` and items awaiting a verdict `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail`; the weekly cap stops model calls and aborts no run. The reviewer call caps (PR 60, merge 200, RC 500) never end a run; items beyond them are `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` (3.15, 10.7, 11.4). |
| Snapshot kinds | `base-os.<gen>`, `app.<build_id>.<gen>`, `explorer.<build_id>.<gen>`, `upgrade.<N-1>` and `upgrade.<N-2>`; every run starts from a revert (7.2). |
| Static impact step | Changed classes -> reverse transitive dependents on the candidate's dependency index (depth 6) -> surfaces by `roots`, unioned with declared surfaces and the map expansion; a surface reached only this way is a `dependency_map_gap` (2.10.2). |
| Surface | Reachable UI unit: tab, sub-tab, section, gadget, panel, dialog, menu, settings page, ticket variant, chain layout, context menu (2.2.1). Ids are dotted slugs with hyphens inside segments. |
| Surface Registry | Git YAML of every surface: id, label, kind, parent, path, primitives, roots, personas, tier, resizable and hosts, target window, data mode, entitlements, `enumerable_by`, workspace, anchors, labels, controls, smoke, owner (2.2.1, 4.5). Validated against the app at every run start. |
| Targeted re-run | Same-session re-capture of an above-threshold checkpoint after the normalize routine, up to twice for a diff and once for an `invariant_violation`, which is re-captured only to confirm it persists; all captures agree (the invariant fires again) = product change, any disagree = `not_settled (reason: unstable)` for the flow owner, with a non-reproducing violation kept as evidence (3.10, 10.5). |
| Tier (surface) | 1 money and orders, 2 analysis, 3 everything else. |
| Tier A, B, C (workspaces) | Canonical per persona (5); real power-user and previous-release workspaces (4 to 8); size-sweep harness (1) (2.3). |
| Two-person rule | A PR author may propose but not alone mark their own tier-1 or tier-2 diffs intended; the triage rotation or the tier's flow owner writes the decision naming the proposer (9.6). Tier-1 baselines are approved by the tier-1 flow owner, never the author of the change. |
| unreviewed | Report state when the run reached captured-and-diffed with pending reviewer items; row 23 items are `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending` and rows 16 to 18 are already final; the report is republished when the queue drains, each late verdict re-evaluated through 3.11 (12.2 Review states) (3.15, 10.7). |
| Watchdog | Separate process: heartbeat file, process tree tracking, screenshot-staleness hang detector, crash artifacts, hs_err_pid collection, kill switch second half, resume; restart budgets per shard 3 app relaunches, 2 Orchestrator restarts and 1 Gateway hook host restart (the second is `aborted_harness (reason: hook_lost)` and consumes no app relaunch) (10.2, 5.14). A Watchdog absent at run start is `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H8)`; one lost mid-run is `aborted_harness (reason: watchdog_dead)`. It never writes SQLite. |
| Weekly coverage review | The system owner's weekly pass over the coverage matrix of the last merge, RC and Nightly runs (9.12): every `not_run (reason: entitlement)` cell, quarantined checkpoints past five business days, and the week's `not_run (reason: budget)` and `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)` totals from run health; each entitlement gap gets a login request or a ticketed row in the Not detectable by design table (2.13), each budget or model gap a sharding or capacity task (1.10, 9.10, 11.6). |
