| Workspace Corpus | Tier A, B and C workspaces in git, hashed, dropped into usergui on snapshot build; ids `ws.tier-a.<persona>`, `ws.tier-b.<name>`, `ws.tier-c.sweep-harness` (lowercase slugs per the 4.1 grammar; 2.3, 4.6). |
| Outcome names | All names in 12.2 are glossary terms; see that table for definitions. |

### 12.2 Outcome taxonomy

This subsection mirrors three authoritative sources and adds nothing to them: the precedence paragraph and the outcome tables are a verbatim copy of 1.10 Outcome taxonomy (authoritative); the reason table and the finding table are verbatim copies of the reason and finding vocabularies of 4.13 Outcome record, which `taxonomy.yaml`, the `outcome_reasons` seed and the `findings.kind` CHECK of 8.3 carry; and the action table is a verbatim copy of 4.14 Decision record. The tracing notes between the tables only point at the sections that produce a code. Where this copy and its source ever differ, the source wins and this copy is the defect.

Verbatim from brief 1.5:

> Per checkpoint: `identical`, `noise`, `intended`, `collateral`, `needs_human`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed`, `not_settled`, `not_comparable` (fingerprint or landmark mismatch), `landmark_missing`, `env_error` (gate failed before the checkpoint), `harness_error`, `not_run` (with reason: entitlement, budget, scope, quarantine), `unregistered_surface`, `needs_baseline`. Per step: `passed`, `passed_after_retry`, `passed_via_agent_fallback` (with the scripted locator failure recorded as a finding), `failed`, `blocked_by_gateway`. Per run: `complete`, `complete_with_env_errors`, `aborted_safety`, `aborted_budget`, `aborted_harness`. Nothing else exists.

Verbatim from 1.10:

Precedence. A checkpoint can produce several results (an invariant fires and the pixel diff is also above threshold). It ends in exactly one outcome, the first that applies in this order: `env_error`, app failure (`assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)`), `harness_error`, `not_run`, `not_comparable`, `not_settled`, `landmark_missing`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed` (every other assertion), `needs_baseline`, `collateral`, `needs_human`, `intended`, `noise`, `identical`. Environment outranks the app and the harness because a hang during a network drop is an environment fact, and an app failure outranks the harness because an exception raised while handling an app failure is evidence of that failure, not a harness fault (10.1). Lower results that also applied stay on the finding record as evidence (a `collateral` classification on an `invariant_violation` finding) but are not outcomes. `unregistered_surface` is a checkpoint of its own created by registry validation and never competes. The rule list in 3.11 Classification decision table implements this order. One refinement inside that list: a region with no calibrated floor cannot be said to be above a threshold, so `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` is decided before `collateral` (3.11 row 15) and is ranked with `collateral` in the report.

Per checkpoint:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identical` | Candidate and base equal pixel for pixel outside mask and redaction regions after settle (`freeze` regions are pixel-diffed, 3.8); invariants and assertions pass; no step on the path ended `passed_via_agent_fallback`. | Diff Engine at pair comparison. | Counted as covered in the matrix as "identical (n)"; not listed. | Nothing. |
| `noise` | Diff below the checkpoint's and region's calibrated A/A floor (reason: `below_floor`), or matching a human-approved noise signature (decision #id). Never assigned by the Reviewer. | Diff Engine with the decision store. | Run health counts; report UI drill-down; suppressed table for signature matches. | Nothing; a weekly 5 percent re-label of signature-based `noise` feeds the overturn metric; a rising count on one checkpoint triggers a calibration review by the flow owner. |
| `intended` | Diff above threshold on a surface a loaded manifest entry declares, and the Reviewer, given the entry, crops and any mock, returns `matches_manifest` at confidence 0.80 or above; or the signature inherits a mark_intended decision. | Diff Engine classification plus asynchronous Reviewer confirmation (3.11 rows 14 and 20). | PR comment Intended with crops at 1:1 and the confirmation; merge and RC reports per PR. | At merge-run triage the capture becomes a baseline candidate; a human approves it with approver, build, reason, ticket (9.8). The Reviewer never promotes. |
| `collateral` | Diff above threshold on a surface no loaded manifest entry declares, including a UI-touching PR with no manifest; or a removed surface (label on base, absent on candidate) that no loaded manifest entry declares (3.11 row 26). | Diff Engine classification by surface declaration alone, no model call (3.11 rows 16 and 17); the Reviewer adds a description and a pointer when available and cannot move it. | Top of PR comment Unexpected by tier, with the consumed primitive, the manifest entry that touched it, layout and size, crops; tier 1 also to the Slack triage channel. | One-click: confirm bug (Jira), mark intended with ticket (manifest amendment; tier 1 and 2 need a second person), request mask with reason (human-created, owner and expiry; refused on money cells and identity fields, and refused with the reason shown when it would exceed the panel's mask budget, 3.8). The decision persists by signature (9.7). A later diff whose signature matches a confirm_bug decision keeps its computed outcome, files under that ticket and is listed under Known bugs without a new alert (3.11 input M, 9.6). |
| `needs_human` | Diff above threshold that is none of the above. Reasons, closed: `reviewer_uncertain` (below 0.80, partial match, no visible difference, cannot judge), `reviewer_no_match` (the Reviewer is confident the change on a declared surface is unrelated to its entry, or does not confirm the removal of a declared surface, 3.11 row 25a; ranked directly after `collateral`), `reviewer_unavailable` (API down, refusal, schema failure, `intended` disabled, or awaiting review with `review_state: pending`), `reviewer_cap` (beyond the per-run reviewer call cap, or still awaiting a verdict when the per-run spend ceiling or the weekly dollar cap stopped model calls, with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail`, 3.15), `no_manifest` (non-UI PR with no manifest), `uncalibrated` (region or fingerprint without a calibrated floor, threshold 0; never `not_comparable`), `rescued_capture` (reached through `passed_via_agent_fallback`, even with a clean or below-floor diff, 3.11 row 11a; never inherits a noise or intended decision), `global_shift` (text-edge-only diff under a `global_rendering_shift` run finding, one cluster), `oracle_unreadable`, `bounds_unreadable`. When two reasons apply, the first in 3.11's fixed order wins and the rest go in `detail`. An exhausted re-run budget is not a reason: the classification stands with `stability: unknown (cause: budget)` (3.10). | Diff Engine plus Reviewer output; Orchestrator for cap, budget and manifest reasons. | PR comment Unexpected below `collateral`; daily digest to the triage rotation at 08:00 America/New_York. | Human disposition within one business day (confirm bug, mark intended with ticket, mark noise); it persists by signature and becomes an eval-set item. When a pending verdict lands, the item is re-evaluated through 3.11's table with the verdict as input R and the outcome becomes what the table gives: `intended`, `noise` only via the A/A floor, or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` (including a removed declared surface the Reviewer does not confirm, 3.11 row 25a) or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_uncertain)`; `review_state` goes `pending` to `done`. If a human decision already exists on the item, the verdict is attached as an annotation only and never changes the outcome or the decision. The one other later change: when the per-run spend ceiling ends the run, an item still pending becomes `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail` and `review_state: done`, and when the job gives up the reason stays `reviewer_unavailable` with `review_state: done` (4.13, 3.15). Nothing else is ever rewritten. |
| `invariant_violation` | A layout invariant INV-01 to INV-15 (2.7 Layout invariants) failed on a capture on all 3 settled frames: sibling bounds intersect, component outside parent, text clipped, ellipsis, required label missing, unexpected scrollbar, font below minimum, placeholder or error text, window off screen, control count wrong, text runs overlap, columns misaligned, focus order wrong, error dialog present, sign and color disagree. Baseline-free. | Invariant Checker, right after capture, on both builds. | PR comment Unexpected with the bounds overlay and the base crop at the same layout and size, by tier and severity; Slack for tier 1. A violation present on both builds is reported once as pre-existing, one severity lower, never dropped. | Confirm bug, or waive with ticket and expiry at most 30 days (the outcome never changes; the finding is suppressed). A wrong invariant for a surface gets a registry exception with owner, reason and expiry. The Reviewer never reclassifies it. |
| `assertion_failed` | An Oracle assertion on the flow step failed: value outside its expectation, arithmetic invariant broken, API comparison outside the delay tolerance, chain header inconsistent with strikes or expirations; or a built-in assertion failed: `app_alive` (stored as `assertion:app_alive` with the cause, `jvm_crash`, `hang`, `oom` or `process_exit`, in `detail`, 4.13; an error dialog with the app alive is INV-14, not this), `size_reached` (a sweep step whose size was not reached after one retry, 2.5.1), `soak.<metric>` (a soak budget breach, 10.11). An OCR calibration miss is `harness_error (reason: ocr_calibration)`, never this. | Oracle at the step (OCR on upscaled crops, CSV export or Copy All, JAB where available, market-data API); Watchdog for `app_alive`. | PR comment Unexpected with extracted and expected values and source, or the crash artifacts; flow owner; tier 1 for `app_alive`. | Confirm bug, or fix the expectation by flow PR. For `app_alive` the rest of the flow or ladder is `not_run (reason: app_crash)` and the app is relaunched through every gate; the next flow starts from its preconditions and a ladder never resumes mid-way; a crash or hang during the relaunch gates, or during the gate sequence of the shard's first launch, is another `app_alive` failure that consumes the relaunch budget, never `env_error`; a `process_exit` during a launcher update or with a changed build manifest is `env_error (gate: launched, reason: version_changed_mid_run)` with no `app_crash` finding and no relaunch consumed (10.2). The Reviewer never reclassifies it. |
| `not_settled` | Settle rule (3.5) not met within max wait, reason: `frames_unstable`, `anchor_missing`, `anti_anchor_present`, `timeout`, `unexpected_window:<title>`; or a targeted re-run disagreed (reason: `unstable`); or the Nightly A/A pass drifted on a frozen checkpoint (reason: `aa_drift`). Last frame kept. | Capture at the checkpoint; Diff Engine after re-run; Calibration Service nightly. | Run health; flow owner. Not an app finding; never in the Unexpected list and never sent to the Reviewer. | No diff, no retry within the run. `flake_event` written; quarantine when the flake score passes 0.10 over 5 observations, 3 unstable in 7 days, 2 verdict flips on one build, 3 consecutive `aa_drift` nights, a gateway threshold (one safety drop, or three integrity drops in one flow, 5.4.8), or, for a whole flow, a 30-day agent-fallback rate above 5 percent (11.5) (3.10, 10.5, 10.6). Time to settle above 2x the calibration p50 is a `settle_regression` finding. |
| `not_comparable` | No pair can be scored: `fingerprint_mismatch` (the differing field named: any must-match fingerprint field, including the data epoch and the bounds source), `window_mismatch` (window title or geometry class differs from the expected target window), `surface_mismatch` (active tab or panel headers do not match the expected screen id on one side). These three are the only `not_comparable` reasons. | Orchestrator at the fingerprint check (whole shard, nothing captured); Capture at the checkpoint. | Run health with the field or screen id; on-call for fingerprint mismatch; the run is `complete_with_env_errors`. | Nothing diffed. Fingerprint: rig fix and re-run. A fingerprint that merely lacks a calibration is not this outcome: its diffs are `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` at threshold 0 and a Calibration run is queued (3.9). Screen id: flow owner checks the flow; candidate alone elsewhere is a suspected navigation regression and a finding. |
| `landmark_missing` | A Region Registry landmark, a registry validation probe anchor, or a step's locator anchor on every scripted rung and (when enabled) the agent rung, not found above its confidence floor on candidate or base. | Diff Engine when anchoring; Orchestrator at validation; Executor when a step fails on its locator. | PR comment Unexpected with the side it was missing on and both crops; flow owner. | Human decides bug or landmark update by region or flow PR. Never a blind diff. Missing on both sides is a flow bug. |
| `env_error` | An Orchestrator gate failed before the checkpoint (`provisioned`, `preflight.<item>`, `launched`, `authenticated`, `paper_mode_asserted`, `settings_attested`, `workspace_loaded`, `fixture_verified`, `canary_flow_passed`, `connectivity`, `rig_lost`; gate names equal the Orchestrator state names), or an environment fault occurred before capture (reasons include `version_mismatch`, `version_changed_mid_run` (gate `launched`, including a launcher restart seen as `process_exit`, 10.2), `rig_spec_mismatch`, `session_kicked` and `agreement_pending` (gate `authenticated`), `fixture_drift` and `delay_state` (gate `fixture_verified`), `occluded` (the gate in force when it was detected, `running` mid-run), `attestation_unreadable` (gate `settings_attested`), `identity_unreadable` (gate `paper_mode_asserted`), `vault_unreachable`, a catalog popup with action abort, a maintenance banner (`maintenance`, the gate in force)). Every `env_error` names its gate. Unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_safety` run take this outcome with the aborting gate as the gate name and the abort reason as the reason (for example `env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: paper_mode_mismatch)`, `env_error (gate: running, reason: kill_switch)`). | Orchestrator, with gate name, reason and screenshot. | On-call channel at once, one alert per run per gate; run health; the same gate in two consecutive runs escalates. Never enters the Diff Engine. | Rig or environment fix; shard re-run if budget allows; fixture drift triggers the fixture reset flow (7.6). |
| `harness_error` | Exception, crash or hang in the harness (Executor, Capture, Diff Engine, Oracle, Stores, Reporter), a failed self-test, a post-run taxonomy query failure, a registry entry found on neither build with the entitlement present, a bounds source or OCR calibration failure, canary generation failure, or canary detection below floor (reasons include `store_write_failed`, `artifact_persist_failed`, `redaction_version_missing`, `bounds_source_unavailable`, `ocr_calibration`, `mask_budget_exceeded`, `invariant_on_aa` (an enabled invariant firing on an A/A pair, 2.7), `registry_entry_not_found`, `export_header_mismatch`, `hook_lost`, `orchestrator_died`, `drill_failed:<item>`, `canary_generation_failed`, `canary_path_divergence`, `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded`, `safety_canary_blind:<canary>`, `validation_self_test`, `chaos_unobserved`, `aa_drift_global`). Unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_harness` run take this outcome with the run's abort reason (for example `harness_error (reason: dead_man)`, `harness_error (reason: watchdog_dead)`, `harness_error (reason: preflight.H8)`). On a Nightly run a missed money-cell mutant's record is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)` while the run itself stays `complete` (10.3); a missed non-money mutant is canary state `missed` and counts toward `detector_degraded`, which marks the class's missed mutants `harness_error (reason: detector_degraded)` once the class falls below its floor. | Watchdog or the failing component's handler. | On-call channel; run health; morning report headline "detector is blind" for the canary case, with the mask, decision or threshold that absorbed the mutant. | Harness bug ticket to the system owner (Jira SENT). Never enters the Diff Engine. |
| `not_run` | In the matrix but not executed. Reasons, closed: `entitlement` (the login lacks it, including every post-Send surface until `paper_send_ok` is approved); `budget` (wall clock, relaunch budget, no lockstep rig free or a lockstep pair that slipped twice, an RC run superseded); `scope` (outside this run type's scope, or no workspace of this persona hosts the surface); `quarantine` (flake statistics, fire drill failure, kill switch or incident; nothing un-quarantines automatically, 10.5; drill and safety-canary flows are never quarantined, their failures page per 9.10); `step_failed:<step>` (an earlier step of its flow ended `failed` or `blocked_by_gateway`); `base_step_failed` (the base build could not reach it and the surface is not new); `app_crash` (the app died earlier in its flow or ladder); `model_unavailable` (an Explorer session or an agent-only step skipped because the model endpoint is down). | Orchestrator at scope computation, budget deadline or flow end; quarantine records. | Coverage matrix cell with the reason verbatim. Never displayed as passed. | Entitlement: the system owner's weekly coverage review (9.12). Budget and model unavailable: run health and the harness on-call. Quarantine: flow owner fix, 5 clean Calibration captures, human removal of the record. Step failures: the step finding carries the fix. |
| `unregistered_surface` | Registry validation found a main menu, tab bar, sub-tab, gadget picker, Setup, settings tree, selector or context menu entry not in the Surface Registry; recorded against synthetic id `unregistered.<probe>.<slug>`. | Orchestrator at the `workspace_loaded` gate by probes P1 to P8. | Unexpected, tier 1 until classified; coverage matrix row `not_registered`; system owner. | Registry stub PR proposed automatically; a human merges it or adds an explicit ignored entry with reason. Repeats every run until then. |
| `needs_baseline` | Candidate captured and invariants passed, but no comparable base exists. Reasons, closed (3.11 input B): `new_surface` (manifest `new_surface: true`, or present on candidate and absent on base), `base_not_settled` (after one base re-capture), `base_env_error`, `base_harness_error`, `lineage_missing` (the RC lineage baseline lacks it), `reuse_missing` (a frozen base capture expected from reuse was not found), `explorer_replay` (a replayed Explorer candidate flow). | Diff Engine when no pair can be formed. | Report section Needs baseline, with the nearest existing baseline by perceptual hash; in a PR comment under Intended if declared as new, else Unexpected. | A human approves the capture as baseline (approver, build, reason, ticket) or files a bug. Never automatic; blocks a clean RC report for tier 1. |

Per step:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `passed` | First attempt completed on a scripted rung of the locator ladder; the step's post-condition passed. | Executor. | Step log; the resolved rung is recorded so drift from rung 1 to 2 or 3 is a maintenance metric. | Nothing. |
| `passed_after_retry` | First attempt failed on every scripted rung; after `reset_input_state` the single permitted retry of the scripted rungs succeeded. One retry per step, never across a capture; the first attempt's screenshot is kept. | Executor. | Run health; flow owner weekly. | Flake statistics; three in 30 days on one step opens a flow maintenance task. |
| `passed_via_agent_fallback` | Every scripted rung failed twice; the agent rung with the restricted toolset reached the target; the declared normalize routine ran before capture. A rescue is capped at 25 actions and 90 seconds; past either cap the step is `failed`. The locator failure is recorded as a `locator_failure` finding with every rung's result, the pre-attempt screenshot and the agent's action trace. | Executor. Disabled by preflight when the model API is unreachable, during login, secret and teardown steps, while the ticket flag is set, or under DR-07 Branch B; the step is then `failed`. | PR comment Unexpected, "scripted locator broke at step X", beside the checkpoint's diff; flow owner. | The checkpoint it leads to is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)` unless a higher-precedence outcome applies. Proposed anchor patch PR with the agent's final target and crop; two fallbacks on one step and build open an update-scripted-flow task. |
| `failed` | The step could not complete within the retry cap: locator not found on any rung, precondition missing, popup catalog action abort, app not responding. The flow ends; teardown and `reset_input_state` run. | Executor. | Unexpected, with the side it failed on and the pre-attempt screenshot beside the base build's screenshot at the same step; flow owner. | The checkpoint the step led to is `landmark_missing` (locator) or `assertion_failed` (assertion or `app_alive`); later checkpoints of the flow are `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`. On the base build only: `needs_baseline` when the manifest marks the surface `new_surface: true`, else `not_run (reason: base_step_failed)`. Candidate-only failure is a suspected regression; both-sides failure is a flow bug. |
| `blocked_by_gateway` | The Input Gateway dropped the step's event: a click without a matching one-shot token, a blocked key while a ticket or confirm dialog was foreground, an Explorer action on a denied target, or the kill switch armed. The flow ends. | Input Gateway hook, from in-memory arm/deny state; the slow half's refusal is logged the same way. | Safety log, on-call channel, flow owner; Explorer owner for deny-list hits. | Later checkpoints `not_run (reason: step_failed:<step>)`. Safety-reason drops (a blocked key, or a click on a deny rect while `order_stage` is set) quarantine the flow and page P1. Integrity-reason drops (token mismatch, expired token, stale arm/deny state) get one retry of the step; three in one flow quarantine the flow and ten in one run trip the kill switch (5.4.8). An attempted send on a scripted flow, including inside its agent rescue, or a kill-switch trip, ends the run `aborted_safety`; in an Explorer session an attempted send ends the session and counts toward the per-run trip (6.8), and a ticket or dialog flag set in the session drops all input, closes the window through the gateway's recovery path, ends the session with finding `explorer_order_stage` and counts toward the per-run trip while the run continues; the 30-second open-dialog kill-switch timer applies to scripted flows and agent rescue only. |

Per run:

| Outcome | Definition | Trigger | Who sees it, where | What happens next |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `complete` | Every in-scope checkpoint has an outcome, none is `env_error` or `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)`, teardown finished and the post-run proof reads PROVEN. | Orchestrator at `reported`. | Report header. | Normal triage. |
| `complete_with_env_errors` | As `complete`, but at least one checkpoint is `env_error` or `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)`, more than 3 re-logins were needed, teardown reported a fault, or the post-run proof reads UNPROVEN (the next run on that login is blocked until a human verifies the account); the cause is recorded as the run reason `relogin_budget`, `teardown_fault` or `unproven_proof` when it is not an `env_error` checkpoint. | Orchestrator. | Report header; on-call channel already notified. | Triage on what ran; env fix and shard re-run per budget. |
| `aborted_safety` | Paper-mode mismatch, attestation mismatch, undeclared working order at run start, kill switch, an attempted send blocked by the gateway, a new Working or Filled row at teardown, a live-format account id read at the paper-mode assertion (6.4), a fire drill that produced a new order row, or an unknown dialog while `order_stage` is set (reasons: `paper_mode_mismatch`, `attestation_mismatch`, `unexpected_working_order`, `kill_switch`, `attempted_send`, `undeclared_order_row`, `live_identity`, `drill_order_placed`, `unknown_dialog_in_order_stage`). Hook enters deny-all; process tree killed; a fresh scripted login performs verified Cancel All; Working and Filled diffed against the start snapshot; proof produced (6.6). | Orchestrator, Input Gateway, Watchdog. | Paged and notified per the single routing of 9.10 (harness on-call at P1, the accountable owner and `#sentinel-safety` among them); post-run proof section; the PR comment's abort block if a PR run. | Incident procedure (6.12), S1 or S2. The rig is disabled and its flows `not_run (reason: quarantine)`; no run starts on that rig or login until a human closes the incident. |
| `aborted_budget` | Wall-clock budget reached before scope finished, a fourth app failure in a shard after its 3 relaunches, a PR run still queued at its start deadline (`pool_saturated`; a queued merge run is coalesced into the next merge run and an RC run goes to the release manager instead, 9.10), the run's model spend reaching the per-run ceiling of 11.4 (ends the run at the next flow boundary; reviewer call caps never end a run, they give `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)`), a 6.4 rate cap reached, or an RC run superseded by a new RC build (1.6) (reasons: `wall_clock`, `app_restart_budget`, `pool_saturated`, `dollar_cap`, `rate_cap`, `superseded`). Explorer budget exhaustion is not this; it ends the Explorer session only. | Orchestrator at the deadline; Watchdog budget. | Report header with `not_run (reason: budget)` counts per tier; on-call for the relaunch case. | Findings triaged as usual; sharding or scope review if the rate exceeds target. |
| `aborted_harness` | Harness crash or hang past the Orchestrator restart budget, a failed preflight H item or self-test, store failure, config lint failure, missing base artifact, a secret found by the post-run scan (report withheld), a failed post-run taxonomy query, the dead-man deadline of a run that reached `running`, or the start deadline of a Nightly or Calibration run that never reached `running` (11.2) (reasons: `preflight.<item>` for a failed H item of 12.7, written as 12.7 writes it, for example `preflight.H8` when the Watchdog is absent at run start; `start_failed` for that start deadline, with every scoped checkpoint `harness_error (reason: start_failed)` and the "canaries pending" banner on the next PR comment; and, mid-run, `store_write_failed`, `artifact_persist_failed`, `import_conflict`, `watchdog_dead`, `heartbeat_unwritable`, `disk_full`, `rig_lost`, `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `config_invalid`, `base_build_missing`, `secret_leaked`, `taxonomy_check_failed`, `dead_man`, `dpi_awareness`, `hook_lost` (a second Gateway hook host restart in one shard; the hook host has its own budget of one restart per shard and never consumes an app relaunch, 5.4.2), `canary_generation_failed` (a Nightly run on which no canary could run at all), `egress_unlogged`, `secret_scan_unavailable`). | Watchdog, Orchestrator, Reporter host. | Harness on-call paged immediately (P1); dead-man alert names run, rig and last heartbeat; the PR check fails with the reason. | Harness bug to the system owner; the run is re-queued once; two in a week freeze harness changes. |

Reason codes, verbatim from 4.13 (its "Introduced by" column names the sections that produce each code). A reason is written `outcome (reason: code)`; `env_error` also carries `gate:`; `assertion_failed` carries `assertion:`. Codes with a parameter take it after a colon. A code outside this table cannot be written (L-OUT-01), so a new failure mode is a change to 4.13 and `taxonomy.yaml` first.

| Outcome | Reason codes | Introduced by |
|---|---|---|
| `noise` | `below_floor`, `decision:<id>` (an approved noise signature or an active mask decision; 8.3 stores the code `decision` with the id in `reason_detail` and in `decision_id`) | 3.11, 4.14 |
| `intended` | none, or `decision:<id>` | 3.11 |
| `collateral` | none (including an undeclared removed surface, 3.11 row 26), `decision:<id>` (a computed `collateral` that matches a `confirm_bug` decision: the outcome is kept and the finding is filed under the ticket, 4.14), `manifest_missing` (no-manifest case (a), 4.3) | 3.11, 4.3, 4.14 |
| `needs_human` | `reviewer_uncertain` (confidence below 0.80, partial match, no visible difference or cannot judge), `reviewer_no_match`, `reviewer_unavailable` (API down, refusal, schema violation, batch expired; `review_state: pending` while queued), `reviewer_cap` (beyond the run's reviewer call cap of 3.15, PR 60, merge 200, RC 500, or excluded by the weekly dollar cap, or still pending when the per-run spend ceiling ended the run, those two with `cause: dollar_cap` in `detail`, 11.4; the pending case is the third later change of the intro and 8.3's trigger permits it; a reviewer cap never ends a run), `no_manifest`, `uncalibrated` (region or fingerprint without a floor, threshold 0), `rescued_capture`, `global_shift`, `oracle_unreadable`, `bounds_unreadable` | 3.7, 3.11, 3.15, 4.3, 4.8, 5.5, 5.10 |
| `invariant_violation` | `INV-01` to `INV-15` (the 2.7 ids; several fire as several findings, the outcome names the first by catalog order) | 2.7 |
| `assertion_failed` | `assertion:<id>`, including three built-ins: `assertion:app_alive`, whose cause (`jvm_crash`, `hang`, `oom`, `process_exit`) goes in `detail` and never in `reason` (written `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with the cause in `detail`; this form is authoritative everywhere, 10.1); `assertion:size_reached` (2.5.1); and `assertion:soak.<metric>` (10.11) | 2.6.2, 2.5.1, 10.1, 10.11 |
| `not_settled` | `frames_unstable`, `anchor_missing`, `anti_anchor_present`, `timeout`, `unexpected_window:<title>`, `unstable` (targeted re-run disagreed), `aa_drift` (Nightly A/A) | 3.5, 3.10, 5.7, 10.5, 10.6 |
| `not_comparable` | exactly three: `fingerprint_mismatch` (the differing fields in `detail`, which is how a data epoch, bounds source or accessible-tree change is named), `window_mismatch`, `surface_mismatch`. A missing calibration is `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)`, never this | 3.3, 4.12, 5.7 |
| `landmark_missing` | `landmark:<id>` (Region Registry landmark, with the side in `side`), `locator:<step>` (step locator exhausted on every rung), `redaction_landmark:<id>` (a redaction anchor not found; nothing stored, nothing released), `probe:<Pn>` (a registry validation probe P1 to P8 whose anchor was not found) | 1.10, 2.2.3, 3.7, 5.5, 6.10 |
| `env_error` | with `gate` (a state name of 5.2, `preflight.<item>`, `connectivity` or `rig_lost`): `gate` (the gate's own check failed with no finer cause; the reason of every `gate: preflight.<item>` failure that has no finer code, for example `env_error (gate: preflight.R1)`), `version_mismatch`, `version_changed_mid_run`, `rig_spec_mismatch`, `fingerprint_unreadable:<field>`, `snapshot_revert_failed`, `install_failed`, `session_kicked`, `authentication_challenge`, `authentication_failed`, `timeout` (login screen absent within the login max wait, 7.7; or, with the gate in force, a run still before `running` at its dead-man deadline, 10.2), `relogin_budget` (checkpoints left when the re-login budget K is spent, 7.7), `vault_unreachable`, `agreement_pending`, `live_mode_selected`, `attestation_unreadable`, `identity_unreadable`, `fixture_drift`, `fixture_maintenance_needed`, `delay_state`, `data_epoch_mismatch`, `prices_stale`, `ondemand_timeout`, `ondemand_state`, `precondition:<check>`, `backend_degraded` (gate `connectivity`, 7.11), `occluded` (with the gate in force, `gate: running` for a capture or an input batch, 5.7, 7.8), `maintenance` (a scheduled maintenance notice, POP-09, `gate: connectivity`, 7.8), and, on unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_safety` run, the run's abort reason (`kill_switch`, `paper_mode_mismatch`, any code of the `aborted_safety` row) with the aborting gate (1.10) | 4.2, 4.9, 4.10, 5.2, 6.3, 6.4, 6.9, 7.2, 7.3, 7.6, 7.7, 7.8, 7.9, 7.11, 10.7, 12.7 |
| `harness_error` | `registry_entry_not_found`, `bounds_source_unavailable`, `ocr_calibration`, `export_header_mismatch`, `mask_budget_exceeded` (a panel's masked plus non-identity redacted share over its budget, or a mask or redaction box on a money cell; the panel and share in `detail`, 4.8), `store_write_failed` (a record the Orchestrator could not write or repair, L-OUT-02, 8.9), `artifact_persist_failed` (an artifact write or read-back that failed after one retry, 8.4), `redaction_version_missing` (8.9), `hook_lost`, `orchestrator_died` (the checkpoint in progress when the Orchestrator died, 10.2), `detector_blind`, `detector_degraded` (the missed mutant's record, 10.3), `safety_canary_blind:<canary>` (a missed safety canary's record, the blind detector named, 6.5, 10.3), `canary_generation_failed` (a mutant that could not be generated, 10.3), `canary_path_divergence`, `drill_failed:<item>` (6.5), `validation_self_test` (the registry probe self-test of 10.3 did not yield its one `unregistered_surface`), `chaos_unobserved` (a chaos stall that produced neither alert nor dead-man row, 10.2), `aa_drift_global`, `chaos_rule_stuck`, `invariant_on_aa` (an enabled invariant that fired on a Nightly A/A pair, which is a harness bug, 2.7, 10.6), `exception:<class>`, and, on unreached checkpoints of an `aborted_harness` run, the run's abort reason (`dead_man`, `start_failed`, `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `watchdog_dead`, `preflight.<item>`, any code of the `aborted_harness` row) (1.10). `step_failed` is never a `harness_error` reason | 2.2.3, 2.7, 2.8.1, 3.7, 3.8, 5.4, 5.10, 5.12, 5.15, 6.5, 7.11, 8.4, 8.9, 10.3, 10.6 |
| `not_run` | `entitlement` (including every post-Send surface until `paper_send_ok`; there is no separate send-policy reason), `budget`, `scope`, `quarantine`, `step_failed:<step>`, `base_step_failed`, `app_crash`, `model_unavailable` (an Explorer session or an agent-only step skipped because the model endpoint is down, 10.7) | brief 1.5, 2.6.3, 3.1, 5.2, 5.6, 5.14, 6.7, 7.11, 10.7 |
| `unregistered_surface` | `probe:<P1..P8>` with the enumerated label in `detail` (8.3 stores the code `probe` with the probe id in `reason_detail`) | 2.2.3 |
| `needs_baseline` | `new_surface`, `base_not_settled`, `base_env_error`, `base_harness_error`, `lineage_missing` (RC), `reuse_missing`, `explorer_replay` (input B of 3.11) | 1.10, 2.9, 3.1, 3.11 |
| run `aborted_safety` | `paper_mode_mismatch`, `attestation_mismatch`, `unexpected_working_order`, `kill_switch`, `attempted_send`, `undeclared_order_row` (an undeclared Working, Filled or Canceled row found at teardown or by the post-run proof, 5.2, 6.6), `live_identity` (a live-format account id read at the paper-mode assertion: not on the allowlist and not matching the paper prefix, 6.4), `drill_order_placed` (a fire drill that produced a new order row, 6.5), `unknown_dialog_in_order_stage` (an unmatched window while `order_stage` is set, 4.10); any other readable selector text that is not an allowlist entry is `paper_mode_mismatch` (6.4) | 1.10, 6.2 to 6.7 |
| run `aborted_budget` | `wall_clock` (the run's wall budget less the report margin reached, 5.2, 11.2), `app_restart_budget` (a fourth app failure in a shard, a crash or hang in the gate sequence of the shard's first launch or of a relaunch included, 5.2, 10.2), `dollar_cap` (the run's model spend, Reviewer, agent rescue and Explorer together, reached the 50-dollar per-run ceiling of 11.4: no further model call, the run ends at the next flow boundary, uncaptured checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`, items still awaiting a verdict `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` with `cause: dollar_cap`; the 25-dollar Explorer session cap and the weekly cap never end a run, 10.7), `pool_saturated` (a PR run still queued at its start deadline; a queued merge run is coalesced into the next merge run and an RC run goes to the release manager instead, 11.2), `rate_cap` (a 6.4 rate cap on logins, symbol changes or staged orders reached), `superseded` (a newer RC build arrived while the RC run was in flight: the run stops at the next flow boundary, its unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`, and the new RC run starts at once, 11.2) | 5.2, 6.4, 10.2, 10.7, 11.2, 11.4 |
| run `aborted_harness` | `config_invalid`, `preflight.<item>` (a failed H item of 12.7, written as 12.7 writes it, for example `preflight.H8` when the Watchdog is absent at run start), `dead_man`, `start_failed` (a Nightly or Calibration run that did not reach `running` by its start deadline, 11.2), `secret_leaked`, `secret_scan_unavailable`, `egress_unlogged`, `base_build_missing`, `taxonomy_check_failed` (the post-run taxonomy query, including L-OUT-07, failed), `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `hook_lost` (second hook host restart in one shard, 5.4.2), `watchdog_dead` (the Watchdog's reverse heartbeat stale mid-run, 5.14), `heartbeat_unwritable` (5.14), `disk_full` (only the Watchdog's mid-run free-space check ends a run this way, including the immediate check an `ENOSPC` requests, 10.2; a single artifact write that fails, `ENOSPC` included, is checkpoint `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)`, 8.4, 8.9), `rig_lost` (a second loss of the same shard, 10.7), `dpi_awareness`, `store_write_failed` (8.9), `artifact_persist_failed` (8.4, 8.9), `import_conflict` (8.9), `canary_generation_failed` (a Nightly run on which no canary could run at all). A blind identity canary is not a run abort: its row is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:identity)` and the dependent flows are `not_run (reason: quarantine)` while the run stays `complete` (6.4) | 1.4, 1.10, 3.4, 4.1, 4.2, 5.2, 5.4, 5.12, 5.14, 6.9, 6.10, 8.9, 10.2, 10.3, 10.8, 11.2 |
| run `complete_with_env_errors` | the cause, when it is not an `env_error` checkpoint: `unproven_proof` (6.6), `teardown_fault` (5.2), `relogin_budget` (7.7) | 5.2, 6.6, 7.7 |

Producers of codes the table lists, for tracing: `dollar_cap` is the per-run model spend ceiling of 11.4 Cost model reached (10.7 Degraded modes); the Explorer session cap of 25 dollars and the weekly cap of 500 dollars never produce it, and the reviewer call caps (PR 60, merge 200, RC 500) give `needs_human (reason: reviewer_cap)` and never end a run (3.15). `superseded` is the RC respin of 1.6 and 11.2: a newer RC build stops the running RC run at the next flow boundary, its unreached checkpoints `not_run (reason: budget)`. `model_unavailable` is an Explorer session or an agent-only step skipped because the model endpoint is down (10.7, the N2 and N5 degraded mode of 7.11). `invariant_on_aa` is an enabled invariant firing on a Nightly A/A pair (2.7, 10.6). `mask_budget_exceeded` is the run-time budget check of 3.8, with the panel and its share in `detail`. `live_identity` is a live-format account id read at the paper-mode assertion (6.4), which also blocks the login; any other readable text that is not an allowlist entry is `paper_mode_mismatch`. `version_changed_mid_run` is written with `gate: launched`, including a `process_exit` during a launcher update or with a changed build manifest, which consumes no relaunch and raises no `app_crash` finding (10.2); `session_kicked` is written with `gate: authenticated` (7.7). `orchestrator_died`, `watchdog_dead`, `heartbeat_unwritable`, `disk_full`, `hook_lost`, `orchestrator_restart_budget`, `dead_man` and `chaos_unobserved` come from 10.2 Watchdog: a heartbeat or artifact write that fails with `ENOSPC` requests the Watchdog's immediate free-space check, and only that check ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: disk_full)`, while a single artifact write that fails is the checkpoint's `harness_error (reason: artifact_persist_failed)` and the run cannot be `complete` (8.9, 10.2). `canary_generation_failed`, `canary_path_divergence`, `safety_canary_blind:<canary>`, `validation_self_test`, `detector_blind` and `detector_degraded` come from 10.3 Canary Service and the mutant catalog; on the synthetic canary row a missed money-cell mutant is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)` and a missed mutant of a class below its floor is `harness_error (reason: detector_degraded)`, while the Nightly run stays `complete`. `aa_drift` and `aa_drift_global` come from 10.6 A/A drift on the Nightly run; `rig_lost` (gate and run reason), `connectivity` and `timeout` from 10.7 Degraded modes; `preflight.<item>` from 12.7 Preflight checklist as 10.8 Self-tests at run start applies it; `pool_saturated` and `start_failed` (a Nightly or Calibration run not at `running` by its start deadline) from 11.2 Cadence and time budgets per run type. Unreached checkpoints of an aborted run always carry the run's abort reason: `harness_error (reason: dead_man)`, `harness_error (reason: preflight.H8)` or another code of the `aborted_harness` row, and `env_error` with the aborting gate and a code of the `aborted_safety` row, for example `env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: paper_mode_mismatch)`. Codes this table no longer carries: `mask_budget:<panel>` (replaced by `mask_budget_exceeded`), the `env_error` code `input_blocked`, and the `env_error` codes `desktop`, `display`, `capture` and `clock` (R2, R6, H3 and R4 failures are `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)` with reason `gate`, or `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.H3)` for H3, 12.7). `relaunch_budget` is not a code: a fourth app failure in a shard, first launch included, is `aborted_budget (reason: app_restart_budget)`. `wall_clock` is the wall budget of 11.2 reached; `undeclared_order_row` and `unproven_proof` come from the post-run proof of 6.6, `teardown_fault` from the teardown row of 5.2, `redaction_landmark:<id>` from 6.10 Stage 1, `probe:<Pn>` from 2.2.3, `exception:<class>` from 10.1, and `maintenance` from POP-09 of 7.8.

Findings, verbatim from 4.13 (its finding vocabulary, the `finding_kinds` of `taxonomy.yaml`). Records attached to a run, checkpoint or step that never change an outcome and do not extend the closed sets (1.10). The table lists 40 kinds, and the `findings.kind` CHECK of 8.3 is generated from the same list and accepts exactly these 40; the kinds `lockstep_slip`, `color_semantic_flip`, `quarantine_proposal`, `calibration_defect`, `anchor_ambiguous`, `layout_changed_library_needs_repair`, `send_guard_breach` and `no_covering_checkpoint` are not finding kinds. "Suppressed by decision #id" is a display state (`decision_id` on the row), not a kind; "missed in PR run" is the label of the `missed_in_pr_run` kind, and "missed by static impact" is the label of the same kind with `detail: static_impact` (1.8, 9.4). `lockstep_slip` and `rerun_budget_exhausted` are run-health counters (1.10, 4.13); `step_events` rows (`gate_decision`, `gate_reason`, `gate_class`, focus corrections, foreign windows) are events, not findings.

| Kind | Meaning | Section |
|---|---|---|
| `collateral`, `intended`, `needs_human`, `invariant_violation`, `assertion_failed`, `landmark_missing`, `needs_baseline`, `unregistered_surface` | the finding is the outcome, carried with its evidence (a `needs_baseline` finding is what `approve_baseline` acts on, 4.14) | 1.10 |
| `dependency_map_gap` | static edge or unowned root missing from the Dependency Map, with the proposed PR | 2.10.2, 4.4 |
| `manifest_missing` | UI-affecting PR with no manifest entry (case (a) of 4.3) | 4.3 |
| `unknown_popup` | unmatched top-level window, with the proposed catalog entry | 4.10, 7.8 |
| `popup_rate_increase` | catalog hits per build rose after a build change | 7.8 |
| `locator_failure` | a step's scripted rungs all failed, whether the agent rescued it (`passed_via_agent_fallback`) or not (`failed`); every rung's result and the proposed anchor patch | 5.5 |
| `app_crash` | process gone or EDT frozen, with hs_err_pid, dumps and log slice; tier 1 | 4.7, 10.1 |
| `explorer_candidate` | an Explorer observation with its signature, trace and replay result | 2.9 |
| `layout_shift`, `landmark_moved`, `color_shift`, `window_geometry_changed` | Diff Engine findings beside the outcome | 3.3, 3.7 |
| `global_rendering_shift` | run level: the granularity-0 pre-pass found a text-edge-only shift across the run; its checkpoints are one `needs_human (reason: global_shift)` cluster | 3.7 |
| `settle_regression` | time to settle above 2x the calibration p50 | 3.5 |
| `gateway_integrity` | an untokened or foreign input event reached the hook, or the hook was reinstalled | 5.4.4, 5.4.8 |
| `new_log_signature` | a new exception signature in the client log slice with the app alive; tier 2 | 10.11, 2.13 B14 |
| `jab_tree_changed` | under DR-01 Branch A, the accessible tree hash at build intake differs from the previous build; the run falls back to Branch B bounds and the registry owner is told; a finding, never a `not_comparable` reason | 11.8 DR-01 |
| `mask_budget_exceeded` | a landmark move or geometry change pushed a panel's masked plus non-identity redacted share over its budget, or a mask or redaction box onto a money cell; beside `harness_error (reason: mask_budget_exceeded)` | 3.8, 4.8, 6.10 |
| `mask_expired`, `floor_exception_expired`, `invariant_exception_expired` | a config record stopped applying at run start | 4.5, 4.8 |
| `redaction_miss` | the OCR sweep caught an identifier the anchor list missed | 6.10 |
| `secret_leaked` | post-run plaintext scan hit; the run is `aborted_harness` | 6.9 |
| `explorer_order_stage` | the ticket or dialog flag was set in an Explorer session: all input dropped, the window closed by the gateway's recovery path, the session ended, counted toward the per-run trip of ten; S1, paged and notified by the safety routing of 9.10, the Explorer owner told; the run continues | 5.4.6, 6.8, 9.10 |
| `missed_in_pr_run` | a merge-run finding on a surface its PR run had in scope but did not report ("missed in PR run"), or on a surface its PR run had `not_run (reason: scope)` that the candidate's dependency index reaches from a class a merged PR changed ("missed by static impact", `detail: static_impact`); opens a harness task | 1.8, 9.4 |
| `artifact_missing` | an object named by an outcome is missing or fails its hash in the weekly audit or on a report page request | 8.6, 8.9 |
| `orphaned_baseline` | an approved baseline whose checkpoint id no longer exists at the config commit | 8.5, 9.8 |
| `canary_miss` | a mutant ended `identical`, `noise` or a suppressed decision row | 10.3 |
| `intended_change_not_observed` | a manifest entry whose declared surfaces showed no diff | 2.12, 9.2 |
| `flow_maintenance_needed` | a Recorder anchor no longer matches the latest approved capture | 5.16, 11.5 |
| `harness_error` | a harness exception that did not take a checkpoint with it (an event that never reached the hook) | 5.4 |
| `memory_warning`, `hardening` | low-memory dialog per build; foreign-process occlusion on a hardened rig | 7.8, 7.12 |

Canary result states (10.3, `state` in `canary_results` in 8.3), not outcomes and not reason codes: a mutant is `detected` when its final outcome is in its expected list; `missed` when the path produced `identical`, `noise` or `intended` instead and the class is still above its floor; `detector_blind` when a money-cell mutant was missed (100 percent required; the 8.3 CHECK makes a money-cell miss always `detector_blind`); `detector_degraded` when its class fell below the rolling floor (the lower of the 14-night median minus 5 points and 90 percent); `generation_failed` when the mutant could not be generated (its row is `harness_error (reason: canary_generation_failed)`). The worst state becomes `detector_state` in `system_state` (`ok` otherwise); `detector_blind` and `generation_failed` page P1 and stamp the banner on every report until the next green Nightly run, and any non-`ok` state blocks RC sign-off. The Nightly run's own outcome stays `complete`; it is `aborted_harness (reason: canary_generation_failed)` only when no canary could run at all. `canary_results.kind` is `mutant`, `safety_canary`, `fire_drill` or `path_equivalence` (8.3).

Review states (4.13, 8.3, 10.7): per outcome row `review_state` is `none` (default; no review applies), `pending` (only on `needs_human` awaiting the Reviewer, with reason `reviewer_unavailable` or `global_shift` while queued, 4.13) or `done`; per run `runs.review_state` is `unreviewed`, `partial` or `reviewed`, and "reviewed" exists only at run level. Preflight writes `review_mode: deferred` and `agent_available: false` when N2 or N5 fails (the degraded mode of 7.11 and 10.7). When a pending verdict lands, the item is re-evaluated through 3.11 with the verdict as input R: `intended` (row 20 or 24), `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` (row 21, or row 25a for a declared removed surface the Reviewer does not confirm) or `needs_human (reason: reviewer_uncertain)` (row 22), and `noise` only through the A/A floor, never from a verdict; `review_state` goes `pending` to `done`. If a human decision already exists on the item, the verdict is attached as an annotation only and changes neither the outcome nor the decision (1.10, 3.11, 10.7).

Classification rows (3.11 Classification decision table), for tracing the outcome tables above: rows 1, 1a and 2 to 9 implement the precedence (row 1 G `env` is `env_error`; row 1a G `app` is `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` with finding `app_crash`; row 2 G `harness` is `harness_error`, including `mask_budget_exceeded`, `artifact_persist_failed` and `invariant_on_aa`; row 3 is `not_run`, including `model_unavailable`); row 9 is `needs_baseline`; row 9a (H `unreadable` with a zero or below-floor diff) is `needs_human (reason: oracle_unreadable)` or `needs_human (reason: bounds_unreadable)`; rows 10 and 11 (`identical`, `noise (reason: below_floor)`) require P `scripted`; row 11a (P `rescued` with a zero or below-floor diff) is `needs_human (reason: rescued_capture)`; row 12 is `not_settled (reason: unstable)`; rows 13 and 14 inherit `noise` and `intended` decisions on scripted paths only, an `intended` one within its ticket scope; row 15 is `uncalibrated`; rows 16 and 17 are `collateral`; row 18 is `no_manifest`; row 19 is `rescued_capture`; rows 20 to 23 are the Reviewer rows; rows 24 to 26 take B `removed` (a surface whose label is on the base and absent on the candidate): `intended` when the Reviewer confirms the removal against a declaring entry (row 24), `needs_human (reason: reviewer_unavailable)` with `review_state: pending` while the verdict is pending (row 25), `needs_human (reason: reviewer_no_match)` when the Reviewer does not confirm a declared removal (row 25a, which also carries `reviewer_unavailable` and `reviewer_cap` for an unavailable or capped verdict), and `collateral` for a removed surface that no entry declares (row 26). When two `needs_human` reasons apply, the first in 3.11's row order wins (9a, 11a, 15, 18, 19, 21, 22, then 23 and 25, then 25a) and the others go in `detail`.

Post-run proof verdicts (6.6; `post_run_proofs.verdict` in 8.3): `PROVEN: no orders sent` (`proven_no_sends`), `PROVEN: only declared sends` (`proven_declared_sends`, the gated branch), `PROVEN: no session established` (`proven_no_session`: the login never authenticated and the gateway log shows no token issued, so no recovery login is attempted and the proof blocks no login) and `UNPROVEN` with reason `recovery_login_failed`, `monitor_unreadable`, `cancel_all_failed`, `snapshot_missing` or `session_unavailable` (`unproven`; `session_unavailable` when a kicked session's login is still unavailable after one retry). UNPROVEN makes the run `complete_with_env_errors` (run reason `unproven_proof`) or leaves it `aborted_safety`, pages at P1 and blocks the next run on that login (`logins.blocked_reason`) until a human verifies the account.

Other record enums (4.13, 8.3): `stability` is `stable`, `unstable` (the `not_settled (reason: unstable)` case) or `unknown`, with `stability_cause` `not_recapturable` or `budget` only when `unknown`; a step's gateway event is `gate_decision` `emitted`, `dropped` (by the hook), `refused` (by the slow half), `late_up` or `none`, with `gate_reason` the 5.4.3 or 5.4.4 code and `gate_class` `allowed`, `safety`, `integrity` or `none`.

Reviewer vocabulary (3.12, 3.13), not part of the outcome taxonomy: tasks `manifest_match`, `describe_collateral`, `manifest_visibility`; verdicts `matches_manifest`, `partially_matches_manifest`, `does_not_match_manifest`, `no_visible_difference`, `cannot_judge`, `not_applicable`; visibility `visible`, `not_visible`, `unsure`, `not_applicable`; change types `overlap`, `missing_element`, `added_element`, `clipped_text`, `shifted`, `resized`, `text_change`, `color_change`, `color_semantic_flip`, `other`. Routing threshold 0.80 maps `matches_manifest` to `intended`.

Finding triage states (4.13, 8.3): `open`, `confirmed_bug`, `intended`, `noise`, `agent_mistake`, `expected_behavior`, `fixed_pending_verify`, `closed`.

Decision actions, stored verdicts and effects, verbatim from 4.14 Decision record (9.6 shows the same mapping from the user's side and 8.3's CHECK enforces it):

| action (UI) | verdict (stored) | Inherited outcome on a later match | Finding `triage_state` | Ticket |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `confirm_bug` | `confirmed_bug` | computed outcome unchanged; finding filed under the ticket, no new alert | `confirmed_bug` | required |
| `mark_intended` | `intended` | `intended (reason: decision:<id>)`; on `invariant_violation` or `assertion_failed` the outcome never changes and the finding is suppressed as waived, expiry at most 30 days | `intended` | required |
| `request_mask` | `noise` once the mask PR merges; nothing before | `noise (reason: decision:<id>)` while the mask is active; a request that would put the panel over its mask budget is refused at submit (L-DEC-04) | `noise` | optional |
| `noise_signature` | `noise` | `noise (reason: decision:<id>)` | `noise` | optional |
| `agent_mistake` | `noise` | the Explorer finding's signature is closed; no checkpoint outcome involved | `agent_mistake` | none |
| `expected_behavior` | `noise` | as `agent_mistake`, for behavior that is by design | `expected_behavior` | none |
| `approve_baseline` | `intended` | the capture becomes the approved baseline for the checkpoint or cluster (9.8); not a signature match | `closed` | optional |
| `reject_baseline` | `confirmed_bug` with a ticket when the candidate shows a defect, else `noise` (the capture is not representative) | the candidate `baselines` row becomes `retired` (8.3, 9.6), `needs_baseline` persists until a new candidate is approved, and the finding returns to Unexpected | `confirmed_bug`, or `open` | required for `confirmed_bug` |
| `fixed_in_build` | `confirmed_bug` (updates the existing decision) | from that build on the run asserts the signature is gone; a return sets `status: reopened` | `fixed_pending_verify`, then `closed` after one clean run | required |

Decision verdicts (8.3): `confirmed_bug`, `intended`, `noise`. Decision status (4.14, 8.3): `active`, `expired`, `superseded`, `reopened`, `revoked`. `revoked` and `superseded` are distinct: a revoke withdraws a decision, sets `revoked_at`, `revoked_by` and `revoke_reason` together and moves the row to `revoked` (the CHECK allows the revoked fields only on a revoked row); a replacement is a new row whose `supersedes` points at the old one, which the writer marks `superseded`. Decision source (4.14, 8.3, 9.7): `report_ui` (default), `pr_comment`, `jira_sync` (a `fixed_in_build` row the Jira poller writes with the ticket resolver's login), `explorer_triage`. Baseline states (9.8, 8.3): `candidate`, `approved`, `retired`; approval is human-only, and a `reject_baseline` leaves the `baselines` row `retired` with `needs_baseline` persisting until a new candidate is approved.

### 12.3 Invariant catalog

Verbatim copy of the table in 2.7 Layout invariants, which is the invariant catalog for the whole spec. Branch A applies under Phase 0 decision DR-01 A (JAB exposes bounds and names), branch B under DR-01 B (OCR word boxes plus template-located controls). Common rules (2.7): bounds source per branch (an element whose bounds cannot be read is `needs_human (reason: bounds_unreadable)` unless a higher-precedence outcome applies; a bridge that dies mid-run is `harness_error (reason: bounds_source_unavailable)`; an OCR calibration miss is `harness_error (reason: ocr_calibration)`); a violation must persist on all 3 settled frames, and one that holds is re-captured once by the targeted re-run of 3.10 to confirm persistence: if the re-capture does not reproduce it, the checkpoint is `not_settled (reason: unstable)` with the violation kept as evidence for the flow owner; a violation present on both builds is pre-existing, reported once at one severity level lower; allowlisted overlapping pairs (tooltips, crosshair, drag ghosts, popup menus, overlay badges) never fire INV-01, INV-02 or INV-11; masks never apply to invariants; S1 heads the Unexpected section, S2 is listed, S3 is under a fold, and a tier-1 surface bumps S2 to S1 and S3 to S2; every fired invariant produces `invariant_violation` with the id as its reason (for example `invariant_violation (reason: INV-01)`), rects and a native crop, and the Reviewer never reclassifies it.

| Id | Statement | Branch A (JAB) | Branch B (OCR and templates) | False-positive controls | Sev | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INV-01 | No two sibling components' bounds intersect | Pairwise intersection of child rects per container, both showing and visible by state | Pairwise intersection of template-located control rects and of panels segmented by border lines and header templates | Overlap at least 4 px on both axes and 2 percent of the smaller rect; allowlist; 3 frames | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-02 | No component extends outside its parent | Child minus parent non-empty by more than 1 px; parent not a viewport with a showing scrollbar | Word box or control rect crossing a located panel border or the client rect by more than 1 px | Viewports excluded unless INV-06 fires; clipped-by-design regions declared per surface | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-03 | No text clipped at a boundary | Render the accessible name with the pinned per-build font metrics table and compare to inner width minus insets; OCR cross-check | Word box touching a cell or control edge within 1 px with OCR text differing from base at the same anchor, or recognized as a strict prefix of a declared label | Confidence floor 70; compare to base text, not a dictionary; a wider value with more digits is excluded when the Oracle digit count differs; inside a `rule` region or on a `masked_live` checkpoint the base-text comparison is replaced by the region's rule (format, decimals, digit count), so a word box at the edge fires only when its text fails that rule or is a strict prefix of a declared label | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-04 | No ellipsis where the base had none | Accessible name versus displayed text ends differently | OCR token ends in "..." or the ellipsis glyph where the base OCR at the same anchor did not | Same anchor on both builds; 3 frames; inside a `rule` region or on a `masked_live` checkpoint the base comparison is replaced by the region's rule, so an ellipsis fires only where that rule's format admits none | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-05 | Required labels present | Accessible names found in the tree | Template above 0.9 or OCR match within one edit in the declared region | Labels declared per surface and checkpoint, never inferred; absence on 3 frames | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-06 | No unexpected scrollbar | Scrollbar role in a container not allowed to scroll at this size | Scrollbar thumb template inside such a panel | Allowed scrollbars listed per surface with the minimum size at which none is expected | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-07 | Minimum legible font height | Font size attribute at least the pinned minimum (9 px font, about 7 px cap height, at the pinned font set) | Median word box cap height in the region at least the minimum in native pixels | Per region, not per word; icons excluded by template; thresholds from the base distribution at calibration | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-08 | No placeholder, loading or error text in a value region | Accessible text in value cells matches none of: Loading, Reconnecting, --, N/A, NaN, null, Infinity, empty-grid strings | OCR of declared value regions against the same set after settle; spinner template absent | Regions with a legitimate placeholder declare it; settle removes transient states first | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-09 | Every top-level window is inside the virtual screen; every owned dialog inside its owner's screen; main frame rect unchanged since run start | Window rects of the process tree versus virtual screen and the pinned frame rect | Same (no JAB needed) | None; off-screen or moved at pinned geometry is a defect | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-10 | Every required control present exactly once | Role and name match per declared control, count equals one | Exactly one template match above the confidence floor in the declared region | Controls declared per surface and checkpoint; a count of zero or two or more both fire; 3 frames | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-11 | No two text runs overlap | Text component bounds pairwise disjoint | Word boxes pairwise disjoint after 1 px erosion, across the whole capture | Allowlist; confidence floor 70; 3 frames | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-12 | Grid columns aligned | Cells of a column share left or right edge within 2 px per declared alignment; header spans the cells | Word boxes share right edge (numeric) or left edge (text) within 2 px; header spans | Alignment per column type; wrapped text excluded; at least 3 rows | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-13 | Focus traversal covers declared controls in order (ticket, confirm dialog) | Tab through the gateway; focus owner from JAB equals the declared sequence | Before and after diff per Tab located against declared rects; the changed rect must be the next control | Keyboard-only ticket flows only; Enter never pressed; Escape only at the end | S2 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-14 | No error dialog or exception window present at capture | Dialog role with title matching the error regex set | Java exception dialog template plus popup catalog error entries | Title regex and template both required; dialog owned by the process tree; the popup sentinel routes error dialogs here, never to the dismiss list; a dead process or frozen EDT is not INV-14 but `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` (2.6.1) | S1 | `invariant_violation` |
| INV-15 | Sign and color agree in P/L and change columns | Sign from JAB value; dominant foreground color of the cell crop against the pinned palette | Sign from OCR extraction; same color test | Declared signed columns only; palette pinned per theme; zero excluded | S1 | `invariant_violation` |

False-positive controls beyond the per-row column: INV-03 and INV-04 compare against the base capture's OCR at the same anchor, so labels already truncated on base do not fire; INV-07 is calibrated once per build on a known label and judged per region, not per word; tooltips, the chart crosshair, drag ghosts, popup menus and overlay badges are excluded by the per-surface allowlist and by the settle rule (mouse parked, focus dropped); INV-14 needs both the title regex and the template, and a dead process or frozen EDT is `assertion_failed (assertion: app_alive)` instead. Branch B is noisier on dense dark grids, so an invariant is enabled for a surface only after the A/A calibration runs show zero false positives for it on frozen checkpoints. Where a surface has no frozen checkpoints (DR-02 Branch B without OnDemand, including under DR-01 Branch B), the enablement test uses the masked_live A/A pairs of 3.9 captured in lockstep with their masks and rule regions in force, and INV-03 and INV-04 use the rule-region control of their rows; structural invariants do not depend on data values, so zero false positives over those calibration captures enables the Branch-B invariant. Until then it is listed per surface as `disabled: calibration pending` in run health, never silently off. An invariant that fires on an A/A pair after enabling is a harness bug recorded as `harness_error (reason: invariant_on_aa)` on the Nightly run (2.7, 4.13). Every invariant has at least one mutant in 12.5 proving it fires: INV-01 M08 and M12, INV-02 M29, INV-03 M10 and M12, INV-04 M11, INV-05 M18 (and M01), INV-06 M17, INV-07 M16, INV-08 M15, INV-09 M30, INV-10 M01 and M02, INV-11 M12, INV-12 M31, INV-13 M32, INV-14 M33, INV-15 M07.

### 12.4 Surface x persona matrix template

Rows are the tier-1 surfaces from the registry enumeration in 2.2.2, with the ids this appendix assigns (hyphens inside segments, dots between: 2.2.1); the probes P1 to P8 correct labels on the first validated run. Columns are the tier A personas. Cell codes are planned coverage: `C` census visit in that persona's workspace, `F` persona flow with assertions, `F$` tier-1 money flow with Oracle checks. Every cell has at least `C` because the census visits every registered surface in every corpus workspace that hosts it; a persona whose workspace does not host the surface is `not_run (reason: scope)` for that cell by design and leaves the denominator (2.12). `S` marks surfaces swept (Ladder S in PR and merge runs, Ladder F in RC runs) in the tier C workspace `ws.tier-c.sweep-harness`. The Reporter prints each cell as `covered (worst outcome, n)`, `not_run (entitlement | budget | scope | quarantine | step_failed:<step> | app_crash | base_step_failed | model_unavailable)`, `blocked:<outcome>` or `not_registered` (2.12). Entitlement values are the closed vocabulary of 2.2.1 and 4.5 (`margin`, `options_L1`, `options_L2`, `options_L3`, `futures`, `forex`, `ira`, `portfolio_margin`, `multi_account`, `paper_send`). Entitlements are per login, so a missing entitlement turns the whole row `not_run (entitlement)` for that profile; phase 1 profiles are paperMoney margin (GOLDEN) and paperMoney IRA (EMPTY). Data mode `frozen` assumes DR-02 branch A; under branch B the row runs `masked_live` with rule regions where OnDemand cannot replay it. In either mode a money cell (Qty, Price, Buying Power Effect, Max Loss, Send, Cancel, Delete) stays a `diff` or `freeze` region at a zero floor that also carries an Oracle rule, never `rule` only and never `mask` (3.8, 4.8 L-RGN-04); the account number and account holder name are identity fields, always redacted and never a region (3.6).

### 12.5 Starter mutant catalog

One catalog file, `sentinel-config/canaries/mutants.yaml`, with the entry schema of 4.11 Mutant catalog entry; this table is authoritative for ids M01 to M33, the seed 20260101 and the `money_cell` flag (10.3), and new entries take the next id. Image mutants are generated at the start of every Nightly run from the approved base capture of the bound checkpoint with seed 20260101, injected as candidate images through the normal diff, Region Registry, invariant, Oracle and Reviewer path, and flagged `synthetic: true` (10.3). Behavioral mutants drive the live app through a `canary` flow (4.11). Class names are the 26 snake_case names of the class table in 10.3, which the class enum of 4.11 and the `defect_class` column of `canary_results` (8.3) carry unchanged: `erased_control`, `swapped_digit`, `swapped_label`, `color_swap`, `shifted_panel`, `clipped_label`, `overlapped_panels`, `missing_row`, `header_change`, `placeholder`, `font_height`, `scrollbar`, `redaction`, `sub_floor`, `global_shift`, `landmark_loss`, `study_removed`, `aa_control`, `wrong_quantity`, `blank_field`, `gateway`, `outside_parent`, `window_offscreen`, `misaligned_column`, `focus_order`, `error_dialog`. M20 and M25 are the controls, M25 the identical control. `money_cell: yes` marks a mutant on a money cell of 3.8, a closed list: Qty, Price, Buying Power Effect, Max Loss, Send, Cancel, Delete. The ladder price column, P/L, balances, the BUY and SELL labels and dialog titles are tier-1 regions, not money cells, so their mutants (M06, M07, M08, M10, M12, M18, M22) are non-money and count toward `detector_degraded`, and the controls M20 and M25 target no cell (10.3); the account number and the account holder name are identity fields, never a money-cell target, and M19 with the redaction canary of 6.10 proves them instead. `money_cell: yes` means detection must stay at 100 percent: one miss sets the canary state `detector_blind`, the mutant's synthetic row is `harness_error (reason: detector_blind)`, the morning report says the detector is blind and RC sign-off blocks while the Nightly run stays `complete`. Other mutants count against the rolling floor of their class (`detector_degraded`). For every image mutant except the two controls, `collateral` or `needs_human` landing on the mutated region also counts as detected; the expected outcome names the primary signal in the taxonomy's own words (12.2) and the invariant ids of 12.3. Checkpoint ids follow the grammar of 4.1: the sweep host is `flexgrid` for a Flexible Grid cell, and a flow checkpoint carries the full `flow_id`. The stock limit order flow is `flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit`, the second worked flow of 4.7 (`s03` the pre-input checkpoint): step `s06` is the filled ticket before Confirm and Send, checkpoint `flow/trade.order-entry.stock/flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit/s06` on the order entry surface `trade.order-entry.stock` (M01, M20), and step `s07` the Order Confirmation dialog, checkpoint `flow/dialog.order-confirmation/flow.trade.order-ticket.stock.limit/s07` (M02 to M06 and M22, as 4.11 binds M02 and M03), the checkpoint 10.2's heartbeat example and 10.3's morning message name for M05.

### 12.6 Run-start attestation checklist

Verbatim copy of the table in 6.3 Run-start settings attestation, which owns the procedure. The Orchestrator runs it at the gates `paper_mode_asserted` (A1, A2) and `settings_attested` (A3 to A11) of every run and again after any re-login (5.2, 6.3). It reads and never repairs: a safety row that mismatches ends the run `aborted_safety` with gate name, row id and screenshot, opens an incident (S1 for A1 and A8, and for A9 when a new row appears; S2 otherwise) and pages on-call, and every scoped checkpoint is `env_error (gate: settings_attested)`; repair is the maintenance flow of 7.6 on a human decision, followed by a fresh attestation. A1 and A2 run first and alone; A3 to A8 run before A9, so the one item that touches a ticket (A9, Confirmation still required) runs with the confirmation setting already read as On and no working orders present. A row unreadable after one re-navigation is `env_error (gate: settings_attested, reason: attestation_unreadable)` on every scoped checkpoint, run `complete_with_env_errors`, P2, and P1 on two consecutive runs; an unreadable A1 or A2 follows 6.4 (`env_error (gate: paper_mode_asserted, reason: identity_unreadable)` with the hook in deny-all). The hot-key list read in A6 is loaded into the gateway's blocked chord list even though it must be empty (5.4.7). Proof: the nightly attestation canary feeds the reader planted crops of A3 to A8 with the state flipped and one unreadable crop each; a miss is `harness_error (reason: safety_canary_blind:attestation)` on the canary's row (state `detector_blind`, 6.5), the morning report says the attestation reader is blind, and no product run starts on that rig until the canary passes (6.3, 10.3); the deny-list, secret-scan, redaction and identity canaries use the same form, `safety_canary_blind:<canary>`. A9 and A10 are proven by every run, and drill item 1 repeats A9 nightly (6.5).

| Id | Item | Where and how read | Expected | On mismatch | On unreadable |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Paper mode | Account selector text, OCR (JAB under DR-01 branch A), after login, before every flow, after any re-login | Exactly equal to one entry of the rig's allowlist (6.4) | Kill process tree, `aborted_safety`, S1 | Identity-unreadable path of 6.4 |

### 12.7 Preflight checklist

Runs on the reverted rig at the `provisioned` gate, before the state machine enters `launched` (5.2, 5.3, 7.11, 10.8). The Rig Manager runs the R, B, N and G items and the harness self-tests H1 to H10 (5.3, 7.11). 32 items in five groups: R rig (R1 to R7), B build (B1 to B3), H harness self-test (H1 to H10), N network (N1 to N7), G gateway and registries (G1 to G5). One retry rule applies to every item: a failed item is retried once after 60 s and both attempts are logged; a second failure takes the item's outcome below (7.11). Nothing is skipped and no item passes by default. Run health lists every item with pass or fail.

Outcomes by group, as 5.3, 7.11 and 10.8 apply them:

- R and B items, G2 to G4, N1 and N6: every scheduled checkpoint `env_error (gate: preflight.<item>)`, for example `env_error (gate: preflight.R7)`, with reason `gate` unless a finer code of 4.13 applies; run `complete_with_env_errors`; on-call channel.
- H items: run `aborted_harness (reason: preflight.<item>)` before any product action, written exactly so (`preflight.H1` to `preflight.H10`), with every scheduled checkpoint `harness_error (reason: preflight.<item>)`, the run's abort reason. A control that blocked the item (EDR, AppLocker, DLP, proxy) is named in `detail` and is a hardening finding (7.12, 11.7 row 4). A Watchdog lost later in the run is `aborted_harness (reason: watchdog_dead)` (10.2); a capturing process found not Per-Monitor-V2 aware at H3 is `aborted_harness (reason: dpi_awareness)` (3.4, 7.1).
- N2 and N5: a degraded mode, never `env_error` and not a checkpoint outcome: the run continues with `review_mode: deferred` and `agent_available: false`; review is deferred (`needs_human` with `review_state: pending`); agent fallback and the Explorer are disabled, so locator failures end `failed` and an Explorer session or agent-only step is `not_run (reason: model_unavailable)`; the report publishes `unreviewed`; N5 also names the blocking control in run health and raises a hardening finding (7.11, 10.7). N3: only the checkpoints with `api_within` assertions are `env_error (gate: preflight.N3)` (reason `gate`; the symbol pre-check falls back to the app quote, 7.9). N4: frozen checkpoints `env_error (gate: preflight.N4)`. N7: the run proceeds, publication retries with backoff, and the dead-man alert covers an unreachable host (10.2).
- G1: a lint `error` ends the run `aborted_harness (reason: config_invalid)` before capture (4.15); an anchor-lint miss is a maintenance item and the run continues (11.5). G5: every checkpoint `not_comparable (reason: fingerprint_mismatch)` naming the field, captures still collected; no Calibration for the fingerprint queues one and routes above-zero diffs to `needs_human (reason: uncalibrated)` (7.13).
- A preflight N1, N3 or N4 failure inside a listed `maintenance_windows` entry reschedules the run once to the window end plus 15 minutes, with a run-health notice instead of `env_error` (7.10, 7.11).

| # | Check | Method | Pass | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
